notes.title: Index
notes.body:
# STS Second Brain

Start here. This is a map of content, not a container — every note below lives
in its own file and links onward.

## Reference library

- [[Reference library]] — catalogue of the standards, papers and texts held locally
- [[Project reports]] — factual index of the 17 Core Geotech reports held locally

## Skills

- [[Skills]] — 184 action-based working aids: mined from the reference library's
  practice documents, from the Rock Mechanics lecture playlist, and from STS's
  own field records in Google Drive ([[Field records catalogue]])

## Learning

- [[Learning loop]] — the recursive cycle: drill flashcards, walk a staged
  learning path, apply it in the field, capture what differed, refine the
  notes, regenerate the decks

## Section maps

Clause numbers and headings only, so a clause can be found without opening the
document.

- [[Section map - AS 1726:2017]]
- [[Section map - AS 2159:2009]]
- [[Section map - AS 2870:2011]]
- [[Section map - AS 3798:2007]]
- [[Section map - AS 4678:2002]]

## Standards

- [[AS 1726 soil and rock description]] — how we describe what comes out of the ground
- [[AS 2159 piling]] — what governs bored pier construction and acceptance
- [[AS 2870 residential site classification]] — reactive site classes

## Materials

- [[Soil description order]] — the sequence we write descriptions in
- [[Rock weathering classes]] — XW through FR, and what each means for founding
- [[Rock strength classes]] — EL through EH and the field tests behind them
- [[Weathered siltstone]] — the founding material on most Sydney basin jobs

## Methods

- [[Bored pier inspection]] — what to check and record at the base of a pier
- [[Rock socket length]] — how socket length is specified, measured and reported
- [[DCP testing]] — blow counts to allowable bearing pressure
- [[Reduced levels and datums]] — RL conventions and the mistakes that follow from getting them wrong
- [[Groundwater observations]] — what a water level in a hole does and does not tell you
- [[Borehole log conventions]] — how our logs are laid out and why

## Working with AI

- [[Reverse prompting]] — hand over context, let the agent ask what it is missing
- [[Graph engineering]] — dependency maps, the fake-edge test, diamonds and checkers

## Decisions

- [[Why pile data carries provenance]] — the Field state model in the pile viewer
- [[Socket compliance is indeterminate by default]] — why unknown never reads as pass

## Templates

- [[Template - site inspection note]]
- [[Template - decision]]

notes.title: Open in Obsidian
notes.body:
# Open in Obsidian

1. Open Obsidian → **Open folder as vault**
2. Choose the folder this file is in (`STS-Second-Brain`)
3. Trust the vault when prompted — the only thing in `.obsidian/` is graph and
   appearance settings, no plugins or scripts

Graph view is on the left ribbon, or `Ctrl+G`. It comes pre-coloured by folder:

| Colour | Folder |
|---|---|
| Violet | the index |
| Blue | standards |
| Green | materials |
| Orange | methods |
| Red | decisions |
| Amber | reference library |
| Grey | templates |

Local graph (`Ctrl+Shift+G` or the note's ⋮ menu) shows what one note connects
to, which is usually more useful than the whole graph once the vault grows.

## Keeping it in step with the web viewer

The Markdown here is the source of truth. After editing, regenerate the web
viewer's index from the repo:

```bash
node scripts/build-vault-index.mjs
```

The repo copy lives at `sts-playground/second-brain/`. If you edit here and
there, they will drift — pick one as the working copy.

## Related

- [[Index]]

notes.title: Socket compliance is indeterminate by default
notes.body:
# Socket compliance is indeterminate by default

**Decision.** When the required socket length is unknown, socket compliance
returns `indeterminate` — never `compliant`.

## Reasoning

Compliance is achieved measured against required. Our inspection reports carry
the achieved length; the requirement lives on the structural drawing, which we
often do not hold. A tool that defaults to pass in that situation manufactures an
engineering conclusion out of an absence of data.

`indeterminate` is a first-class answer with its own colour in the 3D scene,
deliberately not the same orange as a verified socket, so an unassessed pier
cannot read as approved at a glance.

## What it means in practice

On the Carter Street job all 18 inspected piers report as compliance-unknown,
because the report states no required socket. That is the correct reading of the
available information, and it makes the missing document visible.

## Related

- [[Rock socket length]]
- [[AS 2159 piling]]
- [[Why pile data carries provenance]]

notes.title: Why pile data carries provenance
notes.body:
# Why pile data carries provenance

**Decision.** Every engineering value in the pile viewer is a `Field<T>` carrying
value, state, source and confidence, rather than a bare number.

States: `extracted`, `calculated`, `manual`, `inferred`, `verified`,
`conflicting`, `missing`.

## The problem it solves

Once a number is in a spreadsheet it looks like every other number. A toe level
read off a signed report and a toe level someone estimated from a drawing render
identically, and by the time it matters nobody can tell which is which.

## Consequences

- A missing value stays missing all the way to the screen. A pile with no toe
  level has no length — it does not have a length of zero.
- When two sources disagree the field is `conflicting`, both values are kept, and
  the engineer resolves it. Source priority orders them for review; it does not
  pick a winner, because a higher-priority document is only better if it is also
  the current revision, which the tool cannot confirm.
- Piles missing position, levels or diameter are listed as undrawable with the
  blocker named, rather than placed at the origin with a guessed size.

## Cost

More verbose than plain numbers, and every UI component has to render a state.
Accepted — see [[Reduced levels and datums]] for the failure mode this prevents.

## Related

- [[Socket compliance is indeterminate by default]]

notes.title: Learning loop
notes.body:
# Learning loop

The vault as a *recursive* learning system, not a filing cabinet. One cycle:

1. **Drill.** Work a flashcard deck below (Obsidian's Spaced Repetition plugin
   reads the `#flashcards/...` tags; on the web viewer, read the deck and
   self-test). Failed cards name the skills to reread.
2. **Study.** Walk the learning path for the weakest area — each path is
   staged observe → measure → calculate → judge, and is meant to be re-entered
   whenever a later stage exposes a gap in an earlier one.
3. **Apply.** Do the field or office work. The skill notes are working aids;
   the source documents stay the authority.
4. **Capture.** When reality differs from a note — a form revision, a step the
   record never showed, a mistake worth remembering — capture it at the moment
   it happens (the viewer's Capture tab, bank *lesson*, or a quick note in
   Obsidian) naming the skill it belongs to.
5. **Refine.** Periodically fold captures back into the skill notes: amend the
   procedure or caveats, bump `updated`, adjust `confidence`. Then regenerate —
   the decks and paths are built *from* the skill notes
   (`gen-learning.py`), so a refined note automatically becomes refined cards.
   The next Drill runs on the improved vault. That closure is the recursion.

Skills whose sources are records rather than procedures (`field-source`) get
better with every pass of this loop — each capture is new evidence.

notes.title: Flashcards - Drainage
notes.body:
# Flashcards - Drainage

#flashcards/drainage

16 cards generated from the 4 drainage skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Check as-built drainage tolerances and CCTV acceptance under R11" produce?::Completed drainage is verified within construction tolerances and internally inspected, with conforming CCTV reports lodged at the two required milestones.
Before relying on "Check as-built drainage tolerances and CCTV acceptance under R11" — what do you check?::Both CCTV passes done, with the second inside the pre-Completion window • Open drain grade continuity verified along the full length, not just at spot levels • Reports reference WSA 05 condition codes
"Check as-built drainage tolerances and CCTV acceptance under R11" — state the decision rule about: Tolerances apply to the accepted amended set-out where one e…::Tolerances apply to the accepted amended set-out where one exists, not the original drawings.
"Check as-built drainage tolerances and CCTV acceptance under R11" — state the decision rule about: Steps between box culvert units within the intermediate band…::Steps between box culvert units within the intermediate band must be smoothed; larger steps are nonconforming.
What does "Confirm select fill and bedding material conformity for pipes under R11" produce?::Bedding and support fill materials are demonstrated conforming, at the specified testing frequency, before placement around pipes and culverts.
Before relying on "Confirm select fill and bedding material conformity for pipes under R11" — what do you check?::Test methods match those nominated (RMS T201 for grading, RMS T109 for plasticity) • Sampling was done prior to placement, not retrospectively • Certificates of conformity are on file as identified records
"Confirm select fill and bedding material conformity for pipes under R11" — state the decision rule about: Material failing grading or plasticity limits must not be pl…::Material failing grading or plasticity limits must not be placed in the nominated zone - reassign or reject.
"Confirm select fill and bedding material conformity for pipes under R11" — state the decision rule about: If testing frequency in Annexure R11/L has not been met for …::If testing frequency in Annexure R11/L has not been met for the volume placed, the lot lacks conformity evidence regardless of the results in hand.
What does "Manage hold and witness points through R11 drainage construction" produce?::No drainage work proceeds past a required inspection gate without release, avoiding rework and nonconformances.
Before relying on "Manage hold and witness points through R11 drainage construction" — what do you check?::Notice periods met (e.g. 7 days for precast supply documents and certificates of conformity) • Release evidence recorded against each hold point before dependent work started • Surveys before/after removal of inadequate material captured for quantity measurement
"Manage hold and witness points through R11 drainage construction" — state the decision rule about: Work that would alter a held process before release is nonco…::Work that would alter a held process before release is nonconforming even if the end product later tests conforming.
"Manage hold and witness points through R11 drainage construction" — state the decision rule about: Previously submitted precast documentation can be re-certifi…::Previously submitted precast documentation can be re-certified rather than re-submitted only within the currency window stated in Clause 2.4.1.
What does "Verify trench backfill compaction around drainage structures under R11" produce?::A drainage structure backfill lot is accepted or rejected against R11's relative compaction and layering rules, with the correct field density test method used.
Before relying on "Verify trench backfill compaction around drainage structures under R11" — what do you check?::One test method only used per lot for statistical assessment • Layer thickness records consistent with the compacted thickness limit • Moisture control documented so nearby earthworks are not wetted up • Box culvert side/overlay zones backfilled with Type SO Select Fill, with the 1000 mm minimum select fill envelope and geotextile separation where inside rock fi
"Verify trench backfill compaction around drainage structures under R11" — state the decision rule about: If more than 40% by mass is retained on the 37.5 mm sieve, d…::If more than 40% by mass is retained on the 37.5 mm sieve, do not report relative compaction - the result is invalid (Table R11.3 note).
"Verify trench backfill compaction around drainage structures under R11" — state the decision rule about: If the characteristic relative compaction is below the Table…::If the characteristic relative compaction is below the Table R11.2 minimum for that zone, the lot is nonconforming.

## Related

- [[Learning path - Drainage]]
- [[Learning loop]]

notes.title: Flashcards - Earthworks and specifications
notes.body:
# Flashcards - Earthworks and specifications

#flashcards/earthworks

76 cards generated from the 19 earthworks and specifications skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Apply edition-correct compaction criteria when reviewing legacy R44 Ed 3 lots" produce?::Historic or legacy-contract earthworks conformity is assessed against the Ed 3 Rev 15 regime rather than current-edition values, avoiding false nonconformances.
Before relying on "Apply edition-correct compaction criteria when reviewing legacy R44 Ed 3 lots" — what do you check?::Laboratory independence per RMS Q • Test hole repair method documented in the project quality plan • Moisture methods T121/T180 only used with prior calibration against T120
"Apply edition-correct compaction criteria when reviewing legacy R44 Ed 3 lots" — state the decision rule about: Single test method per lot; no mixing of T119 and T173 resul…::Single test method per lot; no mixing of T119 and T173 results statistically.
"Apply edition-correct compaction criteria when reviewing legacy R44 Ed 3 lots" — state the decision rule about: Standard compaction reference applies (Clause 7.2.1) - do no…::Standard compaction reference applies (Clause 7.2.1) - do not judge against modified compaction ratios.
What does "Backfill against bridge abutments and walls" produce?::Structure backfill placed with conforming material, moisture, layer thickness and compaction without damaging or unbalancing the structure.
Before relying on "Backfill against bridge abutments and walls" — what do you check?::Density testing per the minimum-frequency annexure; characteristic relative compaction computed per RMS Q and rounded to 0.1%. • Lot conformity assessed on characteristic value, not individual test minima.
"Backfill against bridge abutments and walls" — state the decision rule about: Field moisture at placement must be 60-90% of optimum unless…::Field moisture at placement must be 60-90% of optimum unless otherwise authorised (b030 Clause 6.4.1).
"Backfill against bridge abutments and walls" — state the decision rule about: Layer/compaction limits: Select Fill under foundations 150 m…::Layer/compaction limits: Select Fill under foundations 150 mm layers at 102% relative compaction; Select Fill behind walls within H/2, 150 mm at 98%; earth fill elsewhere 300 mm at 98% (characteristic
What does "Check earthworks lot compaction conformity under TfNSW R44" produce?::An earthworks lot is statistically assessed for relative compaction and moisture and accepted or rejected against the correct location-based criterion.
Before relying on "Check earthworks lot compaction conformity under TfNSW R44" — what do you check?::Laboratory independence in sampling/testing per TfNSW Q Annexure Q/L • Each layer compacted full depth and conforming before the next layer starts (Clause 7.1) • Rounding applied to 0.1% before comparison
"Check earthworks lot compaction conformity under TfNSW R44" — state the decision rule about: Conformity requires the lower limit of the characteristic va…::Conformity requires the lower limit of the characteristic value to be at or above the Table R44.10 value for that location - individual test values alone do not decide the lot.
"Check earthworks lot compaction conformity under TfNSW R44" — state the decision rule about: Results from different test methods must never be combined i…::Results from different test methods must never be combined in one lot's statistics (Clause 7.3.4).
What does "Classify unsuitable material into NR44's three categories before directing removal" produce?::Faster, better-costed decisions on foundation material: spoil, treat in place, bridge over, or accept - instead of defaulting to blanket removal.
Before relying on "Classify unsuitable material into NR44's three categories before directing removal" — what do you check?::Hold point discipline retained: Principal inspects before each lot of unsuitable is replaced • Before/after surveys captured for quantity measurement • Category decision recorded with its basis (inspection, testing, judgement)
"Classify unsuitable material into NR44's three categories before directing removal" — state the decision rule about: A quick decision with a small extra removal cost usually bea…::A quick decision with a small extra removal cost usually beats a delayed optimal decision.
"Classify unsuitable material into NR44's three categories before directing removal" — state the decision rule about: Material wet but sound can often be placed deep in high fill…::Material wet but sound can often be placed deep in high fills with geotechnical concurrence; monitor heave and pore pressure dissipation rather than rejecting it.
What does "Confirm Selected Material Zone lot conformity under R44 Ed 3" produce?::Selected Material Zone stockpiles and placed lots are proven conforming through the pre-placement CBR regime and the two-stage hold points.
Before relying on "Confirm Selected Material Zone lot conformity under R44 Ed 3" — what do you check?::Lot tonnage vs sample count band • Layer thickness records against the cap • Characteristic (not mean) CBR used for acceptance
"Confirm Selected Material Zone lot conformity under R44 Ed 3" — state the decision rule about: No placement of SMZ material without released stockpile-conf…::No placement of SMZ material without released stockpile-conformity hold point.
"Confirm Selected Material Zone lot conformity under R44 Ed 3" — state the decision rule about: Segregated stone patches or excess fines after placement are…::Segregated stone patches or excess fines after placement are nonconforming regardless of stockpile results.
What does "Excavate and inspect bridge foundations" produce?::Bridge foundation excavations taken to design level, inspected and accepted at the hold point before blinding concrete is placed.
Before relying on "Excavate and inspect bridge foundations" — what do you check?::Levels and dimensions conformity records exist for each foundation member before requesting hold point release. • Cofferdam/shoring design was certified by a chartered professional engineer and submitted at least 5 working days before construction (its own hold point). • Cofferdams removed to at least 0.5 m below finished/natural surface.
"Excavate and inspect bridge foundations" — state the decision rule about: Blasting is prohibited for foundation-member excavation (b03…::Blasting is prohibited for foundation-member excavation (b030 Clause 4.1.2).
"Excavate and inspect bridge foundations" — state the decision rule about: The pre-blinding inspection hold point applies to every foun…::The pre-blinding inspection hold point applies to every foundation member except those supported on piles (b030 Clause 4.4).
What does "Manage over-wet earth fill using NR44 placement strategies" produce?::Over-optimum-moisture material is placed or treated without compromising embankment stability or pavement support, minimising drying downtime.
Before relying on "Manage over-wet earth fill using NR44 placement strategies" — what do you check?::Pore-pressure/heave observations logged layer by layer • Placement zones for wet material clear of pavement deflection influence • Contract cost allocation understood - drying, lime treatment and rehandling sit with the contractor unless specified otherwise
"Manage over-wet earth fill using NR44 placement strategies" — state the decision rule about: Full-width over-wet expansive clay placement risks embankmen…::Full-width over-wet expansive clay placement risks embankment instability - zone it or relocate it.
"Manage over-wet earth fill using NR44 placement strategies" — state the decision rule about: If heave under loaded plant is severe or persists, stop and …::If heave under loaded plant is severe or persists, stop and allow further dissipation or re-treat; do not bury the problem under the next layer.
What does "Run Benkelman Beam deflection lots under R44 Ed 3" produce?::Formation deflection lots are laid out, tested and assessed to the Ed 3 rules, including its distinct minimum lot length and annexure-based formula.
Before relying on "Run Benkelman Beam deflection lots under R44 Ed 3" — what do you check?::Surface prepared for deflection monitoring during SMZ trimming • Test coverage over the SMZ plan area plus any Principal-directed areas • Lot boundaries physically identifiable in the field
"Run Benkelman Beam deflection lots under R44 Ed 3" — state the decision rule about: Testing outside the 3-day post-compaction window invalidates…::Testing outside the 3-day post-compaction window invalidates the lot unless the Principal approved a delay.
"Run Benkelman Beam deflection lots under R44 Ed 3" — state the decision rule about: Exceeding either the deflection limit or the scatter caps bl…::Exceeding either the deflection limit or the scatter caps blocks the hold point release.
What does "Run proof rolling and Benkelman Beam deflection acceptance under R44" produce?::Formation stability is demonstrated by proof rolling and, where specified, quantified by Benkelman Beam deflection, releasing the hold point for placing the Selected Material Zone or pavement.
Before relying on "Run proof rolling and Benkelman Beam deflection acceptance under R44" — what do you check?::Benkelman lot is a continuous, homogeneous length at least one carriageway wide with field-marked boundaries • Testing done within the 3-day window or with documented Principal approval for delay • Witness/hold point notices lodged with the specified lead times
"Run proof rolling and Benkelman Beam deflection acceptance under R44" — state the decision rule about: Visible deformation, rutting or yielding under the proof rol…::Visible deformation, rutting or yielding under the proof roller fails the surface regardless of density results.
"Run proof rolling and Benkelman Beam deflection acceptance under R44" — state the decision rule about: Characteristic deflection above the A4 value triggers re-exa…::Characteristic deflection above the A4 value triggers re-examination of lot boundaries and homogeneity, then re-nomination and retesting.
What does "Select geotextile strength and filtration class" produce?::The correct geotextile strength class and filtration class for a separation/filtration application, matched to fill size, subgrade strength and soil fines.
Before relying on "Select geotextile strength and filtration class" — what do you check?::Application-specific site details (D90, CBR, soil type) recorded in the project annexure table. • High-strength basal reinforcement under embankments on soft ground is outside this spec - use the appropriate reinforcement spec.
"Select geotextile strength and filtration class" — state the decision rule about: Strength class escalates with larger D90 and weaker/saturate…::Strength class escalates with larger D90 and weaker/saturated subgrades; some large-stone saturated cases are simply not permitted with any class (RMS Spec D&C R63 Annexure R63/E Table E.1 notes).
"Select geotextile strength and filtration class" — state the decision rule about: Filtration EOS ceilings tighten as soil fines increase (fine…::Filtration EOS ceilings tighten as soil fines increase (finer soils need smaller opening sizes) with matching minimum flow/permittivity values (Annexure R63/E Table E.1).
What does "Select the correct field density test method for an R44 earthworks lot" produce?::The field density method matches the material's oversize content and layer thickness, so relative compaction results are valid and defensible.
Before relying on "Select the correct field density test method for an R44 earthworks lot" — what do you check?::Smooth surface prepared at each sampling location • Companion sample taken from the correct zone relative to the density test • Oversize proportion and density determined for every sample, whatever the field method
"Select the correct field density test method for an R44 earthworks lot" — state the decision rule about: One test method per lot - choose before testing starts and d…::One test method per lot - choose before testing starts and do not mix (Clause 7.3.4).
"Select the correct field density test method for an R44 earthworks lot" — state the decision rule about: If oversize exceeds the upper Table R44.9 threshold, do not …::If oversize exceeds the upper Table R44.9 threshold, do not report relative compaction at all; the lot needs a procedure-based approach (e.g. rock fill rules) instead.
What does "Sequence R44 hold points from stripping through to formation cover-up" produce?::Earthworks proceed without breaching any of the staged inspection gates, keeping lots releasable and payment claims clean.
Before relying on "Sequence R44 hold points from stripping through to formation cover-up" — what do you check?::Identified records per R44/C3 retained (Earthworks Plan, spoil/borrow records, blasting records, deflection results) • Joint surveys done where Annexure R44/A1 nominates them • Notice periods (typically 1-3 working days, 10 for stockpile/borrow concurrence) tracked in the program
"Sequence R44 hold points from stripping through to formation cover-up" — state the decision rule about: Imported material for the upper zone is blocked until availa…::Imported material for the upper zone is blocked until available suitable site-won material is used or assigned - importing early is a nonconformance with payment consequences.
"Sequence R44 hold points from stripping through to formation cover-up" — state the decision rule about: Any surface that ruts, yields or shows distress must be noti…::Any surface that ruts, yields or shows distress must be notified promptly even between formal gates (Clause 2.4.1).
What does "Size and embed reinforced soil wall" produce?::RSW geometry (reinforcement length, embedment depth, toe berm) meeting the roads-authority minimum dimensions before detailed design starts.
Before relying on "Size and embed reinforced soil wall" — what do you check?::Confirm weak or soft foundation soils have been considered for deeper embedment on the geotechnical engineer's advice. • Confirm lengthened top reinforcement layers for impact loading have not been misclassified as a trapezoidal section.
"Size and embed reinforced soil wall" — state the decision rule about: Minimum reinforcement length: the greater of 2 m or (0.6H + …::Minimum reinforcement length: the greater of 2 m or (0.6H + 1) m for non-abutment walls; the greater of 7 m or (0.6H + 2) m for bridge abutments (r057 Table R57.5).
"Size and embed reinforced soil wall" — state the decision rule about: Minimum embedment ranges from H/20 (level ground, non-abutme…::Minimum embedment ranges from H/20 (level ground, non-abutment) to H/5 (steep toe slope), never less than 0.3 m; abutments on level ground require H/10 (r057 Table R57.6).
What does "Specify reinforced fill for soil wall" produce?::A reinforced fill specification (grading, plasticity, durability, strength parameters) that will realise the design friction angle in the constructed wall.
Before relying on "Specify reinforced fill for soil wall" — what do you check?::Confirm index tests were run on pretreated samples per the specified test-method sequence, not raw feed. • Confirm the adopted design friction angle is not greater than the tested value and respects the 34/36 degree caps. • Confirm electrolytic compatibility or insulation between dissimilar metallic components.
"Specify reinforced fill for soil wall" — state the decision rule about: Fill fails if grading, uniformity coefficient, liquid limit …::Fill fails if grading, uniformity coefficient, liquid limit or plasticity index fall outside Table R57.10 limits (r057 Clause 5.3).
"Specify reinforced fill for soil wall" — state the decision rule about: Maximum particle dimension differs for steel vs geosynthetic…::Maximum particle dimension differs for steel vs geosynthetic reinforcement and must not exceed one third of the lift thickness (r057 Table R57.10 note).
What does "Use NR44 commentary to brief teams on R44 intent and economical material choices" produce?::Site and design teams apply R44 the way the Principal intends - right materials in the right zones, testing effort where it matters - reducing disputes.
Before relying on "Use NR44 commentary to brief teams on R44 intent and economical material choices" — what do you check?::Guide edition (based on R44 Ed 4 Rev 1) mapped against the project's R44 edition for clause renumbering • Team briefings distinguish spec text from commentary • Material selection decisions documented with the economy rationale
"Use NR44 commentary to brief teams on R44 intent and economical material choices" — state the decision rule about: Never cite NR44 as a contractual requirement - it is explici…::Never cite NR44 as a contractual requirement - it is explicitly not a contract document.
"Use NR44 commentary to brief teams on R44 intent and economical material choices" — state the decision rule about: Where NR44 commentary conflicts with the project's R44 editi…::Where NR44 commentary conflicts with the project's R44 edition or contract, the contract wins.
What does "Verify a rock fill compaction routine by trial sections under R44 Ed 3" produce?::Rock fill placing is accepted on a verified procedure basis (routine + proof rolling), since density testing is invalid for coarse rock fill.
Before relying on "Verify a rock fill compaction routine by trial sections under R44 Ed 3" — what do you check?::Rock fill material actually meets rock fill definitions (otherwise earth fill compaction testing applies) • Trial documentation covers all six submission detail items • Production records show the nominated routine followed layer by layer
"Verify a rock fill compaction routine by trial sections under R44 Ed 3" — state the decision rule about: Nonconforming in-process results stop placement: either rede…::Nonconforming in-process results stop placement: either redevelop the routine with new trials (hold point re-applies) or break down/sort the rock to earth fill and follow earth fill rules.
"Verify a rock fill compaction routine by trial sections under R44 Ed 3" — state the decision rule about: Two contiguous sections built in one continuous operation do…::Two contiguous sections built in one continuous operation do not count as two successive trials.
What does "Verify and place geotextile on site" produce?::Geotextile accepted through supply and placement hold points, then installed without damage and with correct overlaps and cover.
Before relying on "Verify and place geotextile on site" — what do you check?::Site test means compared against certificate means - drift beyond the stated standard-deviation rules makes deliveries nonconforming. • No vibratory or heavy compaction plant on initial fill layers. • Trench drain geotextile placed loose and fully enveloping the drainage media.
"Verify and place geotextile on site" — state the decision rule about: Sampling: one roll for the initial 10,000 m2 (or part), then…::Sampling: one roll for the initial 10,000 m2 (or part), then one per 20,000 m2 (Clause 2.4.2).
"Verify and place geotextile on site" — state the decision rule about: Cover placed geotextile within 48 hours (Clause 4.3).…::Cover placed geotextile within 48 hours (Clause 4.3).
What does "Verify external stability of reinforced soil wall" produce?::A reinforced soil wall (RSW) external design certified by a geotechnical engineer against bearing, sliding, overall slip and eccentricity limit states.
Before relying on "Verify external stability of reinforced soil wall" — what do you check?::Confirm the design water table assumption: ground surface level in front of the wall unless flooded/submerged cases apply (r057 Clause 4.2(f)). • Confirm liquefaction screening of granular foundations against the density-index/SPT thresholds in Clause 4.3.1.6 where earthquake load cases apply. • Confirm all material factors used are stated in the design output and are no less stringent than the specification tables.
"Verify external stability of reinforced soil wall" — state the decision rule about: Minimum overall slip factor of safety: 1.35 for walls not su…::Minimum overall slip factor of safety: 1.35 for walls not supporting bridge abutments, 1.6 for walls supporting abutments (constant-volume strength method); alternative peak-strength method requires 1
"Verify external stability of reinforced soil wall" — state the decision rule about: Serviceability eccentricity ratio e/L must stay below 1/6 (r…::Serviceability eccentricity ratio e/L must stay below 1/6 (r057 Clause 4.7.6).
What does "Verify formation surface levels against R44 level tolerances" produce?::Each finished earthworks surface is confirmed inside its level tolerance band, or handled through the below-tolerance acceptance mechanism.
Before relying on "Verify formation surface levels against R44 level tolerances" — what do you check?::Correct tolerance row chosen for the foundation treatment type (drainage layers in rock cuttings have a deeper allowance) • Survey density sufficient to catch localised highs/lows • Level checks done before the surface is covered (linked to the Clause 7.6.2 hold point)
"Verify formation surface levels against R44 level tolerances" — state the decision rule about: Plus-zero upper limits mean any high spot on the formation t…::Plus-zero upper limits mean any high spot on the formation top is nonconforming - trim, don't negotiate.
"Verify formation surface levels against R44 level tolerances" — state the decision rule about: Below-tolerance acceptance with deduction is only available …::Below-tolerance acceptance with deduction is only available in the specific overlying-layer-not-in-Contract case; otherwise rectify.

"Verify formation surface levels against R44 level tolerances" — state the decision rule about: Below tolerance acceptance with deduction is only available …::Below tolerance acceptance with deduction is only available in the specific overlying layer not in Contract case; otherwise rectify. # Flashcards - Field records and site practice

#flashcards/field-records

84 cards generated from the 21 field records and site practice skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Capture borehole location photos with the Solocator compass-GPS overlay" produce?::Each investigation-location photo carries a burnt-in compass ribbon, true bearing, decimal coordinates with stated GPS accuracy, altitude and timestamp, and is renamed to its borehole ID so location and view direction are verifiable later without any external metadata.
Before relying on "Capture borehole location photos with the Solocator compass-GPS overlay" — what do you check?::Overlay shows all five elements: compass ribbon, bearing with (T), lat/long to 6 decimal places, ±accuracy, altitude; plus the timestamp in the corner. • Bearing on the ribbon matches the sketched/planned view direction for that location. • Renamed file IDs match the borehole IDs on the field sheet and site plan for the same day.
"Capture borehole location photos with the Solocator compass-GPS overlay" — state the decision rule about: Use Solocator when the photo must document WHERE a location …::Use Solocator when the photo must document WHERE a location is and WHICH WAY the camera faced (borehole positions, test locations); a time-GPS-only overlay app is sufficient when direction does not ma
"Capture borehole location photos with the Solocator compass-GPS overlay" — state the decision rule about: If GPS accuracy shown in the banner is worse than about ±5-1…::If GPS accuracy shown in the banner is worse than about ±5-10 m, move to open sky or wait before shooting rather than accepting a poor fix.
What does "Compile positioned core photographs into a per-borehole core-photo deliverable" produce?::Raw field snaps of core boxes become a client-ready document with one page per borehole: a perspective-corrected ('positioned') core photo under a standard header giving job, location, survey coordinates, rig, logger and date, issued as Word plus PDF.
Before relying on "Compile positioned core photographs into a per-borehole core-photo deliverable" — what do you check?::Borehole ID in the page title matches the ID readable on the photo board and in-box strip within the image. • In-box depth labels visible in the positioned image are consistent with the stated hole depth and the borehole log. • Easting/northing/RL in each header match the survey schedule for that hole. • Every cored hole in the job appears exactly once; page count equals borehole count.
"Compile positioned core photographs into a per-borehole core-photo deliverable" — state the decision rule about: Keep raw, positioned and compiled versions as three separate…::Keep raw, positioned and compiled versions as three separate layers; never overwrite raw photos with corrected ones.
"Compile positioned core photographs into a per-borehole core-photo deliverable" — state the decision rule about: One borehole per page; where a hole needs several boxes, use…::One borehole per page; where a hole needs several boxes, use additional pages under the same borehole title.
What does "Complete a DCP and Perth penetrometer deep test field sheet (Form S26)" produce?::A completed 'Dynamic Cone & Perth Penetrometer - Deep Test' worksheet recording penetration resistance in blows per 100 mm for up to three test locations, with soil description and refusal coding.
Before relying on "Complete a DCP and Perth penetrometer deep test field sheet (Form S26)" — what do you check?::Test method circled matches the apparatus used • Apparatus function and drop height check circled Y before testing • Blows recorded continuously from start depth with no unexplained gaps • Sheet numbering completed when the job runs to multiple sheets
"Complete a DCP and Perth penetrometer deep test field sheet (Form S26)" — state the decision rule about: NEVER combine DCP and Perth tests on the same work sheet — p…::NEVER combine DCP and Perth tests on the same work sheet — printed as a warning on the form header.
"Complete a DCP and Perth penetrometer deep test field sheet (Form S26)" — state the decision rule about: When testing from the base of a pre-drilled or excavated hol…::When testing from the base of a pre-drilled or excavated hole, record the start depth against the Site No. and use the * code for the pre-drilled interval.
What does "Complete a Report of Pile Hole Inspection form (OP GEO pile hole inspection family)" produce?::A per-pile inspection record proving founding conditions - stratigraphy, socket strength, roughness class and base cleanness - against the design parameters.
Before relying on "Complete a Report of Pile Hole Inspection form (OP GEO pile hole inspection family)" — what do you check?::Depth and RL columns are arithmetically consistent with the ground surface RL. • Every pile has its own numbered form; pile no. matches the piling layout drawing. • Both inspector and reviewer fields completed.
"Complete a Report of Pile Hole Inspection form (OP GEO pile hole inspection family)" — state the decision rule about: Compare actual vs design side by side before the pile is pou…::Compare actual vs design side by side before the pile is poured - any shortfall in socket length, weaker-than-design socket material or undersized hole is raised for engineering direction, not just re
"Complete a Report of Pile Hole Inspection form (OP GEO pile hole inspection family)" — state the decision rule about: Roughness class comes from the printed groove-geometry defin…::Roughness class comes from the printed groove-geometry definitions, not general impressions.
What does "Complete an STS Geotech Drilling Daily Record (drilling/coring time and production log)" produce?::A signed daily record of drilling and coring production for each borehole - set-up, run times, breakdowns and end-of-hole ground summary - that supports invoicing and later log preparation.
Before relying on "Complete an STS Geotech Drilling Daily Record (drilling/coring time and production log)" — what do you check?::Section subtotals (service location, traffic, drilling, coring) should reconcile with the overall start/end times for the day. • Breakdown hours plus productive hours should account for the full shift. • Both field staff and client signatures present before leaving site - the client signature validates chargeable hours.
"Complete an STS Geotech Drilling Daily Record (drilling/coring time and production log)" — state the decision rule about: Every non-productive interval (service location, traffic set…::Every non-productive interval (service location, traffic setup, breakdowns) gets its own timed entry - do not fold standby into drilling hours.
"Complete an STS Geotech Drilling Daily Record (drilling/coring time and production log)" — state the decision rule about: One breakdown row per event, each tied to a BH number, so do…::One breakdown row per event, each tied to a BH number, so downtime can be attributed per hole.
What does "Complete an STS Geotechnical Daily Field Form" produce?::A signed daily record of a field visit — tasks, weather, H&S observations and a narrative of the field work — countersigned by the client representative on the day.
Before relying on "Complete an STS Geotechnical Daily Field Form" — what do you check?::Arrival and departure times filled • Weather block completed • Field staff and client signatures both present • Tasks line matches what the narrative actually reports
"Complete an STS Geotechnical Daily Field Form" — state the decision rule about: The narrative must state the on-site verdict, not just obser…::The narrative must state the on-site verdict, not just observations — the examples end with acceptance ('found suitable') or required action ('additional excavation needed for Class 3 rock for the 1.5
"Complete an STS Geotechnical Daily Field Form" — state the decision rule about: Get the client signature before leaving site — both examples…::Get the client signature before leaving site — both examples are countersigned.
What does "Complete an STS plate load test worksheet (Form S112)" produce?::A completed 'Load Settlement - Time Relationship Worksheet (Plate Load Testing)' recording dial gauge settlements through a load / unload / reload cycle for one test location, ready for office reduction.
Before relying on "Complete an STS plate load test worksheet (Form S112)" — what do you check?::Initial reading row present and flagged in Comments • Every load increment row has all active dial gauges filled • Unload readings recover consistently across gauges (records show recovery on all three gauges) • Header temperatures at start and end both recorded
"Complete an STS plate load test worksheet (Form S112)" — state the decision rule about: One sheet per test location; pages numbered consecutively ac…::One sheet per test location; pages numbered consecutively across the job so PLT1 = page 1, PLT3 = page 3, etc.
"Complete an STS plate load test worksheet (Form S112)" — state the decision rule about: Leave a blank row between the loading, unloading and reloadi…::Leave a blank row between the loading, unloading and reloading stages so the cycle boundaries are unambiguous.
What does "Complete the Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet for AS 3798 Level 1 supervision (Form S69)" produce?::A completed daily site record for Level 1 earthworks supervision — mandatory material-source questions answered, plant and testing logged, and a per-area narrative of placement, compaction, proof rolling and sampling.
Before relying on "Complete the Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet for AS 3798 Level 1 supervision (Form S69)" — what do you check?::All four mandatory questions answered every day • Test number range on the sheet matches the number of density tests actually taken • Every test/sample located on the attached plan • Arrival/departure times filled
"Complete the Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet for AS 3798 Level 1 supervision (Form S69)" — state the decision rule about: If imported fill arrives without a sighted validation certif…::If imported fill arrives without a sighted validation certificate, the form directs: contact the office and arrange the certificate.
"Complete the Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet for AS 3798 Level 1 supervision (Form S69)" — state the decision rule about: If a proof roll finds a soft spot, the record shows the prac…::If a proof roll finds a soft spot, the record shows the practice: define the area, excavate to competent material (record both RLs), backfill with approved material in compacted layers, then density t
What does "Keep and compile a signed STS Site Timesheet (Form A7) for the billing period" produce?::A daily-signed record of site hours (onsite and including travel) per technician and project, compiled into a signed package covering the invoice period.
Before relying on "Keep and compile a signed STS Site Timesheet (Form A7) for the billing period" — what do you check?::Every row signed; an unsigned day is a dispute risk at invoicing. • Total hours minus hours onsite equals a plausible travel allowance for the site. • Compiled package covers the full period with no missing dates that were actually worked.
"Keep and compile a signed STS Site Timesheet (Form A7) for the billing period" — state the decision rule about: Hours onsite and total hours are separate columns - travel i…::Hours onsite and total hours are separate columns - travel is only ever added to the total column.
"Keep and compile a signed STS Site Timesheet (Form A7) for the billing period" — state the decision rule about: A cancelled or rained-off day still gets a row with the hour…::A cancelled or rained-off day still gets a row with the hours actually incurred and a reason note.
What does "Label core boxes using the STS printed photo-board template" produce?::Every core box is photographed behind a standard printed STS board identifying project, client, address, date, borehole and depth, with a 1 m graduated scale bar and colour reference, and with depth progress marked inside the box, so any core photo is self-identifying and dimensionally interpretable.
Before relying on "Label core boxes using the STS printed photo-board template" — what do you check?::All six board fields are legible in the final photo and agree with the borehole log for the same hole and date. • Scale bar and colour chart are unobstructed so measurements and colour can be corrected from the image. • In-box depth marks run consecutively with no missing metres, and the end-of-coring depth matches the logged termination depth.
"Label core boxes using the STS printed photo-board template" — state the decision rule about: Choose the template slide variant that matches the box forma…::Choose the template slide variant that matches the box format being photographed; all variants keep the same six identification fields and 1 m scale bar.
"Label core boxes using the STS printed photo-board template" — state the decision rule about: If a printed board is not available on site, fall back to th…::If a printed board is not available on site, fall back to the legacy manual method: handwritten strip along the box edge (job no, site, BH, date, initials, START depth), white spacer blocks at each me
What does "Log a borehole soil profile by hand on the OP GEO 007a/007b BH soil field log sheets" produce?::A handwritten field borehole soil log with depth-referenced descriptions in the standard order, ready for checking and transcription into the final log.
Before relying on "Log a borehole soil profile by hand on the OP GEO 007a/007b BH soil field log sheets" — what do you check?::Every stratum has all description elements (name, grain size/plasticity, colour, constituents, strength/density, moisture) - a missing element is a gap, not a d • Sample depths on the log agree with sample labels and the daily record. • Logged and Checked signatures with dates are both present before the sheet is filed.
"Log a borehole soil profile by hand on the OP GEO 007a/007b BH soil field log sheets" — state the decision rule about: Primary soil name in capitals with secondary constituents ar…::Primary soil name in capitals with secondary constituents around it, exactly in the printed description order - do not free-form the description.
"Log a borehole soil profile by hand on the OP GEO 007a/007b BH soil field log sheets" — state the decision rule about: Use the 5 m gridline sheet when strata changes or test inter…::Use the 5 m gridline sheet when strata changes or test intervals need better than 0.5 m resolution; switch to continuation sheets rather than crowding one sheet.
What does "Log rock core by hand on the OP GEO 008a/008b BH rock log sheets" produce?::A handwritten cored-borehole field log capturing core recovery, rock description, weathering, inferred strength and defect data against depth.
Before relying on "Log rock core by hand on the OP GEO 008a/008b BH rock log sheets" — what do you check?::TCR/RQD percentages consistent with what is actually in the core box (cross-check against core box photos). • Every defect entry has depth, type and orientation at minimum. • Weathering and strength ticks exist for the full cored depth with no unexplained gaps.
"Log rock core by hand on the OP GEO 008a/008b BH rock log sheets" — state the decision rule about: TCR and RQD are recorded per run, not per lithology - keep r…::TCR and RQD are recorded per run, not per lithology - keep run boundaries visible on the log.
"Log rock core by hand on the OP GEO 008a/008b BH rock log sheets" — state the decision rule about: Strength is inferred in the field from pick/knife/hand behav…::Strength is inferred in the field from pick/knife/hand behaviour and confirmed by Is(50) testing; tick the band, do not write a bare number without basis.
What does "Mark up field density test locations on the project drawing set" produce?::A scanned, annotated project drawing showing every nuclear-gauge density test number at its true location, linking test reports to the works area.
Before relying on "Mark up field density test locations on the project drawing set" — what do you check?::Count of circled/listed numbers equals count of tests reported for the day/area. • Sticky-note groups state which element they cover, not just numbers. • Scan legibility check - circled numbers over dense linework are the first thing lost in a poor scan.
"Mark up field density test locations on the project drawing set" — state the decision rule about: Every test number on the day's gauge record must appear exac…::Every test number on the day's gauge record must appear exactly once on the drawing - the drawing is the location index for the test reports.
"Mark up field density test locations on the project drawing set" — state the decision rule about: Use number ranges on notes only for genuinely contiguous seq…::Use number ranges on notes only for genuinely contiguous sequences; isolated tests get individually placed circles.
What does "Photograph a shrink-swell sample with depth labelling" produce?::A photographic record tying an undisturbed sample to its job number, borehole, depth interval and the laboratory test it is allocated to, before it leaves the field/sample store.
Before relying on "Photograph a shrink-swell sample with depth labelling" — what do you check?::Card text legible in the photo: job/STS number, sample ID, BH, depth interval, test allocation. • Depth interval on card, filename and the borehole log all agree.
"Photograph a shrink-swell sample with depth labelling" — state the decision rule about: The filename must repeat the label (BH + depth interval) so …::The filename must repeat the label (BH + depth interval) so the photo can be found without opening it.
"Photograph a shrink-swell sample with depth labelling" — state the decision rule about: Photograph before any trimming/testing so the as-received co…::Photograph before any trimming/testing so the as-received condition (roots, moisture, layering visible in the record) is documented.
What does "Photograph a site or test location with a time-GPS overlay" produce?::A dated, geolocated, orientation-stamped site photograph that can stand as evidence of site conditions at a specific moment (e.g. bulk excavation level, pier cage delivery, piling rig on site).
Before relying on "Photograph a site or test location with a time-GPS overlay" — what do you check?::Overlay shows the correct site address and a plausible altitude before leaving the vantage point. • Timestamp matches the works being recorded (the stamp is burned into the pixels and cannot be corrected later). • Whole area of interest is inside the frame — excavation face, plant, and fencing visible in the examples.
"Photograph a site or test location with a time-GPS overlay" — state the decision rule about: If the shot is evidentiary (levels, founding conditions, pla…::If the shot is evidentiary (levels, founding conditions, plant on site, progress claims), use the overlay app rather than the plain phone camera — plain PXL_ camera shots also exist in the same folder
"Photograph a site or test location with a time-GPS overlay" — state the decision rule about: Change bearing, not standpoint, between consecutive shots so…::Change bearing, not standpoint, between consecutive shots so the compass stamp documents what direction each frame faces.
What does "Photograph and label a core box" produce?::A single composite photograph per core box that identifies the project, borehole and depth range, gives a true metric scale and colour reference, and lets every core run be located by depth.
Before relying on "Photograph and label a core box" — what do you check?::Board fields legible in the photo and consistent with the drill log (project no., BH no., date, depth range). • Colour chart and greyscale visible for later colour correction. • End-of-core depth written in the box matches the driller's final depth. • Every metre tag readable — the OCR of one record recovered all tags 0.0m-1.0m and 5-20 plus 'END OF CORE- 20.44m', which is the standard to aim for.
"Photograph and label a core box" — state the decision rule about: One composite photo covers a whole box; deeper holes need on…::One composite photo covers a whole box; deeper holes need one photo per box with the board DEPTH field updated to that box's range.
"Photograph and label a core box" — state the decision rule about: Depth tags are written on the tray divider at the start of e…::Depth tags are written on the tray divider at the start of each 1 m run, so any stone in the photo can be depth-located against the board's scale bar.
What does "Record Wenner resistivity readings from the AEMC tester onto the stored-measurements datasheet" produce?::A paper backup of every stored soil-resistivity measurement, tied to test number, operator and site, matching the tester's internal memory.
Before relying on "Record Wenner resistivity readings from the AEMC tester onto the stored-measurements datasheet" — what do you check?::Row count equals stored-measurement count on the tester. • Units stated in the Results column (ohm or ohm-m) - a bare number is ambiguous between resistance and computed resistivity. • Operator and date filled on every page, since pages can separate.
"Record Wenner resistivity readings from the AEMC tester onto the stored-measurements datasheet" — state the decision rule about: The instrument memory is not the record - the datasheet is t…::The instrument memory is not the record - the datasheet is the auditable record; transcribe on site, not back at the office.
"Record Wenner resistivity readings from the AEMC tester onto the stored-measurements datasheet" — state the decision rule about: One row per stored measurement, including repeats - do not o…::One row per stored measurement, including repeats - do not overwrite a bad reading, add the retest as a new row with a comment.
What does "Record nuclear gauge daily standard counts (Form K38)" produce?::A daily standard count check for a nuclear density gauge, verifying density and moisture counts fall within control limits before field density testing, combined with the gauge's remote storage record.
Before relying on "Record nuclear gauge daily standard counts (Form K38)" — what do you check?::Today's density and moisture counts each marked within limits • Mean-of-last-4 recalculated, not copied • Checked By initials present on every row • Storage location, vehicle rego and alarm fields completed for source security
"Record nuclear gauge daily standard counts (Form K38)" — state the decision rule about: Limits are derived from the mean of the last four readings, …::Limits are derived from the mean of the last four readings, so the running mean must be carried forward every day.
"Record nuclear gauge daily standard counts (Form K38)" — state the decision rule about: A count outside its limits fails the daily check — the Y/N c…::A count outside its limits fails the daily check — the Y/N column exists to force that comparison before the gauge is used for field density testing.
What does "Reduce a plate load test in the STS PLATE LOAD TEST workbook and issue the report sheet" produce?::A checked pressure-settlement curve with computed EV1 loading modulus and Ks(PLATE) subgrade reaction, issued as a one-page STS report per test location.
Before relying on "Reduce a plate load test in the STS PLATE LOAD TEST workbook and issue the report sheet" — what do you check?::Average settlement column reproduces the field sheet averages (transcription check per step). • Plate area equals pi/4 x diameter squared for the entered plate. • Curve shape sensible: monotonic settlement on loading, partial recovery on unloading; investigate reversals before issuing. • Report no., project no. and test date match the field worksheet and job records.
"Reduce a plate load test in the STS PLATE LOAD TEST workbook and issue the report sheet" — state the decision rule about: Stage structure in the workbook must mirror the field sheet …::Stage structure in the workbook must mirror the field sheet exactly (preload, loading, unloading, reload) - do not merge stages to smooth the curve.
"Reduce a plate load test in the STS PLATE LOAD TEST workbook and issue the report sheet" — state the decision rule about: If a dial gauge is unused, leave its column empty rather tha…::If a dial gauge is unused, leave its column empty rather than entering zeros, so the average uses only real gauges.
What does "Run the AEMC soil resistivity test (Wenner method) to the STS SOP" produce?::A set of stored apparent soil resistivity measurements at multiple electrode spacings using the AEMC Model 6471, per the STS standard operating procedure.
Before relying on "Run the AEMC soil resistivity test (Wenner method) to the STS SOP" — what do you check?::Battery condition verified before starting • All four leads connected and recognised by the instrument • Reading stable before saving • Electrode status display checked for poor contacts
"Run the AEMC soil resistivity test (Wenner method) to the STS SOP" — state the decision rule about: 'W' on the display is the gate to proceed — never record wit…::'W' on the display is the gate to proceed — never record with 'S' (Schlumberger) selected.
"Run the AEMC soil resistivity test (Wenner method) to the STS SOP" — state the decision rule about: Keep all four electrodes equally spaced at every spacing ste…::Keep all four electrodes equally spaced at every spacing step; the programmed distance must match the actual layout or the auto-calculated resistivity is wrong.
What does "Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in-field reference aids" produce?::Faster, standard-compliant field logging and on-the-spot sanity checks by reaching for the right printed aid instead of memory.
Before relying on "Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in-field reference aids" — what do you check?::Descriptions on completed logs follow the cheat-sheet order and vocabulary. • Any correlated parameter in notes or reports is traceable to the specific chart used.
"Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in-field reference aids" — state the decision rule about: The cheat sheet governs wording on the log; if memory and th…::The cheat sheet governs wording on the log; if memory and the sheet disagree, the sheet wins.
"Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in-field reference aids" — state the decision rule about: Correlations are depth- and moisture-dependent guides (state…::Correlations are depth- and moisture-dependent guides (stated on the aids) - never present a correlated value as a measured one.
