Before relying on "Complete an STS Geotechnical Daily Field Form" — what do you check?::Arrival and departure times filled • Weather block completed • Field staff and client signatures both present • Tasks line matches what the narrative actually reports "Complete an STS Geotechnical Daily Field Form" — state the decision rule about: The narrative must state the on site verdict, not just obser…::The narrative must state the on site verdict, not just observations — the examples end with acceptance ('found suitable') or required action ('additional excavation needed for Class 3 rock for the 1.5 "Complete an STS Geotechnical Daily Field Form" — state the decision rule about: Get the client signature before leaving site — both examples…::Get the client signature before leaving site — both examples are countersigned. What does "Complete an STS plate load test worksheet (Form S112)" produce?::A completed 'Load Settlement Time Relationship Worksheet (Plate Load Testing)' recording dial gauge settlements through a load / unload / reload cycle for one test location, ready for office reduction. Before relying on "Complete an STS plate load test worksheet (Form S112)" — what do you check?::Initial reading row present and flagged in Comments • Every load increment row has all active dial gauges filled • Unload readings recover consistently across gauges (records show recovery on all three gauges) • Header temperatures at start and end both recorded "Complete an STS plate load test worksheet (Form S112)" — state the decision rule about: One sheet per test location; pages numbered consecutively ac…::One sheet per test location; pages numbered consecutively across the job so PLT1 = page 1, PLT3 = page 3, etc. "Complete an STS plate load test worksheet (Form S112)" — state the decision rule about: Leave a blank row between the loading, unloading and reloadi…::Leave a blank row between the loading, unloading and reloading stages so the cycle boundaries are unambiguous. What does "Complete the Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet for AS 3798 Level 1 supervision (Form S69)" produce?::A completed daily site record for Level 1 earthworks supervision — mandatory material source questions answered, plant and testing logged, and a per area narrative of placement, compaction, proof rolling and sampling. Before relying on "Complete the Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet for AS 3798 Level 1 supervision (Form S69)" — what do you check?::All four mandatory questions answered every day • Test number range on the sheet matches the number of density tests actually taken • Every test/sample located on the attached plan • Arrival/departure times filled "Complete the Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet for AS 3798 Level 1 supervision (Form S69)" — state the decision rule about: If imported fill arrives without a sighted validation certif…::If imported fill arrives without a sighted validation certificate, the form directs: contact the office and arrange the certificate. "Complete the Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet for AS 3798 Level 1 supervision (Form S69)" — state the decision rule about: If a proof roll finds a soft spot, the record shows the prac…::If a proof roll finds a soft spot, the record shows the practice: define the area, excavate to competent material (record both RLs), backfill with approved material in compacted layers, then density t What does "Keep and compile a signed STS Site Timesheet (Form A7) for the billing period" produce?::A daily signed record of site hours (onsite and including travel) per technician and project, compiled into a signed package covering the invoice period. Before relying on "Keep and compile a signed STS Site Timesheet (Form A7) for the billing period" — what do you check?::Every row signed; an unsigned day is a dispute risk at invoicing. • Total hours minus hours onsite equals a plausible travel allowance for the site. • Compiled package covers the full period with no missing dates that were actually worked. "Keep and compile a signed STS Site Timesheet (Form A7) for the billing period" — state the decision rule about: Hours onsite and total hours are separate columns travel i…::Hours onsite and total hours are separate columns travel is only ever added to the total column. "Keep and compile a signed STS Site Timesheet (Form A7) for the billing period" — state the decision rule about: A cancelled or rained off day still gets a row with the hour…::A cancelled or rained off day still gets a row with the hours actually incurred and a reason note. What does "Label core boxes using the STS printed photo board template" produce?::Every core box is photographed behind a standard printed STS board identifying project, client, address, date, borehole and depth, with a 1 m graduated scale bar and colour reference, and with depth progress marked inside the box, so any core photo is self identifying and dimensionally interpretable. Before relying on "Label core boxes using the STS printed photo board template" — what do you check?::All six board fields are legible in the final photo and agree with the borehole log for the same hole and date. • Scale bar and colour chart are unobstructed so measurements and colour can be corrected from the image. • In box depth marks run consecutively with no missing metres, and the end of coring depth matches the logged termination depth. "Label core boxes using the STS printed photo board template" — state the decision rule about: Choose the template slide variant that matches the box forma…::Choose the template slide variant that matches the box format being photographed; all variants keep the same six identification fields and 1 m scale bar. "Label core boxes using the STS printed photo board template" — state the decision rule about: If a printed board is not available on site, fall back to th…::If a printed board is not available on site, fall back to the legacy manual method: handwritten strip along the box edge (job no, site, BH, date, initials, START depth), white spacer blocks at each me What does "Log a borehole soil profile by hand on the OP GEO 007a/007b BH soil field log sheets" produce?::A handwritten field borehole soil log with depth referenced descriptions in the standard order, ready for checking and transcription into the final log. Before relying on "Log a borehole soil profile by hand on the OP GEO 007a/007b BH soil field log sheets" — what do you check?::Every stratum has all description elements (name, grain size/plasticity, colour, constituents, strength/density, moisture) a missing element is a gap, not a d • Sample depths on the log agree with sample labels and the daily record. • Logged and Checked signatures with dates are both present before the sheet is filed. "Log a borehole soil profile by hand on the OP GEO 007a/007b BH soil field log sheets" — state the decision rule about: Primary soil name in capitals with secondary constituents ar…::Primary soil name in capitals with secondary constituents around it, exactly in the printed description order do not free form the description. "Log a borehole soil profile by hand on the OP GEO 007a/007b BH soil field log sheets" — state the decision rule about: Use the 5 m gridline sheet when strata changes or test inter…::Use the 5 m gridline sheet when strata changes or test intervals need better than 0.5 m resolution; switch to continuation sheets rather than crowding one sheet. What does "Log rock core by hand on the OP GEO 008a/008b BH rock log sheets" produce?::A handwritten cored borehole field log capturing core recovery, rock description, weathering, inferred strength and defect data against depth. Before relying on "Log rock core by hand on the OP GEO 008a/008b BH rock log sheets" — what do you check?::TCR/RQD percentages consistent with what is actually in the core box (cross check against core box photos). • Every defect entry has depth, type and orientation at minimum. • Weathering and strength ticks exist for the full cored depth with no unexplained gaps. "Log rock core by hand on the OP GEO 008a/008b BH rock log sheets" — state the decision rule about: TCR and RQD are recorded per run, not per lithology keep r…::TCR and RQD are recorded per run, not per lithology keep run boundaries visible on the log. "Log rock core by hand on the OP GEO 008a/008b BH rock log sheets" — state the decision rule about: Strength is inferred in the field from pick/knife/hand behav…::Strength is inferred in the field from pick/knife/hand behaviour and confirmed by Is(50) testing; tick the band, do not write a bare number without basis. What does "Mark up field density test locations on the project drawing set" produce?::A scanned, annotated project drawing showing every nuclear gauge density test number at its true location, linking test reports to the works area. Before relying on "Mark up field density test locations on the project drawing set" — what do you check?::Count of circled/listed numbers equals count of tests reported for the day/area. • Sticky note groups state which element they cover, not just numbers. • Scan legibility check circled numbers over dense linework are the first thing lost in a poor scan. "Mark up field density test locations on the project drawing set" — state the decision rule about: Every test number on the day's gauge record must appear exac…::Every test number on the day's gauge record must appear exactly once on the drawing the drawing is the location index for the test reports. "Mark up field density test locations on the project drawing set" — state the decision rule about: Use number ranges on notes only for genuinely contiguous seq…::Use number ranges on notes only for genuinely contiguous sequences; isolated tests get individually placed circles. What does "Photograph a shrink swell sample with depth labelling" produce?::A photographic record tying an undisturbed sample to its job number, borehole, depth interval and the laboratory test it is allocated to, before it leaves the field/sample store. Before relying on "Photograph a shrink swell sample with depth labelling" — what do you check?::Card text legible in the photo: job/STS number, sample ID, BH, depth interval, test allocation. • Depth interval on card, filename and the borehole log all agree. "Photograph a shrink swell sample with depth labelling" — state the decision rule about: The filename must repeat the label (BH + depth interval) so …::The filename must repeat the label (BH + depth interval) so the photo can be found without opening it. "Photograph a shrink swell sample with depth labelling" — state the decision rule about: Photograph before any trimming/testing so the as received co…::Photograph before any trimming/testing so the as received condition (roots, moisture, layering visible in the record) is documented. What does "Photograph a site or test location with a time GPS overlay" produce?::A dated, geolocated, orientation stamped site photograph that can stand as evidence of site conditions at a specific moment (e.g. bulk excavation level, pier cage delivery, piling rig on site). Before relying on "Photograph a site or test location with a time GPS overlay" — what do you check?::Overlay shows the correct site address and a plausible altitude before leaving the vantage point. • Timestamp matches the works being recorded (the stamp is burned into the pixels and cannot be corrected later). • Whole area of interest is inside the frame — excavation face, plant, and fencing visible in the examples. "Photograph a site or test location with a time GPS overlay" — state the decision rule about: If the shot is evidentiary (levels, founding conditions, pla…::If the shot is evidentiary (levels, founding conditions, plant on site, progress claims), use the overlay app rather than the plain phone camera — plain PXL camera shots also exist in the same folder "Photograph a site or test location with a time GPS overlay" — state the decision rule about: Change bearing, not standpoint, between consecutive shots so…::Change bearing, not standpoint, between consecutive shots so the compass stamp documents what direction each frame faces. What does "Photograph and label a core box" produce?::A single composite photograph per core box that identifies the project, borehole and depth range, gives a true metric scale and colour reference, and lets every core run be located by depth. Before relying on "Photograph and label a core box" — what do you check?::Board fields legible in the photo and consistent with the drill log (project no., BH no., date, depth range). • Colour chart and greyscale visible for later colour correction. • End of core depth written in the box matches the driller's final depth. • Every metre tag readable — the OCR of one record recovered all tags 0.0m 1.0m and 5 20 plus 'END OF CORE 20.44m', which is the standard to aim for. "Photograph and label a core box" — state the decision rule about: One composite photo covers a whole box; deeper holes need on…::One composite photo covers a whole box; deeper holes need one photo per box with the board DEPTH field updated to that box's range. "Photograph and label a core box" — state the decision rule about: Depth tags are written on the tray divider at the start of e…::Depth tags are written on the tray divider at the start of each 1 m run, so any stone in the photo can be depth located against the board's scale bar. What does "Record Wenner resistivity readings from the AEMC tester onto the stored measurements datasheet" produce?::A paper backup of every stored soil resistivity measurement, tied to test number, operator and site, matching the tester's internal memory. Before relying on "Record Wenner resistivity readings from the AEMC tester onto the stored measurements datasheet" — what do you check?::Row count equals stored measurement count on the tester. • Units stated in the Results column (ohm or ohm m) a bare number is ambiguous between resistance and computed resistivity. • Operator and date filled on every page, since pages can separate. "Record Wenner resistivity readings from the AEMC tester onto the stored measurements datasheet" — state the decision rule about: The instrument memory is not the record the datasheet is t…::The instrument memory is not the record the datasheet is the auditable record; transcribe on site, not back at the office. "Record Wenner resistivity readings from the AEMC tester onto the stored measurements datasheet" — state the decision rule about: One row per stored measurement, including repeats do not o…::One row per stored measurement, including repeats do not overwrite a bad reading, add the retest as a new row with a comment. What does "Record nuclear gauge daily standard counts (Form K38)" produce?::A daily standard count check for a nuclear density gauge, verifying density and moisture counts fall within control limits before field density testing, combined with the gauge's remote storage record. Before relying on "Record nuclear gauge daily standard counts (Form K38)" — what do you check?::Today's density and moisture counts each marked within limits • Mean of last 4 recalculated, not copied • Checked By initials present on every row • Storage location, vehicle rego and alarm fields completed for source security "Record nuclear gauge daily standard counts (Form K38)" — state the decision rule about: Limits are derived from the mean of the last four readings, …::Limits are derived from the mean of the last four readings, so the running mean must be carried forward every day. "Record nuclear gauge daily standard counts (Form K38)" — state the decision rule about: A count outside its limits fails the daily check — the Y/N c…::A count outside its limits fails the daily check — the Y/N column exists to force that comparison before the gauge is used for field density testing. What does "Reduce a plate load test in the STS PLATE LOAD TEST workbook and issue the report sheet" produce?::A checked pressure settlement curve with computed EV1 loading modulus and Ks(PLATE) subgrade reaction, issued as a one page STS report per test location. Before relying on "Reduce a plate load test in the STS PLATE LOAD TEST workbook and issue the report sheet" — what do you check?::Average settlement column reproduces the field sheet averages (transcription check per step). • Plate area equals pi/4 x diameter squared for the entered plate. • Curve shape sensible: monotonic settlement on loading, partial recovery on unloading; investigate reversals before issuing. • Report no., project no. and test date match the field worksheet and job records. "Reduce a plate load test in the STS PLATE LOAD TEST workbook and issue the report sheet" — state the decision rule about: Stage structure in the workbook must mirror the field sheet …::Stage structure in the workbook must mirror the field sheet exactly (preload, loading, unloading, reload) do not merge stages to smooth the curve. "Reduce a plate load test in the STS PLATE LOAD TEST workbook and issue the report sheet" — state the decision rule about: If a dial gauge is unused, leave its column empty rather tha…::If a dial gauge is unused, leave its column empty rather than entering zeros, so the average uses only real gauges. What does "Run the AEMC soil resistivity test (Wenner method) to the STS SOP" produce?::A set of stored apparent soil resistivity measurements at multiple electrode spacings using the AEMC Model 6471, per the STS standard operating procedure. Before relying on "Run the AEMC soil resistivity test (Wenner method) to the STS SOP" — what do you check?::Battery condition verified before starting • All four leads connected and recognised by the instrument • Reading stable before saving • Electrode status display checked for poor contacts "Run the AEMC soil resistivity test (Wenner method) to the STS SOP" — state the decision rule about: 'W' on the display is the gate to proceed — never record wit…::'W' on the display is the gate to proceed — never record with 'S' (Schlumberger) selected. "Run the AEMC soil resistivity test (Wenner method) to the STS SOP" — state the decision rule about: Keep all four electrodes equally spaced at every spacing ste…::Keep all four electrodes equally spaced at every spacing step; the programmed distance must match the actual layout or the auto calculated resistivity is wrong. What does "Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in field reference aids" produce?::Faster, standard compliant field logging and on the spot sanity checks by reaching for the right printed aid instead of memory. Before relying on "Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in field reference aids" — what do you check?::Descriptions on completed logs follow the cheat sheet order and vocabulary. • Any correlated parameter in notes or reports is traceable to the specific chart used. "Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in field reference aids" — state the decision rule about: The cheat sheet governs wording on the log; if memory and th…::The cheat sheet governs wording on the log; if memory and the sheet disagree, the sheet wins. "Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in field reference aids" — state the decision rule about: Correlations are depth and moisture dependent guides (state…::Correlations are depth and moisture dependent guides (stated on the aids) never present a correlated value as a measured one. Related Learning path Field records and site practice Learning loop

notes.body:
# Flashcards - General practice

#flashcards/general

32 cards generated from the 8 general practice skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Compile excavation submission package for road authority" produce?::A complete concurrence submission (dilapidation survey, design documentation, drawings, specifications, monitoring plan) lodged with the road authority ahead of construction.
Before relying on "Compile excavation submission package for road authority" — what do you check?::Design report addresses ruptured-utility or underpinning scenarios where utility-owner requirements are not established. • Damming effects on groundwater considered in design levels. • Authority site access for compliance review is provided for.
"Compile excavation submission package for road authority" — state the decision rule about: Submission is required at least six weeks before constructio…::Submission is required at least six weeks before construction commencement (RMS_ Attachment A_ GTD 2012-01.pdf submission section).
"Compile excavation submission package for road authority" — state the decision rule about: In the 2012 direction, no part of a ground anchor may be sha…::In the 2012 direction, no part of a ground anchor may be shallower than 2 m below surface within the road reserve (later superseded by a different depth in GTD 2020/001) - always apply the current dir
What does "Finalise logs and manage sample custody" produce?::Reviewed, finalised borehole logs and a defensible sample retention/chain-of-custody position through construction claims windows.
Before relying on "Finalise logs and manage sample custody" — what do you check?::No FINAL log issued with outstanding laboratory results. • Sample ownership/custody understood (samples become the department's property until disposal or repossession).
"Finalise logs and manage sample custody" — state the decision rule about: Untested soil samples retained at least 90 days after the ge…::Untested soil samples retained at least 90 days after the geotechnical report (guideline section 6.1).
"Finalise logs and manage sample custody" — state the decision rule about: Undisturbed tube samples degrade and are generally not usefu…::Undisturbed tube samples degrade and are generally not useful for testing after about 3-6 months - schedule testing accordingly (guideline section 6.1).
What does "Investigate ground for excavation adjacent to road" produce?::A geotechnical investigation scoped to the authority's minimums for retaining-wall design beside transport infrastructure.
Before relying on "Investigate ground for excavation adjacent to road" — what do you check?::Groundwater conditions established, including accidental cases (e.g. main breaks, damming). • Investigation depth measured below final excavation level, not existing surface.
"Investigate ground for excavation adjacent to road" — state the decision rule about: At least one borehole per 30 m of wall length, taken at leas…::At least one borehole per 30 m of wall length, taken at least 3 m into competent material below final excavation level (gtd-2020-001 geotechnical investigations section).
"Investigate ground for excavation adjacent to road" — state the decision rule about: Test-pit-only investigations are generally not acceptable (g…::Test-pit-only investigations are generally not acceptable (gtd-2020-001 geotechnical investigations section).
What does "Log rock core with defect groups" produce?::Rock core logs capturing weathering, strength, RQD per rock-mass unit and grouped defect descriptions suitable for design and kinematic assessment.
Before relying on "Log rock core with defect groups" — what do you check?::Defect spacing histogram reconciles with RQD and the listed defect sets. • Drilling-induced breaks excluded from defect statistics. • 'Massive' only used where observed at greater than 1 m scale.
"Log rock core with defect groups" — state the decision rule about: Overlapping weathering terms (e.g. HW/MW) are not permitted …::Overlapping weathering terms (e.g. HW/MW) are not permitted for a unit; minor zones 0.1-1.0 m are detailed in the weathering column, and intervals under 100 mm go to the additional-data column (guidel
"Log rock core with defect groups" — state the decision rule about: Aperture measured in mm; infill thicker than 1 mm described …::Aperture measured in mm; infill thicker than 1 mm described as a seam or vein with composition and thickness (guideline defect notes).
What does "Log soil strata to TMR convention" produce?::Borehole/test-pit soil descriptions in the standard row order and naming convention, ready for review and model building.
Before relying on "Log soil strata to TMR convention" — what do you check?::Groundwater strike depth and time recorded; piezometer readings dated on final logs. • Geologist present in the field for all investigation stages. • Component percentages sum sensibly and match the assigned name hierarchy.
"Log soil strata to TMR convention" — state the decision rule about: All descriptions must follow AS 1726:2017 and the authority'…::All descriptions must follow AS 1726:2017 and the authority's terms-and-symbols form; field logging is completed in the field wherever physically possible (guideline sections 1.1, 2.2.2).
"Log soil strata to TMR convention" — state the decision rule about: Final soil names/classifications are set by laboratory resul…::Final soil names/classifications are set by laboratory results, not field impressions (guideline section 3.1).
What does "Look up standard geotechnical logging terms, symbols and classification tables (TMR GEOT 017/10)" produce?::Fast, consistent AS 1726:2017-aligned terminology for logging soil and rock — particle size fractions, accessory-component wording, plasticity, consistency/density, moisture, rock strength/weathering, defect descriptions, and standard symbols/abbreviations.
Before relying on "Look up standard geotechnical logging terms, symbols and classification tables (TMR GEOT 017/10)" — what do you check?::Table numbers cross-checked against AS 1726:2017 before quoting thresholds in deliverables.
"Look up standard geotechnical logging terms, symbols and classification tables (TMR GEOT 017/10)" — state the decision rule about: Use this form together with the TMR Guideline for Geotechnic…::Use this form together with the TMR Guideline for Geotechnical Logging; AS 1726:2017 is the governing reference where a conflict appears.
"Look up standard geotechnical logging terms, symbols and classification tables (TMR GEOT 017/10)" — state the decision rule about: For non-TMR projects, confirm the client's preferred logging…::For non-TMR projects, confirm the client's preferred logging standard — thresholds differ between AS 1726:2017 and older 1993-era logs.
What does "Plan excavation support next to transport infrastructure" produce?::A retaining-structure design basis for a development excavation adjacent to state roads that will obtain TfNSW concurrence.
Before relying on "Plan excavation support next to transport infrastructure" — what do you check?::Unplanned excavation case (AS 5100.3 Section 13.3.1) explicitly included in stability design. • Utilities in the influence zone identified and their owners' movement tolerances addressed. • Both temporary and permanent structures covered in the design report.
"Plan excavation support next to transport infrastructure" — state the decision rule about: Not acceptable as permanent retention: steel sheet piles bel…::Not acceptable as permanent retention: steel sheet piles below the water table, and wall toes founded on unsupported rock ledges of quality inferior to medium-strength rock (Class III in the Sydney sa
"Plan excavation support next to transport infrastructure" — state the decision rule about: Minimum serviceability UDLs: 20 kPa traffic plus 10 kPa othe…::Minimum serviceability UDLs: 20 kPa traffic plus 10 kPa other surcharge (gtd-2020-001 design loads section).
What does "Screen trenchless crossing for authority review" produce?::A quick, defensible decision on whether a proposed trenchless under-road crossing needs formal roads-authority review.
Before relying on "Screen trenchless crossing for authority review" — what do you check?::Ground quality claim is backed by boreholes/test pits at entry, exit and at most 30 m spacing. • Cover measured to the excavation obvert, not the pipe crown after lining.
"Screen trenchless crossing for authority review" — state the decision rule about: Effective ground cover below 1.5 m is not acceptable at all …::Effective ground cover below 1.5 m is not acceptable at all (TS 02088 Figure 1).
"Screen trenchless crossing for authority review" — state the decision rule about: In stiff/medium-dense-or-better ground: diameter up to 250 m…::In stiff/medium-dense-or-better ground: diameter up to 250 mm passes without review; larger diameters pass if cover is at least 7 diameters including at least 2 diameters of bedrock, or at least 10 di

"Look up standard geotechnical logging terms, symbols and classification tables (TMR GEOT 017/10)" — state the decision rule about: For non TMR projects, confirm the client's preferred logging…::For non TMR projects, confirm the client's preferred logging standard — thresholds differ between AS 1726:2017 and older 1993 era logs. What does "Plan excavation support next to transport infrastructure" produce?::A retaining structure design basis for a development excavation adjacent to state roads that will obtain TfNSW concurrence. Before relying on "Plan excavation support next to transport infrastructure" — what do you check?::Unplanned excavation case (AS 5100.3 Section 13.3.1) explicitly included in stability design. • Utilities in the influence zone identified and their owners' movement tolerances addressed. • Both temporary and permanent structures covered in the design report. "Plan excavation support next to transport infrastructure" — state the decision rule about: Not acceptable as permanent retention: steel sheet piles bel…::Not acceptable as permanent retention: steel sheet piles below the water table, and wall toes founded on unsupported rock ledges of quality inferior to medium strength rock (Class III in the Sydney sa "Plan excavation support next to transport infrastructure" — state the decision rule about: Minimum serviceability UDLs: 20 kPa traffic plus 10 kPa othe…::Minimum serviceability UDLs: 20 kPa traffic plus 10 kPa other surcharge (gtd 2020 001 design loads section). What does "Screen trenchless crossing for authority review" produce?::A quick, defensible decision on whether a proposed trenchless under road crossing needs formal roads authority review. Before relying on "Screen trenchless crossing for authority review" — what do you check?::Ground quality claim is backed by boreholes/test pits at entry, exit and at most 30 m spacing. • Cover measured to the excavation obvert, not the pipe crown after lining. "Screen trenchless crossing for authority review" — state the decision rule about: Effective ground cover below 1.5 m is not acceptable at all …::Effective ground cover below 1.5 m is not acceptable at all (TS 02088 Figure 1). "Screen trenchless crossing for authority review" — state the decision rule about: In stiff/medium dense or better ground: diameter up to 250 m…::In stiff/medium dense or better ground: diameter up to 250 mm passes without review; larger diameters pass if cover is at least 7 diameters including at least 2 diameters of bedrock, or at least 10 di Related Learning path General practice Learning loop

notes.body:
# Flashcards - Monitoring and vibration

#flashcards/monitoring

24 cards generated from the 6 monitoring and vibration skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Assess human exposure against vibration values" produce?::A pass/exceedance assessment of measured or predicted building vibration against preferred and maximum human-comfort values, including dose calculation for intermittent sources.
Before relying on "Assess human exposure against vibration values" — what do you check?::Crest factor limits observed when using rms-based estimation for varying signals. • Assessment report includes instrumentation, methodology, site map, criteria, predictions vs criteria, mitigation discussion and compliance method (Section 4.7). • Prediction methods validated and stated with assumptions and expected accuracy; scenarios at start and 10 years.
"Assess human exposure against vibration values" — state the decision rule about: Continuous-vibration preferred values for residences: z-axis…::Continuous-vibration preferred values for residences: z-axis 0.010 m/s2 daytime and 0.007 m/s2 night-time (maxima double), with lower values for critical areas and higher for offices/workshops (vibrat
"Assess human exposure against vibration values" — state the decision rule about: Impulsive-vibration preferred values are substantially highe…::Impulsive-vibration preferred values are substantially higher for residences (e.g. z-axis 0.30 daytime / 0.10 night-time m/s2) except in critical areas where continuous values persist (vibrationguide0
What does "Classify vibration and select assessment criteria" produce?::The correct human-comfort vibration criterion (continuous, impulsive or intermittent/VDV) selected for a source, with excluded cases routed to the right framework.
Before relying on "Classify vibration and select assessment criteria" — what do you check?::Assessment location is where people are affected (inside buildings), with a justified transfer function if measuring outside. • Building resonance considered - indoor values can exceed external ground values.
"Classify vibration and select assessment criteria" — state the decision rule about: Three or fewer events per assessment period: assess as impul…::Three or fewer events per assessment period: assess as impulsive; more: assess as intermittent via VDV (vibrationguide0643 Section 2.1, Table 2.1).
"Classify vibration and select assessment criteria" — state the decision rule about: Daytime is defined 7 am to 10 pm, night-time 10 pm to 7 am (…::Daytime is defined 7 am to 10 pm, night-time 10 pm to 7 am (vibrationguide0643 Table 2.2 note).
What does "Design and monitor trenchless under road crossing" produce?::A trenchless crossing design and settlement-monitoring regime meeting roads-authority technical requirements for concurrence.
Before relying on "Design and monitor trenchless under road crossing" — what do you check?::Investigation depth reaches at least 2 m into competent material below invert. • Cumulative settlement from successive project stages included in the assessment. • Condition survey of sensitive assets completed where damage risk exists.
"Design and monitor trenchless under road crossing" — state the decision rule about: Minimum serviceability traffic UDL 20 kPa plus minimum 10 kP…::Minimum serviceability traffic UDL 20 kPa plus minimum 10 kPa non-traffic surcharge (TS 02088 design loads section).
"Design and monitor trenchless under road crossing" — state the decision rule about: Preliminary settlement limits: total surface settlement 15 m…::Preliminary settlement limits: total surface settlement 15 mm and differential no more than 6 mm over any 2 m (TS 02088 ground deformations section).
What does "Measure ground and building vibration correctly" produce?::Vibration measurements whose transducer mounting, dynamic range and location make them valid for assessment against criteria.
Before relying on "Measure ground and building vibration correctly" — what do you check?::Transducer orientation per manufacturer, aligned to source direction where relevant. • Instrumentation meets the referenced BS performance requirements. • Background vibration defined and quantified.
"Measure ground and building vibration correctly" — state the decision rule about: Transducer plus monitoring unit mass must not exceed 10% of …::Transducer plus monitoring unit mass must not exceed 10% of the building element's mass (vibrationguide0643 Section 4.4).
"Measure ground and building vibration correctly" — state the decision rule about: Never use double-sided foam tape for mounting (Section 4.4).…::Never use double-sided foam tape for mounting (Section 4.4).
What does "Run staged monitoring and hold points for supported excavation" produce?::An instrumentation, trigger and hold-point regime that keeps an adjacent-to-road excavation verified stage by stage.
Before relying on "Run staged monitoring and hold points for supported excavation" — what do you check?::Two independent consistent baseline sets before any works. • Hold point certifications explicitly compare encountered geotechnical conditions to the investigation report and record corrective actions. • Monitoring continues until the defined stability criterion (post-completion month or three stable weekly readings) is met.
"Run staged monitoring and hold points for supported excavation" — state the decision rule about: Instrumentation typically required for cantilever walls reta…::Instrumentation typically required for cantilever walls retaining over 3 m and propped/anchored walls over 6 m (gtd-2020-001 instrumentation section).
"Run staged monitoring and hold points for supported excavation" — state the decision rule about: Minimum two inclinometers installed at least 3 m below wall …::Minimum two inclinometers installed at least 3 m below wall toe level (gtd-2020-001 instrumentation section).
What does "Select field density test method by oversize" produce?::A valid in-situ density / relative compaction result using the test method appropriate to the material's oversize fraction and layer thickness.
Before relying on "Select field density test method by oversize" — what do you check?::Field moisture methods T121/T180 only used after correlation against the oven method for the materials being compacted. • Results rounded to nearest 0.1% and characteristic value computed per RMS Q.
"Select field density test method by oversize" — state the decision rule about: Oversize <= 20%: nuclear gauge or sand replacement permitted…::Oversize <= 20%: nuclear gauge or sand replacement permitted; 20-40%: sand replacement only (no nuclear gauge); > 40%: relative compaction is invalid - report only the oversize percentage (b030 Table 
"Select field density test method by oversize" — state the decision rule about: Do not use the nuclear gauge where layer thickness exceeds 3…::Do not use the nuclear gauge where layer thickness exceeds 300 mm (b030 Clause 6.4.3).

## Related

- [[Learning loop]]

notes.title: Flashcards - Parameters and correlations
notes.body:
# Flashcards - Parameters and correlations

#flashcards/parameters

56 cards generated from the 14 parameters and correlations skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Adjust rock footing design for cut faces, horizontal loads and moment loading" produce?::Bearing, sliding and rotation checks corrected for footings near excavation crests or carrying non-centric loads, where the standard centric-vertical guideline values do not apply.
Before relying on "Adjust rock footing design for cut faces, horizontal loads and moment loading" — what do you check?::Face inspection scope written into the specification. • Existing buildings at a new excavation crest checked for both bearing and kinematic failure modes. • Vertical-horizontal capacity interaction reconsidered where lateral load is a significant case.
"Adjust rock footing design for cut faces, horizontal loads and moment loading" — state the decision rule about: If adversely oriented defects daylight or nearly daylight in…::If adversely oriented defects daylight or nearly daylight in the face, kinematic failure governs regardless of class-based bearing values.
"Adjust rock footing design for cut faces, horizontal loads and moment loading" — state the decision rule about: Shale base friction is more complex than sandstone and depen…::Shale base friction is more complex than sandstone and depends on construction and inspection specifics; do not carry the sandstone friction coefficient across.
What does "Adopt saturated strength and stiffness values for Hawkesbury Sandstone design" produce?::Substance UCS and modulus inputs selected on a saturated basis, avoiding the systematic overestimate that dry-tested Hawkesbury Sandstone produces.
Before relying on "Adopt saturated strength and stiffness values for Hawkesbury Sandstone design" — what do you check?::Reported UCS statistics separated by wet/dry condition before averaging. • Modulus basis (secant vs tangent, stress range) stated with every value.
"Adopt saturated strength and stiffness values for Hawkesbury Sandstone design" — state the decision rule about: Resaturating dried specimens generally restores the saturate…::Resaturating dried specimens generally restores the saturated strength (for material from below the water table), so retesting is a valid recovery route.
"Adopt saturated strength and stiffness values for Hawkesbury Sandstone design" — state the decision rule about: Clayey sandstones show the strongest wet/dry sensitivity; tr…::Clayey sandstones show the strongest wet/dry sensitivity; treat low wet/dry ratios as a durability warning as well.
What does "Assign preliminary hydrogeological parameters to Sydney rock classes for groundwater modelling" produce?::Class-linked first-pass ranges of hydraulic conductivity, porosity, drainable storage and mass stiffness for saturated groundwater models of Hawkesbury Sandstone and Wianamatta shale, with structural features handled explicitly.
Before relying on "Assign preliminary hydrogeological parameters to Sydney rock classes for groundwater modelling" — what do you check?::Packer/pumping test data used to confirm or override the tabulated ranges wherever available. • Specific storage consistent with the adopted mass modulus, not independently assumed.
"Assign preliminary hydrogeological parameters to Sydney rock classes for groundwater modelling" — state the decision rule about: Use the class linkage only for preliminary, saturated-condit…::Use the class linkage only for preliminary, saturated-condition analyses on projects where the classification already frames the geological model; it is not a hydrogeological classification.
"Assign preliminary hydrogeological parameters to Sydney rock classes for groundwater modelling" — state the decision rule about: For unsaturated analyses, additional suction-dependent funct…::For unsaturated analyses, additional suction-dependent functions are required that the class tables do not provide.
What does "Classify Sydney sandstone and shale with the Pells three-criteria system and state the controlling criterion" produce?::A defensible Class I-V assignment for Hawkesbury Sandstone or Ashfield Shale, with the rock volume and controlling criterion recorded, and misuse of the system avoided.
Before relying on "Classify Sydney sandstone and shale with the Pells three-criteria system and state the controlling criterion" — what do you check?::UCS values are for saturated substance, not dry. • Defect spacing is true spacing, not apparent spacing in inclined core. • Seam percentage is computed over the correct zone of influence (1.5 times least footing dimension for pads; socket length plus footing width for sockets).
"Classify Sydney sandstone and shale with the Pells three-criteria system and state the controlling criterion" — state the decision rule about: Never classify from pile-rig cuttings or from drilling resis…::Never classify from pile-rig cuttings or from drilling resistance; the system needs quantitative strength, spacing and seam data.
"Classify Sydney sandstone and shale with the Pells three-criteria system and state the controlling criterion" — state the decision rule about: Do not apply the system to small components of the rock mass…::Do not apply the system to small components of the rock mass, to major fault zones, or to zones affected by dykes and sills.
What does "Cross-check every SPT-derived parameter against expected ranges and independent tests" produce?::A quality-assurance habit applied to all SPT correlations: each derived parameter validated for plausibility, corrected consistently, and traced to its correlation before entering design.
Before relying on "Cross-check every SPT-derived parameter against expected ranges and independent tests" — what do you check?::Every reported parameter carries its correction convention and correlation citation. • No parameter is used for a material type that Table 9 does not support.
"Cross-check every SPT-derived parameter against expected ranges and independent tests" — state the decision rule about: If an SPT-derived value falls outside the expected range and…::If an SPT-derived value falls outside the expected range and cannot be reconciled with independent data, discard or downweight it rather than average it in.
"Cross-check every SPT-derived parameter against expected ranges and independent tests" — state the decision rule about: Prefer correlations from the major reviews (e.g. Stroud 1989…::Prefer correlations from the major reviews (e.g. Stroud 1989) over single-site relations unless the site matches the single-site geology.
What does "Derive granular soil friction angle from corrected SPT blow counts" produce?::A design effective friction angle for sands and gravels from SPT resistance, corrected for hammer energy and overburden, with awareness of the triaxial versus plane-strain distinction.
Before relying on "Derive granular soil friction angle from corrected SPT blow counts" — what do you check?::Correction convention (N1, N60, (N1)60) stated explicitly with every value. • Derived phi' within the plausible band for the soil's grading and angularity.
"Derive granular soil friction angle from corrected SPT blow counts" — state the decision rule about: If the deposit is cemented or aged, standard density-based c…::If the deposit is cemented or aged, standard density-based correlations may not apply.
"Derive granular soil friction angle from corrected SPT blow counts" — state the decision rule about: Compare SPT-derived phi' with values from other in-situ or l…::Compare SPT-derived phi' with values from other in-situ or laboratory tests wherever possible before adoption.
What does "Estimate Hawkesbury Sandstone UCS from index tests and treat the correlations as screening tools" produce?::Preliminary UCS estimates from point load, Brazilian tensile or sonic velocity data, with correlation scatter explicitly acknowledged.
Before relying on "Estimate Hawkesbury Sandstone UCS from index tests and treat the correlations as screening tools" — what do you check?::Saturation state of index specimens matches the design (saturated) basis. • Derived values fall within the class-consistent UCS range for the material logged.
"Estimate Hawkesbury Sandstone UCS from index tests and treat the correlations as screening tools" — state the decision rule about: The point load test behaves close to a pure tensile measure …::The point load test behaves close to a pure tensile measure here; do not stack a point-load-to-UCS conversion on top of a tensile-to-UCS conversion.
"Estimate Hawkesbury Sandstone UCS from index tests and treat the correlations as screening tools" — state the decision rule about: Do not use generic worldwide Is50 multipliers (e.g. 22-24 as…::Do not use generic worldwide Is50 multipliers (e.g. 22-24 as universal) without checking the local range.
What does "Estimate the Sydney Basin natural stress field and validate it before stress-sensitive design" produce?::Initial in situ stress inputs from the simple depth-based equations, upgraded by a measurement and cross-checking campaign wherever stress concentrations or depth make the design stress-sensitive.
Before relying on "Estimate the Sydney Basin natural stress field and validate it before stress-sensitive design" — what do you check?::Conflicting results between techniques investigated, not averaged away. • Measurements near dykes treated as potentially unrepresentative (documented reversals across the Elgas cavern dyke).
"Estimate the Sydney Basin natural stress field and validate it before stress-sensitive design" — state the decision rule about: Hydrofracture is most reliable for stress directions, less s…::Hydrofracture is most reliable for stress directions, less so for magnitudes, in this geology.
"Estimate the Sydney Basin natural stress field and validate it before stress-sensitive design" — state the decision rule about: Expect stress-field consistency at the scale of hundreds of …::Expect stress-field consistency at the scale of hundreds of metres, not at bedding or block scale.
What does "Estimate weak rock strength and stiffness from SPT N60 with explicit reliability limits" produce?::Order-of-magnitude undrained strength, unconfined compressive strength and stiffness values for weak rocks from extrapolated SPT resistance, bounded by the documented scatter and material-type limitations.
Before relying on "Estimate weak rock strength and stiffness from SPT N60 with explicit reliability limits" — what do you check?::Extrapolation method for refusal tests documented. • Material type comparable to the calibration deposits before relying on the coefficients.
"Estimate weak rock strength and stiffness from SPT N60 with explicit reliability limits" — state the decision rule about: Expect at least ~20% scatter about the mean even below N60 o…::Expect at least ~20% scatter about the mean even below N60 of 200 blows/300mm, and worse at higher strengths; treat outputs as estimates, not measurements.
"Estimate weak rock strength and stiffness from SPT N60 with explicit reliability limits" — state the decision rule about: The correlations are proven mainly on Mercia/Keuper mudstone…::The correlations are proven mainly on Mercia/Keuper mudstones, Bunter Sandstone and Millstone Grit; reliability in other deposits is unknown.
What does "Screen Hawkesbury Sandstone durability with sodium sulphate soundness before exposed or marine use" produce?::A durability grading of sandstone for breakwater, cladding or dimension-stone applications based on sodium sulphate soundness loss, cross-checked against wet/dry strength ratio and expansive clay content.
Before relying on "Screen Hawkesbury Sandstone durability with sodium sulphate soundness before exposed or marine use" — what do you check?::Test method and cycle count recorded with every soundness result. • Grading matched to actual exposure aggressiveness.
"Screen Hawkesbury Sandstone durability with sodium sulphate soundness before exposed or marine use" — state the decision rule about: Low saturated strength combined with high sulphate loss flag…::Low saturated strength combined with high sulphate loss flags unsatisfactory field performance (the exposed Botany Bay case: ~6 MPa saturated UCS with very high loss failed in service).
"Screen Hawkesbury Sandstone durability with sodium sulphate soundness before exposed or marine use" — state the decision rule about: Porosity strongly influences dimension-stone performance; me…::Porosity strongly influences dimension-stone performance; measure it under standard conditions (ASTM C97 approach).
What does "Screen laboratory and field soil results against published typical ranges before design use" produce?::Early detection of implausible test results or data gaps by comparing site values with the typical property ranges per soil class compiled in Carter & Bentley.
Before relying on "Screen laboratory and field soil results against published typical ranges before design use" — what do you check?::Classification of the sample confirmed before the range comparison. • Screening outcomes documented in the ground model.
"Screen laboratory and field soil results against published typical ranges before design use" — state the decision rule about: An out-of-range result is a trigger for investigation, not a…::An out-of-range result is a trigger for investigation, not automatic rejection.
"Screen laboratory and field soil results against published typical ranges before design use" — state the decision rule about: Never let range-derived estimates govern final design of sig…::Never let range-derived estimates govern final design of significant structures without confirmatory testing.
What does "Select a soil parameter correlation and record its provenance using Carter and Bentley" produce?::A defensible preliminary soil parameter chosen from the Carter & Bentley compendium, with its class basis, applicability limits and citation documented, and with the value explicitly flagged as an estimate pending testing.
Before relying on "Select a soil parameter correlation and record its provenance using Carter and Bentley" — what do you check?::Correlation applicability limits verified against the site soils. • Every correlation-derived value distinguishable from measured values in the design record.
"Select a soil parameter correlation and record its provenance using Carter and Bentley" — state the decision rule about: Prefer correlations tied to classification tests actually pe…::Prefer correlations tied to classification tests actually performed for the site over generic typical-value tables.
"Select a soil parameter correlation and record its provenance using Carter and Bentley" — state the decision rule about: Where two correlations disagree materially, carry the range …::Where two correlations disagree materially, carry the range forward rather than picking the favourable end.
What does "Select rock mass and defect parameters for numerical modelling in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Sydney shale" produce?::A parameter set (mass modulus, strength, permeability, GSI, defect normal and shear stiffness, defect friction) for numerical analysis of Sydney-region excavations, drawn from the Bertuzzi & Pells (2002) tables with data-provenance understood.
Before relying on "Select rock mass and defect parameters for numerical modelling in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Sydney shale" — what do you check?::Adopted mass modulus consistent with field-measured benchmarks (e.g. ~800-1100 MPa for borderline Class III sandstone at Lucas Heights; ~1200 MPa Class III from • Elastic ks/kn expectation (0.33-0.5) recognised as unconservative relative to the observed ~0.1 recommendation.
"Select rock mass and defect parameters for numerical modelling in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Sydney shale" — state the decision rule about: The foundation classification is a communication tool, not a…::The foundation classification is a communication tool, not a design tool, for non-foundation works: tunnels, slopes and basements must be designed by applied mechanics with these parameters, not by cl
"Select rock mass and defect parameters for numerical modelling in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Sydney shale" — state the decision rule about: Where kn/ks matter to results, run sensitivity analyses; the…::Where kn/ks matter to results, run sensitivity analyses; the authors flag a paucity of data for these.
What does "Set serviceability bearing pressures on Sydney rock from allowable settlement and class-based mass modulus" produce?::A footing bearing pressure derived explicitly from the structure's allowable settlement using class-based mass modulus, instead of blind adoption of the tabulated 1%-settlement guideline values.
Before relying on "Set serviceability bearing pressures on Sydney rock from allowable settlement and class-based mass modulus" — what do you check?::Computed settlement stays within the approximately linear pressure range for the class. • Semi-infinite-mass elastic equations recognised as potentially conservative. • Differential settlement between adjacent footings assessed, not just individual settlements.
"Set serviceability bearing pressures on Sydney rock from allowable settlement and class-based mass modulus" — state the decision rule about: If proposed pressures exceed the tabulated guidelines substa…::If proposed pressures exceed the tabulated guidelines substantially, the designer must confirm the adopted moduli by site-specific investigation and construction verification, including spoon testing 
"Set serviceability bearing pressures on Sydney rock from allowable settlement and class-based mass modulus" — state the decision rule about: Where footing sizes differ widely, do not use the 1% guideli…::Where footing sizes differ widely, do not use the 1% guideline pressures uncritically; equal pressures on an 800 mm and a 4500 mm footing produce very different settlements and can cause unacceptable 

## Related
