Before relying on "Adopt saturated strength and stiffness values for Hawkesbury Sandstone design" — what do you check?::Reported UCS statistics separated by wet/dry condition before averaging. • Modulus basis (secant vs tangent, stress range) stated with every value. "Adopt saturated strength and stiffness values for Hawkesbury Sandstone design" — state the decision rule about: Resaturating dried specimens generally restores the saturate…::Resaturating dried specimens generally restores the saturated strength (for material from below the water table), so retesting is a valid recovery route. "Adopt saturated strength and stiffness values for Hawkesbury Sandstone design" — state the decision rule about: Clayey sandstones show the strongest wet/dry sensitivity; tr…::Clayey sandstones show the strongest wet/dry sensitivity; treat low wet/dry ratios as a durability warning as well. What does "Assign preliminary hydrogeological parameters to Sydney rock classes for groundwater modelling" produce?::Class linked first pass ranges of hydraulic conductivity, porosity, drainable storage and mass stiffness for saturated groundwater models of Hawkesbury Sandstone and Wianamatta shale, with structural features handled explicitly. Before relying on "Assign preliminary hydrogeological parameters to Sydney rock classes for groundwater modelling" — what do you check?::Packer/pumping test data used to confirm or override the tabulated ranges wherever available. • Specific storage consistent with the adopted mass modulus, not independently assumed. "Assign preliminary hydrogeological parameters to Sydney rock classes for groundwater modelling" — state the decision rule about: Use the class linkage only for preliminary, saturated condit…::Use the class linkage only for preliminary, saturated condition analyses on projects where the classification already frames the geological model; it is not a hydrogeological classification. "Assign preliminary hydrogeological parameters to Sydney rock classes for groundwater modelling" — state the decision rule about: For unsaturated analyses, additional suction dependent funct…::For unsaturated analyses, additional suction dependent functions are required that the class tables do not provide. What does "Classify Sydney sandstone and shale with the Pells three criteria system and state the controlling criterion" produce?::A defensible Class I V assignment for Hawkesbury Sandstone or Ashfield Shale, with the rock volume and controlling criterion recorded, and misuse of the system avoided. Before relying on "Classify Sydney sandstone and shale with the Pells three criteria system and state the controlling criterion" — what do you check?::UCS values are for saturated substance, not dry. • Defect spacing is true spacing, not apparent spacing in inclined core. • Seam percentage is computed over the correct zone of influence (1.5 times least footing dimension for pads; socket length plus footing width for sockets). "Classify Sydney sandstone and shale with the Pells three criteria system and state the controlling criterion" — state the decision rule about: Never classify from pile rig cuttings or from drilling resis…::Never classify from pile rig cuttings or from drilling resistance; the system needs quantitative strength, spacing and seam data. "Classify Sydney sandstone and shale with the Pells three criteria system and state the controlling criterion" — state the decision rule about: Do not apply the system to small components of the rock mass…::Do not apply the system to small components of the rock mass, to major fault zones, or to zones affected by dykes and sills. What does "Cross check every SPT derived parameter against expected ranges and independent tests" produce?::A quality assurance habit applied to all SPT correlations: each derived parameter validated for plausibility, corrected consistently, and traced to its correlation before entering design. Before relying on "Cross check every SPT derived parameter against expected ranges and independent tests" — what do you check?::Every reported parameter carries its correction convention and correlation citation. • No parameter is used for a material type that Table 9 does not support. "Cross check every SPT derived parameter against expected ranges and independent tests" — state the decision rule about: If an SPT derived value falls outside the expected range and…::If an SPT derived value falls outside the expected range and cannot be reconciled with independent data, discard or downweight it rather than average it in. "Cross check every SPT derived parameter against expected ranges and independent tests" — state the decision rule about: Prefer correlations from the major reviews (e.g. Stroud 1989…::Prefer correlations from the major reviews (e.g. Stroud 1989) over single site relations unless the site matches the single site geology. What does "Derive granular soil friction angle from corrected SPT blow counts" produce?::A design effective friction angle for sands and gravels from SPT resistance, corrected for hammer energy and overburden, with awareness of the triaxial versus plane strain distinction. Before relying on "Derive granular soil friction angle from corrected SPT blow counts" — what do you check?::Correction convention (N1, N60, (N1)60) stated explicitly with every value. • Derived phi' within the plausible band for the soil's grading and angularity. "Derive granular soil friction angle from corrected SPT blow counts" — state the decision rule about: If the deposit is cemented or aged, standard density based c…::If the deposit is cemented or aged, standard density based correlations may not apply. "Derive granular soil friction angle from corrected SPT blow counts" — state the decision rule about: Compare SPT derived phi' with values from other in situ or l…::Compare SPT derived phi' with values from other in situ or laboratory tests wherever possible before adoption. What does "Estimate Hawkesbury Sandstone UCS from index tests and treat the correlations as screening tools" produce?::Preliminary UCS estimates from point load, Brazilian tensile or sonic velocity data, with correlation scatter explicitly acknowledged. Before relying on "Estimate Hawkesbury Sandstone UCS from index tests and treat the correlations as screening tools" — what do you check?::Saturation state of index specimens matches the design (saturated) basis. • Derived values fall within the class consistent UCS range for the material logged. "Estimate Hawkesbury Sandstone UCS from index tests and treat the correlations as screening tools" — state the decision rule about: The point load test behaves close to a pure tensile measure …::The point load test behaves close to a pure tensile measure here; do not stack a point load to UCS conversion on top of a tensile to UCS conversion. "Estimate Hawkesbury Sandstone UCS from index tests and treat the correlations as screening tools" — state the decision rule about: Do not use generic worldwide Is50 multipliers (e.g. 22 24 as…::Do not use generic worldwide Is50 multipliers (e.g. 22 24 as universal) without checking the local range. What does "Estimate the Sydney Basin natural stress field and validate it before stress sensitive design" produce?::Initial in situ stress inputs from the simple depth based equations, upgraded by a measurement and cross checking campaign wherever stress concentrations or depth make the design stress sensitive. Before relying on "Estimate the Sydney Basin natural stress field and validate it before stress sensitive design" — what do you check?::Conflicting results between techniques investigated, not averaged away. • Measurements near dykes treated as potentially unrepresentative (documented reversals across the Elgas cavern dyke). "Estimate the Sydney Basin natural stress field and validate it before stress sensitive design" — state the decision rule about: Hydrofracture is most reliable for stress directions, less s…::Hydrofracture is most reliable for stress directions, less so for magnitudes, in this geology. "Estimate the Sydney Basin natural stress field and validate it before stress sensitive design" — state the decision rule about: Expect stress field consistency at the scale of hundreds of …::Expect stress field consistency at the scale of hundreds of metres, not at bedding or block scale. What does "Estimate weak rock strength and stiffness from SPT N60 with explicit reliability limits" produce?::Order of magnitude undrained strength, unconfined compressive strength and stiffness values for weak rocks from extrapolated SPT resistance, bounded by the documented scatter and material type limitations. Before relying on "Estimate weak rock strength and stiffness from SPT N60 with explicit reliability limits" — what do you check?::Extrapolation method for refusal tests documented. • Material type comparable to the calibration deposits before relying on the coefficients. "Estimate weak rock strength and stiffness from SPT N60 with explicit reliability limits" — state the decision rule about: Expect at least ~20% scatter about the mean even below N60 o…::Expect at least ~20% scatter about the mean even below N60 of 200 blows/300mm, and worse at higher strengths; treat outputs as estimates, not measurements. "Estimate weak rock strength and stiffness from SPT N60 with explicit reliability limits" — state the decision rule about: The correlations are proven mainly on Mercia/Keuper mudstone…::The correlations are proven mainly on Mercia/Keuper mudstones, Bunter Sandstone and Millstone Grit; reliability in other deposits is unknown. What does "Screen Hawkesbury Sandstone durability with sodium sulphate soundness before exposed or marine use" produce?::A durability grading of sandstone for breakwater, cladding or dimension stone applications based on sodium sulphate soundness loss, cross checked against wet/dry strength ratio and expansive clay content. Before relying on "Screen Hawkesbury Sandstone durability with sodium sulphate soundness before exposed or marine use" — what do you check?::Test method and cycle count recorded with every soundness result. • Grading matched to actual exposure aggressiveness. "Screen Hawkesbury Sandstone durability with sodium sulphate soundness before exposed or marine use" — state the decision rule about: Low saturated strength combined with high sulphate loss flag…::Low saturated strength combined with high sulphate loss flags unsatisfactory field performance (the exposed Botany Bay case: ~6 MPa saturated UCS with very high loss failed in service). "Screen Hawkesbury Sandstone durability with sodium sulphate soundness before exposed or marine use" — state the decision rule about: Porosity strongly influences dimension stone performance; me…::Porosity strongly influences dimension stone performance; measure it under standard conditions (ASTM C97 approach). What does "Screen laboratory and field soil results against published typical ranges before design use" produce?::Early detection of implausible test results or data gaps by comparing site values with the typical property ranges per soil class compiled in Carter & Bentley. Before relying on "Screen laboratory and field soil results against published typical ranges before design use" — what do you check?::Classification of the sample confirmed before the range comparison. • Screening outcomes documented in the ground model. "Screen laboratory and field soil results against published typical ranges before design use" — state the decision rule about: An out of range result is a trigger for investigation, not a…::An out of range result is a trigger for investigation, not automatic rejection. "Screen laboratory and field soil results against published typical ranges before design use" — state the decision rule about: Never let range derived estimates govern final design of sig…::Never let range derived estimates govern final design of significant structures without confirmatory testing. What does "Select a soil parameter correlation and record its provenance using Carter and Bentley" produce?::A defensible preliminary soil parameter chosen from the Carter & Bentley compendium, with its class basis, applicability limits and citation documented, and with the value explicitly flagged as an estimate pending testing. Before relying on "Select a soil parameter correlation and record its provenance using Carter and Bentley" — what do you check?::Correlation applicability limits verified against the site soils. • Every correlation derived value distinguishable from measured values in the design record. "Select a soil parameter correlation and record its provenance using Carter and Bentley" — state the decision rule about: Prefer correlations tied to classification tests actually pe…::Prefer correlations tied to classification tests actually performed for the site over generic typical value tables. "Select a soil parameter correlation and record its provenance using Carter and Bentley" — state the decision rule about: Where two correlations disagree materially, carry the range …::Where two correlations disagree materially, carry the range forward rather than picking the favourable end. What does "Select rock mass and defect parameters for numerical modelling in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Sydney shale" produce?::A parameter set (mass modulus, strength, permeability, GSI, defect normal and shear stiffness, defect friction) for numerical analysis of Sydney region excavations, drawn from the Bertuzzi & Pells (2002) tables with data provenance understood. Before relying on "Select rock mass and defect parameters for numerical modelling in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Sydney shale" — what do you check?::Adopted mass modulus consistent with field measured benchmarks (e.g. ~800 1100 MPa for borderline Class III sandstone at Lucas Heights; ~1200 MPa Class III from • Elastic ks/kn expectation (0.33 0.5) recognised as unconservative relative to the observed ~0.1 recommendation. "Select rock mass and defect parameters for numerical modelling in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Sydney shale" — state the decision rule about: The foundation classification is a communication tool, not a…::The foundation classification is a communication tool, not a design tool, for non foundation works: tunnels, slopes and basements must be designed by applied mechanics with these parameters, not by cl "Select rock mass and defect parameters for numerical modelling in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Sydney shale" — state the decision rule about: Where kn/ks matter to results, run sensitivity analyses; the…::Where kn/ks matter to results, run sensitivity analyses; the authors flag a paucity of data for these. What does "Set serviceability bearing pressures on Sydney rock from allowable settlement and class based mass modulus" produce?::A footing bearing pressure derived explicitly from the structure's allowable settlement using class based mass modulus, instead of blind adoption of the tabulated 1% settlement guideline values. Before relying on "Set serviceability bearing pressures on Sydney rock from allowable settlement and class based mass modulus" — what do you check?::Computed settlement stays within the approximately linear pressure range for the class. • Semi infinite mass elastic equations recognised as potentially conservative. • Differential settlement between adjacent footings assessed, not just individual settlements. "Set serviceability bearing pressures on Sydney rock from allowable settlement and class based mass modulus" — state the decision rule about: If proposed pressures exceed the tabulated guidelines substa…::If proposed pressures exceed the tabulated guidelines substantially, the designer must confirm the adopted moduli by site specific investigation and construction verification, including spoon testing "Set serviceability bearing pressures on Sydney rock from allowable settlement and class based mass modulus" — state the decision rule about: Where footing sizes differ widely, do not use the 1% guideli…::Where footing sizes differ widely, do not use the 1% guideline pressures uncritically; equal pressures on an 800 mm and a 4500 mm footing produce very different settlements and can cause unacceptable Related Learning path Parameters and correlations Learning loop

notes.title: Flashcards - Pavements
notes.body:
# Flashcards - Pavements

#flashcards/pavements

24 cards generated from the 6 pavements skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Accept marginal granular material via shear strength" produce?::A defensible acceptance pathway for materials failing grading/particle-shape criteria but demonstrating adequate shear strength, limited to permitted traffic categories.
Before relying on "Accept marginal granular material via shear strength" — what do you check?::Conditioning at the specified fraction of optimum moisture and full standard-compaction density before triaxial testing. • Hold point submission includes nominated PSD when grading was the failed criterion.
"Accept marginal granular material via shear strength" — state the decision rule about: Unbound strength-based acceptance is only available for Traf…::Unbound strength-based acceptance is only available for Traffic Categories C and D (RTA 3051 Clause 8.2.1 and Figure 3051.2 notes).
"Accept marginal granular material via shear strength" — state the decision rule about: Texas triaxial classification-number ceilings vary by catego…::Texas triaxial classification-number ceilings vary by category and layer (e.g. tighter for base than subbase) per Table 3051.4.
What does "Control insitu binder spreading and mixing" produce?::Binder incorporated uniformly at or above the target rate, within weather and working-time constraints, with records supporting lot conformity.
Before relying on "Control insitu binder spreading and mixing" — what do you check?::Spilled binder removed within 12 hours and never incorporated. • UCS samples moulded within three hours of initial mixing, cured per accelerated regime, times recorded (dc_r071 Clause 8.2). • Alternative incorporation methods treated as an Alternative Construction Method hold point.
"Control insitu binder spreading and mixing" — state the decision rule about: Field Target Spread Rate = design rate plus at least 0.2 kg/…::Field Target Spread Rate = design rate plus at least 0.2 kg/m2; quicklime spread rate = hydrated design rate x 0.76 (dc_r071 Clause 5.2.4.2).
"Control insitu binder spreading and mixing" — state the decision rule about: Lengths spread below 95% of the field target may receive fur…::Lengths spread below 95% of the field target may receive further binder to make up the rate (dc_r071 Clause 5.2.4.3).
What does "Design modified pavement mix" produce?::A nominated mix design for a modified (not bound) pavement course accepted through the hold point before any pavement work starts.
Before relying on "Design modified pavement mix" — what do you check?::Blended binder components within plus/minus 3% of nominated blend percentages. • SDS and safe handling procedures for binders included in the quality plan.
"Design modified pavement mix" — state the decision rule about: Nominated Working Time (per RMS T147) must exceed 6 hours (d…::Nominated Working Time (per RMS T147) must exceed 6 hours (dc_r071 Clause 4.1).
"Design modified pavement mix" — state the decision rule about: UCS at 28 days normal or 7 days accelerated curing must be l…::UCS at 28 days normal or 7 days accelerated curing must be less than 1 MPa, tested per RMS T116 (dc_r071 Clause 4.1).
What does "Evaluate granular base subbase material" produce?::Acceptance or rejection of a proposed granular base/subbase mix against the traffic-category-dependent grading, plasticity, strength and durability criteria.
Before relying on "Evaluate granular base subbase material" — what do you check?::All contributing size fractions tested for wet strength, including the finer fraction for blended materials. • UCS ceiling applies to mixes containing recycled concrete, bricks or slag (self-cementing check). • Recycled constituents checked against the foreign-material limits table.
"Evaluate granular base subbase material" — state the decision rule about: Traffic Category A unbound base must be heavy-duty designati…::Traffic Category A unbound base must be heavy-duty designation assessed under the particle-size clause (RTA 3051 Clause 5.2.2).
"Evaluate granular base subbase material" — state the decision rule about: Pretreatment breakdown is unacceptable if any sieve passing …::Pretreatment breakdown is unacceptable if any sieve passing increases by more than 3 points (or exits the grading envelope) or PI rises by more than 3 (or exceeds table limits) (RTA 3051 Clause 5.4).
What does "Prove pavement process with trial section" produce?::A trial pavement section demonstrating that materials, plant and methods achieve specified compaction, thickness and levels before full production is released.
Before relying on "Prove pavement process with trial section" — what do you check?::Trial results cover compaction, course thickness, levels and specified pavement properties, not just density. • Nonconforming trial sections dispositioned through the nonconformity process.
"Prove pavement process with trial section" — state the decision rule about: Trial length must be between 100 m and 200 m for the propose…::Trial length must be between 100 m and 200 m for the proposed lot width (dc_r071 Clause 6.3).
"Prove pavement process with trial section" — state the decision rule about: Witness point notification at least 3 working days before tr…::Witness point notification at least 3 working days before trial construction (dc_r071 Clause 6.3).
What does "Verify unbound modified course conformity" produce?::Lot-by-lot conformity verdicts for a placed unbound/modified pavement course covering compaction, geometry, surface and readiness for sealing.
Before relying on "Verify unbound modified course conformity" — what do you check?::Underlying surface levels higher than design are flagged as nonconforming before placing. • Test holes reinstated to equivalent compaction. • Weekly conformity certificate plus daily moisture/density submissions.
"Verify unbound modified course conformity" — state the decision rule about: Layer compacted thickness must be 100-150 mm (dc_r071 Clause…::Layer compacted thickness must be 100-150 mm (dc_r071 Clause 6.5).
"Verify unbound modified course conformity" — state the decision rule about: Characteristic relative compaction: heavy-duty base 100% (mo…::Characteristic relative compaction: heavy-duty base 100% (modified compaction); heavy-duty subbase and non-heavy-duty material 102% (standard compaction) (dc_r071 Table R71.1).

## Related

- [[Learning path - Pavements]]
- [[Learning loop]]

notes.title: Flashcards - Piling and Sydney rock
notes.body:
# Flashcards - Piling and Sydney rock

#flashcards/piling-rock

52 cards generated from the 13 piling and sydney rock skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Apply limit state load combinations and geotechnical reduction factors to rock foundation design" produce?::Strength and serviceability limit state checks for pads and sockets on Sydney rock using the paper's recommended phi_g values, filling the gap where AS 2159's tabulated factors do not cover rock-socket methods.
Before relying on "Apply limit state load combinations and geotechnical reduction factors to rock foundation design" — what do you check?::All relevant AS 1170.1 combinations screened, not just the typical governing pair. • phi_g category justified by documented local test data. • Structural strength of the pile checked separately from geotechnical strength.
"Apply limit state load combinations and geotechnical reduction factors to rock foundation design" — state the decision rule about: The recommended phi_g values presume assured construction QC…::The recommended phi_g values presume assured construction QC of sidewall and base cleanliness; without it, be very conservative and do not apply prescriptive factors.
"Apply limit state load combinations and geotechnical reduction factors to rock foundation design" — state the decision rule about: Serviceability frequently governs socket design, so the modu…::Serviceability frequently governs socket design, so the modulus reduction is not optional in practice.
What does "Check uplift sockets and anchors for piston pullout and rock cone liftout" produce?::Ultimate-limit-state verification of a tension socket or anchor against both shaft pullout and liftout of a surrounding rock mass, using the paper's simplified cone model.
Before relying on "Check uplift sockets and anchors for piston pullout and rock cone liftout" — what do you check?::Overlapping cones from anchor groups accounted for. • Groundwater level and buoyancy assumptions explicit. • Roughness/cleanliness assumptions for the shear values are achievable by the drilling method.
"Check uplift sockets and anchors for piston pullout and rock cone liftout" — state the decision rule about: In Classes I-III the liftout mass tends to slab-like shapes;…::In Classes I-III the liftout mass tends to slab-like shapes; in Classes IV-V it approaches the classic soil-anchor cone - choose the governing mechanism accordingly.
"Check uplift sockets and anchors for piston pullout and rock cone liftout" — state the decision rule about: Anchors with plates, nuts or under-reams behave differently …::Anchors with plates, nuts or under-reams behave differently and are outside this method.
What does "Choose the load-carrying mechanism for a rock foundation before selecting design parameters" produce?::A deliberate base-only, side-shear-only or combined design basis for a footing or socket, consistent with geometry, constructability and the applied mechanics of side/base load sharing.
Before relying on "Choose the load-carrying mechanism for a rock foundation before selecting design parameters" — what do you check?::Sidewall roughness assessed against the R1-R4 scheme (reproduced in the companion papers). • Cleanliness method (drilling under water, water-stir, cleaning teeth) matched to rock sensitivity to water.
"Choose the load-carrying mechanism for a rock foundation before selecting design parameters" — state the decision rule about: If ultimate end-bearing capacity is uncertain, do not design…::If ultimate end-bearing capacity is uncertain, do not design for full side slip.
"Choose the load-carrying mechanism for a rock foundation before selecting design parameters" — state the decision rule about: If sockets are drilled by simple augers without attention to…::If sockets are drilled by simple augers without attention to cleanliness, modern parameters are inappropriate; only very conservative allowable loads are defensible.
What does "Design a rock socket for sidewall slip with the Rowe and Armitage chart procedure" produce?::An efficient socket design that mobilises non-brittle sidewall slip while keeping base response within its linear-elastic limit, typically saving significant socket length over elastic design.
Before relying on "Design a rock socket for sidewall slip with the Rowe and Armitage chart procedure" — what do you check?::Worked-example order of magnitude: 18 MN strength load on a 0.75 m socket gave L/D ~6.3 with settlement ~7 mm, versus L/D ~9.2 elastically. • Design constrained by the governing criterion identified (in the example, the base linearity limit, not ULS or SLS).
"Design a rock socket for sidewall slip with the Rowe and Armitage chart procedure" — state the decision rule about: This is the author's recommended design tool: chart-based, f…::This is the author's recommended design tool: chart-based, fast, and transparent about geometric and geotechnical sensitivities.
"Design a rock socket for sidewall slip with the Rowe and Armitage chart procedure" — state the decision rule about: Non-brittle slip requires R2+ roughness; the elasto-plastic …::Non-brittle slip requires R2+ roughness; the elasto-plastic (purely cohesive interface) assumption is safe only then.
What does "Design prestressed anchor bond zones in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Ashfield Shale from proof-test-based values" produce?::An anchor bond length designed on proven (proof-test) average bond stresses rather than on an unmeasurable 'ultimate bond strength', with every production anchor verified by proof loading.
Before relying on "Design prestressed anchor bond zones in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Ashfield Shale from proof-test-based values" — what do you check?::Diamond-cored holes flagged: generalised roughness assumptions do not apply to them. • Importance-category and geotechnical reduction factors from AS 5100.3 / AS 4678 reconciled (the paper notes the two codes conflict). • Creep acceptance criteria defined per current testing standards (EN ISO 22477-5 direction).
"Design prestressed anchor bond zones in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Ashfield Shale from proof-test-based values" — state the decision rule about: If more capacity is needed than a ~4 m bond length provides,…::If more capacity is needed than a ~4 m bond length provides, use a single-bore multiple-anchor system rather than lengthening the bond.
"Design prestressed anchor bond zones in Hawkesbury Sandstone and Ashfield Shale from proof-test-based values" — state the decision rule about: Do not transfer compression-socket side-shear values (tau = …::Do not transfer compression-socket side-shear values (tau = alpha beta UCS with alpha ~0.2) directly to anchors: Poisson effects reverse, L/D is 20-50 instead of 1-6, and there is no end-bearing backu
What does "Estimate lateral response of a rock socket with the Carter and Kulhawy elastic solutions" produce?::Elastic lateral displacement and head rotation estimates for a laterally loaded rock socket, with the shaft correctly categorised as flexible, rigid or intermediate, and honest treatment of the weak state of ultimate lateral capacity methods.
Before relying on "Estimate lateral response of a rock socket with the Carter and Kulhawy elastic solutions" — what do you check?::Flexible/rigid classification verified before choosing equations. • G* computed with the specified Poisson adjustment, not raw shear modulus.
"Estimate lateral response of a rock socket with the Carter and Kulhawy elastic solutions" — state the decision rule about: Solutions for laterally loaded piles in soil do not cover sh…::Solutions for laterally loaded piles in soil do not cover short stiff sockets in rock; do not extrapolate soil methods.
"Estimate lateral response of a rock socket with the Carter and Kulhawy elastic solutions" — state the decision rule about: If lateral loading is a serious design driver, expect to sup…::If lateral loading is a serious design driver, expect to supplement closed forms with finite element analysis (as done for the Sydney Monorail).
What does "Estimate pile capacity directly from SPT N values using published direct methods and reconcile them" produce?::Preliminary unit base and shaft resistance estimates from SPT-based direct methods (Meyerhof 1976; Bazaraa & Kurkur 1986; Decourt 1995; a geometric-mean N method), applied with the correct N-averaging zones and pile-type coefficients.
Before relying on "Estimate pile capacity directly from SPT N values using published direct methods and reconcile them" — what do you check?::N values corrected (energy, and overburden where the method assumes it) per the original method's convention. • Averaging windows scaled by the actual pile diameter.
"Estimate pile capacity directly from SPT N values using published direct methods and reconcile them" — state the decision rule about: Bored piles take substantially lower coefficients than drive…::Bored piles take substantially lower coefficients than driven piles in every method; never reuse driven-pile coefficients for bored piles.
"Estimate pile capacity directly from SPT N values using published direct methods and reconcile them" — state the decision rule about: Method-to-method scatter is expected; a wide spread signals …::Method-to-method scatter is expected; a wide spread signals that direct SPT methods alone are insufficient for the site.
What does "Estimate socket side shear from unconfined compressive strength with roughness and mass-stiffness corrections" produce?::A peak average side-shear resistance for a rock socket derived from tau = alpha x beta x qu, with geology-specific alpha and a modulus-ratio reduction, instead of a generic worldwide best-fit value.
Before relying on "Estimate socket side shear from unconfined compressive strength with roughness and mass-stiffness corrections" — what do you check?::Roughness at least R2 confirmed to justify non-brittle plastic behaviour. • beta consistent with the defect-controlled mass modulus actually adopted elsewhere in the design.
"Estimate socket side shear from unconfined compressive strength with roughness and mass-stiffness corrections" — state the decision rule about: Smeared or bentonite-cast sockets plot far below the clean-s…::Smeared or bentonite-cast sockets plot far below the clean-socket trend; do not use clean-socket alpha values for them.
"Estimate socket side shear from unconfined compressive strength with roughness and mass-stiffness corrections" — state the decision rule about: Where site or geology-specific data exist, they override wor…::Where site or geology-specific data exist, they override worldwide correlations.
What does "Inspect bored pile sockets for sidewall smear and base cleanliness before certifying design assumptions" produce?::A socket confirmed (or rejected) as meeting the cleanliness and roughness conditions that modern high-capacity side-shear and end-bearing design values assume.
Before relying on "Inspect bored pile sockets for sidewall smear and base cleanliness before certifying design assumptions" — what do you check?::Sidewall substantially free of crushed/smeared material; base debris within design limits. • Rock class at founding level matches design assumption. • NSW confined-space requirements (harness, breathing apparatus, crane licence for lowering personnel) satisfied for manned descent.
"Inspect bored pile sockets for sidewall smear and base cleanliness before certifying design assumptions" — state the decision rule about: Piles that cannot be inspected (method precludes descent or …::Piles that cannot be inspected (method precludes descent or camera access) must not be designed with the high side-shear and end-bearing parameters of the referenced methods.
"Inspect bored pile sockets for sidewall smear and base cleanliness before certifying design assumptions" — state the decision rule about: Piles formed under drilling mud should not normally use para…::Piles formed under drilling mud should not normally use parameters applicable to piles formed dry or under water.
What does "Select an axial design method for a rock socket: elastic, side-slip, or non-linear" produce?::A justified choice among the three accepted socket design families (elastic; Rowe & Armitage side-slip; non-linear/ROCKET-type), matched to construction quality, data availability and whether sidewall slip may be mobilised.
Before relying on "Select an axial design method for a rock socket: elastic, side-slip, or non-linear" — what do you check?::Same mass modulus basis used consistently across side shear, settlement and load-sharing calculations. • ROCKET results checked for its computational truncation quirks (displacement capped at half the roughness chord length; chord lengths limited to 10% of diameter
"Select an axial design method for a rock socket: elastic, side-slip, or non-linear" — state the decision rule about: Sockets needing base resistance require full sidewall slip; …::Sockets needing base resistance require full sidewall slip; all the safety margin then sits in end bearing.
"Select an axial design method for a rock socket: elastic, side-slip, or non-linear" — state the decision rule about: R2 or better roughness is required for the non-brittle (elas…::R2 or better roughness is required for the non-brittle (elasto-plastic) sidewall assumption underpinning the slip methods.
What does "Select class-based end bearing, shaft adhesion and modulus design values for Sydney sandstone and shale" produce?::Ultimate and serviceability end-bearing pressures, ultimate shaft adhesion and typical mass modulus chosen by rock class for limit state design of pads and sockets, with boundary-footing adjustments where needed.
Before relying on "Select class-based end bearing, shaft adhesion and modulus design values for Sydney sandstone and shale" — what do you check?::Class assignment satisfies all three criteria (strength, defect spacing, seams). • Load-displacement linearity assumption valid up to the serviceability values used. • Adhesion only claimed where inspection confirms cleanliness and roughness.
"Select class-based end bearing, shaft adhesion and modulus design values for Sydney sandstone and shale" — state the decision rule about: End bearing is usually settlement-controlled, so arbitrary n…::End bearing is usually settlement-controlled, so arbitrary nominal boundary reductions are illogical; use the settlement-equalising 60% guideline or explicit analysis.
"Select class-based end bearing, shaft adhesion and modulus design values for Sydney sandstone and shale" — state the decision rule about: Pick modulus within the class range according to whether the…::Pick modulus within the class range according to whether the rock sits at the upper or lower bound of the class.
What does "Size a rock socket with the elastic chart method when sidewall slip is not permitted" produce?::A conservative socket length and diameter satisfying strength and serviceability limit states with all behaviour kept elastic, using the load-proportion and settlement-influence charts.
Before relying on "Size a rock socket with the elastic chart method when sidewall slip is not permitted" — what do you check?::Chart axes and Ep/Er curve selection consistent with the assessed moduli. • Settlement computed with the serviceability load, not S*.
"Size a rock socket with the elastic chart method when sidewall slip is not permitted" — state the decision rule about: Adopt this method when sidewall slip must not occur, or when…::Adopt this method when sidewall slip must not occur, or when end-bearing capacity is too uncertain to rely on; expect materially longer sockets than slip-based design (6.9 m vs 4.7 m in the worked exa
"Size a rock socket with the elastic chart method when sidewall slip is not permitted" — state the decision rule about: Charts shown assume uniform rock modulus; use the extended c…::Charts shown assume uniform rock modulus; use the extended chart sets for differing base/shaft moduli or recessed sockets.
What does "Specify construction and supervision requirements for socketed bored piles in Sydney rock" produce?::Contract documents that lock in the workmanship (cleanliness, roughness, concreting, inspection regime) required for modern high-capacity socket design values to be valid.
Before relying on "Specify construction and supervision requirements for socketed bored piles in Sydney rock" — what do you check?::Specification clauses are consistent with the actual design assumptions (roughness class, cleanliness limits, inspection method). • Contractual independence of the inspector from the piling contractor. • Reporting items align with the paper's Clause A6.2 list.
"Specify construction and supervision requirements for socketed bored piles in Sydney rock" — state the decision rule about: If tremie placement under water is proposed, only accept it …::If tremie placement under water is proposed, only accept it where the engineer is satisfied socket cleanliness is achieved and the contractor has proven underwater concreting experience.
"Specify construction and supervision requirements for socketed bored piles in Sydney rock" — state the decision rule about: If high side-shear/end-bearing values are not economically a…::If high side-shear/end-bearing values are not economically achievable through the specified workmanship, do not invoke them in design.

notes.body:
# Flashcards - Rock mechanics

#flashcards/rock-mechanics

88 cards generated from the 22 rock mechanics skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Assess the onset depth of rockburst and spalling in a tunnel" produce?::An estimate of the depth below which brittle problems (rockburst, spalling) can be expected for a tunnel in strong rock, from an empirical crack-initiation stress and the overburden gradient
Before relying on "Assess the onset depth of rockburst and spalling in a tunnel" — what do you check?::Track units through the calculation: MPa to kPa (times 10^3) before dividing by unit weight in kN/m3 to get metres • Compare the computed initiation stress with the case-study scatter in the source chart rather than treating the line as exact
"Assess the onset depth of rockburst and spalling in a tunnel" — state the decision rule about: If the rock is weak or heavily jointed, this brittle-failure…::If the rock is weak or heavily jointed, this brittle-failure screening does not apply — the failure mode will be different
"Assess the onset depth of rockburst and spalling in a tunnel" — state the decision rule about: Tunnels planned shallower than the computed threshold depth …::Tunnels planned shallower than the computed threshold depth are not expected to see spalling/rockburst for that rock strength
What does "Assign a Geological Strength Index (GSI) to a rock mass in the field" produce?::A GSI value expressed as a range (e.g. 45 plus or minus 5) for an exposed rock mass, from a joint assessment of blockiness/structure and joint surface conditions on the GSI chart
Before relying on "Assign a Geological Strength Index (GSI) to a rock mass in the field" — what do you check?::Structure and surface-condition assessments were made independently before combining on the chart • The reported range acknowledges the chart's resolution rather than implying precision
"Assign a Geological Strength Index (GSI) to a rock mass in the field" — state the decision rule about: More weathering generally means both more joints (structure …::More weathering generally means both more joints (structure degrades) and worse surface condition — the assessment tends to move diagonally on the chart
"Assign a Geological Strength Index (GSI) to a rock mass in the field" — state the decision rule about: GSI below about 20 is very difficult to assess reliably; the…::GSI below about 20 is very difficult to assess reliably; the chart also works poorly for laminated/sheared/disintegrated structures
What does "Calculate rock mass rating (RMR) with tunnel drive-direction adjustments" produce?::A summed RMR value, rock mass class (A-E), and tunnel-adjusted rating for a described rock mass, including the groundwater rating derived from pore-pressure-to-stress ratio
Before relying on "Calculate rock mass rating (RMR) with tunnel drive-direction adjustments" — what do you check?::Confirm the sum uses all five components exactly once before applying the tunnel adjustment • Confirm water pressure and stress use consistent units (kPa) before taking the ratio • Confirm the three-digit orientation number was treated as dip direction and the two-digit as dip
"Calculate rock mass rating (RMR) with tunnel drive-direction adjustments" — state the decision rule about: A strength of 75 MPa must be UCS, not point load index — poi…::A strength of 75 MPa must be UCS, not point load index — point load values cannot be that high
"Calculate rock mass rating (RMR) with tunnel drive-direction adjustments" — state the decision rule about: If a joint description straddles two table boxes, take the a…::If a joint description straddles two table boxes, take the average of the two ratings using engineering judgment
What does "Classify a rock mass with the Q-system for tunnel design" produce?::A Q rating for a tunnel rock mass computed from six factors, positioning the mass on the quality scale used for empirical tunnel support decisions
Before relying on "Classify a rock mass with the Q-system for tunnel design" — what do you check?::Confirm each of the six factors was sourced from the description rather than defaulted • Recompute the three quotients separately to see which block (block size, shear strength, stress) controls the rating • Compare your Q against an independent assessor's; values should agree within a band
"Classify a rock mass with the Q-system for tunnel design" — state the decision rule about: If strength is supplied as point load index, convert to UCS …::If strength is supplied as point load index, convert to UCS before the SRF ratio — do not use point load index directly
"Classify a rock mass with the Q-system for tunnel design" — state the decision rule about: When no unit weight is given, use the average-rock assumptio…::When no unit weight is given, use the average-rock assumption of 0.027 MPa per metre depth for vertical stress
What does "Classify rock material strength and weathering grade by field index tests on core" produce?::A field strength grade (extremely low to extremely high) and weathering grade (fresh to extremely weathered) assigned to rock core using hand, thumb, and geological-pick index tests
Before relying on "Classify rock material strength and weathering grade by field index tests on core" — what do you check?::Strength grade and weathering grade assigned to the same interval should be mutually consistent
"Classify rock material strength and weathering grade by field index tests on core" — state the decision rule about: Weathering grade is a good proxy indicator of strength: heav…::Weathering grade is a good proxy indicator of strength: heavily weathered implies weak, fresh or slightly weathered implies high strength
"Classify rock material strength and weathering grade by field index tests on core" — state the decision rule about: If material is so weathered it behaves as soil, log and asse…::If material is so weathered it behaves as soil, log and assess it as soil, not rock
What does "Conduct a scanline discontinuity survey of a rock face" produce?::A field record, per discontinuity along a scanline, of type, orientation, persistence, aperture/infill, roughness, and spacing/count — the inputs needed by rock mass classification systems
Before relying on "Conduct a scanline discontinuity survey of a rock face" — what do you check?::Every discontinuity crossing the scanline has an entry — none skipped • Count along the line and measured spacings are mutually consistent
"Conduct a scanline discontinuity survey of a rock face" — state the decision rule about: Spacing and discontinuity count are the priority measurement…::Spacing and discontinuity count are the priority measurements: they feed classification systems and indicate rock mass strength
"Conduct a scanline discontinuity survey of a rock face" — state the decision rule about: Record infill material type whenever a joint is not clean — …::Record infill material type whenever a joint is not clean — soil infill (clay, sand) changes behaviour
What does "Derive Hoek-Brown rock mass strength from triaxial lab data in RocData" produce?::Rock mass strength parameters (rock mass UCS, tensile strength, and equivalent Mohr-Coulomb cohesion and friction angle) for a tunnel, fitted from triaxial test data and scaled by GSI and disturbance
Before relying on "Derive Hoek-Brown rock mass strength from triaxial lab data in RocData" — what do you check?::Compare fitted mi with published typical values for the rock type (about 17.8 fitted vs typical basalt values in the example) • Run a GSI sensitivity sweep to see how strongly discontinuities control the rock mass strength before fixing a single value
"Derive Hoek-Brown rock mass strength from triaxial lab data in RocData" — state the decision rule about: Use D = 0 only when excavation genuinely causes minimal dist…::Use D = 0 only when excavation genuinely causes minimal disturbance (e.g. TBM); blast damage pushes D toward 1
"Derive Hoek-Brown rock mass strength from triaxial lab data in RocData" — state the decision rule about: GSI = 100 means discontinuities do not reduce strength and r…::GSI = 100 means discontinuities do not reduce strength and rock mass UCS equals the intact UCS; lowering GSI collapses strength rapidly (in the demo, dropping GSI from 85 to about 50 cut rock mass UCS
What does "Derive friction angle and cohesion from rock triaxial data using the Mohr-Coulomb criterion in principal-stress form" produce?::Friction angle, cohesion, and unconfined compressive strength for a rock from multiple triaxial tests, via a linear fit of sigma-1 at failure against sigma-3
Before relying on "Derive friction angle and cohesion from rock triaxial data using the Mohr-Coulomb criterion in principal-stress form" — what do you check?::Slope and intercept both come from the same fitted envelope • Angle arithmetic checked: sqrt of slope, then arctan, then subtract 45, then multiply by 2 • Back-substitute phi and c to confirm the envelope reproduces the unconfined intercept
"Derive friction angle and cohesion from rock triaxial data using the Mohr-Coulomb criterion in principal-stress form" — state the decision rule about: Take sigma-c from the fit through all tests, not from the si…::Take sigma-c from the fit through all tests, not from the single unconfined (sigma-3 = 0) test — six points give a more accurate value than one (the lone unconfined test read 25 MPa vs the fitted 31.6
"Derive friction angle and cohesion from rock triaxial data using the Mohr-Coulomb criterion in principal-stress form" — state the decision rule about: For soils the shear-stress form of Mohr-Coulomb is used inst…::For soils the shear-stress form of Mohr-Coulomb is used instead; the principal-stress form is the rock convention
What does "Describe discontinuities in rock core using standard symbol sets" produce?::A complete per-discontinuity description (type, inclination, roughness, aperture, infill/coating) matching the symbol strings found on borehole logs
Before relying on "Describe discontinuities in rock core using standard symbol sets" — what do you check?::Each logged discontinuity carries depth, type, inclination, roughness, aperture, and surface/infill condition — no field left blank • Filling thickness recorded whenever aperture is 'filled'
"Describe discontinuities in rock core using standard symbol sets" — state the decision rule about: Stain vs veneer vs coating is decided by the thickness of th…::Stain vs veneer vs coating is decided by the thickness of the discoloration/mineral layer (stain = discoloration only, veneer < 1 mm, coating > 1 mm)
"Describe discontinuities in rock core using standard symbol sets" — state the decision rule about: Roughness is always assessed as waviness class first, textur…::Roughness is always assessed as waviness class first, texture second
What does "Estimate RQD from volumetric joint count, joint spacing, and joint frequency" produce?::An RQD estimate from field joint surveys (without core) via the volumetric joint count correlation, plus conversions between joint count, spacing, and frequency
Before relying on "Estimate RQD from volumetric joint count, joint spacing, and joint frequency" — what do you check?::Each set's contribution to Jv is count divided by its own measured length, not raw counts added together • Spacing converted to metres before taking the reciprocal for frequency
"Estimate RQD from volumetric joint count, joint spacing, and joint frequency" — state the decision rule about: The correlation works well at high RQD; below roughly RQD 20…::The correlation works well at high RQD; below roughly RQD 20 it may not perform well — treat low-end results with caution
"Estimate RQD from volumetric joint count, joint spacing, and joint frequency" — state the decision rule about: These are empirical estimates for classification-system inpu…::These are empirical estimates for classification-system inputs (e.g. RMR), not replacements for measured core RQD
What does "Estimate joint shear strength with Barton's criterion for a tunnel or slope" produce?::The shear strength of a jointed rock mass at a given depth, computed from joint roughness, joint wall strength, residual friction angle and normal stress
Before relying on "Estimate joint shear strength with Barton's criterion for a tunnel or slope" — what do you check?::Confirm each input has its own basis: JRC from surface profiling, JCS from Schmidt hammer, residual friction angle from tilt test or a documented assumption • Verify unit conversions: density in g/cm3 to unit weight in kN/m3, then stress in kPa converted to MPa
"Estimate joint shear strength with Barton's criterion for a tunnel or slope" — state the decision rule about: The greater the normal stress, the greater the computed shea…::The greater the normal stress, the greater the computed shear strength — always evaluate at the actual depth of the block or opening
"Estimate joint shear strength with Barton's criterion for a tunnel or slope" — state the decision rule about: Porous, water-bearing rocks such as sandstone need the groun…::Porous, water-bearing rocks such as sandstone need the groundwater check; a few tight joints in fresh granite may justify assuming dry conditions
What does "Estimate jointed rock shear strength with the Barton-Bandis criterion in RocData" produce?::Equivalent cohesion and friction angle for a jointed rock mass, plus shear strength at a specified depth, for use in slope stability analysis
Before relying on "Estimate jointed rock shear strength with the Barton-Bandis criterion in RocData" — what do you check?::Confirm the shear stress-normal stress curve starts at the origin as expected for a jointed criterion • Sanity-check the fitted friction angle against the input residual friction angle and roughness
"Estimate jointed rock shear strength with the Barton-Bandis criterion in RocData" — state the decision rule about: No shear box data available: use published residual friction…::No shear box data available: use published residual friction angles for the lithology rather than guessing
"Estimate jointed rock shear strength with the Barton-Bandis criterion in RocData" — state the decision rule about: JRC estimated visually from the Barton chart is acceptable; …::JRC estimated visually from the Barton chart is acceptable; a 2-point difference in JRC has only a small effect on the result
What does "Estimate rock mass friction angle and cohesion from GSI-mi charts" produce?::Quick chart-based estimates of rock mass friction angle and cohesion suitable for preliminary slope stability analysis, without running software
Before relying on "Estimate rock mass friction angle and cohesion from GSI-mi charts" — what do you check?::Sanity-check the inputs against the geology: a UCS far below the fresh-rock typical range (e.g. basalt at 14 MPa when fresh basalt often exceeds 100 MPa) togeth • Cross-check chart estimates against software such as RocData if available
"Estimate rock mass friction angle and cohesion from GSI-mi charts" — state the decision rule about: Reading the friction angle to the nearest degree is enough; …::Reading the friction angle to the nearest degree is enough; a 1-2 degree spread between readers is acceptable
"Estimate rock mass friction angle and cohesion from GSI-mi charts" — state the decision rule about: Small differences in the cohesion ratio read from the chart …::Small differences in the cohesion ratio read from the chart are acceptable; the method is an estimate, not a precise value
What does "Estimate slope rock mass strength in RocData from reference tables without lab data" produce?::Rock mass strength parameters (rock mass UCS, tensile strength, cohesion and friction angle) for an excavated slope, built entirely from reference tables when no laboratory tests exist
Before relying on "Estimate slope rock mass strength in RocData from reference tables without lab data" — what do you check?::Compare the entered UCS with the table range for the rock type as a plausibility check • Confirm the density-to-unit-weight conversion before entering it • Note how far rock mass UCS falls below intact UCS — a large drop is expected for very blocky rock and signals that intact values must not be used in slope desig
"Estimate slope rock mass strength in RocData from reference tables without lab data" — state the decision rule about: Reference-table estimation is acceptable for preliminary wor…::Reference-table estimation is acceptable for preliminary work when no lab data exist, but it is explicitly an estimate, not precise data
"Estimate slope rock mass strength in RocData from reference tables without lab data" — state the decision rule about: A few points of GSI disagreement between assessors is tolera…::A few points of GSI disagreement between assessors is tolerable; document the descriptive basis (structure and surface condition) behind the pick
What does "Estimate the diggability index and class for weathered rock" produce?::A diggability index and class that indicates how easily a weathered rock mass can be dug and guides equipment and cost planning
Before relying on "Estimate the diggability index and class for weathered rock" — what do you check?::Confirm spacing values were converted from fracture counts correctly (spacing = 1 / joints per metre) • Confirm every applicable row was scored, including bedding only where bedding planes exist
"Estimate the diggability index and class for weathered rock" — state the decision rule about: Either UCS or point load index can enter the strength row — …::Either UCS or point load index can enter the strength row — use whichever was measured
"Estimate the diggability index and class for weathered rock" — state the decision rule about: When a value sits exactly on a category boundary, take the s…::When a value sits exactly on a category boundary, take the slightly more adverse category
What does "Fit Hoek-Brown intact-rock parameters (sigma-ci, mi, tensile strength) from triaxial test data" produce?::Unconfined compressive strength, the material constant mi, and an estimated tensile strength for intact rock, obtained by linearising the intact-rock special case of the Hoek-Brown criterion against triaxial results
Before relying on "Fit Hoek-Brown intact-rock parameters (sigma-ci, mi, tensile strength) from triaxial test data" — what do you check?::Intercept and slope are taken from the fit through all tests, not from any single test • Back-substitute the fitted sigma-ci and mi into the criterion and confirm the test points are reasonably reproduced
"Fit Hoek-Brown intact-rock parameters (sigma-ci, mi, tensile strength) from triaxial test data" — state the decision rule about: s = 1 and alpha = 0.5 apply only to intact rock (lab-scale s…::s = 1 and alpha = 0.5 apply only to intact rock (lab-scale samples or exposures without discontinuities); jointed rock masses need the generalized criterion with mb, s, alpha from rock mass characteri
"Fit Hoek-Brown intact-rock parameters (sigma-ci, mi, tensile strength) from triaxial test data" — state the decision rule about: Harder rock geology gives higher mi — mi varies with rock ty…::Harder rock geology gives higher mi — mi varies with rock type
What does "Interpret the rock-core section of a borehole log" produce?::Correct reading of a real borehole log's rock columns — weathering grade, strength grade, fracture spacing, RQD, core recovery, and the per-depth discontinuity records — and recognition of where soil logging conventions stop and rock conventions begin
Before relying on "Interpret the rock-core section of a borehole log" — what do you check?::Fracture spacing, RQD and core recovery tell a consistent story for each interval • Every discontinuity record has a depth and a full symbol string
"Interpret the rock-core section of a borehole log" — state the decision rule about: Absence of weathering/strength/spacing data over an interval…::Absence of weathering/strength/spacing data over an interval signals soil-type material, not missing data
"Interpret the rock-core section of a borehole log" — state the decision rule about: High RQD plus wide fracture spacing plus full recovery toget…::High RQD plus wide fracture spacing plus full recovery together indicate good quality rock mass; treat inconsistencies between them as a prompt to re-examine the log
What does "Plot and manage discontinuity data in Dips" produce?::A correctly configured Dips file with discontinuity orientations plotted as poles or great circles, extra attribute columns, and summary charts, ready for kinematic analysis
Before relying on "Plot and manage discontinuity data in Dips" — what do you check?::Spot-check the plot: a near-vertical entry must fall near the perimeter side away from the centre and a near-horizontal one near the centre (for poles this rela • Open a library tutorial file to compare structure when unsure how attribute columns should look
"Plot and manage discontinuity data in Dips" — state the decision rule about: Set the orientation format before entering data — mixing for…::Set the orientation format before entering data — mixing formats silently corrupts every subsequent analysis
"Plot and manage discontinuity data in Dips" — state the decision rule about: Use pole plots for large data sets (hundreds of points) and …::Use pole plots for large data sets (hundreds of points) and great circles when a few individual planes need to be seen
What does "Plot discontinuity great circles and poles on a stereonet by hand" produce?::Hand-drawn great circles (and poles) on tracing paper representing measured dip / dip-direction pairs from a field discontinuity survey
Before relying on "Plot discontinuity great circles and poles on a stereonet by hand" — what do you check?::Verify the tracing returned to the original orientation using the marked cardinal points before reading results • Verify the dip count started at 0 on the perimeter, not at the centre (for great circles); the pole count runs from the centre
"Plot discontinuity great circles and poles on a stereonet by hand" — state the decision rule about: Three digits in an orientation pair always denote dip direct…::Three digits in an orientation pair always denote dip direction; the remaining value is dip
"Plot discontinuity great circles and poles on a stereonet by hand" — state the decision rule about: Use a pole (one point) instead of a great circle when a comp…::Use a pole (one point) instead of a great circle when a compact representation of many joints is needed
What does "Read dip and dip direction from stereonet great circles and poles" produce?::Correct interpretation of discontinuity dip magnitude and dip direction from either great-circle or pole representations on a stereonet
Before relying on "Read dip and dip direction from stereonet great circles and poles" — what do you check?::Convert between representations as a self-check: the pole and its great circle must give the same dip and dip direction • Confirm the answer against the perimeter azimuth graduations (0/90/180/270)
"Read dip and dip direction from stereonet great circles and poles" — state the decision rule about: Great circle near centre = steep; pole near centre = shallow…::Great circle near centre = steep; pole near centre = shallow — always state which representation you are reading before applying the closeness rule
"Read dip and dip direction from stereonet great circles and poles" — state the decision rule about: Two poles at the same azimuth but different radii represent …::Two poles at the same azimuth but different radii represent planes with the same dip direction but different dips
What does "Screen a tunnel for squeezing using the rock-mass-strength to in-situ-stress ratio" produce?::An estimate of expected tunnel strain and squeezing severity class for a tunnel in weak rock, from an empirical strength/stress chart
Before relying on "Screen a tunnel for squeezing using the rock-mass-strength to in-situ-stress ratio" — what do you check?::Confirm unit consistency: 0.027 times depth in metres yields MPa directly • Confirm the strength value used is rock mass strength, not intact rock strength
"Screen a tunnel for squeezing using the rock-mass-strength to in-situ-stress ratio" — state the decision rule about: Low strength/stress ratios mean high strain: the lower the r…::Low strength/stress ratios mean high strain: the lower the ratio, the more severe the squeezing class
"Screen a tunnel for squeezing using the rock-mass-strength to in-situ-stress ratio" — state the decision rule about: Very severe classes flag risk of local tunnel collapse and d…::Very severe classes flag risk of local tunnel collapse and demand support design attention
What does "Select a rock excavation method (dig, rip or blast) from a strength-spacing chart" produce?::The most economical open-excavation method for a rock mass, chosen from point load strength and discontinuity spacing
Before relying on "Select a rock excavation method (dig, rip or blast) from a strength-spacing chart" — what do you check?::Verify axis scales (both often logarithmic) before plotting • Confirm the spacing used is an average from mapping, not a single measurement
"Select a rock excavation method (dig, rip or blast) from a strength-spacing chart" — state the decision rule about: Prefer a site- or rock-specific UCS to point-load correlatio…::Prefer a site- or rock-specific UCS to point-load correlation over the general factor of 24 when one has been established
"Select a rock excavation method (dig, rip or blast) from a strength-spacing chart" — state the decision rule about: Method cost and complexity escalate from digging to ripping …::Method cost and complexity escalate from digging to ripping to blasting — the chart zone drives plant selection and project cost planning

Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here. Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not verification. Numbers still come from the source. treating the line as exact "Assess the onset depth of rockburst and spalling in a tunnel" — state the decision rule about: If the rock is weak or heavily jointed, this brittle failure…::If the rock is weak or heavily jointed, this brittle failure screening does not apply — the failure mode will be different "Assess the onset depth of rockburst and spalling in a tunnel" — state the decision rule about: Tunnels planned shallower than the computed threshold depth …::Tunnels planned shallower than the computed threshold depth are not expected to see spalling/rockburst for that rock strength What does "Assign a Geological Strength Index (GSI) to a rock mass in the field" produce?::A GSI value expressed as a range (e.g. 45 plus or minus 5) for an exposed rock mass, from a joint assessment of blockiness/structure and joint surface conditions on the GSI chart Before relying on "Assign a Geological Strength Index (GSI) to a rock mass in the field" — what do you check?::Structure and surface condition assessments were made independently before combining on the chart • The reported range acknowledges the chart's resolution rather than implying precision "Assign a Geological Strength Index (GSI) to a rock mass in the field" — state the decision rule about: More weathering generally means both more joints (structure …::More weathering generally means both more joints (structure degrades) and worse surface condition — the assessment tends to move diagonally on the chart "Assign a Geological Strength Index (GSI) to a rock mass in the field" — state the decision rule about: GSI below about 20 is very difficult to assess reliably; the…::GSI below about 20 is very difficult to assess reliably; the chart also works poorly for laminated/sheared/disintegrated structures What does "Calculate rock mass rating (RMR) with tunnel drive direction adjustments" produce?::A summed RMR value, rock mass class (A E), and tunnel adjusted rating for a described rock mass, including the groundwater rating derived from pore pressure to stress ratio Before relying on "Calculate rock mass rating (RMR) with tunnel drive direction adjustments" — what do you check?::Confirm the sum uses all five components exactly once before applying the tunnel adjustment • Confirm water pressure and stress use consistent units (kPa) before taking the ratio • Confirm the three digit orientation number was treated as dip direction and the two digit as dip "Calculate rock mass rating (RMR) with tunnel drive direction adjustments" — state the decision rule about: A strength of 75 MPa must be weathered) assigned to rock core using hand, thumb, and geological pick index tests Before relying on "Classify rock material strength and weathering grade by field index tests on core" — what do you asse…::If material is so weathered it behaves as soil, log and assess it as soil, not rock What does "Conduct a scanline discontinuity survey of a rock face" produce?::A field record, per discontinuity along a scanline, of type, orientation, persistence, aperture/infill, roughness, and spacing/count — the inputs needed by rock mass classification systems Before relying on "Conduct a metre) • Confirm every applicable row was scored, including bedding only where bedding planes exist "Estimate the diggability index and class for weathered rock" — state the decision rule about: Either UCS or point load index can enter the strength row — …::Either UCS or point load index can enter the strength row — use whichever was measured "Estimate the diggability index and class for weathered rock" — state the decision rule about: When a value sits exactly on a category boundary, take the s…::When a value sits exactly on a category boundary, take the slightly more adverse category What does "Fit Hoek Brown intact rock parameters (sigma ci, mi, tensile strength) from triaxial test data" produce?::Unconfined compressive strength, the material constant mi, and an estimated tensile strength for intact rock, obtained by linearising the intact rock special case of the Hoek Brown criterion against triaxial results Before relying on "Fit Hoek Brown intact rock parameters (sigma ci, mi, tensile strength) from triaxial test data" — what do you check?::Intercept and slope are taken from the fit through all tests, not from any single test • Back substitute the fitted sigma ci and mi into the criterion and confirm the test points are reasonably reproduced "Fit Hoek Brown intact rock parameters (sigma ci, mi, tensile strength) from triaxial test data" — state the decision rule about: s = 1 and alpha = 0.5 apply only to intact rock (lab scale s…::s = 1 and alpha = 0.5 apply only to intact rock (lab scale samples or exposures without discontinuities); jointed rock masses need the generalized criterion with mb, s, alpha from rock mass characteri "Fit Hoek Brown intact rock parameters (sigma ci, mi, tensile strength) from triaxial test data" — state the decision rule about: Harder rock geology gives higher mi — mi varies with rock ty…::Harder rock geology gives higher mi — mi varies with rock type What does "Interpret the rock core section of a borehole log" produce?::Correct reading of a real borehole log's rock columns — weathering grade, strength grade, fracture spacing, RQD, core recovery, and the per depth discontinuity records — and recognition of where soil logging conventions stop and rock conventions begin Before relying on "Interpret the rock core section of a borehole log" — what do you check?::Fracture spacing, RQD and core recovery tell a consistent story for each interval • Every discontinuity record has a depth and a full symbol string "Interpret the rock core section of a borehole log" — state the decision rule about: Absence of weathering/strength/spacing data over an interval…::Absence of weathering/strength/spacing data over an interval signals soil type material, not missing data "Interpret the rock core section of a borehole log" — state the decision rule about: High RQD plus wide fracture spacing plus full recovery toget…::High RQD plus wide fracture spacing plus full recovery together indicate good quality rock mass; treat inconsistencies between them as a prompt to re examine the log What does "Plot and manage discontinuity data in Dips" produce?::A correctly configured Dips file with discontinuity orientations plotted as poles or great circles, extra attribute columns, and summary charts, ready for kinematic analysis Before relying on "Plot and manage discontinuity data in Dips" — what do you check?::Spot check the plot: a near vertical entry must fall near the perimeter side away from the centre and a near horizontal one near the centre (for poles this rela • Open a library tutorial file to compare structure when unsure how attribute columns should look "Plot and manage discontinuity data in Dips" — state the decision rule about: Set the orientation format before entering data — mixing for…::Set the orientation format before entering data — mixing formats silently corrupts every subsequent analysis "Plot and manage discontinuity data in Dips" — state the decision rule about: Use pole plots for large data sets (hundreds of points) and …::Use pole plots for large data sets (hundreds of points) and great circles when a few individual planes need to be seen What does "Plot discontinuity great circles and poles on a stereonet by hand" produce?::Hand drawn great circles (and poles) on tracing paper representing measured dip / dip direction pairs from a field discontinuity survey Before relying on "Plot discontinuity great circles and poles on a stereonet by hand" — what do you check?::Verify the tracing returned to the original orientation using the marked cardinal points before reading results • Verify the dip count started at 0 on the perimeter, not at the centre (for great circles); the pole count runs from the centre "Plot discontinuity great circles and poles on a stereonet by hand" — state the decision rule about: Three digits in an orientation pair always denote dip direct…::Three digits in an orientation pair always denote dip direction; the remaining value is dip "Plot discontinuity great circles and poles on a stereonet by hand" — state the decision rule about: Use a pole (one point) instead of a great circle when a comp…::Use a pole (one point) instead of a great circle when a compact representation of many joints is needed What does "Read dip and dip direction from stereonet great circles and poles" produce?::Correct interpretation of discontinuity dip magnitude and dip direction from either great circle or pole representations on a stereonet Before relying on "Read dip and dip direction from stereonet great circles and poles" — what do you check?::Convert between representations as a self check: the pole and its great circle must give the same dip and dip direction • Confirm the answer against the perimeter azimuth graduations (0/90/180/270) "Read dip and dip direction from stereonet great circles and poles" — state the decision rule about: Great circle near centre = steep; pole near centre = shallow…::Great circle near centre = steep; pole near centre = shallow — always state which representation you are reading before applying the closeness rule "Read dip and dip direction from stereonet great circles and poles" — state the decision rule about: Two poles at the same azimuth but different radii represent …::Two poles at the same azimuth but different radii represent planes with the same dip direction but different dips What does "Screen a tunnel for squeezing using the rock mass strength to in situ stress ratio" produce?::An estimate of expected tunnel strain and squeezing severity class for a tunnel in weak rock, from an empirical strength/stress chart Before relying on "Screen a tunnel for squeezing using the rock mass strength to in situ stress ratio" — what do you check?::Confirm unit consistency: 0.027 times depth in metres yields MPa directly • Confirm the strength value used is rock mass strength, not intact rock strength "Screen a tunnel for squeezing using the rock mass strength to in situ stress ratio" — state the decision rule about: Low strength/stress ratios mean high strain: the lower the r…::Low strength/stress ratios mean high strain: the lower the ratio, the more severe the squeezing class "Screen a tunnel for squeezing using the rock mass strength to in situ stress ratio" — state the decision rule about: Very severe classes flag risk of local tunnel collapse and d…::Very severe classes flag risk of local tunnel collapse and demand support design attention What does "Select a rock excavation method (dig, rip or blast) from a strength spacing chart" produce?::The most economical open excavation method for a rock mass, chosen from point load strength and discontinuity spacing Before relying on "Select a rock excavation method (dig, rip or blast) from a strength spacing chart" — what do you check?::Verify axis scales (both often logarithmic) before plotting • Confirm the spacing used is an average from mapping, not a single measurement "Select a rock excavation method (dig, rip or blast) from a strength spacing chart" — state the decision rule about: Prefer a site or rock specific UCS to point load correlatio…::Prefer a site or rock specific UCS to point load correlation over the general factor of 24 when one has been established "Select a rock excavation method (dig, rip or blast) from a strength spacing chart" — state the decision rule about: Method cost and complexity escalate from digging to ripping …::Method cost and complexity escalate from digging to ripping to blasting — the chart zone drives plant selection and project cost planning Related Learning path Rock mechanics Learning loop
