notes.body:
# Flashcards - Salinity and aggressivity

#flashcards/salinity

60 cards generated from the 15 salinity and aggressivity skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Assess sodic soils and prescribe gypsum, lime and tillage treatment" produce?::A sodicity diagnosis (ESP-based) and a treatment plan (gypsum rate, lime blend, tillage discipline, ripping strategy) that restores structure, infiltration and drainage without creating new salinity problems.
Before relying on "Assess sodic soils and prescribe gypsum, lime and tillage treatment" — what do you check?::ESP computed from lab data, not inferred from dispersion score alone. • Untreated control strip retained for comparison. • pH (CaCl2) measured before choosing lime or blends. • Re-inspection scheduled (ripping/gypsum benefits fade in 2-3 years).
"Assess sodic soils and prescribe gypsum, lime and tillage treatment" — state the decision rule about: If the non-sodic topsoil is deeper than about 15-20 cm, a gy…::If the non-sodic topsoil is deeper than about 15-20 cm, a gypsum response is unlikely — the existing structure already supports growth; target subsoil constraints instead.
"Assess sodic soils and prescribe gypsum, lime and tillage treatment" — state the decision rule about: Gypsum works two ways (slightly raising soil-solution salini…::Gypsum works two ways (slightly raising soil-solution salinity to suppress swelling, and Ca-for-Na cation exchange); saline water mimics the first mechanism, but avoid saline irrigation as a fix — it 
What does "Classify site salinity and select concrete strength and cover for residential slabs and footings" produce?::A concrete grade and reinforcement cover matched to the site's ECe salinity class so slabs and footings achieve their design life in saline ground.
Before relying on "Classify site salinity and select concrete strength and cover for residential slabs and footings" — what do you check?::EC measurement method (EC1:5 vs ECe saturation extract) and conversion factors documented before classification. • Aggressivity classification cross-checked against AS 2159 exposure tables and the project spec. • Cover selections compatible with AS 2870 details for the chosen footing system.
"Classify site salinity and select concrete strength and cover for residential slabs and footings" — state the decision rule about: Treat the plastic membrane as an additional safeguard, not t…::Treat the plastic membrane as an additional safeguard, not the primary durability measure — codes permit 20 MPa on the basis of a perfect membrane, but specifying strength/cover for the actual exposur
"Classify site salinity and select concrete strength and cover for residential slabs and footings" — state the decision rule about: Because standard concrete grades step ~25% apart, small ECe …::Because standard concrete grades step ~25% apart, small ECe uncertainties rarely change the selected grade — do not over-refine the salinity estimate for this purpose.
What does "Control concrete placement, compaction and curing for durability in saline ground" produce?::Site concreting practice (water control, compaction method, curing duration, crack control, membrane installation) that delivers the low permeability the durability design assumes.
Before relying on "Control concrete placement, compaction and curing for durability in saline ground" — what do you check?::Batch dockets confirm no site water addition beyond specification. • Vibration continued until air release ceased; no honeycombing at stripped faces. • Curing regime documented per surface, including edges. • Membrane integrity (laps, penetrations, punctures) inspected immediately before pouring.
"Control concrete placement, compaction and curing for durability in saline ground" — state the decision rule about: Permeability, not strength per se, governs durability — stre…::Permeability, not strength per se, governs durability — strength is only an indicator; therefore prioritise water-cement ratio, compaction and curing over chasing grade alone.
"Control concrete placement, compaction and curing for durability in saline ground" — state the decision rule about: In saline ground a weak, poorly cured surface skin defeats t…::In saline ground a weak, poorly cured surface skin defeats the specified cover; if curing was compromised, treat the effective cover as reduced when assessing acceptability.
What does "Design a soil and groundwater sampling program for salinity testing" produce?::A defensible sampling regime (locations, depths, sample handling, lab selection) that yields reliable salinity, sodicity and corrosivity data per landform unit.
Before relying on "Design a soil and groundwater sampling program for salinity testing" — what do you check?::Every sample clearly labelled with site number and depth interval; lab report documents methods, equipment and units. • Laboratory holds NATA or ISO 9000 accreditation for the tests used. • Groundwater chemistry compared across bores/depths to test whether waters share a common source. • New profile data lodged in the public soil database (SALIS in NSW) for future reuse.
"Design a soil and groundwater sampling program for salinity testing" — state the decision rule about: Number of lab profiles: use the ranges in Table 1 column 6 o…::Number of lab profiles: use the ranges in Table 1 column 6 of the booklet (p. 6) tied to mapping scale, and weigh the per-profile lab cost (2002 figure: about $150/sample, i.e. ~$1050 for a 7-depth pr
"Design a soil and groundwater sampling program for salinity testing" — state the decision rule about: Use field test kits to screen which properties justify full …::Use field test kits to screen which properties justify full laboratory analysis.
What does "Design and rehabilitate road pavements in salinity-affected areas" produce?::Road designs and rehabilitation strategies that keep water out of the pavement and subgrade ('umbrella' approach), resist saline attack, and avoid the road itself worsening salinity.
Before relying on "Design and rehabilitate road pavements in salinity-affected areas" — what do you check?::Surface maintained free of ponding (also a hydroplaning hazard) and cracks sealed promptly. • Subsurface drain grades sufficient to prevent silting and maintain flow (a commonly underestimated failure). • Sealing aggregates and construction water meet salt limits (RTA-era limits cited: maximum ~600 ppm chloride and ~400 ppm sulphate ions). • Capping layers meet the specified permeability (VicRoads example: <5 x 10^-9 m/s at OMC +/-5%, 98% +/-1% standard density ratio).
"Design and rehabilitate road pavements in salinity-affected areas" — state the decision rule about: If a network built to standard details shows widespread earl…::If a network built to standard details shows widespread early distress, upgrade the standard details (the Wyndham approach: standard configurations with lime-stabilised clay subgrades per traffic tier
"Design and rehabilitate road pavements in salinity-affected areas" — state the decision rule about: Low-permeability subgrade layers concentrate water and salt …::Low-permeability subgrade layers concentrate water and salt — pair any low-permeability formation layer with edge subsurface drains to remove perched water.
What does "Diagnose water and salt entry pathways in salt-affected buildings" produce?::Identification of the water source(s), transport mechanism and attack mechanism driving salt damage, so that remediation targets cause rather than symptom.
Before relying on "Diagnose water and salt entry pathways in salt-affected buildings" — what do you check?::All plausible water sources surveyed (pipes, pools, irrigation, gutters, ground levels, groundwater) before attributing to one. • Damage pattern (below vs above DPC, base of wall vs cavity, external vs internal) is consistent with the diagnosed pathway. • Salt type identified where remediation cost justifies analysis.
"Diagnose water and salt entry pathways in salt-affected buildings" — state the decision rule about: If damage continues after water sources are controlled, susp…::If damage continues after water sources are controlled, suspect hygroscopic salts and slow watertable response rather than a missed leak.
"Diagnose water and salt entry pathways in salt-affected buildings" — state the decision rule about: Deep salty soil layers are unlikely to matter unless a water…::Deep salty soil layers are unlikely to matter unless a water pathway or cut/fill brings them into play.
What does "Manage salinity in subdivision and single-lot development design" produce?::Development-scale measures (drainage, earthworks, landscaping, water management) that keep groundwater and salt away from structures and avoid creating new salinity.
Before relying on "Manage salinity in subdivision and single-lot development design" — what do you check?::Drainage layers beneath fill are actually drained (not just present). • Capping-layer proposals assessed for long-term capillary bypass, not just short-term covering. • Sediment and erosion control plans account for saline and sodic soils. • Monitoring (piezometers) persists through construction into occupation.
"Manage salinity in subdivision and single-lot development design" — state the decision rule about: If an existing salinity problem is identified, design every …::If an existing salinity problem is identified, design every element for it and aim the subdivision design at improving conditions over time (tree planting, drainage that lowers groundwater and leaches
"Manage salinity in subdivision and single-lot development design" — state the decision rule about: If only potential hazard exists, either demonstrate no futur…::If only potential hazard exists, either demonstrate no future problem or build basic durability measures into concrete elements now — guarantees over a 50-year design life are hard to sustain.
What does "Measure soil salinity by EC1:5 and classify it using field texture" produce?::A repeatable field/lab workflow converting a 1:5 soil:water EC reading into an ECe value and salinity class via texture-based multipliers.
Before relying on "Measure soil salinity by EC1:5 and classify it using field texture" — what do you check?::EC meter calibrated against buffer before each batch. • Enough dried fines prepared (the procedure sheet targets at least ~108 g of -425 um material). • Jars cleaned/drained between samples to avoid carryover. • Multiplier used is recorded next to each result.
"Measure soil salinity by EC1:5 and classify it using field texture" — state the decision rule about: Always keep EC1:5, ECe and ECw distinct in records; only ECe…::Always keep EC1:5, ECe and ECw distinct in records; only ECe (texture-corrected) feeds the salinity class.
"Measure soil salinity by EC1:5 and classify it using field texture" — state the decision rule about: Clay-dominated soils are hardest to texture — add water slow…::Clay-dominated soils are hardest to texture — add water slowly and re-add soil if over-wetted before judging ribbon length.
What does "Plan a phased site investigation for urban salinity" produce?::A staged investigation (desktop review through to management plan) scaled to the development type, that identifies salt stores, water movement and the two-way impacts between the development and salinity processes.
Before relying on "Plan a phased site investigation for urban salinity" — what do you check?::At least one soil profile per landform unit, with profiles arranged in transects across the site. • Field observations reconcile with lab results (a mapped salt scald should return high lab salinity; if not, suspect labelling or reporting errors). • Groundwater interpretation distinguishes local, intermediate and regional systems and recharge vs discharge behaviour before management options are chosen. • Piezometers are located where they can survive construction for ongoing monitoring.
"Plan a phased site investigation for urban salinity" — state the decision rule about: Set sample numbers from the mapping scale and land use inten…::Set sample numbers from the mapping scale and land use intensity using the booklet's Table 1 (p. 6): denser sampling for larger-scale mapping and more intensive uses (e.g. roughly 6-18 initial observa
"Plan a phased site investigation for urban salinity" — state the decision rule about: Use fewer samples when landscape/soil variability is low, lo…::Use fewer samples when landscape/soil variability is low, local knowledge is good, or the land use will not mobilise salt (no irrigation, effluent disposal or clearing); use more when the opposite hol
What does "Present and interpret urban salinity investigation results" produce?::Results reported with unambiguous units, spatial context (maps, transects, depth profiles) and a process interpretation (recharge vs discharge, through-flow, corrosion risk) that supports management decisions.
Before relying on "Present and interpret urban salinity investigation results" — what do you check?::Every table states units and conversion factors used. • Field-observed salinity outbreaks reconcile with lab data; discrepancies trigger a labelling/reporting audit. • Interpretation distinguishes ECw (water measurements — snapshot only) from soil ECe.
"Present and interpret urban salinity investigation results" — state the decision rule about: If salinity is reported as EC1:5 without texture conversion,…::If salinity is reported as EC1:5 without texture conversion, results understate ECe by about x14 (sandy loam) to x6 (heavy clay) — always state which quantity is reported.
"Present and interpret urban salinity investigation results" — state the decision rule about: dS/m expressed in mS/m is 100x larger numerically; misread s…::dS/m expressed in mS/m is 100x larger numerically; misread scale factors are the classic reporting failure.
What does "Recognise urban salinity indicators in the field" produce?::Rapid, low-cost identification of sites where salinity is present or emerging, triggering targeted testing rather than assumption.
Before relying on "Recognise urban salinity indicators in the field" — what do you check?::Each suspected indicator has a follow-up test or inspection recorded. • Alternative causes (plumbing leaks, condensation, poor drainage) explicitly considered. • Observations photographed and located for the site map.
"Recognise urban salinity indicators in the field" — state the decision rule about: Presence of salt-tolerant plants alone does not prove active…::Presence of salt-tolerant plants alone does not prove active salinity — they may simply be planted or opportunistic; use them to justify testing, not conclusions.
"Recognise urban salinity indicators in the field" — state the decision rule about: A tide mark plus efflorescence points to rising damp carryin…::A tide mark plus efflorescence points to rising damp carrying salts; damage from the top of walls down points to falling damp (gutters/roof) instead.
What does "Select and interpret soil tests for water movement and corrosivity" produce?::A test suite and interpretation that establishes how water (and therefore salt) moves through the site and how aggressive the soil/groundwater will be to concrete and steel.
Before relying on "Select and interpret soil tests for water movement and corrosivity" — what do you check?::Units match the comparison standard exactly: sulphate as % soil weight, chloride as ppm or mg/L, resistivity as ohm.cm — otherwise the AS 2159 tables cannot be  • EC results labelled as EC1:5, EC1:2 or ECe with conversion factors stated. • Dispersibility considered alongside sodicity: low-sodium soils with poor structure and low organic matter can still be highly dispersive.
"Select and interpret soil tests for water movement and corrosivity" — state the decision rule about: AS 2159 distinguishes soil condition classes: (A) high-perme…::AS 2159 distinguishes soil condition classes: (A) high-permeability soils below groundwater vs (B) low-permeability soils and all soils above groundwater; in urban settings where leaks and perched wat
"Select and interpret soil tests for water movement and corrosivity" — state the decision rule about: Where water flow can be concentrated (through-flow layers, p…::Where water flow can be concentrated (through-flow layers, pale-coloured horizons), expect concentrated salt — corrosivity sampling should target these zones.
What does "Select surface treatments for pavements by salt content before sealing" produce?::A seal/prime strategy chosen from measured salt content of pavement fines, preventing salt crystallisation from blistering and destroying thin bituminous surfacings.
Before relying on "Select surface treatments for pavements by salt content before sealing" — what do you check?::Salt content measured on the correct fraction (fines) and reported as % with method stated. • Aggregate and water salt certificates reviewed before sealing. • Post-sealing surveillance for blistering in the first seasons.
"Select surface treatments for pavements by salt content before sealing" — state the decision rule about: Light treatments (primes, primerseals) left exposed in salin…::Light treatments (primes, primerseals) left exposed in saline conditions will distress — minimise the time between primerseal and final seal.
"Select surface treatments for pavements by salt content before sealing" — state the decision rule about: If salt exceeds ~3% in fines, do not proceed on a standard m…::If salt exceeds ~3% in fines, do not proceed on a standard method; investigate (source of salt, moisture regime) and trial treatments.
What does "Specify salt-resistant masonry, damp-proof courses and membranes" produce?::Masonry and moisture-barrier specifications (brick class, mortar, DPC height and continuity, under-slab membrane) that meet BCA/AS requirements for saline sites and avoid the common DPC failure modes.
Before relying on "Specify salt-resistant masonry, damp-proof courses and membranes" — what do you check?::DPC continuity verified around the full perimeter and above finished ground/paving at the specified height. • Membrane laps, penetration sealing and extension to ground level inspected before the pour (it is hidden early in construction). • Landscaping plans checked for future DPC bridging (garden beds, paths against walls).
"Specify salt-resistant masonry, damp-proof courses and membranes" — state the decision rule about: If salinity status is unknown, exposure-grade bricks and a d…::If salinity status is unknown, exposure-grade bricks and a damp-proof (not vapour) membrane are cheap insurance relative to repair cost — Australia-wide, most urban sites have some water source capabl
"Specify salt-resistant masonry, damp-proof courses and membranes" — state the decision rule about: Existing NSW council policies in saline areas typically add:…::Existing NSW council policies in saline areas typically add: 50 mm sand under slab, 32 MPa concrete, seven days curing, plus the high-impact membrane — check the local policy since councils may exceed
What does "Stabilise road subgrades with lime in saline and wet conditions" produce?::A lime-stabilised subgrade that is drier, stiffer, less moisture-reactive and lower-permeability, reducing water and salt movement into the pavement and watertable.
Before relying on "Stabilise road subgrades with lime in saline and wet conditions" — what do you check?::Lime spread rate and mixing uniformity verified (two-pass minimum). • Strength gain tracked over time with CBR/UCS testing rather than assumed at 7 days. • Shrinkage cracks in bound layers sealed promptly after appearing.
"Stabilise road subgrades with lime in saline and wet conditions" — state the decision rule about: Choose modification vs bound behaviour deliberately (indicat…::Choose modification vs bound behaviour deliberately (indicative Austroads bands: modified 0.7-1.5 MPa UCS; lightly bound 1.5-3.0 MPa; bound above 3.0 MPa) — bound layers cut water entry but crack and 
"Stabilise road subgrades with lime in saline and wet conditions" — state the decision rule about: Organic matter in the soil, even in small quantities, can re…::Organic matter in the soil, even in small quantities, can reduce the lime reaction's effectiveness — test and adjust.

What does "Design and rehabilitate road pavements in salinity affected areas" produce?::Road designs and rehabilitation strategies that keep water out of the pavement and subgrade ('umbrella' approach), resist saline attack, and avoid the road itself worsening salinity. "Design and rehabilitate road pavements in salinity affected areas" — state the decision rule about: If a network built to standard details shows widespread earl…::If a network built to standard details shows widespread early distress, upgrade the standard details (the Wyndham approach: standard configurations with lime stabilised clay subgrades per traffic tier "Design and rehabilitate road pavements in salinity affected areas" — state the decision rule about: Low permeability subgrade layers concentrate water and salt …::Low permeability subgrade layers concentrate water and salt — pair any low permeability formation layer with edge subsurface drains to remove perched water. What does "Diagnose water and salt entry pathways in salt affected buildings" produce?::Identification of the water source(s), transport mechanism and attack mechanism driving salt damage, so that remediation targets cause rather than symptom. Before relying on "Diagnose water and salt entry pathways in salt affected buildings" — what do you check?::All plausible water sources surveyed (pipes, pools, irrigation, gutters, ground levels, groundwater) before attributing to one. • Damage pattern (below vs above DPC, base of wall vs cavity, external vs internal) is consistent with the diagnosed pathway. • Salt type identified where remediation cost justifies analysis. "Diagnose water and salt entry pathways in salt affected buildings" — state the decision rule about: If damage continues after water sources are controlled, susp…::If damage continues after water sources are controlled, suspect hygroscopic salts and slow watertable response rather than a missed leak. "Diagnose water and salt entry pathways in salt affected buildings" — state the decision rule about: Deep salty soil layers are unlikely to matter unless a water…::Deep salty soil layers are unlikely to matter unless a water pathway or cut/fill brings them into play. What does "Manage salinity in subdivision and single lot development design" produce?::Development scale measures (drainage, earthworks, landscaping, water management) that keep groundwater and salt away from structures and avoid creating new salinity. Before relying on "Manage salinity in subdivision and single lot development design" — what do you check?::Drainage layers beneath fill are actually drained (not just present). • Capping layer proposals assessed for long term capillary bypass, not just short term covering. • Sediment and erosion control plans account for saline and sodic soils. • Monitoring (piezometers) persists through construction into occupation. "Manage salinity in subdivision and single lot development design" — state the decision rule about: If an existing salinity problem is identified, design every …::If an existing salinity problem is identified, design every element for it and aim the subdivision design at improving conditions over time (tree planting, drainage that lowers groundwater and leaches "Manage salinity in subdivision and single lot development design" — state the decision rule about: If only potential hazard exists, either demonstrate no futur…::If only potential hazard exists, either demonstrate no future problem or build basic durability measures into concrete elements now — guarantees over a 50 year design life are hard to sustain. What does "Measure soil salinity by EC1:5 and classify it using field texture" produce?::A repeatable field/lab workflow converting a 1:5 soil:water EC reading into an ECe value and salinity class via texture based multipliers. Before relying on "Measure soil salinity by EC1:5 and classify it using field texture" — what do you check?::EC meter calibrated against buffer before each batch. • Enough dried fines prepared (the procedure sheet targets at least ~108 g of 425 um material). • Jars cleaned/drained between samples to avoid carryover. • Multiplier used is recorded next to each result. "Measure soil salinity by EC1:5 and classify it using field texture" — state the decision rule about: Always keep EC1:5, ECe and ECw distinct in records; only ECe…::Always keep EC1:5, ECe and ECw distinct in records; only ECe (texture corrected) feeds the salinity class. "Measure soil salinity by EC1:5 and classify it using field texture" — state the decision rule about: Clay dominated soils are hardest to texture — add water slow…::Clay dominated soils are hardest to texture — add water slowly and re add soil if over wetted before judging ribbon length. What does "Plan a phased site investigation for urban salinity" produce?::A staged investigation (desktop review through to management plan) scaled to the development type, that identifies salt stores, water movement and the two way impacts between the development and salinity processes. Before relying on "Plan a phased site investigation for urban salinity" — what do you check?::At least one soil profile per landform unit, with profiles arranged in transects across the site. • Field observations reconcile with lab results (a mapped salt scald should return high lab salinity; if not, suspect labelling or reporting errors). • Groundwater interpretation distinguishes local, intermediate and regional systems and recharge vs discharge behaviour before management options are chosen. • Piezometers are located where they can survive construction for ongoing monitoring. "Plan a phased site investigation for urban salinity" — state the decision rule about: Set sample numbers from the mapping scale and land use inten…::Set sample numbers from the mapping scale and land use intensity using the booklet's Table 1 (p. 6): denser sampling for larger scale mapping and more intensive uses (e.g. roughly 6 18 initial observa "Plan a phased site investigation for urban salinity" — state the decision rule about: Use fewer samples when landscape/soil variability is low, lo…::Use fewer samples when landscape/soil variability is low, local knowledge is good, or the land use will not mobilise salt (no irrigation, effluent disposal or clearing); use more when the opposite hol What does "Present and interpret urban salinity investigation results" produce?::Results reported with unambiguous units, spatial context (maps, transects, depth profiles) and a process interpretation (recharge vs discharge, through flow, corrosion risk) that supports management decisions. Before relying on "Present and interpret urban salinity investigation results" — what do you check?::Every table states units and conversion factors used. • Field observed salinity outbreaks reconcile with lab data; discrepancies trigger a labelling/reporting audit. • Interpretation distinguishes ECw (water measurements — snapshot only) from soil ECe. "Present and interpret urban salinity investigation results" — state the decision rule about: If salinity is reported as EC1:5 without texture conversion,…::If salinity is reported as EC1:5 without texture conversion, results understate ECe by about x14 (sandy loam) to x6 (heavy clay) — always state which quantity is reported. "Present and interpret urban salinity investigation results" — state the decision rule about: dS/m expressed in mS/m is 100x larger numerically; misread s…::dS/m expressed in mS/m is 100x larger numerically; misread scale factors are the classic reporting failure. What does "Recognise urban salinity indicators in the field" produce?::Rapid, low cost identification of sites where salinity is present or emerging, triggering targeted testing rather than assumption. Before relying on "Recognise urban salinity indicators in the field" — what do you check?::Each suspected indicator has a follow up test or inspection recorded. • Alternative causes (plumbing leaks, condensation, poor drainage) explicitly considered. • Observations photographed and located for the site map. "Recognise urban salinity indicators in the field" — state the decision rule about: Presence of salt tolerant plants alone does not prove active…::Presence of salt tolerant plants alone does not prove active salinity — they may simply be planted or opportunistic; use them to justify testing, not conclusions. "Recognise urban salinity indicators in the field" — state the decision rule about: A tide mark plus efflorescence points to rising damp carryin…::A tide mark plus efflorescence points to rising damp carrying salts; damage from the top of walls down points to falling damp (gutters/roof) instead. What does "Select and interpret soil tests for water movement and corrosivity" produce?::A test suite and interpretation that establishes how water (and therefore salt) moves through the site and how aggressive the soil/groundwater will be to concrete and steel. Before relying on "Select and interpret soil tests for water movement and corrosivity" — what do you check?::Units match the comparison standard exactly: sulphate as % soil weight, chloride as ppm or mg/L, resistivity as ohm.cm — otherwise the AS 2159 tables cannot be • EC results labelled as EC1:5, EC1:2 or ECe with conversion factors stated. • Dispersibility considered alongside sodicity: low sodium soils with poor structure and low organic matter can still be highly dispersive. "Select and interpret soil tests for water movement and corrosivity" — state the decision rule about: AS 2159 distinguishes soil condition classes: (A) high perme…::AS 2159 distinguishes soil condition classes: (A) high permeability soils below groundwater vs (B) low permeability soils and all soils above groundwater; in urban settings where leaks and perched wat "Select and interpret soil tests for water movement and corrosivity" — state the decision rule about: Where water flow can be concentrated (through flow layers, p…::Where water flow can be concentrated (through flow layers, pale coloured horizons), expect concentrated salt — corrosivity sampling should target these zones. What does "Select surface treatments for pavements by salt content before sealing" produce?::A seal/prime strategy chosen from measured salt content of pavement fines, preventing salt crystallisation from blistering and destroying thin bituminous surfacings. Before relying on "Select surface treatments for pavements by salt content before sealing" — what do you check?::Salt content measured on the correct fraction (fines) and reported as % with method stated. • Aggregate and water salt certificates reviewed before sealing. • Post sealing surveillance for blistering in the first seasons. "Select surface treatments for pavements by salt content before sealing" — state the decision rule about: Light treatments (primes, primerseals) left exposed in salin…::Light treatments (primes, primerseals) left exposed in saline conditions will distress — minimise the time between primerseal and final seal. "Select surface treatments for pavements by salt content before sealing" — state the decision rule about: If salt exceeds ~3% in fines, do not proceed on a standard m…::If salt exceeds ~3% in fines, do not proceed on a standard method; investigate (source of salt, moisture regime) and trial treatments. What does "Specify salt resistant masonry, damp proof courses and membranes" produce?::Masonry and moisture barrier specifications (brick class, mortar, DPC height and continuity, under slab membrane) that meet BCA/AS requirements for saline sites and avoid the common DPC failure modes. Before relying on "Specify salt resistant masonry, damp proof courses and membranes" — what do you check?::DPC continuity verified around the full perimeter and above finished ground/paving at the specified height. • Membrane laps, penetration sealing and extension to ground level inspected before the pour (it is hidden early in construction). • Landscaping plans checked for future DPC bridging (garden beds, paths against walls). "Specify salt resistant masonry, damp proof courses and membranes" — state the decision rule about: If salinity status is unknown, exposure grade bricks and a d…::If salinity status is unknown, exposure grade bricks and a damp proof (not vapour) membrane are cheap insurance relative to repair cost — Australia wide, most urban sites have some water source capabl "Specify salt resistant masonry, damp proof courses and membranes" — state the decision rule about: Existing NSW council policies in saline areas typically add:…::Existing NSW council policies in saline areas typically add: 50 mm sand under slab, 32 MPa concrete, seven days curing, plus the high impact membrane — check the local policy since councils may exceed What does "Stabilise road subgrades with lime in saline and wet conditions" produce?::A lime stabilised subgrade that is drier, stiffer, less moisture reactive and lower permeability, reducing water and salt movement into the pavement and watertable. Before relying on "Stabilise road subgrades with lime in saline and wet conditions" — what do you check?::Lime spread rate and mixing uniformity verified (two pass minimum). • Strength gain tracked over time with CBR/UCS testing rather than assumed at 7 days. • Shrinkage cracks in bound layers sealed promptly after appearing. "Stabilise road subgrades with lime in saline and wet conditions" — state the decision rule about: Choose modification vs bound behaviour deliberately (indicat…::Choose modification vs bound behaviour deliberately (indicative Austroads bands: modified 0.7 1.5 MPa UCS; lightly bound 1.5 3.0 MPa; bound above 3.0 MPa) — bound layers cut water entry but crack and "Stabilise road subgrades with lime in saline and wet conditions" — state the decision rule about: Organic matter in the soil, even in small quantities, can re…::Organic matter in the soil, even in small quantities, can reduce the lime reaction's effectiveness — test and adjust. Related Learning path Salinity and aggressivity Learning loop

notes.title: Flashcards - Slope stability
notes.body:
# Flashcards - Slope stability

#flashcards/slope-stability

104 cards generated from the 26 slope stability skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Assess staged load cases and anchor reinforcement for a planar rock slope" produce?::A comparison of factor of safety across dry, water-filled, seismic and anchored cases that shows which conditions govern and what anchor force restores stability
Before relying on "Assess staged load cases and anchor reinforcement for a planar rock slope" — what do you check?::Confirm the factor of safety decreases monotonically as water then seismic load are added; if not, a term has the wrong sign • Cross-check each case against software (RocPlane reproduced 1.54, 1.07, 0.92 and about 1.4 with a 400 kN bolt at 35 degree plunge)
"Assess staged load cases and anchor reinforcement for a planar rock slope" — state the decision rule about: Obtain the seismic coefficient from the design standard for …::Obtain the seismic coefficient from the design standard for the project region; near zero in aseismic areas, larger in seismically active countries
"Assess staged load cases and anchor reinforcement for a planar rock slope" — state the decision rule about: Anchor inclination changes effectiveness — flatter or steepe…::Anchor inclination changes effectiveness — flatter or steeper installation angles raise or lower the factor of safety, so optimise angle as well as force
What does "Calculate the safety factor of a rock slope against planar (block) failure" produce?::A factor of safety against sliding of a block on a planar failure surface using the simplified dry, no-tension-crack formula, with a stability interpretation and a cohesion sensitivity check
Before relying on "Calculate the safety factor of a rock slope against planar (block) failure" — what do you check?::Angle roles not swapped: i is the face angle, theta is the failure plane dip • Units consistent (kPa with kN/m3) throughout • Sensitivity to cohesion evaluated before declaring a marginal slope stable
"Calculate the safety factor of a rock slope against planar (block) failure" — state the decision rule about: FoS greater than 1 indicates stable, less than 1 unstable; a…::FoS greater than 1 indicates stable, less than 1 unstable; a value at about 1 means critical/marginally stable — a small perturbation such as some water can tip it to failure
"Calculate the safety factor of a rock slope against planar (block) failure" — state the decision rule about: A failure plane dip greater than the friction angle (42 vs 3…::A failure plane dip greater than the friction angle (42 vs 33 degrees here) means friction alone cannot hold the block — cohesion is doing critical work
What does "Classify rock slope movements using the Varnes movement-type system" produce?::A movement-type classification (fall, topple, planar or rotational slide, lateral spread, creep, or complex) for a rock slope, with the diagnostic field evidence for each
Before relying on "Classify rock slope movements using the Varnes movement-type system" — what do you check?::Verify the inferred failure surface shape (planar vs circular) against weathering condition • Check trigger consistency: earthquake-dependent mechanisms should correlate with regional seismicity
"Classify rock slope movements using the Varnes movement-type system" — state the decision rule about: Daylighting discontinuity plus tension crack points to plana…::Daylighting discontinuity plus tension crack points to planar slide potential
"Classify rock slope movements using the Varnes movement-type system" — state the decision rule about: Gentle basal plane under a huge rock mass on saturated clay …::Gentle basal plane under a huge rock mass on saturated clay plus seismic trigger points to lateral spread; rainfall alone will not trigger it
What does "Compute a planar-failure factor of safety in RocPlane and verify by hand" produce?::A deterministic factor of safety for a rock block sliding on a single failure plane, cross-checked against a hand calculation
Before relying on "Compute a planar-failure factor of safety in RocPlane and verify by hand" — what do you check?::Reproduce the software result with the hand formula at least once to confirm inputs are interpreted correctly • Double-check the two unit conversions: kN/m3 to MN/m3 for unit weight, and kPa to MPa for cohesion
"Compute a planar-failure factor of safety in RocPlane and verify by hand" — state the decision rule about: Deterministic analysis is appropriate when each parameter ha…::Deterministic analysis is appropriate when each parameter has a single known value; use probabilistic settings if you hold ranges for cohesion, friction angle or unit weight
"Compute a planar-failure factor of safety in RocPlane and verify by hand" — state the decision rule about: Set the upper face angle to zero when the slope profile abov…::Set the upper face angle to zero when the slope profile above the crest is a straight continuation with no bench
What does "Compute a wedge failure factor of safety in Swedge" produce?::A deterministic factor of safety for a rock wedge formed by two intersecting joints in a slope face, including sensitivity to water filling of the joints
Before relying on "Compute a wedge failure factor of safety in Swedge" — what do you check?::Verify units on entry: density in t/m3 versus unit weight in MN/m3 • Run the percent-filled water sweep — safety factor falls slightly at modest saturation and drops sharply at full saturation, so check the design case includes a
"Compute a wedge failure factor of safety in Swedge" — state the decision rule about: The orientation of a line of intersection is described by tr…::The orientation of a line of intersection is described by trend and plunge, not dip and dip direction — the software computes it from the two joint planes
"Compute a wedge failure factor of safety in Swedge" — state the decision rule about: For observed wedge failures, cohesion on the joints is typic…::For observed wedge failures, cohesion on the joints is typically taken as zero, leaving friction to resist sliding
What does "Compute the factor of safety of a planar rock slope failure with tension crack by hand" produce?::A hand-calculated factor of safety for a planar failure surface behind a slope crest, including geometry-derived tension crack depth, failure plane length and block weight
Before relying on "Compute the factor of safety of a planar rock slope failure with tension crack by hand" — what do you check?::Confirm all forces are expressed per metre width of slope so units are consistent (kN/m) • Check that omitted effects (seismic, water, anchor) are explicitly zeroed rather than left in with stale values • Compare the dry-slope result against software (RocPlane reproduces 1.54 for this example)
"Compute the factor of safety of a planar rock slope failure with tension crack by hand" — state the decision rule about: Factor of safety above 1 indicates stability; below 1 indica…::Factor of safety above 1 indicates stability; below 1 indicates the block can fail
"Compute the factor of safety of a planar rock slope failure with tension crack by hand" — state the decision rule about: Water in the tension crack acts twice: U reduces frictional …::Water in the tension crack acts twice: U reduces frictional resistance and V adds driving force — include both
What does "Compute traffic exposure ratings (average vehicle risk and percent decision sight distance) for rockfall rating" produce?::Two traffic-related inputs to the rockfall hazard rating: the average vehicle risk along the affected road length and the ratio of actual to decision sight distance
Before relying on "Compute traffic exposure ratings (average vehicle risk and percent decision sight distance) for rockfall rating" — what do you check?::Confirm the road length was converted to kilometres before use • Confirm units of traffic volume (per hour vs per day) match the formula form being used
"Compute traffic exposure ratings (average vehicle risk and percent decision sight distance) for rockfall rating" — state the decision rule about: If computed average vehicle risk exceeds 100 percent, cap it…::If computed average vehicle risk exceeds 100 percent, cap it at 100 percent (maximum points) for the rating
"Compute traffic exposure ratings (average vehicle risk and percent decision sight distance) for rockfall rating" — state the decision rule about: Lower percent decision sight distance is worse; if close to …::Lower percent decision sight distance is worse; if close to a tabulated boundary and no time to interpolate, adopt the worse (higher-point) category
What does "Conduct a landslide hazard analysis and build the site geotechnical model (AGS 2007)" produce?::A documented geotechnical model with characterised landslide hazards, estimated annual probabilities and travel distances, forming the front half of a defensible Landslide Risk Management (LRM) report.
Before relying on "Conduct a landslide hazard analysis and build the site geotechnical model (AGS 2007)" — what do you check?::Cross-sections at natural scale (plus a natural-scale summary if exaggeration used). • Hazards addressed above, below and adjacent to the site, not just within the lot. • Frequency reasoning documented transparently, with sensitivity/uncertainty stated; expert-judgement accuracy typically half to two orders of magnitude.
"Conduct a landslide hazard analysis and build the site geotechnical model (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Choose the qualitative likelihood term FROM the estimated pr…::Choose the qualitative likelihood term FROM the estimated probability — never adopt a probability from a qualitative term (practitioners diverge by orders of magnitude, Section 5.4.2(a)).
"Conduct a landslide hazard analysis and build the site geotechnical model (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Investigation is adequate only when the model explains slope…::Investigation is adequate only when the model explains slope processes, landslide extent, triggers and process rates; otherwise investigate further (Section 5.2.8).
What does "Estimate landslide risk and evaluate it against tolerable criteria (AGS 2007)" produce?::Quantified risk to life and quantified or qualitative risk to property for every landslide hazard, summed and compared against regulator tolerable-risk criteria to decide accept/treat.
Before relying on "Estimate landslide risk and evaluate it against tolerable criteria (AGS 2007)" — what do you check?::All hazards summed — not just the dominant one — for comparison with criteria. • P(T:S) between 0 and 1, with building occupancy taken as ~1.0 for houses per Section 7.1 unless justified. • Sensitivity of the result to uncertain inputs displayed; conservative outcome adopted where unjustified uncertainty remains.
"Estimate landslide risk and evaluate it against tolerable criteria (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Risk to life is always assessed quantitatively for the perso…::Risk to life is always assessed quantitatively for the person most at risk; property risk may be qualitative/semi-quantitative for screening or data-poor cases (Sections 3.3.4, 7.2).
"Estimate landslide risk and evaluate it against tolerable criteria (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Existing landslides attract the stricter 'new' criterion eve…::Existing landslides attract the stricter 'new' criterion even if remediation is not otherwise required (Table 1 note 5).
What does "Estimate wedge failure factor of safety with the wedge factor K method" produce?::A quick friction-only factor of safety for a rock wedge formed by two intersecting discontinuity planes, identifying whether the wedge is stable
Before relying on "Estimate wedge failure factor of safety with the wedge factor K method" — what do you check?::Verify which given angle is plunge vs trend before computing (two-digit vs three-digit convention) • Check that unused given data (e.g. slope face dip/dip direction) was genuinely not required rather than forgotten
"Estimate wedge failure factor of safety with the wedge factor K method" — state the decision rule about: K greater than 1 reflects the wedging effect: a wedge confin…::K greater than 1 reflects the wedging effect: a wedge confined by two planes is more stable than an equivalent planar block at the same inclination
"Estimate wedge failure factor of safety with the wedge factor K method" — state the decision rule about: This hand method excludes cohesion and water pressure; when …::This hand method excludes cohesion and water pressure; when either matters, or geometry is complex, move to software analysis
What does "Forecast time to rock slope collapse from displacement monitoring data" produce?::An empirical estimate of the number of days until collapse of an accelerating rock slide, from the onset velocity of progressive movement
Before relying on "Forecast time to rock slope collapse from displacement monitoring data" — what do you check?::Confirm the trend of the progressive stage is well established (near-linear on the chart) before extrapolating • Read the log velocity axis carefully; small reading errors change the forecast substantially
"Forecast time to rock slope collapse from displacement monitoring data" — state the decision rule about: Regressive-stage movement alone does not warrant collapse fo…::Regressive-stage movement alone does not warrant collapse forecasting; the method applies once progressive acceleration is established
"Forecast time to rock slope collapse from displacement monitoring data" — state the decision rule about: Treat the forecast as an order-of-magnitude planning tool: t…::Treat the forecast as an order-of-magnitude planning tool: the correlation is highly empirical and will not hold in all cases
What does "Rate rockfall hazard for a slope inventory using a point-based rating system" produce?::A summed hazard rating for each inspected slope that ranks it for remediation priority and sets the re-inspection or mitigation response
Before relying on "Rate rockfall hazard for a slope inventory using a point-based rating system" — what do you check?::Confirm every factor received a score and that extrapolated scores respect the table caps • Cross-check subjective scores (geology, history, ditch) against the written site description • Verify the same rating system and category boundaries are used consistently across the whole inventory so rankings are comparable
"Rate rockfall hazard for a slope inventory using a point-based rating system" — state the decision rule about: Total below about 300 points: low priority, re-inspect on th…::Total below about 300 points: low priority, re-inspect on the normal cycle
"Rate rockfall hazard for a slope inventory using a point-based rating system" — state the decision rule about: Total of about 500 points or more: act immediately with reme…::Total of about 500 points or more: act immediately with remedial works
What does "Run a Monte Carlo probabilistic planar-failure analysis in RocPlane" produce?::A probability of failure and factor-of-safety distribution for a planar rock slope that reflects the measured scatter in strength and water conditions
Before relying on "Run a Monte Carlo probabilistic planar-failure analysis in RocPlane" — what do you check?::Cumulative probability read at factor of safety = 1 must match the reported probability of failure • Relative min/max plus the mean must stay within physical bounds (0-100 percent for water fill) • Zero probability of failure should correspond to a histogram entirely above factor of safety 1
"Run a Monte Carlo probabilistic planar-failure analysis in RocPlane" — state the decision rule about: Vary only parameters with real measured uncertainty; fixing …::Vary only parameters with real measured uncertainty; fixing well-surveyed geometry keeps the result interpretable
"Run a Monte Carlo probabilistic planar-failure analysis in RocPlane" — state the decision rule about: Water fill percentage dominates the failure probability in t…::Water fill percentage dominates the failure probability in this problem — invest site investigation effort there
What does "Run a basic circular slip-surface slope stability analysis in Slide2 (Quick Start)" produce?::A computed factor of safety and critical circular slip surface for a homogeneous dry slope, using a Grid Search, with results interpreted and a second scenario compared.
Before relying on "Run a basic circular slip-surface slope stability analysis in Slide2 (Quick Start)" — what do you check?::Search coverage adequate (contours and surface cloud reviewed), not just the single reported FS. • Results consistent across at least two search methods before relying on the minimum FS.
"Run a basic circular slip-surface slope stability analysis in Slide2 (Quick Start)" — state the decision rule about: Treat 'Global Minimum' with caution — it is only the minimum…::Treat 'Global Minimum' with caution — it is only the minimum among surfaces actually searched; grid location, spacing, Radius Increment and Slope Limits all change the answer.
"Run a basic circular slip-surface slope stability analysis in Slide2 (Quick Start)" — state the decision rule about: The critical surface can differ between analysis methods; ch…::The critical surface can differ between analysis methods; check each method separately.
What does "Run a deterministic planar-failure analysis in RocPlane and cross-validate hand calculations" produce?::A software factor of safety for a planar rock slope failure under dry, wet, seismic and anchored cases that matches independent hand calculation
Before relying on "Run a deterministic planar-failure analysis in RocPlane and cross-validate hand calculations" — what do you check?::Wedge weight, failure plane length, tension crack length, U and V reported by the software should reproduce hand-calculated values (1241 kN/m, 13.3 m, 4.35 m, 2 • Each added adverse effect should lower the factor of safety; each support should raise it
"Run a deterministic planar-failure analysis in RocPlane and cross-validate hand calculations" — state the decision rule about: Horizontal seismic direction is the worst case for this geom…::Horizontal seismic direction is the worst case for this geometry
"Run a deterministic planar-failure analysis in RocPlane and cross-validate hand calculations" — state the decision rule about: Decreasing the bolt plunge angle increases stability for thi…::Decreasing the bolt plunge angle increases stability for this setup — vary plunge and force to reach the target factor of safety
What does "Run a finite element groundwater seepage analysis coupled with slope stability in Slide2" produce?::A steady-state FE seepage solution (phreatic surface, pore pressure/total head contours, flow vectors) whose pore pressures feed directly into the limit-equilibrium slope stability run, including optional matric suction strength above the water table.
Before relying on "Run a finite element groundwater seepage analysis coupled with slope stability in Slide2" — what do you check?::FE water table position plausible against known groundwater levels (it is the P=0 iso-line). • Ponded water auto-created where intended by the head boundary conditions. • Iso-line and query checks confirm the pressure field (e.g. pond-bottom pressure head equals pond depth).
"Run a finite element groundwater seepage analysis coupled with slope stability in Slide2" — state the decision rule about: Always compute and review the groundwater solution separatel…::Always compute and review the groundwater solution separately before the stability analysis, even though Slide will chain them automatically.
"Run a finite element groundwater seepage analysis coupled with slope stability in Slide2" — state the decision rule about: Negative pressure heads above the water table are matric suc…::Negative pressure heads above the water table are matric suction; they affect strength only if phi-b > 0.
What does "Run a flexural-toppling kinematic analysis in Dips" produce?::A screening verdict on toppling risk for a rock cut, from the percentage of poles falling in the critical zone defined by the slip limit and lateral limits
Before relying on "Run a flexural-toppling kinematic analysis in Dips" — what do you check?::Cross-check the manual plane-and-cone construction against the built-in kinematic analysis output • Verify the friction angle entered matches the investigation value (the lecturer initially mistyped 30 for 35)
"Run a flexural-toppling kinematic analysis in Dips" — state the decision rule about: A critical-pole percentage above about 6 percent raises a re…::A critical-pole percentage above about 6 percent raises a red flag and warrants a more thorough toppling investigation (the example returned 20 of 303 poles = 6.6 percent, flagged as a concern)
"Run a flexural-toppling kinematic analysis in Dips" — state the decision rule about: Toppling candidates are discontinuities dipping steeply into…::Toppling candidates are discontinuities dipping steeply into the slope, roughly parallel to the slope face within the lateral limits
What does "Run a planar-failure kinematic analysis in Dips" produce?::A screening verdict on whether a jointed rock cut is at risk of planar sliding, based on the percentage of discontinuity poles that both daylight and exceed the friction angle
Before relying on "Run a planar-failure kinematic analysis in Dips" — what do you check?::Verify the manual envelope-plus-cone construction against the software's built-in kinematic analysis result • Check the input dialog echoes the intended slope dip, dip direction and friction angle before accepting results
"Run a planar-failure kinematic analysis in Dips" — state the decision rule about: Both conditions must hold for planar failure: the plane dayl…::Both conditions must hold for planar failure: the plane daylights, and its dip exceeds the friction angle
"Run a planar-failure kinematic analysis in Dips" — state the decision rule about: If the critical percentage is below about 6 percent, planar …::If the critical percentage is below about 6 percent, planar failure is not considered a significant risk for the rock mass; in the example 1 pole out of 303 (under 1 percent) meant no planar failure c
What does "Run a probabilistic slope stability analysis in Slide2" produce?::Probability of failure, mean FS and reliability index for the critical slip surface, with input random variables (cohesion, phi, unit weight) defined statistically and convergence verified.
Before relying on "Run a probabilistic slope stability analysis in Slide2" — what do you check?::Convergence plot flat at the final PF/mean FS values; else increase samples. • Sampled statistics approach input statistics as sample count grows. • Pseudo-random vs random seed setting understood — pseudo-random gives reproducible results.
"Run a probabilistic slope stability analysis in Slide2" — state the decision rule about: Set relative min/max at least ~3 standard deviations for Nor…::Set relative min/max at least ~3 standard deviations for Normal variables so the distribution is not truncated.
"Run a probabilistic slope stability analysis in Slide2" — state the decision rule about: A reliability index of at least ~3 is the commonly recommend…::A reliability index of at least ~3 is the commonly recommended minimum assurance of safe design (tutorial guidance).
What does "Run a seismic slope stability analysis in Slide2 (pseudo-static, critical kc and Newmark displacement)" produce?::Seismic performance of a slope expressed three ways in one multi-scenario model: pseudo-static FS under a chosen seismic coefficient, the critical seismic coefficient ky giving FS = 1 per surface, and Newmark permanent displacement from a real earthquake record.
Before relying on "Run a seismic slope stability analysis in Slide2 (pseudo-static, critical kc and Newmark displacement)" — what do you check?::Seismic coefficient sign/direction matches the failure direction. • Advanced Seismic Analysis checkbox enabled before expecting ky or Newmark output. • Chosen seismic record's PGA/PGV appropriate to the site hazard; record source documented (Slide's Newmark engine is based on USGS SLAMMER).
"Run a seismic slope stability analysis in Slide2 (pseudo-static, critical kc and Newmark displacement)" — state the decision rule about: Pseudo-static FS < 1 does not itself mean failure — the ky a…::Pseudo-static FS < 1 does not itself mean failure — the ky and Newmark analyses quantify how much shaking is needed and how far the mass would move.
"Run a seismic slope stability analysis in Slide2 (pseudo-static, critical kc and Newmark displacement)" — state the decision rule about: Many surfaces with ky below the design coefficient corrobora…::Many surfaces with ky below the design coefficient corroborates a pseudo-static FS near or below 1 at that coefficient.
What does "Run a slope stability analysis with a pore water pressure grid in Slide2" produce?::A factor of safety for a slope whose pore pressures are interpolated from a discrete grid of total head (or pressure head / pore pressure) values, with ponded water modelled by a water table.
Before relying on "Run a slope stability analysis with a pore water pressure grid in Slide2" — what do you check?::Grid covers the zone slip surfaces will sample; sparse coverage produces interpolation artefacts. • Ponded water hatch appears where expected after adding the water table. • Queried pore pressure profile along the critical surface looks physically reasonable.
"Run a slope stability analysis with a pore water pressure grid in Slide2" — state the decision rule about: Points above the water table are assigned zero pore pressure…::Points above the water table are assigned zero pore pressure even if grid interpolation says otherwise — useful protection when the grid is sparse.
"Run a slope stability analysis with a pore water pressure grid in Slide2" — state the decision rule about: Choose grid type (total head vs pressure head vs pore pressu…::Choose grid type (total head vs pressure head vs pore pressure) in Project Settings to match the data source.
What does "Select layered rockfall protection measures for a rock slope" produce?::A practical, cost-conscious combination of scaling, benches, fence or barrier, ditch and drapery mesh that contains future rockfalls on a loose-rock slope
Before relying on "Select layered rockfall protection measures for a rock slope" — what do you check?::After design, confirm each hazard path is addressed: crest sources (scaled/meshed), mid-slope trajectories (bench/mesh), toe run-out (fence, barrier or ditch) • Plan periodic cleanout of benches and ditches as part of the scheme
"Select layered rockfall protection measures for a rock slope" — state the decision rule about: Scaling comes first on essentially any slope with rockfall p…::Scaling comes first on essentially any slope with rockfall potential
"Select layered rockfall protection measures for a rock slope" — state the decision rule about: Spend on high-capacity fencing only when large rock sizes or…::Spend on high-capacity fencing only when large rock sizes or high-value infrastructure justify it; modest rock sizes may need only an inexpensive fence
What does "Select, document and maintain landslide risk mitigation measures (AGS 2007)" produce?::A mitigation plan that brings landslide risk to tolerable levels, with design life, maintenance regime, responsibilities and reporting that satisfy AGS 2007 minimum standards and survive regulator scrutiny.
Before relying on "Select, document and maintain landslide risk mitigation measures (AGS 2007)" — what do you check?::Residual risk after mitigation recalculated and shown to meet the criteria — not asserted. • Design life stated on drawings; shortfall components covered by an explicit maintenance regime. • Mitigation plan reviewed for workability; land-title annotation or equivalent enforcement mechanism in place.
"Select, document and maintain landslide risk mitigation measures (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Risk cannot be removed, only reduced — if no option reaches …::Risk cannot be removed, only reduced — if no option reaches tolerable levels, development should not proceed or must be radically conditioned.
"Select, document and maintain landslide risk mitigation measures (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Monitoring/warning counts as consequence reduction only when…::Monitoring/warning counts as consequence reduction only when the warning-to-action time is realistically sufficient.
What does "Simulate rockfall trajectories and bench effectiveness in RocFall" produce?::A statistical picture of where falling rocks end up on a benched rock slope, used to judge whether a bench catches rocks or lets them reach the toe
Before relying on "Simulate rockfall trajectories and bench effectiveness in RocFall" — what do you check?::Always simulate a population of rocks with distributed parameters, not a single deterministic rock • Compare simulated behaviour with observed fallen-rock positions on site where available
"Simulate rockfall trajectories and bench effectiveness in RocFall" — state the decision rule about: If most rocks stop on the bench, the bench is effective; roc…::If most rocks stop on the bench, the bench is effective; rocks that bounce over the bench and run to the toe drive the need for further protection
"Simulate rockfall trajectories and bench effectiveness in RocFall" — state the decision rule about: Rocks that come to rest close to the bench edge should be tr…::Rocks that come to rest close to the bench edge should be treated as a future hazard — rain or wind can move them over the edge later
What does "Size a rockfall catch ditch with the Ritchie chart" produce?::Required width and depth of a catch ditch at the toe of a rock slope, from slope height and slope angle
Before relying on "Size a rockfall catch ditch with the Ritchie chart" — what do you check?::Verify the computed slope angle against the chart axis range before reading values • Confirm the ditch geometry is buildable at the site (excavation depth of the order of 1.8 m in the example)
"Size a rockfall catch ditch with the Ritchie chart" — state the decision rule about: Width and depth both increase with slope height and depend o…::Width and depth both increase with slope height and depend on slope angle; always read both line families
"Size a rockfall catch ditch with the Ritchie chart" — state the decision rule about: If the design point does not sit on chart lines, interpolate…::If the design point does not sit on chart lines, interpolate rather than rounding to the nearer line
What does "Size and position a rockfall barrier by iterative capacity testing in RocFall" produce?::A barrier location, height and energy capacity that actually stops the simulated rock population, found by iteration rather than a single guess
Before relying on "Size and position a rockfall barrier by iterative capacity testing in RocFall" — what do you check?::Re-run the full rock population after every barrier change; a barrier that stops some trajectories may still be bypassed by others • Check the animation to confirm rocks are stopped rather than bouncing over
"Size and position a rockfall barrier by iterative capacity testing in RocFall" — state the decision rule about: A cheap low-capacity fence is acceptable only if the simulat…::A cheap low-capacity fence is acceptable only if the simulation shows it stops the expected rock sizes and energies
"Size and position a rockfall barrier by iterative capacity testing in RocFall" — state the decision rule about: If neither realistic capacity nor repositioning stops the ro…::If neither realistic capacity nor repositioning stops the rocks, revisit the overall protection concept rather than forcing the barrier
