notes.text: Flashcards Slope stability flashcards/slope stability 104 cards generated from the 26 slope stability skill notes ( Question::Answer , one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here. Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not verification. Numbers still come from the source. What does "Assess staged load cases and anchor reinforcement for a planar rock slope" produce?::A comparison of factor of safety across dry, water filled, seismic and anchored cases that shows which conditions govern and what anchor force restores stability Before relying on "Assess staged load cases and anchor reinforcement for a planar rock slope" — what do you check?::Confirm the factor of safety decreases monotonically as water then seismic load are added; if not, a term has the wrong sign • Cross check each case against software (RocPlane reproduced 1.54, 1.07, 0.92 and about 1.4 with a 400 kN bolt at 35 degree plunge) "Assess staged load cases and anchor reinforcement for a planar rock slope" — state the decision rule about: Obtain the seismic coefficient from the design standard for …::Obtain the seismic coefficient from the design standard for the project region; near zero in aseismic areas, larger in seismically active countries "Assess staged load cases and anchor reinforcement for a planar rock slope" — state the decision rule about: Anchor inclination changes effectiveness — flatter or steepe…::Anchor inclination changes effectiveness — flatter or steeper installation angles raise or lower the factor of safety, so optimise angle as well as force What does "Calculate the safety factor of a rock slope against planar (block) failure" produce?::A factor of safety against sliding of a block on a planar failure surface using the simplified dry, no tension crack formula, with a stability interpretation and a cohesion sensitivity check Before relying on "Calculate the safety factor of a rock slope against planar (block) failure" — what do you check?::Angle roles not swapped: i is the face angle, theta is the failure plane dip • Units consistent (kPa with kN/m3) throughout • Sensitivity to cohesion evaluated before declaring a marginal slope stable "Calculate the safety factor of a rock slope against planar (block) failure" — state the decision rule about: FoS greater than 1 indicates stable, less than 1 unstable; a…::FoS greater than 1 indicates stable, less than 1 unstable; a value at about 1 means critical/marginally stable — a small perturbation such as some water can tip it to failure "Calculate the safety factor of a rock slope against planar (block) failure" — state the decision rule about: A failure plane dip greater than the friction angle (42 vs 3…::A failure plane dip greater than the friction angle (42 vs 33 degrees here) means friction alone cannot hold the block — cohesion is doing critical work What does "Classify rock slope movements using the Varnes movement type system" produce?::A movement type classification (fall, topple, planar or rotational slide, lateral spread, creep, or complex) for a rock slope, with the diagnostic field evidence for each Before relying on "Classify rock slope movements using the Varnes movement type system" — what do you check?::Verify the inferred failure surface shape (planar vs circular) against weathering condition • Check trigger consistency: earthquake dependent mechanisms should correlate with regional seismicity "Classify rock slope movements using the Varnes movement type system" — state the decision rule about: Daylighting discontinuity plus tension crack points to plana…::Daylighting discontinuity plus tension crack points to planar slide potential "Classify rock slope movements using the Varnes movement type system" — state the decision rule about: Gentle basal plane under a huge rock mass on saturated clay …::Gentle basal plane under a huge rock mass on saturated clay plus seismic trigger points to lateral spread; rainfall alone will not trigger it What does "Compute a planar failure factor of safety in RocPlane and verify by hand" produce?::A deterministic factor of safety for a rock block sliding on a single failure plane, cross checked against a hand calculation Before relying on "Compute a planar failure factor of safety in RocPlane and verify by hand" — what do you check?::Reproduce the software result with the hand formula at least once to confirm inputs are interpreted correctly • Double check the two unit conversions: kN/m3 to MN/m3 for unit weight, and kPa to MPa for cohesion "Compute a planar failure factor of safety in RocPlane and verify by hand" — state the decision rule about: Deterministic analysis is appropriate when each parameter ha…::Deterministic analysis is appropriate when each parameter has a single known value; use probabilistic settings if you hold ranges for cohesion, friction angle or unit weight "Compute a planar failure factor of safety in RocPlane and verify by hand" — state the decision rule about: Set the upper face angle to zero when the slope profile abov…::Set the upper face angle to zero when the slope profile above the crest is a straight continuation with no bench What does "Compute a wedge failure factor of safety in Swedge" produce?::A deterministic factor of safety for a rock wedge formed by two intersecting joints in a slope face, including sensitivity to water filling of the joints Before relying on "Compute a wedge failure factor of safety in Swedge" — what do you check?::Verify units on entry: density in t/m3 versus unit weight in MN/m3 • Run the percent filled water sweep — safety factor falls slightly at modest saturation and drops sharply at full saturation, so check the design case includes a "Compute a wedge failure factor of safety in Swedge" — state the decision rule about: The orientation of a line of intersection is described by tr…::The orientation of a line of intersection is described by trend and plunge, not dip and dip direction — the software computes it from the two joint planes "Compute a wedge failure factor of safety in Swedge" — state the decision rule about: For observed wedge failures, cohesion on the joints is typic…::For observed wedge failures, cohesion on the joints is typically taken as zero, leaving friction to resist sliding What does "Compute the factor of safety of a planar rock slope failure with tension crack by hand" produce?::A hand calculated factor of safety for a planar failure surface behind a slope crest, including geometry derived tension crack depth, failure plane length and block weight Before relying on "Compute the factor of safety of a planar rock slope failure with tension crack by hand" — what do you check?::Confirm all forces are expressed per metre width of slope so units are consistent (kN/m) • Check that omitted effects (seismic, water, anchor) are explicitly zeroed rather than left in with stale values • Compare the dry slope result against software (RocPlane reproduces 1.54 for this example) "Compute the factor of safety of a planar rock slope failure with tension crack by hand" — state the decision rule about: Factor of safety above 1 indicates stability; below 1 indica…::Factor of safety above 1 indicates stability; below 1 indicates the block can fail "Compute the factor of safety of a planar rock slope failure with tension crack by hand" — state the decision rule about: Water in the tension crack acts twice: U reduces frictional …::Water in the tension crack acts twice: U reduces frictional resistance and V adds driving force — include both What does "Compute traffic exposure ratings (average vehicle risk and percent decision sight distance) for rockfall rating" produce?::Two traffic related inputs to the rockfall hazard rating: the average vehicle risk along the affected road length and the ratio of actual to decision sight distance Before relying on "Compute traffic exposure ratings (average vehicle risk and percent decision sight distance) for rockfall rating" — what do you check?::Confirm the road length was converted to kilometres before use • Confirm units of traffic volume (per hour vs per day) match the formula form being used "Compute traffic exposure ratings (average vehicle risk and percent decision sight distance) for rockfall rating" — state the decision rule about: If computed average vehicle risk exceeds 100 percent, cap it…::If computed average vehicle risk exceeds 100 percent, cap it at 100 percent (maximum points) for the rating "Compute traffic exposure ratings (average vehicle risk and percent decision sight distance) for rockfall rating" — state the decision rule about: Lower percent decision sight distance is worse; if close to …::Lower percent decision sight distance is worse; if close to a tabulated boundary and no time to interpolate, adopt the worse (higher point) category What does "Conduct a landslide hazard analysis and build the site geotechnical model (AGS 2007)" produce?::A documented geotechnical model with characterised landslide hazards, estimated annual probabilities and travel distances, forming the front half of a defensible Landslide Risk Management (LRM) report. Before relying on "Conduct a landslide hazard analysis and build the site geotechnical model (AGS 2007)" — what do you check?::Cross sections at natural scale (plus a natural scale summary if exaggeration used). • Hazards addressed above, below and adjacent to the site, not just within the lot. • Frequency reasoning documented transparently, with sensitivity/uncertainty stated; expert judgement accuracy typically half to two orders of magnitude. "Conduct a landslide hazard analysis and build the site geotechnical model (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Choose the qualitative likelihood term FROM the estimated pr…::Choose the qualitative likelihood term FROM the estimated probability — never adopt a probability from a qualitative term (practitioners diverge by orders of magnitude, Section 5.4.2(a)). "Conduct a landslide hazard analysis and build the site geotechnical model (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Investigation is adequate only when the model explains slope…::Investigation is adequate only when the model explains slope processes, landslide extent, triggers and process rates; otherwise investigate further (Section 5.2.8). What does "Estimate landslide risk and evaluate it against tolerable criteria (AGS 2007)" produce?::Quantified risk to life and quantified or qualitative risk to property for every landslide hazard, summed and compared against regulator tolerable risk criteria to decide accept/treat. Before relying on "Estimate landslide risk and evaluate it against tolerable criteria (AGS 2007)" — what do you check?::All hazards summed — not just the dominant one — for comparison with criteria. • P(T:S) between 0 and 1, with building occupancy taken as ~1.0 for houses per Section 7.1 unless justified. • Sensitivity of the result to uncertain inputs displayed; conservative outcome adopted where unjustified uncertainty remains. "Estimate landslide risk and evaluate it against tolerable criteria (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Risk to life is always assessed quantitatively for the perso…::Risk to life is always assessed quantitatively for the person most at risk; property risk may be qualitative/semi quantitative for screening or data poor cases (Sections 3.3.4, 7.2). "Estimate landslide risk and evaluate it against tolerable criteria (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Existing landslides attract the stricter 'new' criterion eve…::Existing landslides attract the stricter 'new' criterion even if remediation is not otherwise required (Table 1 note 5). What does "Estimate wedge failure factor of safety with the wedge factor K method" produce?::A quick friction only factor of safety for a rock wedge formed by two intersecting discontinuity planes, identifying whether the wedge is stable Before relying on "Estimate wedge failure factor of safety with the wedge factor K method" — what do you check?::Verify which given angle is plunge vs trend before computing (two digit vs three digit convention) • Check that unused given data (e.g. slope face dip/dip direction) was genuinely not required rather than forgotten "Estimate wedge failure factor of safety with the wedge factor K method" — state the decision rule about: K greater than 1 reflects the wedging effect: a wedge confin…::K greater than 1 reflects the wedging effect: a wedge confined by two planes is more stable than an equivalent planar block at the same inclination "Estimate wedge failure factor of safety with the wedge factor K method" — state the decision rule about: This hand method excludes cohesion and water pressure; when …::This hand method excludes cohesion and water pressure; when either matters, or geometry is complex, move to software analysis What does "Forecast time to rock slope collapse from displacement monitoring data" produce?::An empirical estimate of the number of days until collapse of an accelerating rock slide, from the onset velocity of progressive movement Before relying on "Forecast time to rock slope collapse from displacement monitoring data" — what do you check?::Confirm the trend of the progressive stage is well established (near linear on the chart) before extrapolating • Read the log velocity axis carefully; small reading errors change the forecast substantially "Forecast time to rock slope collapse from displacement monitoring data" — state the decision rule about: Regressive stage movement alone does not warrant collapse fo…::Regressive stage movement alone does not warrant collapse forecasting; the method applies once progressive acceleration is established "Forecast time to rock slope collapse from displacement monitoring data" — state the decision rule about: Treat the forecast as an order of magnitude planning tool: t…::Treat the forecast as an order of magnitude planning tool: the correlation is highly empirical and will not hold in all cases What does "Rate rockfall hazard for a slope inventory using a point based rating system" produce?::A summed hazard rating for each inspected slope that ranks it for remediation priority and sets the re inspection or mitigation response Before relying on "Rate rockfall hazard for a slope inventory using a point based rating system" — what do you check?::Confirm every factor received a score and that extrapolated scores respect the table caps • Cross check subjective scores (geology, history, ditch) against the written site description • Verify the same rating system and category boundaries are used consistently across the whole inventory so rankings are comparable "Rate rockfall hazard for a slope inventory using a point based rating system" — state the decision rule about: Total below about 300 points: low priority, re inspect on th…::Total below about 300 points: low priority, re inspect on the normal cycle "Rate rockfall hazard for a slope inventory using a point based rating system" — state the decision rule about: Total of about 500 points or more: act immediately with reme…::Total of about 500 points or more: act immediately with remedial works What does "Run a Monte Carlo probabilistic planar failure analysis in RocPlane" produce?::A probability of failure and factor of safety distribution for a planar rock slope that reflects the measured scatter in strength and water conditions Before relying on "Run a Monte Carlo probabilistic planar failure analysis in RocPlane" — what do you check?::Cumulative probability read at factor of safety = 1 must match the reported probability of failure • Relative min/max plus the mean must stay within physical bounds (0 100 percent for water fill) • Zero probability of failure should correspond to a histogram entirely above factor of safety 1 "Run a Monte Carlo probabilistic planar failure analysis in RocPlane" — state the decision rule about: Vary only parameters with real measured uncertainty; fixing …::Vary only parameters with real measured uncertainty; fixing well surveyed geometry keeps the result interpretable "Run a Monte Carlo probabilistic planar failure analysis in RocPlane" — state the decision rule about: Water fill percentage dominates the failure probability in t…::Water fill percentage dominates the failure probability in this problem — invest site investigation effort there What does "Run a basic circular slip surface slope stability analysis in Slide2 (Quick Start)" produce?::A computed factor of safety and critical circular slip surface for a homogeneous dry slope, using a Grid Search, with results interpreted and a second scenario compared. Before relying on "Run a basic circular slip surface slope stability analysis in Slide2 (Quick Start)" — what do you check?::Search coverage adequate (contours and surface cloud reviewed), not just the single reported FS. • Results consistent across at least two search methods before relying on the minimum FS. "Run a basic circular slip surface slope stability analysis in Slide2 (Quick Start)" — state the decision rule about: Treat 'Global Minimum' with caution — it is only the minimum…::Treat 'Global Minimum' with caution — it is only the minimum among surfaces actually searched; grid location, spacing, Radius Increment and Slope Limits all change the answer. "Run a basic circular slip surface slope stability analysis in Slide2 (Quick Start)" — state the decision rule about: The critical surface can differ between analysis methods; ch…::The critical surface can differ between analysis methods; check each method separately. What does "Run a deterministic planar failure analysis in RocPlane and cross validate hand calculations" produce?::A software factor of safety for a planar rock slope failure under dry, wet, seismic and anchored cases that matches independent hand calculation Before relying on "Run a deterministic planar failure analysis in RocPlane and cross validate hand calculations" — what do you check?::Wedge weight, failure plane length, tension crack length, U and V reported by the software should reproduce hand calculated values (1241 kN/m, 13.3 m, 4.35 m, 2 • Each added adverse effect should lower the factor of safety; each support should raise it "Run a deterministic planar failure analysis in RocPlane and cross validate hand calculations" — state the decision rule about: Horizontal seismic direction is the worst case for this geom…::Horizontal seismic direction is the worst case for this geometry "Run a deterministic planar failure analysis in RocPlane and cross validate hand calculations" — state the decision rule about: Decreasing the bolt plunge angle increases stability for thi…::Decreasing the bolt plunge angle increases stability for this setup — vary plunge and force to reach the target factor of safety What does "Run a finite element groundwater seepage analysis coupled with slope stability in Slide2" produce?::A steady state FE seepage solution (phreatic surface, pore pressure/total head contours, flow vectors) whose pore pressures feed directly into the limit equilibrium slope stability run, including optional matric suction strength above the water table. "Run a finite element groundwater seepage analysis coupled with slope stability in Slide2" — state the decision rule about: Always compute and review the groundwater solution separatel…::Always compute and review the groundwater solution separately before the stability analysis, even though Slide will chain them automatically. "Run a finite element groundwater seepage analysis coupled with slope stability in Slide2" — state the decision rule about: Negative pressure heads above the water table are matric suc…::Negative pressure heads above the water table are matric suction; they affect strength only if phi b 0. slip limit and lateral limits Before relying on "Run a flexural toppling kinematic analysis in Dips" — what do you check?::Cross check the manual plane and cone construction against the built in kinematic analysis output • Verify the friction angle entered matches the investigation value (the lecturer initially mistyped 30 for 35) "Run a flexural toppling kinematic analysis in Dips" — state the decision rule about: A critical pole percentage above about 6 percent raises a re…::A critical pole percentage above about 6 percent raises a red flag and warrants a more thorough toppling investigation (the example returned 20 of 303 poles = 6.6 percent, flagged as a concern) "Run a flexural toppling kinematic analysis in Dips" — state the decision rule about: Toppling candidates are discontinuities dipping steeply into…::Toppling candidates are discontinuities dipping steeply into the slope, roughly parallel to the slope face within the lateral limits What does "Run a planar failure kinematic analysis in Dips" produce?::A screening verdict on whether a jointed rock cut is at risk of planar sliding, based on the percentage of discontinuity poles that both daylight and exceed the friction angle Before relying on "Run a planar failure kinematic analysis in Dips" — what do you check?::Verify the manual envelope plus cone construction against the software's built in kinematic analysis result • Check the input dialog echoes the intended slope dip, dip direction and friction angle before accepting results "Run a planar failure kinematic analysis in Dips" — state the decision rule about: Both conditions must hold for planar failure: the plane dayl…::Both conditions must hold for planar failure: the plane daylights, and its dip exceeds the friction angle "Run a planar failure kinematic analysis in Dips" — state the decision rule about: If the critical percentage is below about 6 percent, planar …::If the critical percentage is below about 6 percent, planar failure is not considered a significant risk for the rock mass; in the example 1 pole out of 303 (under 1 percent) meant no planar failure c What does "Run a probabilistic slope stability analysis in Slide2" produce?::Probability of failure, mean FS and reliability index for the critical slip surface, with input random variables (cohesion, phi, unit weight) defined statistically and convergence verified. What does "Select layered rockfall protection measures for a rock slope" produce?::A practical, cost conscious combination of scaling, benches, fence or barrier, ditch and drapery mesh that contains future rockfalls on a loose rock slope Before relying on "Select layered rockfall protection measures for a rock slope" — what do you check?::After design, confirm each hazard path is addressed: crest sources (scaled/meshed), mid slope trajectories (bench/mesh), toe run out (fence, barrier or ditch) • Plan periodic cleanout of benches and ditches as part of the scheme "Select layered rockfall protection measures for a rock slope" — state the decision rule about: Scaling comes first on essentially any slope with rockfall p…::Scaling comes first on essentially any slope with rockfall potential "Select layered rockfall protection measures for a rock slope" — state the decision rule about: Spend on high capacity fencing only when large rock sizes or…::Spend on high capacity fencing only when large rock sizes or high value infrastructure justify it; modest rock sizes may need only an inexpensive fence What does "Select, document and maintain landslide risk mitigation measures (AGS 2007)" produce?::A mitigation plan that brings landslide risk to tolerable levels, with design life, maintenance regime, responsibilities and reporting that satisfy AGS 2007 minimum standards and survive regulator scrutiny. Before relying on "Select, document and maintain landslide risk mitigation measures (AGS 2007)" — what do you check?::Residual risk after mitigation recalculated and shown to meet the criteria — not asserted. • Design life stated on drawings; shortfall components covered by an explicit maintenance regime. • Mitigation plan reviewed for workability; land title annotation or equivalent enforcement mechanism in place. "Select, document and maintain landslide risk mitigation measures (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Risk cannot be removed, only reduced — if no option reaches …::Risk cannot be removed, only reduced — if no option reaches tolerable levels, development should not proceed or must be radically conditioned. "Select, document and maintain landslide risk mitigation measures (AGS 2007)" — state the decision rule about: Monitoring/warning counts as consequence reduction only when…::Monitoring/warning counts as consequence reduction only when the warning to action time is realistically sufficient. What does "Simulate rockfall trajectories and bench effectiveness in RocFall" produce?::A statistical picture of where falling rocks end up on a benched rock slope, used to judge whether a bench catches rocks or lets them reach the toe Before relying on "Simulate rockfall trajectories and bench effectiveness in RocFall" — what do you check?::Always simulate a population of rocks with distributed parameters, not a single deterministic rock • Compare simulated behaviour with observed fallen rock positions on site where available "Simulate rockfall trajectories and bench effectiveness in RocFall" — state the decision rule about: If most rocks stop on the bench, the bench is effective; roc…::If most rocks stop on the bench, the bench is effective; rocks that bounce over the bench and run to the toe drive the need for further protection "Simulate rockfall trajectories and bench effectiveness in RocFall" — state the decision rule about: Rocks that come to rest close to the bench edge should be tr…::Rocks that come to rest close to the bench edge should be treated as a future hazard — rain or wind can move them over the edge later What does "Size a rockfall catch ditch with the Ritchie chart" produce?::Required width and depth of a catch ditch at the toe of a rock slope, from slope height and slope angle Before relying on "Size a rockfall catch ditch with the Ritchie chart" — what do you check?::Verify the computed slope angle against the chart axis range before reading values • Confirm the ditch geometry is buildable at the site (excavation depth of the order of 1.8 m in the example) "Size a rockfall catch ditch with the Ritchie chart" — state the decision rule about: Width and depth both increase with slope height and depend o…::Width and depth both increase with slope height and depend on slope angle; always read both line families "Size a rockfall catch ditch with the Ritchie chart" — state the decision rule about: If the design point does not sit on chart lines, interpolate…::If the design point does not sit on chart lines, interpolate rather than rounding to the nearer line What does "Size and position a rockfall barrier by iterative capacity testing in RocFall" produce?::A barrier location, height and energy capacity that actually stops the simulated rock population, found by iteration rather than a single guess Before relying on "Size and position a rockfall barrier by iterative capacity testing in RocFall" — what do you check?::Re run the full rock population after every barrier change; a barrier that stops some trajectories may still be bypassed by others • Check the animation to confirm rocks are stopped rather than bouncing over "Size and position a rockfall barrier by iterative capacity testing in RocFall" — state the decision rule about: A cheap low capacity fence is acceptable only if the simulat…::A cheap low capacity fence is acceptable only if the simulation shows it stops the expected rock sizes and energies "Size and position a rockfall barrier by iterative capacity testing in RocFall" — state the decision rule about: If neither realistic capacity nor repositioning stops the ro…::If neither realistic capacity nor repositioning stops the rocks, revisit the overall protection concept rather than forcing the barrier Related Learning path Slope stability Learning loop

notes.body:
# Flashcards - Field and laboratory testing

#flashcards/testing

101 cards generated from the 26 field and laboratory testing skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Assess earthworks lot acceptance statistically from PLT results" produce?::The engineer can decide, per the German ZTV E-StB scheme, whether an inspection lot of compacted ground passes based on randomly located test results.
Before relying on "Assess earthworks lot acceptance statistically from PLT results" — what do you check?::Confirm n matches the lot-size table before testing. • Verify the requirement is expressed as a 10% minimum quantile before applying the Q formula.
"Assess earthworks lot acceptance statistically from PLT results" — state the decision rule about: The statistical method suits any ground but is particularly …::The statistical method suits any ground but is particularly recommended for large lots, lots where uniformity of compaction matters, quick-turnaround test methods, and trial compactions (p. 5-6).
"Assess earthworks lot acceptance statistically from PLT results" — state the decision rule about: Rejection applies to the whole lot area, not just failing po…::Rejection applies to the whole lot area, not just failing points.
What does "Calculate Ev1 and Ev2 deformation moduli from a PLT load-settlement curve" produce?::The engineer can fit the measured load-settlement data and compute the first- and second-cycle strain moduli the way the AX01 evaluation does, and check machine output by hand.
Before relying on "Calculate Ev1 and Ev2 deformation moduli from a PLT load-settlement curve" — what do you check?::The fitted polynomial should track the measured curve smoothly; the worked example gives Ev1 = 43 MN/m2 and Ev2 = 94 MN/m2 for its curve (p. 4). • Hand-calculated values should match the AX01 electronic evaluation for the same data.
"Calculate Ev1 and Ev2 deformation moduli from a PLT load-settlement curve" — state the decision rule about: Use sigma_0max of the cycle being evaluated in the secant fo…::Use sigma_0max of the cycle being evaluated in the secant formula.
"Calculate Ev1 and Ev2 deformation moduli from a PLT load-settlement curve" — state the decision rule about: Ev2/Ev1 serves as the compaction parameter; Ev1 and Ev2 char…::Ev2/Ev1 serves as the compaction parameter; Ev1 and Ev2 characterise stiffness (p. 11).
What does "Calculate the Westergaard modulus of subgrade reaction from PLT data" produce?::The engineer can derive the subgrade reaction modulus ks for pavement or airfield design from a plate load test, including the correction when a 300 mm plate is used instead of 762 mm.
Before relying on "Calculate the Westergaard modulus of subgrade reaction from PLT data" — what do you check?::Hand value should match the ks on the DIN-mode printout (the sample record shows 40 MN/m3). • Confirm the stress was read from the first-loading branch, not the reload curve.
"Calculate the Westergaard modulus of subgrade reaction from PLT data" — state the decision rule about: The 300 mm plate substitution is only reasonable when the la…::The 300 mm plate substitution is only reasonable when the layer beneath the plate is homogeneous to a depth of 1.5 times the plate diameter (stated 'without liability', p. 11).
What does "Check Ev2 and Ev2/Ev1 against German subgrade and base course requirements" produce?::The engineer can compare measured moduli with the ZTV E-StB / ZTV SoB-StB acceptance values for formation levels, frost protection layers and unbound base courses, and use PLT as a stand-in for density testing on coarse soils.
Before relying on "Check Ev2 and Ev2/Ev1 against German subgrade and base course requirements" — what do you check?::Confirm both the Ev2 floor and the Ev2/Ev1 ceiling are satisfied before assigning a degree of compaction. • Confirm the underlying formation modulus tier (Ev2 >= 120 or >= 100 MN/m2) before selecting the base course requirement.
"Check Ev2 and Ev2/Ev1 against German subgrade and base course requirements" — state the decision rule about: Choose the quantile-based check (ZTV E-StB) for earthworks l…::Choose the quantile-based check (ZTV E-StB) for earthworks lots and the minimum-value check (ZTV SoB-StB) for unbound base courses.
"Check Ev2 and Ev2/Ev1 against German subgrade and base course requirements" — state the decision rule about: PLT-for-density substitution only applies to coarse/mixed so…::PLT-for-density substitution only applies to coarse/mixed soils with fines below 15% by mass.
What does "Clean, pack and store PLT equipment after testing" produce?::The engineer can decommission the kit in a way that avoids corrosion and sensor damage, and route the day's data to the supervising engineers.
Before relying on "Clean, pack and store PLT equipment after testing" — what do you check?::Case interior and equipment are dry before closing. • Datasheet is fully completed and data has been handed to the supervising engineers.
"Clean, pack and store PLT equipment after testing" — state the decision rule about: If moisture is found in the case, dry the open case indoors …::If moisture is found in the case, dry the open case indoors before storage rather than packing wet.
What does "Compute the size-corrected point load strength index Is(50) from test data" produce?::A normalised point load strength index Is(50) for each valid test, from peak load and sample dimensions, for both diametral and axial loading configurations
Before relying on "Compute the size-corrected point load strength index Is(50) from test data" — what do you check?::De route matches the loading configuration (direct diameter for diametral, equivalent-area formula for axial) • Units consistent: P in kN, dimensions in mm, with the factor of 1000 applied once • Size correction applied after, not instead of, the uncorrected index calculation
"Compute the size-corrected point load strength index Is(50) from test data" — state the decision rule about: A markedly low Is(50) may reflect weathering or an invalid f…::A markedly low Is(50) may reflect weathering or an invalid failure mode from the test rather than intrinsic strength — check the test video/record before reporting
"Compute the size-corrected point load strength index Is(50) from test data" — state the decision rule about: A spreadsheet with the formulas pre-built is the practical w…::A spreadsheet with the formulas pre-built is the practical way to process multiple tests
What does "Derive rock mass strength parameters from triaxial test data with Hoek-Brown fitting in RSData" produce?::Intact rock parameters (UCS, mi) fitted from triaxial data and scaled rock mass parameters (rock mass UCS, tensile strength, cohesion, friction angle) for a specific slope application
Before relying on "Derive rock mass strength parameters from triaxial test data with Hoek-Brown fitting in RSData" — what do you check?::Confirm the fitted curve passes sensibly through the test points before accepting UCS and mi • Verify the parameter panel switches from intact-rock to rock-mass labelling after GSI and D are applied • Check the envelope stress range corresponds to the actual slope height
"Derive rock mass strength parameters from triaxial test data with Hoek-Brown fitting in RSData" — state the decision rule about: Prefer laboratory-derived mi over tabulated mi by lithology;…::Prefer laboratory-derived mi over tabulated mi by lithology; use the table only when no test data exist
"Derive rock mass strength parameters from triaxial test data with Hoek-Brown fitting in RSData" — state the decision rule about: GSI 100 means intact sample scale — never carry intact param…::GSI 100 means intact sample scale — never carry intact parameters directly into rock mass design
What does "Determine UCS and Young's modulus from unconfined compression test data" produce?::A stress-strain curve, peak unconfined compressive strength, and Young's modulus (E) for a rock core from raw load-deformation laboratory data
Before relying on "Determine UCS and Young's modulus from unconfined compression test data" — what do you check?::Confirm strain was converted out of percent before dividing — this is the step that most commonly corrupts E by a factor of 100 • Confirm load-to-stress conversion units (kN over m2 gives kPa)
"Determine UCS and Young's modulus from unconfined compression test data" — state the decision rule about: Very small strain ranges at failure (of order 0.05%) indicat…::Very small strain ranges at failure (of order 0.05%) indicate a hard rock likely to show brittle behaviour
"Determine UCS and Young's modulus from unconfined compression test data" — state the decision rule about: A very high computed E is plausible when measured strains ar…::A very high computed E is plausible when measured strains are very low — sanity-check E against how stiff the curve looks
What does "Determine the CBR of cement- or lime-stabilised road materials to RMS T132" produce?::A reported soaked CBR, dry density and swell for road materials modified/stabilised with small proportions of cementitious binder, for either laboratory mix designs or field-mixed samples.
Before relying on "Determine the CBR of cement- or lime-stabilised road materials to RMS T132" — what do you check?::Mixing-to-compaction time window observed (simulates field workability loss). • Available lime (CaO + Ca(OH)2) verified via T430 or supplier certification when lime is used. • Binder in the lab matches the field additive source and grading where possible — coarse quicklime can hydrate after compaction and disintegrate specimens (Claus
"Determine the CBR of cement- or lime-stabilised road materials to RMS T132" — state the decision rule about: The method is not applicable to heavily bound materials or h…::The method is not applicable to heavily bound materials or high binder contents — penetration resistance becomes too high (Clause 1(b)).
"Determine the CBR of cement- or lime-stabilised road materials to RMS T132" — state the decision rule about: If penetration cannot exceed 2.5 mm, the CBR test is not app…::If penetration cannot exceed 2.5 mm, the CBR test is not appropriate and must be abandoned; beyond 2.5 mm, terminate to protect equipment and record maximum penetration (Clause 6(w)).
What does "Determine the California Bearing Ratio of remoulded road construction material to RMS T117" produce?::A reported CBR (with swell, densities and moisture ratios) for a laboratory-compacted, optionally soaked specimen of the passing-19 mm fraction of a road construction material.
Before relying on "Determine the California Bearing Ratio of remoulded road construction material to RMS T117" — what do you check?::LMR and LDR of the moulded specimen within target tolerances; report both target and achieved values. • Force device calibrated over the range appropriate to the expected CBR. • Layer thickness uniformity within ~5 mm; specimen not underfilled/overfilled beyond limits (else remould with fresh material).
"Determine the California Bearing Ratio of remoulded road construction material to RMS T117" — state the decision rule about: Static compaction is not permitted for this test (Clause 2(c…::Static compaction is not permitted for this test (Clause 2(c)).
"Determine the California Bearing Ratio of remoulded road construction material to RMS T117" — state the decision rule about: If penetration of at least 2.5 mm cannot be achieved, stop a…::If penetration of at least 2.5 mm cannot be achieved, stop and report maximum penetration only.
What does "Determine the liquid limit of road construction materials to TfNSW T108" produce?::A reported liquid limit (to the stated rounding, or 'Not obtainable') for soils, gravels, crushed rock, recycled and RAP materials, derived from a multi-point Casagrande-apparatus test.
Before relying on "Determine the liquid limit of road construction materials to TfNSW T108" — what do you check?::Apparatus check results recorded (drop height, wear, hinge play, tool tip width) before testing. • Consecutive-blow agreement within one blow before accepting each point. • Points evenly distributed across the specified blow range and taken drier-to-wetter.
"Determine the liquid limit of road construction materials to TfNSW T108" — state the decision rule about: If the soil pat slips in the cup, remix with added water and…::If the soil pat slips in the cup, remix with added water and retry; if slipping persists, discard results and report that the liquid limit could not be obtained (Clause 6(d)(iv)).
"Determine the liquid limit of road construction materials to TfNSW T108" — state the decision rule about: If blow count increases after adding water, reject all previ…::If blow count increases after adding water, reject all previous points and restart from the mixing step (Clause 6(f)).
What does "Estimate on-site elastic modulus from laboratory CBR-mold plate bearing tests" produce?::The engineer can predict the field elastic modulus of a compacted coarse-grained soil from small-scale laboratory plate load tests in a CBR mold, using the paper's calibrated equations.
Before relying on "Estimate on-site elastic modulus from laboratory CBR-mold plate bearing tests" — what do you check?::Laboratory density and water content replicate the field values before crediting the prediction. • The lab-to-field regression assumes a zero intercept (no load, no settlement); confirm the fitted trend is roughly linear for your soil.
"Estimate on-site elastic modulus from laboratory CBR-mold plate bearing tests" — state the decision rule about: Use this approach for coarse-grained embankment/subgrade soi…::Use this approach for coarse-grained embankment/subgrade soils where triaxial or oedometer moduli are impractical (largest grains too big relative to standard molds).
"Estimate on-site elastic modulus from laboratory CBR-mold plate bearing tests" — state the decision rule about: For maximum stiffness and least settlement, compact on the d…::For maximum stiffness and least settlement, compact on the dry side of optimum water content - moduli fell as compaction water content rose (Conclusions, p. 10).
What does "Estimate rock unconfined compressive strength from Schmidt hammer rebound data" produce?::A defensible UCS estimate (as a range, in MPa) for a rock surface from ten field rebound readings, with or without a measured rock density
Before relying on "Estimate rock unconfined compressive strength from Schmidt hammer rebound data" — what do you check?::Confirm exactly the highest and lowest of the ten readings were removed before averaging • Confirm units: unit weight in kN/m3, strength in MPa
"Estimate rock unconfined compressive strength from Schmidt hammer rebound data" — state the decision rule about: If rock density is unknown (common in the field), assume an …::If rock density is unknown (common in the field), assume an average rock unit weight of 27 kN/m3 rather than skipping the estimate
"Estimate rock unconfined compressive strength from Schmidt hammer rebound data" — state the decision rule about: Report a strength range (e.g. about 67-69 MPa); small differ…::Report a strength range (e.g. about 67-69 MPa); small differences in chart reading are acceptable
What does "Interpret an AX01a printed plate bearing test record" produce?::The engineer can read a DIN 18134-300 test record, verify its metadata, and judge pass/fail against the nominal Ev2 and Ev2/Ev1 targets.
Before relying on "Interpret an AX01a printed plate bearing test record" — what do you check?::Deflection at the end of unloading versus the first-cycle maximum gives the plastic (unrecovered) settlement. • GPS coordinates match the intended test location.
"Interpret an AX01a printed plate bearing test record" — state the decision rule about: Both the Ev2 floor and the Ev2/Ev1 ceiling must pass for com…::Both the Ev2 floor and the Ev2/Ev1 ceiling must pass for compaction acceptance; a high Ev2 alone does not save a failed ratio.
"Interpret an AX01a printed plate bearing test record" — state the decision rule about: A failed ratio with adequate Ev2 typically signals further c…::A failed ratio with adequate Ev2 typically signals further compaction of the layer is achievable.
What does "Maintain, calibrate and troubleshoot the AX 01a plate bearing tester" produce?::The engineer can keep the device within its calibration and safety regime and diagnose common hydraulic faults in the field.
Before relying on "Maintain, calibrate and troubleshoot the AX 01a plate bearing tester" — what do you check?::Calibration date on the device Info screen is within the last year. • Force zero is checked (and reset unloaded if drifted, e.g. from temperature) before testing (p. 13).
"Maintain, calibrate and troubleshoot the AX 01a plate bearing tester" — state the decision rule about: Any visible damage means do not test - the manual treats thi…::Any visible damage means do not test - the manual treats this as a potentially fatal hazard.
"Maintain, calibrate and troubleshoot the AX 01a plate bearing tester" — state the decision rule about: Repairs only by Anix or Anix-authorised staff; non-genuine p…::Repairs only by Anix or Anix-authorised staff; non-genuine parts void safe operation.
What does "Perform point load tests with sample-geometry screening and failure-mode vetting" produce?::Valid peak failure loads from point load tests on rock core, with unsuitable samples and invalid failure modes screened out
Before relying on "Perform point load tests with sample-geometry screening and failure-mode vetting" — what do you check?::Geometry check passed and recorded before loading • Failure plane inspected and judged valid before the force reading is kept • Peak force and dimensions written down immediately per test
"Perform point load tests with sample-geometry screening and failure-mode vetting" — state the decision rule about: Reject a test where failure ran along a pre-existing crack o…::Reject a test where failure ran along a pre-existing crack or broke only at the sample edge (seen with a weathered sample that failed at 0.265 kN); weathered samples are prone to this
"Perform point load tests with sample-geometry screening and failure-mode vetting" — state the decision rule about: One or two samples is never enough — a minimum of three test…::One or two samples is never enough — a minimum of three tests per rock type, more if material is available
What does "Plan and interpret a seismic geophysical survey for site investigation" produce?::A cost-effective picture of subsurface layer boundaries over a large area from seismic wave velocities, correctly caveated and tied to borehole control
Before relying on "Plan and interpret a seismic geophysical survey for site investigation" — what do you check?::Confirm layer boundary picks against borehole logs before reporting • Sanity-check velocity-derived strength classes against samples taken from the borehole
"Plan and interpret a seismic geophysical survey for site investigation" — state the decision rule about: Choose seismic methods when the area is large and budget mat…::Choose seismic methods when the area is large and budget matters: cheaper than boreholes, SPT or lab programmes, and covers area rather than points
"Plan and interpret a seismic geophysical survey for site investigation" — state the decision rule about: Never interpret geology from velocities without borehole con…::Never interpret geology from velocities without borehole confirmation; the combination of seismic coverage plus borehole control is presented as the best approach
What does "Prepare equipment and field records before a plate load test" produce?::The engineer can mobilise to site with a complete, serviceable PLT kit and a datasheet that captures all identifying information before loading begins.
Before relying on "Prepare equipment and field records before a plate load test" — what do you check?::All items on the equipment list are packed before leaving. • Every header field on the datasheet is completed before the test starts.
"Prepare equipment and field records before a plate load test" — state the decision rule about: Recharge whenever battery charge is under 50% (p. 1).…::Recharge whenever battery charge is under 50% (p. 1).
"Prepare equipment and field records before a plate load test" — state the decision rule about: Do not proceed to site with damaged equipment, especially da…::Do not proceed to site with damaged equipment, especially damaged hydraulic hoses.
What does "Run a DIN 18134 plate load test on the AX 01a" produce?::The engineer can execute the full two-cycle DIN 18134 loading sequence on the AX 01a electronic box and obtain Ev1, Ev2 and their ratio on site.
Before relying on "Run a DIN 18134 plate load test on the AX 01a" — what do you check?::Force reading is zero before preload; settlement auto-zeroed at Adjust and preload steps. • Watch the tilt of the hydraulic cylinder and extension throughout loading (p. 7). • Results screen shows record number, date/time, Ev1, Ev2 and the ratio.
"Run a DIN 18134 plate load test on the AX 01a" — state the decision rule about: Holding ON/OFF for about 2 s aborts the test with nothing st…::Holding ON/OFF for about 2 s aborts the test with nothing stored - use only to abandon a test.
"Run a DIN 18134 plate load test on the AX 01a" — state the decision rule about: If the sequence is not completed, the device cannot compute …::If the sequence is not completed, the device cannot compute Ev1/Ev2 and will show no moduli (p. 8).
What does "Run a plate load test to Norwegian standard SVV 15.328 on the AX 01a" produce?::The engineer can switch the AX 01a to the SVV 15.328 procedure, hold stages to a settlement-rate criterion instead of fixed times, and read E1/E2 from the printout.
Before relying on "Run a plate load test to Norwegian standard SVV 15.328 on the AX 01a" — what do you check?::No underlined readings should be stored - underlining flags settlement still exceeding 0.02 mm since the last reading. • Printout lists E1, E2 and alternate E2 values for review.
"Run a plate load test to Norwegian standard SVV 15.328 on the AX 01a" — state the decision rule about: Use SVV mode when the project specifies Norwegian road-admin…::Use SVV mode when the project specifies Norwegian road-administration testing; stage holds are settlement-rate governed, unlike DIN's fixed 60 s.
"Run a plate load test to Norwegian standard SVV 15.328 on the AX 01a" — state the decision rule about: Pick the alternate E2 for a lower stage when the upper part …::Pick the alternate E2 for a lower stage when the upper part of the second-cycle curve departs from straight.
What does "Run an on-site plate bearing test with time-settlement acceptance criteria" produce?::The engineer can execute an ASTM D 1194-style plate bearing test on compacted fill, recording settlement over time and knowing when a load stage is complete.
Before relying on "Run an on-site plate bearing test with time-settlement acceptance criteria" — what do you check?::Settlement rate below 0.02 mm/min before ending a stage. • Total settlement under 25 mm. • Post-test density and moisture confirm the layer met compaction targets (at least 95% of modified maximum dry unit weight in the paper's practice).
"Run an on-site plate bearing test with time-settlement acceptance criteria" — state the decision rule about: Use stress in the 50-150 kPa range when the data will feed t…::Use stress in the 50-150 kPa range when the data will feed the elastic-modulus formula (Eq. 1).
"Run an on-site plate bearing test with time-settlement acceptance criteria" — state the decision rule about: Compare wet-side, OWC and dry-side results separately - sett…::Compare wet-side, OWC and dry-side results separately - settlement rises with compaction water content.
What does "Run the slake durability test through two cycles and record the masses for the durability index" produce?::A complete set of drum-and-sample mass records over two wet-dry abrasion cycles, ready for computing the second-cycle slake durability index used for durability classification
Before relying on "Run the slake durability test through two cycles and record the masses for the durability index" — what do you check?::Water level set at the pre-marked height about 20 mm below the drum axis before each cycle • Drum connections secure before rotation • All four masses recorded: empty drum, drum+rock initial, drum+rock after cycle 1 drying, drum+rock after cycle 2 drying
"Run the slake durability test through two cycles and record the masses for the durability index" — state the decision rule about: The classification is based on the second-cycle index, so th…::The classification is based on the second-cycle index, so the test is not complete after one cycle
"Run the slake durability test through two cycles and record the masses for the durability index" — state the decision rule about: Follow the Franklin and Chandra testing procedure (named by …::Follow the Franklin and Chandra testing procedure (named by the lecturer) for the setup details
What does "Select loading stages, plate size and reaction load for a plate load test" produce?::The engineer can pick the plate diameter and jack capacity that suit the target bearing pressure, set out a compliant six-stage loading schedule, and size the reaction weight.
Before relying on "Select loading stages, plate size and reaction load for a plate load test" — what do you check?::Maximum stage load plus 10 kN does not exceed the reaction mass available. • Stage loads divided by the plate factor reproduce the intended stresses.
"Select loading stages, plate size and reaction load for a plate load test" — state the decision rule about: Larger plates suit weaker ground and lower target stresses; …::Larger plates suit weaker ground and lower target stresses; the 300 mm plate is needed for high-pressure verification.
"Select loading stages, plate size and reaction load for a plate load test" — state the decision rule about: 200 kN devices fall outside DIN 18134 - their stage values a…::200 kN devices fall outside DIN 18134 - their stage values are recommendations only.
What does "Set up the plate load test loading train under a reaction counterweight" produce?::The engineer can position a reaction weight, prepare the bearing surface, and assemble the plate, load cell, hydraulic cylinder and ball joint ready for loading.
Before relying on "Set up the plate load test loading train under a reaction counterweight" — what do you check?::The sand-drop mark confirms the plate is centred under the jacking point. • The piston contacts the ball joint with no load registered and no jamming of the ball joint bolt.
"Set up the plate load test loading train under a reaction counterweight" — state the decision rule about: Use bedding sand only when the prepared surface is rough (p.…::Use bedding sand only when the prepared surface is rough (p. 3).
"Set up the plate load test loading train under a reaction counterweight" — state the decision rule about: Use piston extensions when the cylinder cannot otherwise rea…::Use piston extensions when the cylinder cannot otherwise reach the ball joint (p. 3).
What does "Set up the reference beam and zero the PLT sensors" produce?::The engineer can install the displacement reference beam clear of the loaded zone, align the transducer on the plate centre, and zero both displacement and force channels before loading.
Before relying on "Set up the reference beam and zero the PLT sensors" — what do you check?::Transducer tip is at the plate centre and nearly fully retracted at zero. • Plate bubble remains centred at the end of setup. • All star knobs tight; cables clipped so they cannot snag.
"Set up the reference beam and zero the PLT sensors" — state the decision rule about: Zero the force sensor only while the cylinder is demonstrabl…::Zero the force sensor only while the cylinder is demonstrably unloaded (visible flex in the train) (p. 6).
What does "Transfer AX 01a test data from the SD card into Excel" produce?::The engineer can pull stored test records off the device's SD card into the supplied Excel template and generate per-test sheets for reporting.
Before relying on "Transfer AX 01a test data from the SD card into Excel" — what do you check?::Number of records shown matches the device's card-info count. • Each transferred sheet reproduces the Ev values printed on site.
"Transfer AX 01a test data from the SD card into Excel" — state the decision rule about: Use read-file, not the card-reader path, for AX 01a data; th…::Use read-file, not the card-reader path, for AX 01a data; the dedicated card reader is only for the previous device generation.
"Transfer AX 01a test data from the SD card into Excel" — state the decision rule about: Optionally export via the separate software to ASCII .csv or…::Optionally export via the separate software to ASCII .csv or GGU .pdr formats when other programs need the data (p. 4).
