Numbers still come from the source. What does "Assess earthworks lot acceptance statistically from PLT results" produce?::The engineer can decide, per the German ZTV E StB scheme, whether an inspection lot of compacted ground passes based on randomly located test results. Before relying on "Assess earthworks lot acceptance statistically from PLT results" — what do you check?::Confirm n matches the lot size table before testing. • Verify the requirement is expressed as a 10% minimum quantile before applying the Q formula. "Assess earthworks lot acceptance statistically from PLT results" — state the decision rule about: The statistical method suits any ground but is particularly …::The statistical method suits any ground but is particularly recommended for large lots, lots where uniformity of compaction matters, quick turnaround test methods, and trial compactions (p. 5 6). "Assess earthworks lot acceptance statistically from PLT results" — state the decision rule about: Rejection applies to the whole lot area, not just failing po…::Rejection applies to the whole lot area, not just failing points. What does "Calculate Ev1 and Ev2 deformation moduli from a PLT load settlement curve" produce?::The engineer can fit the measured load settlement data and compute the first and second cycle strain moduli the way the AX01 evaluation does, and check machine output by hand. Before relying on "Calculate Ev1 and Ev2 deformation moduli from a PLT load settlement curve" — what do you check?::The fitted polynomial should track the measured curve smoothly; the worked example gives Ev1 = 43 MN/m2 and Ev2 = 94 MN/m2 for its curve (p. 4). • Hand calculated values should match the AX01 electronic evaluation for the same data. "Calculate Ev1 and Ev2 deformation moduli from a PLT load settlement curve" — state the decision rule about: Use sigma 0max of the cycle being evaluated in the secant fo…::Use sigma 0max of the cycle being evaluated in the secant formula. "Calculate Ev1 and Ev2 deformation moduli from a PLT load settlement curve" — state the decision rule about: Ev2/Ev1 serves as the compaction parameter; Ev1 and Ev2 char…::Ev2/Ev1 serves as the compaction parameter; Ev1 and Ev2 characterise stiffness (p. 11). What does "Calculate the Westergaard modulus of subgrade reaction from PLT data" produce?::The engineer can derive the subgrade reaction modulus ks for pavement or airfield design from a plate load test, including the correction when a 300 mm plate is used instead of 762 mm. Before relying on "Calculate the Westergaard modulus of subgrade reaction from PLT data" — what do you check?::Hand value should match the ks on the DIN mode printout (the sample record shows 40 MN/m3). • Confirm the stress was read from the first loading branch, not the reload curve. "Calculate the Westergaard modulus of subgrade reaction from PLT data" — state the decision rule about: The 300 mm plate substitution is only reasonable when the la…::The 300 mm plate substitution is only reasonable when the layer beneath the plate is homogeneous to a depth of 1.5 times the plate diameter (stated 'without liability', p. 11). What does "Check Ev2 and Ev2/Ev1 against German subgrade and base course requirements" produce?::The engineer can compare measured moduli with the ZTV E StB / ZTV SoB StB acceptance values for formation levels, frost protection layers and unbound base courses, and use PLT as a stand in for density testing on coarse soils. Before relying on "Check Ev2 and Ev2/Ev1 against German subgrade and base course requirements" — what do you check?::Confirm both the Ev2 floor and the Ev2/Ev1 ceiling are satisfied before assigning a degree of compaction. • Confirm the underlying formation modulus tier (Ev2 = 120 or = 100 MN/m2) before selecting the base course requirement. "Check Ev2 and Ev2/Ev1 against German subgrade and base course requirements" — state the decision rule about: Choose the quantile based check (ZTV E StB) for earthworks l…::Choose the quantile based check (ZTV E StB) for earthworks lots and the minimum value check (ZTV SoB StB) for unbound base courses. "Check Ev2 and Ev2/Ev1 against German subgrade and base course requirements" — state the decision rule about: PLT for density substitution only applies to coarse/mixed so…::PLT for density substitution only applies to coarse/mixed soils with fines below 15% by mass. What does "Clean, pack and store PLT equipment after testing" produce?::The engineer can decommission the kit in a way that avoids corrosion and sensor damage, and route the day's data to the supervising engineers. Before relying on "Clean, pack and store PLT equipment after testing" — what do you check?::Case interior and equipment are dry before closing. • Datasheet is fully completed and data has been handed to the supervising engineers. "Clean, pack and store PLT equipment after testing" — state the decision rule about: If moisture is found in the case, dry the open case indoors …::If moisture is found in the case, dry the open case indoors before storage rather than packing wet. What does "Compute the size corrected point load strength index Is(50) from test data" produce?::A normalised point load strength index Is(50) for each valid test, from peak load and sample dimensions, for both diametral and axial loading configurations Before relying on "Compute the size corrected point load strength index Is(50) from test data" — what do you check?::De route matches the loading configuration (direct diameter for diametral, equivalent area formula for axial) • Units consistent: P in kN, dimensions in mm, with the factor of 1000 applied once • Size correction applied after, not instead of, the uncorrected index calculation "Compute the size corrected point load strength index Is(50) from test data" — state the decision rule about: A markedly low Is(50) may reflect weathering or an invalid f…::A markedly low Is(50) may reflect weathering or an invalid failure mode from the test rather than intrinsic strength — check the test video/record before reporting "Compute the size corrected point load strength index Is(50) from test data" — state the decision rule about: A spreadsheet with the formulas pre built is the practical w…::A spreadsheet with the formulas pre built is the practical way to process multiple tests What does "Derive rock mass strength parameters from triaxial test data with Hoek Brown fitting in RSData" produce?::Intact rock parameters (UCS, mi) fitted from triaxial data and scaled rock mass parameters (rock mass UCS, tensile strength, cohesion, friction angle) for a specific slope application Before relying on "Derive rock mass strength parameters from triaxial test data with Hoek Brown fitting in RSData" — what do you check?::Confirm the fitted curve passes sensibly through the test points before accepting UCS and mi • Verify the parameter panel switches from intact rock to rock mass labelling after GSI and D are applied • Check the envelope stress range corresponds to the actual slope height "Derive rock mass strength parameters from triaxial test data with Hoek Brown fitting in RSData" — state the decision rule about: Prefer laboratory derived mi over tabulated mi by lithology;…::Prefer laboratory derived mi over tabulated mi by lithology; use the table only when no test data exist "Derive rock mass strength parameters from triaxial test data with Hoek Brown fitting in RSData" — state the decision rule about: GSI 100 means intact sample scale — never carry intact param…::GSI 100 means intact sample scale — never carry intact parameters directly into rock mass design What does "Determine UCS and Young's modulus from unconfined compression test data" produce?::A stress strain curve, peak unconfined compressive strength, and Young's modulus (E) for a rock core from raw load deformation laboratory data Before relying on "Determine UCS and Young's modulus from unconfined compression test data" — what do you check?::Confirm strain was converted out of percent before dividing — this is the step that most commonly corrupts E by a factor of 100 • Confirm load to stress conversion units (kN over m2 gives kPa) "Determine UCS and Young's modulus from unconfined compression test data" — state the decision rule about: Very small strain ranges at failure (of order 0.05%) indicat…::Very small strain ranges at failure (of order 0.05%) indicate a hard rock likely to show brittle behaviour "Determine UCS and Young's modulus from unconfined compression test data" — state the decision rule about: A very high computed E is plausible when measured strains ar…::A very high computed E is plausible when measured strains are very low — sanity check E against how stiff the curve looks What does "Determine the CBR of cement or lime stabilised road materials to RMS T132" produce?::A reported soaked CBR, dry density and swell for road materials modified/stabilised with small proportions of cementitious binder, for either laboratory mix designs or field mixed samples. Before relying on "Determine the CBR of cement or lime stabilised road materials to RMS T132" — what do you check?::Mixing to compaction time window observed (simulates field workability loss). • Available lime (CaO + Ca(OH)2) verified via T430 or supplier certification when lime is used. • Binder in the lab matches the field additive source and grading where possible — coarse quicklime can hydrate after compaction and disintegrate specimens (Claus "Determine the CBR of cement or lime stabilised road materials to RMS T132" — state the decision rule about: The method is not applicable to heavily bound materials or h…::The method is not applicable to heavily bound materials or high binder contents — penetration resistance becomes too high (Clause 1(b)). "Determine the CBR of cement or lime stabilised road materials to RMS T132" — state the decision rule about: If penetration cannot exceed 2.5 mm, the CBR test is not app…::If penetration cannot exceed 2.5 mm, the CBR test is not appropriate and must be abandoned; beyond 2.5 mm, terminate to protect equipment and record maximum penetration (Clause 6(w)). What does "Determine the California Bearing Ratio of remoulded road construction material to RMS T117" produce?::A reported CBR (with swell, densities and moisture ratios) for a laboratory compacted, optionally soaked specimen of the passing 19 mm fraction of a road construction material. Before relying on "Determine the California Bearing Ratio of remoulded road construction material to RMS T117" — what do you check?::LMR and LDR of the moulded specimen within target tolerances; report both target and achieved values. • Force device calibrated over the range appropriate to the expected CBR. • Layer thickness uniformity within ~5 mm; specimen not underfilled/overfilled beyond limits (else remould with fresh material). "Determine the California Bearing Ratio of remoulded road construction material to RMS T117" — state the decision rule about: Static compaction is not permitted for this test (Clause 2(c…::Static compaction is not permitted for this test (Clause 2(c)). "Determine the California Bearing Ratio of remoulded road construction material to RMS T117" — state the decision rule about: If penetration of at least 2.5 mm cannot be achieved, stop a…::If penetration of at least 2.5 mm cannot be achieved, stop and report maximum penetration only. What does "Determine the liquid limit of road construction materials to TfNSW T108" produce?::A reported liquid limit (to the stated rounding, or 'Not obtainable') for soils, gravels, crushed rock, recycled and RAP materials, derived from a multi point Casagrande apparatus test. Before relying on "Determine the liquid limit of road construction materials to TfNSW T108" — what do you check?::Apparatus check results recorded (drop height, wear, hinge play, tool tip width) before testing. • Consecutive blow agreement within one blow before accepting each point. • Points evenly distributed across the specified blow range and taken drier to wetter. "Determine the liquid limit of road construction materials to TfNSW T108" — state the decision rule about: If the soil pat slips in the cup, remix with added water and…::If the soil pat slips in the cup, remix with added water and retry; if slipping persists, discard results and report that the liquid limit could not be obtained (Clause 6(d)(iv)). "Determine the liquid limit of road construction materials to TfNSW T108" — state the decision rule about: If blow count increases after adding water, reject all previ…::If blow count increases after adding water, reject all previous points and restart from the mixing step (Clause 6(f)). What does "Estimate on site elastic modulus from laboratory CBR mold plate bearing tests" produce?::The engineer can predict the field elastic modulus of a compacted coarse grained soil from small scale laboratory plate load tests in a CBR mold, using the paper's calibrated equations. Before relying on "Estimate on site elastic modulus from laboratory CBR mold plate bearing tests" — what do you check?::Laboratory density and water content replicate the field values before crediting the prediction. • The lab to field regression assumes a zero intercept (no load, no settlement); confirm the fitted trend is roughly linear for your soil. "Estimate on site elastic modulus from laboratory CBR mold plate bearing tests" — state the decision rule about: Use this approach for coarse grained embankment/subgrade soi…::Use this approach for coarse grained embankment/subgrade soils where triaxial or oedometer moduli are impractical (largest grains too big relative to standard molds). "Estimate on site elastic modulus from laboratory CBR mold plate bearing tests" — state the decision rule about: For maximum stiffness and least settlement, compact on the d…::For maximum stiffness and least settlement, compact on the dry side of optimum water content moduli fell as compaction water content rose (Conclusions, p. 10). What does "Estimate rock unconfined compressive strength from Schmidt hammer rebound data" produce?::A defensible UCS estimate (as a range, in MPa) for a rock surface from ten field rebound readings, with or without a measured rock density Before relying on "Estimate rock unconfined compressive strength from Schmidt hammer rebound data" — what do you check?::Confirm exactly the highest and lowest of the ten readings were removed before averaging • Confirm units: unit weight in kN/m3, strength in MPa "Estimate rock unconfined compressive strength from Schmidt hammer rebound data" — state the decision rule about: If rock density is unknown (common in the field), assume an …::If rock density is unknown (common in the field), assume an average rock unit weight of 27 kN/m3 rather than skipping the estimate "Estimate rock unconfined compressive strength from Schmidt hammer rebound data" — state the decision rule about: Report a strength range (e.g. about 67 69 MPa); small differ…::Report a strength range (e.g. about 67 69 MPa); small differences in chart reading are acceptable What does "Interpret an AX01a printed plate bearing test record" produce?::The engineer can read a DIN 18134 300 test record, verify its metadata, and judge pass/fail against the nominal Ev2 and Ev2/Ev1 targets. Before relying on "Interpret an AX01a printed plate bearing test record" — what do you check?::Deflection at the end of unloading versus the first cycle maximum gives the plastic (unrecovered) settlement. • GPS coordinates match the intended test location. "Interpret an AX01a printed plate bearing test record" — state the decision rule about: Both the Ev2 floor and the Ev2/Ev1 ceiling must pass for com…::Both the Ev2 floor and the Ev2/Ev1 ceiling must pass for compaction acceptance; a high Ev2 alone does not save a failed ratio. "Interpret an AX01a printed plate bearing test record" — state the decision rule about: A failed ratio with adequate Ev2 typically signals further c…::A failed ratio with adequate Ev2 typically signals further compaction of the layer is achievable. What does "Maintain, calibrate and troubleshoot the AX 01a plate bearing tester" produce?::The engineer can keep the device within its calibration and safety regime and diagnose common hydraulic faults in the field. Before relying on "Maintain, calibrate and troubleshoot the AX 01a plate bearing tester" — what do you check?::Calibration date on the device Info screen is within the last year. • Force zero is checked (and reset unloaded if drifted, e.g. from temperature) before testing (p. 13). "Maintain, calibrate and troubleshoot the AX 01a plate bearing tester" — state the decision rule about: Any visible damage means do not test the manual treats thi…::Any visible damage means do not test the manual treats this as a potentially fatal hazard. "Maintain, calibrate and troubleshoot the AX 01a plate bearing tester" — state the decision rule about: Repairs only by Anix or Anix authorised staff; non genuine p…::Repairs only by Anix or Anix authorised staff; non genuine parts void safe operation. What does "Perform point load tests with sample geometry screening and failure mode vetting" produce?::Valid peak failure loads from point load tests on rock core, with unsuitable samples and invalid failure modes screened out Before relying on "Perform point load tests with sample geometry screening and failure mode vetting" — what do you check?::Geometry check passed and recorded before loading • Failure plane inspected and judged valid before the force reading is kept • Peak force and dimensions written down immediately per test "Perform point load tests with sample geometry screening and failure mode vetting" — state the decision rule about: Reject a test where failure ran along a pre existing crack o…::Reject a test where failure ran along a pre existing crack or broke only at the sample edge (seen with a weathered sample that failed at 0.265 kN); weathered samples are prone to this "Perform point load tests with sample geometry screening and failure mode vetting" — state the decision rule about: One or two samples is never enough — a minimum of three test…::One or two samples is never enough — a minimum of three tests per rock type, more if material is available What does "Plan and interpret a seismic geophysical survey for site investigation" produce?::A cost effective picture of subsurface layer boundaries over a large area from seismic wave velocities, correctly caveated and tied to borehole control Before relying on "Plan and interpret a seismic geophysical survey for site investigation" — what do you check?::Confirm layer boundary picks against borehole logs before reporting • Sanity check velocity derived strength classes against samples taken from the borehole "Plan and interpret a seismic geophysical survey for site investigation" — state the decision rule about: Choose seismic methods when the area is large and budget mat…::Choose seismic methods when the area is large and budget matters: cheaper than boreholes, SPT or lab programmes, and covers area rather than points "Plan and interpret a seismic geophysical survey for site investigation" — state the decision rule about: Never interpret geology from velocities without borehole con…::Never interpret geology from velocities without borehole confirmation; the combination of seismic coverage plus borehole control is presented as the best approach What does "Prepare equipment and field records before a plate load test" produce?::The engineer can mobilise to site with a complete, serviceable PLT kit and a datasheet that captures all identifying information before loading begins. Before relying on "Prepare equipment and field records before a plate load test" — what do you check?::All items on the equipment list are packed before leaving. • Every header field on the datasheet is completed before the test starts. "Prepare equipment and field records before a plate load test" — state the decision rule about: Recharge whenever battery charge is under 50% (p. 1).…::Recharge whenever battery charge is under 50% (p. 1). "Prepare equipment and field records before a plate load test" — state the decision rule about: Do not proceed to site with damaged equipment, especially da…::Do not proceed to site with damaged equipment, especially damaged hydraulic hoses. What does "Run a DIN 18134 plate load test on the AX 01a" produce?::The engineer can execute the full two cycle DIN 18134 loading sequence on the AX 01a electronic box and obtain Ev1, Ev2 and their ratio on site. Before relying on "Run a DIN 18134 plate load test on the AX 01a" — what do you check?::Force reading is zero before preload; settlement auto zeroed at Adjust and preload steps. • Watch the tilt of the hydraulic cylinder and extension throughout loading (p. 7). • Results screen shows record number, date/time, Ev1, Ev2 and the ratio. "Run a DIN 18134 plate load test on the AX 01a" — state the decision rule about: Holding ON/OFF for about 2 s aborts the test with nothing st…::Holding ON/OFF for about 2 s aborts the test with nothing stored use only to abandon a test. "Run a DIN 18134 plate load test on the AX 01a" — state the decision rule about: If the sequence is not completed, the device cannot compute …::If the sequence is not completed, the device cannot compute Ev1/Ev2 and will show no moduli (p. 8). What does "Run a plate load test to Norwegian standard SVV 15.328 on the AX 01a" produce?::The engineer can switch the AX 01a to the SVV 15.328 procedure, hold stages to a settlement rate criterion instead of fixed times, and read E1/E2 from the printout. Before relying on "Run a plate load test to Norwegian standard SVV 15.328 on the AX 01a" — what do you check?::No underlined readings should be stored underlining flags settlement still exceeding 0.02 mm since the last reading. • Printout lists E1, E2 and alternate E2 values for review. "Run a plate load test to Norwegian standard SVV 15.328 on the AX 01a" — state the decision rule about: Use SVV mode when the project specifies Norwegian road admin…::Use SVV mode when the project specifies Norwegian road administration testing; stage holds are settlement rate governed, unlike DIN's fixed 60 s. "Run a plate load test to Norwegian standard SVV 15.328 on the AX 01a" — state the decision rule about: Pick the alternate E2 for a lower stage when the upper part …::Pick the alternate E2 for a lower stage when the upper part of the second cycle curve departs from straight. What does "Run an on site plate bearing test with time settlement acceptance criteria" produce?::The engineer can execute an ASTM D 1194 style plate bearing test on compacted fill, recording settlement over time and knowing when a load stage is complete. Before relying on "Run an on site plate bearing test with time settlement acceptance criteria" — what do you check?::Settlement rate below 0.02 mm/min before ending a stage. • Total settlement under 25 mm. • Post test density and moisture confirm the layer met compaction targets (at least 95% of modified maximum dry unit weight in the paper's practice). "Run an on site plate bearing test with time settlement acceptance criteria" — state the decision rule about: Use stress in the 50 150 kPa range when the data will feed t…::Use stress in the 50 150 kPa range when the data will feed the elastic modulus formula (Eq. 1). "Run an on site plate bearing test with time settlement acceptance criteria" — state the decision rule about: Compare wet side, OWC and dry side results separately sett…::Compare wet side, OWC and dry side results separately settlement rises with compaction water content. What does "Run the slake durability test through two cycles and record the masses for the durability index" produce?::A complete set of drum and sample mass records over two wet dry abrasion cycles, ready for computing the second cycle slake durability index used for durability classification Before relying on "Run the slake durability test through two cycles and record the masses for the durability index" — what do you check?::Water level set at the pre marked height about 20 mm below the drum axis before each cycle • Drum connections secure before rotation • All four masses recorded: empty drum, drum+rock initial, drum+rock after cycle 1 drying, drum+rock after cycle 2 drying "Run the slake durability test through two cycles and record the masses for the durability index" — state the decision rule about: The classification is based on the second cycle index, so th…::The classification is based on the second cycle index, so the test is not complete after one cycle "Run the slake durability test through two cycles and record the masses for the durability index" — state the decision rule about: Follow the Franklin and Chandra testing procedure (named by …::Follow the Franklin and Chandra testing procedure (named by the lecturer) for the setup details What does "Select loading stages, plate size and reaction load for a plate load test" produce?::The engineer can pick the plate diameter and jack capacity that suit the target bearing pressure, set out a compliant six stage loading schedule, and size the reaction weight. Before relying on "Select loading stages, plate size and reaction load for a plate load test" — what do you check?::Maximum stage load plus 10 kN does not exceed the reaction mass available. • Stage loads divided by the plate factor reproduce the intended stresses. "Select loading stages, plate size and reaction load for a plate load test" — state the decision rule about: Larger plates suit weaker ground and lower target stresses; …::Larger plates suit weaker ground and lower target stresses; the 300 mm plate is needed for high pressure verification. "Select loading stages, plate size and reaction load for a plate load test" — state the decision rule about: 200 kN devices fall outside DIN 18134 their stage values a…::200 kN devices fall outside DIN 18134 their stage values are recommendations only. What does "Set up the plate load test loading train under a reaction counterweight" produce?::The engineer can position a reaction weight, prepare the bearing surface, and assemble the plate, load cell, hydraulic cylinder and ball joint ready for loading. Before relying on "Set up the plate load test loading train under a reaction counterweight" — what do you check?::The sand drop mark confirms the plate is centred under the jacking point. • The piston contacts the ball joint with no load registered and no jamming of the ball joint bolt. "Set up the plate load test loading train under a reaction counterweight" — state the decision rule about: Use bedding sand only when the prepared surface is rough (p.…::Use bedding sand only when the prepared surface is rough (p. 3). "Set up the plate load test loading train under a reaction counterweight" — state the decision rule about: Use piston extensions when the cylinder cannot otherwise rea…::Use piston extensions when the cylinder cannot otherwise reach the ball joint (p. 3). What does "Set up the reference beam and zero the PLT sensors" produce?::The engineer can install the displacement reference beam clear of the loaded zone, align the transducer on the plate centre, and zero both displacement and force channels before loading. Before relying on "Set up the reference beam and zero the PLT sensors" — what do you check?::Transducer tip is at the plate centre and nearly fully retracted at zero. • Plate bubble remains centred at the end of setup. • All star knobs tight; cables clipped so they cannot snag. "Set up the reference beam and zero the PLT sensors" — state the decision rule about: Zero the force sensor only while the cylinder is demonstrabl…::Zero the force sensor only while the cylinder is demonstrably unloaded (visible flex in the train) (p. 6). What does "Transfer AX 01a test data from the SD card into Excel" produce?::The engineer can pull stored test records off the device's SD card into the supplied Excel template and generate per test sheets for reporting. Before relying on "Transfer AX 01a test data from the SD card into Excel" — what do you check?::Number of records shown matches the device's card info count. • Each transferred sheet reproduces the Ev values printed on site. "Transfer AX 01a test data from the SD card into Excel" — state the decision rule about: Use read file, not the card reader path, for AX 01a data; th…::Use read file, not the card reader path, for AX 01a data; the dedicated card reader is only for the previous device generation. "Transfer AX 01a test data from the SD card into Excel" — state the decision rule about: Optionally export via the separate software to ASCII .csv or…::Optionally export via the separate software to ASCII .csv or GGU .pdr formats when other programs need the data (p. 4). Related Learning path Field and laboratory testing Learning loop

notes.title: Flashcards - Working platforms
notes.body:
# Flashcards - Working platforms

#flashcards/working-platforms

16 cards generated from the 4 working platforms skill notes
(`Question::Answer`, one per line — the format Obsidian's Spaced Repetition
plugin reads). Cards test what a skill produces, what you check before
trusting it, and its decision rules. The deck is regenerated from the skill
notes, so refining a note refines its cards — do not edit cards here.

Answers are paraphrased working aids: getting a card right is recall, not
verification. Numbers still come from the source.

What does "Assess and prepare a subgrade before installing a working platform" produce?::A characterised, inspected and prepared subgrade with soft spots, hard spots, voids and drainage issues resolved, so the platform design assumptions are valid on the ground actually built on.
Before relying on "Assess and prepare a subgrade before installing a working platform" — what do you check?::Subgrade inspection record signed off by a competent person immediately prior to platform placement. • Weak zones and hard spots identified relative to the design's stated strength assumptions (Box 3). • Drainage installed/verified before and during platform life; risk assessments lodged in the health and safety file including what underlies the platform.
"Assess and prepare a subgrade before installing a working platform" — state the decision rule about: If actual subgrade strength or variability differs from the …::If actual subgrade strength or variability differs from the design's stated characteristic values, refer back to the platform designer before proceeding.
"Assess and prepare a subgrade before installing a working platform" — state the decision rule about: Where a surface crust or vegetated layer contributes strengt…::Where a surface crust or vegetated layer contributes strength and is retained, inform the permanent-works designer so later removal can be arranged.
What does "Design a granular working platform for tracked plant using the punching-shear method" produce?::A minimum working-platform thickness (with or without geosynthetic reinforcement) that safely supports piling rigs and cranes on a weak subgrade, following the BRE BR 470 routine design calculation.
Before relying on "Design a granular working platform for tracked plant using the punching-shear method" — what do you check?::Verify the punching applicability checks in the Figure A6 flowchart were all passed, not just the thickness equation. • Confirm plant loading was derived per EN 791/EN 996 for the worst rig orientation and jib position, including dynamic and wind loading where relevant. • Confirm groundwater near surface was included for granular subgrades — it strongly reduces bearing resistance (Appendix A3). • Have a competent geotechnical person critically appraise the result — the method is semi-empirical with major simplifications.
"Design a granular working platform for tracked plant using the punching-shear method" — state the decision rule about: Do not use the routine method for very soft cohesive subgrad…::Do not use the routine method for very soft cohesive subgrades below the lower cu applicability bound (~20 kPa, Appendix A2) — special measures and sophisticated analysis needed; above the upper bound
"Design a granular working platform for tracked plant using the punching-shear method" — state the decision rule about: The punching-shear model is invalid where the platform is no…::The punching-shear model is invalid where the platform is not significantly stronger than the subgrade, or where thickness-to-track-width ratio D/W exceeds the stated limit (Appendix A1.4).
What does "Operate, maintain and repair a working platform through its service life" produce?::A platform that keeps performing to its design over the works duration, with controlled usage, monitored condition, prompt reinstatement of excavations, and clear responsibility for upkeep.
Before relying on "Operate, maintain and repair a working platform through its service life" — what do you check?::Regular documented inspections; deteriorating areas detected before they become hazards. • All excavations through the platform logged and reinstated to spec; empty pile bores backfilled. • Platform edges, exclusion zones and unfinished areas clearly marked and physically controlled.
"Operate, maintain and repair a working platform through its service life" — state the decision rule about: Most rig instability incidents trace to maintenance/repair f…::Most rig instability incidents trace to maintenance/repair failures rather than design or installation defects — treat deterioration signals as safety-critical, not cosmetic.
"Operate, maintain and repair a working platform through its service life" — state the decision rule about: Rig bouncing when travelling is not covered by design calcul…::Rig bouncing when travelling is not covered by design calculations; it must be prevented operationally, with specialist advice if it persists.
What does "Specify, install and quality-control working platform material" produce?::A platform built from suitable granular (or approved recycled) material, placed and compacted to specification with records proving it, including correctly installed geosynthetics.
Before relying on "Specify, install and quality-control working platform material" — what do you check?::Certification that the platform was installed as specified, backed by supervision and test records. • Small plate tests recognised as unrepresentative — plate size versus track size documented. • Geosynthetic cover thickness before compaction plant traffics over it.
"Specify, install and quality-control working platform material" — state the decision rule about: If platform material is excavated and re-used elsewhere on s…::If platform material is excavated and re-used elsewhere on site, re-check it still meets the design assumptions before re-use.
"Specify, install and quality-control working platform material" — state the decision rule about: On cohesive formations in wet conditions, provide a granular…::On cohesive formations in wet conditions, provide a granular filter layer or geofabric to stop upward fines migration degrading the platform.

## Related

- [[Learning path - Working platforms]]
- [[Learning loop]]

Before relying on "Assess and prepare a subgrade before installing a working platform" — what do you check?::Subgrade inspection record signed off by a competent person immediately prior to platform placement. • Weak zones and hard spots identified relative to the design's stated strength assumptions (Box 3). • Drainage installed/verified before and during platform life; risk assessments lodged in the health and safety file including what underlies the platform. "Assess and prepare a subgrade before installing a working platform" — state the decision rule about: If actual subgrade strength or variability differs from the …::If actual subgrade strength or variability differs from the design's stated characteristic values, refer back to the platform designer before proceeding. "Assess and prepare a subgrade before installing a working platform" — state the decision rule about: Where a surface crust or vegetated layer contributes strengt…::Where a surface crust or vegetated layer contributes strength and is retained, inform the permanent works designer so later removal can be arranged. What does "Design a granular working platform for tracked plant using the punching shear method" produce?::A minimum working platform thickness (with or without geosynthetic reinforcement) that safely supports piling rigs and cranes on a weak subgrade, following the BRE BR 470 routine design calculation. Before relying on "Design a granular working platform for tracked plant using the punching shear method" — what do you check?::Verify the punching applicability checks in the Figure A6 flowchart were all passed, not just the thickness equation. • Confirm plant loading was derived per EN 791/EN 996 for the worst rig orientation and jib position, including dynamic and wind loading where relevant. • Confirm groundwater near surface was included for granular subgrades — it strongly reduces bearing resistance (Appendix A3). • Have a competent geotechnical person critically appraise the result — the method is semi empirical with major simplifications. "Design a granular working platform for tracked plant using the punching shear method" — state the decision rule about: Do not use the routine method for very soft cohesive subgrad…::Do not use the routine method for very soft cohesive subgrades below the lower cu applicability bound (~20 kPa, Appendix A2) — special measures and sophisticated analysis needed; above the upper bound "Design a granular working platform for tracked plant using the punching shear method" — state the decision rule about: The punching shear model is invalid where the platform is no…::The punching shear model is invalid where the platform is not significantly stronger than the subgrade, or where thickness to track width ratio D/W exceeds the stated limit (Appendix A1.4). What does "Operate, maintain and repair a working platform through its service life" produce?::A platform that keeps performing to its design over the works duration, with controlled usage, monitored condition, prompt reinstatement of excavations, and clear responsibility for upkeep. Before relying on "Operate, maintain and repair a working platform through its service life" — what do you check?::Regular documented inspections; deteriorating areas detected before they become hazards. • All excavations through the platform logged and reinstated to spec; empty pile bores backfilled. • Platform edges, exclusion zones and unfinished areas clearly marked and physically controlled. "Operate, maintain and repair a working platform through its service life" — state the decision rule about: Most rig instability incidents trace to maintenance/repair f…::Most rig instability incidents trace to maintenance/repair failures rather than design or installation defects — treat deterioration signals as safety critical, not cosmetic. "Operate, maintain and repair a working platform through its service life" — state the decision rule about: Rig bouncing when travelling is not covered by design calcul…::Rig bouncing when travelling is not covered by design calculations; it must be prevented operationally, with specialist advice if it persists. What does "Specify, install and quality control working platform material" produce?::A platform built from suitable granular (or approved recycled) material, placed and compacted to specification with records proving it, including correctly installed geosynthetics. Before relying on "Specify, install and quality control working platform material" — what do you check?::Certification that the platform was installed as specified, backed by supervision and test records. • Small plate tests recognised as unrepresentative — plate size versus track size documented. • Geosynthetic cover thickness before compaction plant traffics over it. "Specify, install and quality control working platform material" — state the decision rule about: If platform material is excavated and re used elsewhere on s…::If platform material is excavated and re used elsewhere on site, re check it still meets the design assumptions before re use. "Specify, install and quality control working platform material" — state the decision rule about: On cohesive formations in wet conditions, provide a granular…::On cohesive formations in wet conditions, provide a granular filter layer or geofabric to stop upward fines migration degrading the platform. Related Learning path Working platforms Learning loop

notes.title: Reference library
notes.body:
# Reference library

A catalogue of the geotechnical reference material held locally, so it can be
found from the notes that use it.

**These are pointers, not copies.** The standards, papers and textbooks are
licensed or copyright material and are not reproduced in this vault — the notes
record what a document covers and where it sits, and the document itself stays
where it is. Anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

Local root: `C:\Users\pored\Downloads\G materials`

## By topic

- [[Library - Australian Standards]] — AS series held locally
- [[Library - RMS and TfNSW specifications]] — roads specs and test methods
- [[Library - Pells papers on Sydney sandstone and shale]] — the local rock-socket literature
- [[Library - plate load testing]] — PLT procedure, spreadsheets and training
- [[Library - salinity and sodic soils]] — western Sydney salinity guidance
- [[Library - reference texts and parameter sources]] — textbooks and correlation sources
- [[Field records catalogue]] — STS field sheets, photos and scans in Google Drive

## Section maps

Clause-level finding aids for the standards whose text could be read. Headings
only — no clause text is reproduced.

- [[Section map - AS 1726:2017]]
- [[Section map - AS 2159:2009]] — OCR-rebuilt; the local PDF has no text layer
- [[Section map - AS 2870:2011]]
- [[Section map - AS 3798:2007]]
- [[Section map - AS 4678:2002]]

## Project reports

- [[Project reports]] — the 17 Core Geotech documents held alongside these
  references, indexed one note per document

## Housekeeping notes

The root folder holds several duplicates — `AS 1726 2017` and `AS1726-2017`
are both present, `AS3798` appears twice, and `Australian and RMS Standards/`
contains a second copy of the whole `Australian/` and `RMS/` trees. Two files
are zero bytes (`CG24-0518-A Rev 1.pdf`, `CG25-0768-1, Site plan_BB.pdf`) and
will not open. Worth a tidy before this becomes the reference of record.

notes.title: Field records catalogue
notes.body:
# Field records catalogue

The STS field data held in Google Drive — three years of completed field
sheets, blank form masters, labelled photographs and scans — catalogued so the
skill notes tagged `field-source` can point back to the records they were
reconstructed from. Each heading links to the Drive folder itself.

**These are project records, not procedures.** They show how forms were
actually filled in and how photos were actually taken on real jobs. Project
names, readings and results stay in the records — the skill notes carry the
method only. Confirm anything reconstructed here against the current STS form
and procedure before treating it as the standard method.

Coverage: a pilot pass sampled ten folders; a second pass swept the remaining
field-data folders and the blank STS/OP GEO form masters. Files over the
10 MB download limit (18 of ~450) could not be read; folders that held only
duplicates of already-mined forms, or uncontrolled phone shots with no
evidenced practice, are listed without separate skills.

### [2520E-G/Site Photos](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1hb16_fDKe6tLeoXQIBEtbMWQk5lmTEu5)

Site progress and evidence photographs for job 2520E-G: time-GPS overlay photos (date-time, compass bearing, address, altitude, speed, compass rose and map inset burned into the image) of a bulk excavation with piling rig and pier reinforcement cages, alongside plain phone-camera (PXL_) shots of the same works. (e.g. `TimePhoto_20260624_100529.jpg`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Photograph a site or test location with a time-GPS overlay]]

### [Core Photo](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_eC-u9MJx9PIN8p4PMUaPlwo24SmI0Jd)

Composite core box photographs taken with the STS core photo board (QR code, project/client/address/date/borehole/depth fields, colour reference chart and 1 m scale bar), with metre-depth tags on every core row and annotated spacer blocks marking coring start and end depths. (e.g. `IMG_0798.jpg`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Photograph and label a core box]]

### [Shrink Swell photo](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/15Da-eO0H1_2TlX0rj-ULS7vWGB7ai5qM)

Labelled photographs of undisturbed tube samples allocated to shrink-swell testing — sample, tube and a handwritten card (job/STS number, sample ID, borehole and depth interval, 'S/swell') in one frame, filenames repeating the borehole and depth interval. (e.g. `BH1 0.7-1.0m.jpg`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Photograph a shrink-swell sample with depth labelling]]

### [Field Sheets](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1UDSG9BqRx863c7OPoE1SngRPtDpaHA7c)

Phone photographs of completed handwritten plate load test worksheets (Form S112, 'Load Settlement - Time Relationship Worksheet') from the McEvoy Street Alexandria job — one page per test location with load/unload/reload dial gauge readings. (e.g. `PLT1.jpg`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Complete an STS plate load test worksheet (Form S112)]]

### [Field Sheets (1)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1B1BB-lhHW7amaaQPghZeT0w6e5LJkkHZ)

Scanned PDF copies of the same Form S112 plate load worksheets from a different job (105-113 Hollinsworth Road, Marsden Park, testing DGB20 pavement material to 180 kN). (e.g. `PLT-1 (1).pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Complete an STS plate load test worksheet (Form S112)]]

### [2520E-G/Field Sheets](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1O7dzYgQSRsQ7OLhC2YBTX2Xfg_hKMVfO)

Scanned per-job bundles of handwritten field paperwork: a DCP & Perth Penetrometer deep test sheet (Form S26) plus signed Geotechnical Daily Field Forms from consecutive bored pier inspection visits. (e.g. `2427E-G.pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Complete a DCP and Perth penetrometer deep test field sheet (Form S26)]]
  - [[Complete an STS Geotechnical Daily Field Form]]

### [Field Resistivity Test](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QByOoKKqEFQmU13Mr1CeUCaOdCgHG-uY)

Standard operating procedures for field resistivity work — a 3-page STS SOP for the AEMC Model 6471 Wenner soil resistivity test covering connections, electrode layout, instrument setup, measurement, storage and shutdown. (e.g. `SOP - AEMC Resistivity Test.pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Run the AEMC soil resistivity test (Wenner method) to the STS SOP]]
  - [[Record Wenner resistivity readings from the AEMC tester onto the stored-measurements datasheet]]

### [02 LEVEL1 DAILY SITE REPORT](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/15p0U775nBhgYID17KHzhnZo2GQG4dlYS)

Completed Form S69 'Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet' daily reports for AS 3798 Level 1 earthworks supervision at Marsden Park — mandatory fill-source questions, plant lists, density test number ranges and per-area placement/compaction/proof-roll narratives. (e.g. `Level 1 Daily Sheet 25-02-026.pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Complete the Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet for AS 3798 Level 1 supervision (Form S69)]]

### [Site Record 2025](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XLon9csGZSsF2DWH0CqP6qvQCpFsVEor)

Earlier (2025) daily site records on the same Form S69 for the same Level 1 earthworks project, including basin excavation, salinity and groundwater observations under a saline soil management plan. (e.g. `05.pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Complete the Geotechnical Testing & Site Record Sheet for AS 3798 Level 1 supervision (Form S69)]]

### [Field standard count](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1zdC1_rccSFRiMap0BCqOBcrz7v3cEEnv)

Scanned Form K38 'Daily Standard Count Check & Remote Storage Record Sheet' logs for nuclear density gauges — daily density and moisture standard counts with running 4-reading means, control limits and within-limits checks, plus gauge storage/security details. (e.g. `density reading_250818_075031.pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Record nuclear gauge daily standard counts (Form K38)]]

### [Field Sheets (STS blank templates + reference)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rCD7fbgkmw25X-tA-t5IrFkkowNPHZbZ)

Blank STS/OP GEO form masters (Drilling Daily Record, Daily Log revisions, BH soil/rock log sheets 5 m and 10 m, pile hole inspection form, core box label) plus the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts. (e.g. `OP GEO 007b RevB bh soil log 10m.pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Complete an STS Geotech Drilling Daily Record (drilling/coring time and production log)]]
  - [[Log a borehole soil profile by hand on the OP GEO 007a/007b BH soil field log sheets]]
  - [[Log rock core by hand on the OP GEO 008a/008b BH rock log sheets]]
  - [[Complete a Report of Pile Hole Inspection form (OP GEO pile hole inspection family)]]
  - [[Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in-field reference aids]]
  - [[Label core boxes using the STS printed photo-board template]]

### [O4 DAILY SITE TIMESHEET](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CY2GworTaSCTbci5s9Q6eIho1CWdc7Yq)

Signed monthly compilation of handwritten Form A7 Site Timesheet blocks (daily start/finish, onsite vs travel-inclusive hours, per-day signatures) for job 32913/1829E-L. (e.g. `329131829E-L(30-01-2026 TO 25-02-2026).pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Keep and compile a signed STS Site Timesheet (Form A7) for the billing period]]

### [PLT calc](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Lj04tWwlE_P-sDJDDwF0GGpXC0kXB7bd)

Office-side plate load test calculation workbooks (Input Data / Report / Calibration Chart tabs computing EV1 and Ks) with their issued PDF report sheets for PLT1-5. (e.g. `PLATE LOAD TEST-PLT1.xls`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Reduce a plate load test in the STS PLATE LOAD TEST workbook and issue the report sheet]]

### [Field Density Test Locations Drawings](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1YtCUY34T3mX0LJz8_yu4CH8lH7rBfW1r)

Scanned project drawings hand-marked with circled nuclear density test numbers and sticky-note test groupings for the Flomar/Marsden Park earthworks, plus location screenshots. (e.g. `flomar_250819_071947.pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Mark up field density test locations on the project drawing set]]

### [Field Sheets/2206E-G](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Y9gNnh71BHge4XNas0AZ9qtnB-t0ifCO)

An 8-page scanned completed field package for job 32913/2206E-G combining a filled Geotechnical Daily Field Form (with site-plan sketch) and S112 plate load worksheets. (e.g. `SCANNED FIELD WORK SHEETS.pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - _No separate skill — evidence folded into the skills above or judged already covered._

### [Field Sheets/1181](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1bR3fGKwv5rNBd1hQCIMpm0LFx74erAdM)

Scanned completed S26 Dynamic Cone & Perth Penetrometer deep-test sheets (job 32913/1181E-L, Marsden Park) with dated sticky-note location labels. (e.g. `32913-1181.pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - _No separate skill — evidence folded into the skills above or judged already covered._

### [Field Sheets/2097E-G/Zone H](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1M7FGGIbN6XXE5AEJu1_gDGoh5i3LKI_x)

Phone photos of completed handwritten S112 plate load test worksheets for job 2097E-G Zone H. (e.g. `IMG_9435.jpeg`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - _No separate skill — evidence folded into the skills above or judged already covered._

### [Site photos (Solocator)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1dotRhoa91MR1CUYksmBHCaHOVh8sAA_u)

May 2026 borehole-location photos taken with the Solocator app (compass ribbon, true bearing, decimal GPS +/- accuracy, altitude, timestamp burnt in), with keepers renamed BH1-BH4.jpg. (e.g. `Solocator-2026-05-07 10-22-29 (1).jpg`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Capture borehole location photos with the Solocator compass-GPS overlay]]

### [Core Photos (MP4 compilation)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1IQNiIpMSeAvCaL_RZ2207Zbp6JaB49mm)

The compiled per-borehole core-photograph deliverable (MP4 Core Photos.docx/pdf, one header-tabled page per hole) together with the positioned MP4-BHxx source images. (e.g. `MP4 Core Photos.pdf`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Label core boxes using the STS printed photo-board template]]
  - [[Compile positioned core photographs into a per-borehole core-photo deliverable]]

### [Core Photo/Positioned](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qJehuDwc0qNtq1JTDR41mIn2oGJzL_4v)

Perspective-corrected core box photos renamed to zone-borehole IDs (MP4-BHxx, MP5-BHxx) sitting alongside their raw UUID-named originals, the intermediate layer between raw core snaps and the compiled deliverable. (e.g. `MP4-BH04.jpg`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Compile positioned core photographs into a per-borehole core-photo deliverable]]

### [Photos (Nov 2021 site photo dump)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14K5dneiImUM5LsKjdz0HGdOs8eXImzX4)

Nov 2021 phone-photo dump mixing uncontrolled residential streetscape/dwelling shots (no overlay or board) with legacy handwritten core-box labelling photos (edge strip with job/site/BH/date/initials/start depth, metre spacer blocks, tape measure, END-depth block). (e.g. `IMG20211126131944.jpg`)

- Skills reconstructed from it:
  - [[Label core boxes using the STS printed photo-board template]]

notes.body:
# Library - Pells papers on Sydney sandstone and shale

`G materials/Pells Paper/`. The local literature behind how sockets in Sydney
sandstone and shale are classified and designed — directly relevant to
[[Rock socket length]] and [[Weathered siltstone]].

| Paper | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Pells, Mostyn & Wong (2019) — Classification of sandstones and shales in the Sydney region | The classification scheme used locally to describe Sydney basin rock |
| Pells — The design of socketed piles in rock | Socket design method, side resistance and end bearing |
| Pells — Bored piles socketed into shale and sandstone | Field behaviour of sockets in the local materials |
| Pells — Foundations on sandstone and shale in the Sydney region | Founding practice across the basin |
| Substance and mass properties for the design of engineering structures in the Hawkesbury Sandstone | Intact vs mass properties — the distinction that matters for defect-controlled rock |

## What to take from these

Intact strength and mass behaviour diverge in bedded rock, which is the point
made in [[Rock strength classes]]. A socket in shale that rates medium on hand
specimens can be governed by bedding partings rather than intact strength.

> Copyright papers. Cite them, do not paste them.

notes.title: Library - reference texts and parameter sources
notes.body:
# Library - reference texts and parameter sources

Where a parameter comes from when it is not measured on the job. Every value
taken from here is a published correlation, not a site measurement, and is
recorded as such — see [[Why pile data carries provenance]].

| Source | Use |
|---|---|
| Look, *Handbook of Geotechnical Investigation and Design Tables* (2014) | First stop for indicative parameters and correlations |
| `Correlations of Soil Properties.pdf` | Correlation compendium |
| `8 Determination of Geotechnical Parameters.pdf` | Parameter selection method |
| Schnaid, *In Situ Testing in Geomechanics* | Interpreting in-situ tests |
| Das, *Principles of Geotechnical Engineering* (8th ed.) | General reference |
| Lambe & Whitman, *Soil Mechanics* | Fundamentals |
| `SPT direct methods for prediction of pile bearing capacity...pdf` | SPT-to-pile-capacity methods |
| `Munsell Color Chart.pdf` | Colour description — pair with [[Soil description order]] |
| `Shallow Bearing Capacity - Various Methods and Settlement Rev 4.xltm` | Our bearing capacity spreadsheet |
| `Earth pressure calculations.xlsx` | Retaining wall pressures |
| `Working Platforms for tracked plant.pdf` | Working platform design for piling rigs |

## The discipline that matters here

A correlation is valid for the material and test it was derived from. Carrying
an SPT-based capacity into a rock socket, or a sand correlation into clay,
produces a confident number with no basis. State the source and the assumed
material whenever one of these is used.

## Related

notes.title: Rock strength classes
notes.body:
# Rock strength classes

Field estimates of unconfined compressive strength, per
[[AS 1726 soil and rock description]]. Assessed with a geological pick and
hand pressure, and recorded as an estimate — a field class is not a laboratory
UCS result and should never be reported as one.

| Class | Approx. UCS | Field behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| EL — extremely low | < 0.6 MPa | Crumbles under firm hand pressure |
| VL — very low | 0.6–2 MPa | Peels with a knife; deep pick indentation |
| L — low | 2–6 MPa | Pick indents; cannot be peeled |
| M — medium | 6–20 MPa | Shallow pick indentation |
| H — high | 20–60 MPa | Hand specimen breaks with one firm hammer blow |
| VH — very high | 60–200 MPa | Several blows to break |
| EH — extremely high | > 200 MPa | Chips only |

## The judgement to be careful with

Strength varies with moisture and with defect spacing. A tightly bedded siltstone
can rate medium on intact fragments and behave far weaker as a mass because it
parts along bedding. Log the defects as well as the intact strength.

## Related

- [[Rock weathering classes]]
- [[Rock socket length]]

notes.title: Rock weathering classes
notes.body:
# Rock weathering classes

Per [[AS 1726 soil and rock description]], in decreasing order of weathering:

- **RS** — residual soil. Soil texture; original fabric destroyed.
- **XW** — extremely weathered. Has soil strength but rock fabric survives.
- **HW** — highly weathered. Discoloured throughout, strength much reduced.
- **MW** — moderately weathered. Discoloured, partly reduced strength.
- **SW** — slightly weathered. Slight discolouration, strength near fresh.
- **FR** — fresh. No visible weathering.

## Where the founding decision sits

For bored piers, the usual requirement is founding in rock that is at worst
moderately weathered and of a stated minimum strength — weathering class alone
does not carry the requirement. XW material can look convincingly like rock in
the base of a pier and still behave as a stiff soil. Class it honestly and pair
it with a strength assessment; see [[Rock strength classes]].

## Related

- [[Weathered siltstone]]
- [[Bored pier inspection]]

notes.title: Soil description order
notes.body:
# Soil description order

The sequence a soil description is written in, per [[AS 1726 soil and rock description]].

**SOIL NAME: plasticity or particle characteristics, colour, secondary
components, structure, consistency or density, moisture, origin**

Example as logged: `CLAY: high plasticity, pale grey mottled red-orange, trace
fine sand, stiff, moist, residual`

## Why the order is fixed

Logs are read as a column, scanned for change. Putting the governing material
first means the eye catches the boundary. Everything after it is qualification.

## Consistency vs density

Consistency terms (very soft, soft, firm, stiff, very stiff, hard) are for
cohesive soils. Density index terms (very loose, loose, medium dense, dense,
very dense) are for granular soils. Mixing the two — "dense clay" — is a logging
error that will be picked up in review.

## Related

- [[Rock weathering classes]]
- [[Borehole log conventions]]

notes.title: Weathered siltstone
notes.body:
# Weathered siltstone

The material most of our western Sydney bored piers found on. Ashfield Shale and
related Wianamatta Group siltstones, weathered from the surface down.

## Typical profile

Residual high-plasticity silty clay, pale grey mottled red-orange, roughly
0.0–1.2 m thick, over extremely to moderately weathered siltstone. Rockhead is
often gradational rather than a clean surface, which is why proving it needs the
pier base inspected rather than a depth called from a nearby borehole.

*Source: STS report 26/0988, 24-26 Carter Street Lidcombe, 18 piers inspected
27 Jul 2026 — piers founded 1.8–3.3 m below platform with sockets 0.6–2.0 m.*

## What to watch

- Slaking. Exposed siltstone softens quickly once wet, which is the reason
  [[AS 2159 piling]] wants concrete placed promptly.
- The XW/HW boundary is where most disagreements happen. See
  [[Rock weathering classes]].

## Related

- [[Bored pier inspection]]

notes.title: Bored pier inspection
notes.body:
# Bored pier inspection

What gets checked and recorded at the base of a bored pier before concrete.

## On site

1. Confirm the pier reference against the [[Borehole log conventions|structural drawing]] — pier tag, not just position.
2. Record depth to founding level and depth to rockhead, both below the working platform.
3. Describe the founding material: [[Rock weathering classes|weathering]], [[Rock strength classes|strength]], defects.
4. Measure the achieved socket — see [[Rock socket length]].
5. Confirm the base is clean and free of loose or softened material.
6. Note groundwater — see [[Groundwater observations]].
7. Photograph the base with the pier tag visible in frame.

## What the report can and cannot say

It can say the exposed material was competent and consistent with the design
assumption at the time of inspection. It cannot certify the pile. Acceptance
against the design requirement needs the required socket length from the
approved drawing, which the inspection report often does not carry — see
[[Socket compliance is indeterminate by default]].

## The recurring failure

Reporting a depth without the platform level it was measured from. A depth below
ground is not a level, and once the platform is cut or filled the number means
nothing. See [[Reduced levels and datums]].

## Related

- [[AS 2159 piling]]

notes.title: Borehole log conventions
notes.body:
# Borehole log conventions

How our logs are laid out, and the reasons behind the layout.

## Columns

Depth scale, graphic log, material description, sampling and in-situ tests,
water, and remarks. The depth scale runs downward with the description beside
it, so a reader scanning for a boundary tracks one column.

## Description

Per [[Soil description order]] for soil and the weathering plus strength pairing
for rock — [[Rock weathering classes]], [[Rock strength classes]].

## What must appear on every log

- Hole reference, and the method and rig used.
- Surface RL and its datum, or an explicit note that it is assumed. See
  [[Reduced levels and datums]].
- Date drilled and who logged it.
- Groundwater observations with timing — [[Groundwater observations]].
- Where the log was terminated and why: target depth, refusal, or obstruction.

## Related

- [[AS 1726 soil and rock description]]

notes.title: DCP testing
notes.body:
# DCP testing

Dynamic cone penetrometer — 9 kg hammer, 510 mm drop, driving a 20 mm cone.
Blows per 100 mm increment. Quick, cheap, and shallow.

## What it is good for

Consistency and density profiling in the top couple of metres, checking that
founding material is as expected across a footprint, and identifying soft spots
and fill.

## What it is not

It is not a bearing capacity test. Correlations from blow counts to allowable
bearing pressure carry wide scatter, and they are correlations for the material
type assumed. Applying a sand correlation to clay produces a confident number
that is wrong.

## Reporting

Report the blow count profile. If an allowable bearing pressure is given,
state the correlation used, the assumed material and the depth range it applies
over, and flag refusal or possible obstruction rather than reading it as very
dense material.

## Related

- [[AS 2870 residential site classification]]
- [[Groundwater observations]]

notes.title: Graph engineering
notes.body:
# Graph engineering

A way of laying out agent work as a dependency map rather than a list of steps.

- **Node** — one unit of work. One input, one output. The smaller and more
  defined, the more useful.
- **Edge** — a real dependency. It exists only when the second node consumes
  what the first produced.

## The fake-edge test

Write the steps as boxes, draw an arrow between each consecutive pair, then ask
of every arrow: *does data from A actually go into B?* If not, the arrow is an
artefact of the order you typed things in, and the wait it imposes is free time
you are giving away. Anything with no incoming arrow can start immediately.

Most workflows hold two or three fake edges. "Review file A, then review file B"
is the classic — B never reads A's output.

## The diamond

One node fans out to several independent nodes, which all converge on one node
that combines them. The convergence waits for the slowest branch rather than the
sum of all branches.

Two conditions. The parallel nodes must be genuinely independent, and the
convergence must actually need all of them. If it only needs one, the rest are
wasted work.

## Checker nodes

Parallelism removes the natural checkpoints where you would have spotted a bad
result. A branch that returns nothing, or hallucinates, feeds into synthesis
alongside good branches and the final answer is confidently wrong — with the
error diluted enough to be hard to trace.

A checker sits between the parallel layer and the convergence and does no work
of its own. It looks for empty outputs, outputs that contradict each other,
off-topic results, low confidence, and format errors that would break parsing.
Flagged branches are retried or dropped, never merged.

## Static vs dynamic

Static graphs are fixed before the run: fast, predictable, auditable. Dynamic
graphs grow as they run, with nodes deciding what comes next — flexible, but
what actually ran is not what you drew, which makes debugging and auditing
harder. Reach for static first. Never use dynamic where you need to audit
exactly what ran and why, which for engineering work is most of the time.

## Where this already exists in our work

The `geoflow-verify-graph` skill in this repo is a diamond: independent
read-only verifier agents fan out, a barrier collects their reports, findings
are reduced, fixed, and re-verified. The reduce step is the checker.

## Where graphs break

Three failure modes, all worth designing against before you hit them.

**Context collapse.** Fan out to hundreds of nodes and try to feed every raw
output into one synthesis step, and you exhaust the context window before
synthesis begins. Fix: layer the fan-in — group into batches, summarise each
batch, then consolidate the summaries rather than the raw outputs.

**False independence.** Two nodes look independent because neither prompt
mentions the other, but they write to the same file or share a rate-limited
API. That is a hidden edge. Audit for shared *resources*, not just shared data —
a write conflict needs an edge even with no data dependency.

**Silent node failure.** In a chain a failure stops everything, which is
annoying but obvious. In a graph one dead node among two hundred disappears into
a report that looks complete. Fix: the fan-in checks the count it received
against the count it expected and says so when they differ, rather than quietly
synthesising partial data. This is the same principle as
[[Socket compliance is indeterminate by default]] — missing input produces a
stated gap, never a confident answer.

## Loops versus graphs

A loop is one unit of self-improvement: try, measure, adjust, repeat. Its known
failure is Goodhart — it optimises the metric you named and nothing else, so a
bot tuned to close tickets fast closes them fast while satisfaction falls. A
graph mitigates this structurally: several nodes with different jobs check each
other, so no single metric drives the system.

The shift in practice is that you stop writing the agent that does everything
top to bottom and start designing the dependency structure. The agents fill in
the nodes; you own the edges.

## Caution for engineering use

The parallel-then-combine shape is right for review and search. It is wrong for
anything where one branch's finding should change what another branch looks for
— which happens often in ground investigation, where a single unexpected result
should redirect the whole enquiry rather than being averaged in with the rest.

## Related

- [[Reverse prompting]]
- [[Socket compliance is indeterminate by default]] — a checker in a different guise

notes.title: Groundwater observations
notes.body:
# Groundwater observations

A water level in an open hole is an observation at a moment, not a water table.

## What to record

- Depth to water, and the time since the hole was advanced to that depth.
- Whether water was added during drilling.
- Whether the level was still rising when observed.
- Seepage: at what depth, and whether it was a defined horizon.
- "Not encountered" as an explicit statement, because absence of a note is not
  the same as absence of water.

## Why the caveat matters

In low-permeability clay a hole can take days to equilibrate, so a short-term
reading understates the standing level. In fractured rock the reading may reflect
one defect rather than a regional level. Neither is a design groundwater level
without a standpipe and repeat readings.

## Related

- [[Bored pier inspection]]
- [[DCP testing]]

notes.title: Reduced levels and datums
notes.body:
# Reduced levels and datums

RL is height above a datum, increasing upward. Depth is measured downward from a
surface. They are not interchangeable and the confusion between them causes real
errors.

```
depth below platform = platform RL − toe RL
toe RL              = platform RL − depth below platform
```

## Rules we hold to

- Every depth is recorded with the surface it was measured from.
- Every level records its datum — AHD, or a stated site datum, or "assumed".
- An assumed datum is written as assumed. A level on an assumed datum cannot be
  compared with a surveyed one, and a model built on it is dimensionally right
  and absolutely wrong.

## Where it bites

A report that tabulates depths below ground with no platform RL cannot be turned
into a model with true levels. The pile viewer marks the platform level
`inferred` in that case and flags every level derived from it, rather than
quietly assuming zero — see [[Why pile data carries provenance]].

## Related

notes.text: Reduced levels and datums RL is height above a datum, increasing upward. Depth is measured downward from a surface. They are not interchangeable and the confusion between them causes real errors. Rules we hold to Every depth is recorded with the surface it was measured from. Every level records its datum — AHD, or a stated site datum, or "assumed". An assumed datum is written as assumed. A level on an assumed datum cannot be compared with a surveyed one, and a model built on it is dimensionally right and absolutely wrong. Where it bites A report that tabulates depths below ground with no platform RL cannot be turned into a model with true levels. The pile viewer marks the platform level inferred in that case and flags every level derived from it, rather than quietly assuming zero — see Why pile data carries provenance. notes.title: Reverse prompting
notes.body:
# Reverse prompting

Instead of writing a prompt, hand over context and let the agent ask what else it
needs. The useful form is a single question:

> Based on what you know about me and my goals, what more could I give you so you
> can help faster and take more off my plate?

Then: *what can you do right now that moves us toward that?*

## Why it works

Not because the model knows things you don't. It works because the model can see
the shape of the gap in what you've given it, and asking forces you to articulate
things you'd otherwise leave tacit. Most bad AI output traces to missing context
rather than weak reasoning, and this closes that gap faster than you guessing what
to include.

## Where it does not

The model cannot ask about a domain it has no purchase on, so in narrow technical
work you still have to seed it. And questions cost your attention — a long
interview that produces a note you could have written in two minutes is a net
loss. Keep interviews short and aimed at knowledge that is genuinely in your head
and nowhere else.

## How it is used here

The Capture mode in the [[Index|second brain]] viewer is this idea made concrete:
pick a note type and it interviews you, then emits a vault-ready Markdown note
with frontmatter, tags and wikilinks. The questions are a fixed bank rather than
an LLM, so it works offline and produces the same structure every time. A live
model asking follow-ups would need an API key and a backend, which the static
worker does not have.

## Related

- [[Template - site inspection note]]

notes.title: Rock socket length
notes.body:
# Rock socket length

The length of pier penetrating competent rock, measured from proved rockhead to
the toe.

```
socket = top-of-bedrock RL − toe RL
```

## Required vs achieved

Two different numbers that get confused constantly.

- **Required** comes from the approved structural drawing or pile schedule. It
  is a design requirement.
- **Achieved** is what was built and measured on site.

A report giving only the achieved socket cannot demonstrate compliance. The tool
handles this by refusing to call it a pass — see
[[Socket compliance is indeterminate by default]].

## Measuring honestly

Rockhead is often gradational in [[Weathered siltstone]], so the socket depends
on where you call the top of competent rock. Record the weathering class at that
level, not just the depth, so the call can be reviewed.

## Related

- [[Bored pier inspection]]
- [[Why pile data carries provenance]]

notes.body:
# CG24-0137-A - Burra Park desktop review, Badgerys Creek

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG24-0137-A Rev 0.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG24-0137-A Rev 0 |
| Issued | 2024-02-05 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | Development Risk Management Pty Ltd, Suite 7, 265-271 Pennant Hills Road, Thornleigh NSW 2120 (Attention: Nalin De Silva) |
| Site | 1953-2109 Burra Park, Elizabeth Drive, Badgerys Creek NSW - about 344ha total, with the review limited to the Stage 1 (southern) portion of about 172ha south of the proposed M12 motorway |
| Project | Proposed Industrial Development (Burra Park industrial estate) |
| Document type | geotechnical desktop review and data gap analysis |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Desktop review of three earlier Douglas Partners reports plus survey and
cut/fill drawings, to summarise known ground conditions for the Stage 1 land and
identify gaps in the existing data. No new fieldwork was undertaken by CG.

## Fieldwork

Not stated in the report.

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Blacktown residual soil landscape over most of the site - clayey soils derived from Wianamatta Group sedimentary rocks, mostly shale
- South Creek landscape along the creeks - alluvial/fluvial soils transported towards creek lines
- Per DP 2022b: depth to top of weathered rock 1.3m to 4.2m below ground level; depth to medium or higher strength rock 8.0m to more than 10m

## Rock

Reported by Douglas Partners (DP 2022b) from eight boreholes (four from 2020 to
6.7-11.0m, four more to 9-10m, both with NMLC/rock coring). Top of weathered
rock 1.3m to 4.2m depth; medium or higher strength rock 8.0m to >10m. CG
cautions that high strength Minchinbury Sandstone layers may occur at the
Bringelly Shale / Ashfield Shale interface even though this is not shown on
geological maps.

## Groundwater

No groundwater information is given in this document.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Total site area | about 344 (project described as about 350ha overall) | ha |
| Stage 1 study area (south of M12, based on Six Map) | about 172 | ha |
| Frontage to Elizabeth Drive | about 1,350 | m |
| Site elevation range | about RL 75m AHD near Elizabeth Drive to about RL 50m AHD near Cosgroves Creek | m AHD |
| DP 2019 salinity distribution (40 samples from 10 test pits) | Non Saline 47.5%, Slightly Saline 20.0%, Moderately Saline 25.0%, Highly Saline 0.0%, Very Saline 7.5% | % |
| Test pits with moderately or higher saline soils below 0.5m (DP 2019) | 6 of 10 | - |

| DP 2019 site classification (AS2870-2011) | typically Class M (moderately reactive) and Class H (highly reactive) | - |
| DP 2019 sodicity (40 samples) | 33% non sodic, 25% sodic, 43% highly sodic | - |
| Sodicity thresholds cited | ESP 5-15% sodic; ESP >15% highly sodic | % |
| Aggressive soil thresholds cited | pH less than 5.5 and chloride/sulphate above 5000 mg/kg | - |
| DP 2019 CBR range (5 tests, samples from 0.3-1.0m) | 3.5 to 6 | % |
| DP 2022a salinity (78 samples from 14 test pits) | 29 samples (about 37%) moderately saline or higher | - |
