notes.body:
# CG25-1254-B - Queenscliff culvert replacement

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG25-1254-B Rev 0.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG25-1254-B Rev 0 |
| Issued | 2025-10-24 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd, Suite 2.01, 828 Pacific Highway, Gordon NSW 2072 |
| Site | Northern end of Queenscliff Beach NSW, on the sandstone rock platform adjacent to the ocean pool and promenade (Northern Beaches Council LGA) |
| Project | Proposed Culvert Replacement |
| Document type | geotechnical investigation for marine/intertidal remedial works |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Investigation of the ground beneath a dislodged stormwater culvert outlet in the
intertidal zone. Two cored boreholes and laboratory testing supported advice on
depth to bedrock, allowable bearing pressure, anchor design parameters, site
preparation and aggressivity for reinstatement of the outlet.

## Fieldwork

- BYDA search before drilling; specialist on-site services search
- Field investigation on 7 October 2025, logged to AS1726 (2017)
- Walkover survey of landform, site conditions and adjacent structures
- Two boreholes BH01 and BH02 cored by NMLC technique with portable rock coring equipment, terminated at 5.67m to 5.86m; 50mm hole size; core photographed
- Drilling contractor Tightsight Sampling Pty Ltd; BH01 R.L. surface 1.55m, BH02 R.L. surface 1.59m
- Selected rock core samples sent to NATA accredited laboratories under Chain of Custody
- Test locations measured from the supplied plan to about +/-1m

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Bedrock only: SANDSTONE, slightly weathered, fine grained, pale grey, yellow brown, few planar discontinuities, medium to wide spacing, oxide staining on some faces, surfaces mostly fresh to slightly stained, medium to high strength, Class III/II; base >5.67 - >5.86m

## Rock

Hawkesbury Sandstone (Rh), slightly weathered Class III/II, medium to high
strength, encountered from the rock platform surface to the base of both holes.
Is50 values 0.085 to 0.84MPa (very low to medium strength classification),
estimated UCS 1.27 to 12.6MPa. Eight PLSI tests: BH01 2.7-2.8m 0.56/0.31 Medium;
BH01 2.9-3.0m 0.72/0.44 Medium; BH01 3.9-4.0m 0.32/0.46 Medium; BH01 4.9-5.0m
0.37/0.74 Medium; BH02 2.94-3.0m 0.38/0.47 Medium; BH02 3.46-3.56m 0.085/0.27
Very Low; BH02 4.0-4.08m 0.37/0.24 Medium; BH02 5.58-5.6m 0.45/0.84 Medium
(diametral/axial MPa).

## Groundwater

No regional water table was measured. Drilling was within the intertidal zone
with the collar on the rock platform and the hole advancing in seawater from the
start, so observed water levels reflected tides and wave setup rather than
groundwater. Levels are expected to fluctuate rapidly with tides, swell and
rainfall, and seepage from the sandstone face may vary seasonally. No long-term
monitoring was undertaken.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Borehole termination depths | 5.67 to 5.86 | m |
| Hole size | 50 | mm |
| R.L. surface, BH01 / BH02 | 1.55 / 1.59 | m |
| Is50 range | 0.085 to 0.84 | MPa |
| Estimated UCS range | 1.27 to 12.6 | MPa |
| Allowable bearing pressure, Class III/II sandstone | 8 | MPa |
| Settlement criterion governing the ABP | total settlement not to exceed 1% of the minimum footing dimension | - |
| Ultimate compressive socket side shear for anchors/grouted dowels in Class III/II sandstone | 1,200 | kPa |
| Aggressivity, BH01 5.0-5.4m Sandstone/Bedrock | FMC 6.7%, pH 9.5, conductivity 828 uS/cm, resistivity 1,210 Ohm.cm, chloride 1,060 ppm, sulphate 250 ppm | - |
| Aggressivity, BH02 3.56-3.58m Sandstone/Bedrock | FMC 14.8%, pH 9.5, conductivity 686 uS/cm, resistivity 1,460 Ohm.cm, chloride 970 ppm, sulphate 240 ppm | - |
| Aggressivity classification (AS2159-2009) | Mild for concrete piles (Table 6.4.2(C)); Moderate for steel piles (Table 6.5.2(C)) | - |
| Laboratory testing quantities | 8 PLSI (AS4133.4.1); 1 aggressivity suite (APHA) | - |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

- Undertake dilapidation surveys of nearby structures before construction and have owners confirm the records
- Schedule work around low tide with standby allowance for adverse swell; install barriers, exclusion zones and spotters and keep emergency egress along the promenade and pool
- Secure permits for working on/near water, council land, maritime/coastal areas, heritage and ecology; locate subsurface services before demolition
- Treat any dewatering as temporary tide management only, not groundwater drawdown; discharge in accordance with regulations
- Plan lifts for restricted access using small plant or portable tools and secure equipment against wave action
- Design footings on Class III/II sandstone for an allowable bearing pressure of 8MPa, selecting a working pressure that keeps total settlement under 1% of the minimum footing dimension; reduce parameters where unfavourable defects, clay seams or open joints occur
- Design anchors and grouted dowels in Class III/II sandstone on an ultimate compressive socket side shear of 1,200 kPa, with cleaned sockets at R2 roughness or better and full grout contact
- Provide marine-grade corrosion protection for permanent anchors and locate bond zones below potential scour and beneath any weak weathered surface zone
- Proof-load representative anchors and record load-displacement before lock-off
- Clear founding areas of marine growth, debris and softened material and have them inspected before grout or concrete placement
- Govern durability design by the marine splash/tidal environment rather than the soil aggressivity results, which are typically less severe
- Keep records of hole cleanliness/roughness, grout pressures and volumes, proof-test results, as-built founding levels and photographs of prepared bearing surfaces

## Stated limitations

- Prepared for the exclusive use of H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd for the described development
- Conclusions based on interpolation between two boreholes; conditions can vary between test locations
- Depths and layer thicknesses in Table 2 apply to the investigation locations and may not represent the whole site
- Aggressivity ratings relate to soil contact conditions only
- Not to be used as part of a project specification without CG review and agreement; must be read in its entirety with the Information Sheets
- Listed further geotechnical inputs are hold points only; the contractor remains responsible for means, methods, temporary works and approvals

## Reviewer flags

Table 3 (aggressivity) is column-scrambled in the extraction; values mapped by
header order. Two minor text inconsistencies: Section 8.1 says 'Two (2) samples
were collected' while Table 1 records the aggressivity suite quantity as 1 (two
rows of results are reported); Section 7.2 describes the site as underlain by
'Wianamatta Group Hawkesbury Sandstone (Rh)' whereas Hawkesbury Sandstone sits
below the Wianamatta Group. Only bedrock was logged - no soil profile. Author
Jeevan Reddy, reviewer Raj Singh, approved 24.10.2025.

## Standards cited

AS1726-2017 Geotechnical Site Investigation, AS2159-2009 Piling - Design and Construction (Tables 6.4.2(C) and 6.5.2(C)), AS4133.4.1 (Point Load Strength Index), APHA (aggressivity suite), Pells, Mostyn, Bertuzzi and Wong, Classification of Sandstones and Shales in the Sydney Region: A forty year review, Vol 54 No 2, June 2019, Sydney 1:100,000 Geological Series Sheet 9130 (Edition 1) 1983

Eight PLSI tests: BH01 2.7 2.8m 0.56/0.31 Medium; BH01 2.9 3.0m 0.72/0.44 Medium; BH01 3.9 4.0m 0.32/0.46 Medium; BH01 4.9 5.0m 0.37/0.74 Medium; BH02 2.94 3.0m 0.38/0.47 Medium; BH02 3.46 3.56m 0.085/0.27 Very Low; BH02 4.0 4.08m 0.37/0.24 Medium; BH02 5.58 5.6m 0.45/0.84 Medium (diametral/axial MPa). Groundwater No regional water table was measured. Drilling was within the intertidal zone with the collar on the rock platform and the hole advancing in seawater from the start, so observed water levels reflected tides and wave setup rather than groundwater. Levels are expected to fluctuate rapidly with tides, swell and rainfall, and seepage from the sandstone face may vary seasonally. No long term monitoring was undertaken. See Groundwater observations for what a level in a hole does and does not tell you. Design values as reported Value Figure Unit : : : Borehole termination depths 5.67 to 5.86 m Hole size 50 mm R.L. surface, BH01 / BH02 1.55 / 1.59 m Is50 range 0.085 to 0.84 MPa Estimated UCS range 1.27 to 12.6 MPa Allowable bearing pressure, Class III/II sandstone 8 MPa Settlement criterion governing the ABP total settlement not to exceed 1% of the minimum footing dimension Ultimate compressive socket side shear for anchors/grouted dowels in Class III/II sandstone 1,200 kPa Aggressivity, BH01 5.0 5.4m Sandstone/Bedrock FMC 6.7%, pH 9.5, conductivity 828 uS/cm, resistivity 1,210 Ohm.cm, chloride 1,060 ppm, sulphate 250 ppm Aggressivity, BH02 3.56 3.58m Sandstone/Bedrock FMC 14.8%, pH 9.5, conductivity 686 uS/cm, resistivity 1,460 Ohm.cm, chloride 970 ppm, sulphate 240 ppm Aggressivity classification (AS2159 2009) Mild for concrete piles (Table 6.4.2(C)); Moderate for steel piles (Table 6.5.2(C)) Laboratory testing quantities 8 PLSI (AS4133.4.1); 1 aggressivity suite (APHA) These are the report's numbers, not this vault's. They apply to the site, loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own limitations. Re derive or re check before using them anywhere else. Recommendations Undertake dilapidation surveys of nearby structures before construction and have owners confirm the records Schedule work around low tide with standby allowance for adverse swell; install barriers, exclusion zones and spotters and keep emergency egress along the promenade and pool Secure permits for working on/near water, council land, maritime/coastal areas, heritage and ecology; locate subsurface services before demolition Treat any dewatering as temporary tide management only, not groundwater drawdown; discharge in accordance with regulations Plan lifts for restricted access using small plant or portable tools and secure equipment against wave action Design footings on Class III/II sandstone for an allowable bearing pressure of 8MPa, selecting a working pressure that keeps total settlement under 1% of the minimum footing dimension; reduce parameters where unfavourable defects, clay seams or open joints occur Design anchors and grouted dowels in Class III/II sandstone on an ultimate compressive socket side shear of 1,200 kPa, with cleaned sockets at R2 roughness or better and full grout contact Provide marine grade corrosion protection for permanent anchors and locate bond zones below potential scour and beneath any weak weathered surface zone Proof load representative anchors and record load displacement before lock off Clear founding areas of marine growth, debris and softened material and have them inspected before grout or concrete placement Govern durability design by the marine splash/tidal environment rather than the soil aggressivity results, which are typically less severe Keep records of hole cleanliness/roughness, grout pressures and volumes, proof test results, as built founding levels and photographs of prepared bearing surfaces Stated limitations Prepared for the exclusive use of H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd for the described development Conclusions based on interpolation between two boreholes; notes.body:
# CG25-1430-A - Caddies Creek Reserve, Beaumont Hills

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG25-1430-A Rev 0.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG25-1430-A Rev 0 |
| Issued | 2026-01-18 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | Environmental Group Australia Pty Ltd, 36E Fitzroy Street, Marrickville NSW 2204 |
| Site | Caddies Creek Reserve Stage 2, Sanctuary Drive, Beaumont Hills NSW (The Hills Shire Council LGA) |
| Project | Proposed Caddies Creek Reserve Stage 2 - Football Centre of Excellence and associated reserve infrastructure |
| Document type | geotechnical investigation |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Core Geotech investigated the Stage 2 reserve footprint to characterise ground
conditions for four soccer pitches, car parks and access roads, a Centre of
Excellence building, sports field lighting poles, and vehicle and pedestrian
bridges over Caddies Creek and an unnamed tributary. Work covered a walkover, 41
boreholes with in-situ testing, laboratory testing, and engineering advice on
earthworks, pavement design, foundations, groundwater and soil aggressivity.
Advice is preliminary and intended to support concept and early design
development.

## Fieldwork

- Site walkover survey and BYDA search plus contractor on-site services search
- 41 boreholes (BH01 to BH41) drilled with ute and track mounted rigs using 110 mm solid flight auger, terminated/refused at 2 m to 6.45 m
- 5 of those holes (BH32, BH33, BH39, BH40, BH41) extended by NMLC rock coring after auger refusal, to 8.12 m to 8.36 m
- DCP, pocket penetrometer and SPT testing in selected boreholes
- Groundwater observations during and shortly after drilling; holes backfilled by hand with spoil
- Disturbed sampling for NATA-accredited geotechnical and chemical laboratory testing
- Fieldwork undertaken on 28 October 2025, 2 to 6 November 2025, 13 November 2025, and 3, 10 and 11 December 2025

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Playing fields and turf areas (BH11-BH18, BH20-BH22, BH24-BH31, BH34) - Topsoil: silty clay/silty sand, fine to medium grained, grey, low plasticity fines, grass rootlets, moist; base 0.2-0.5 m
- Playing fields - Fill (local only): silty clay / silty sandy clay / clayey gravel / gravelly clay, low to high plasticity, brown and grey, moisture < plastic limit; base 0.5-2.5 m
- Playing fields - Alluvium: clay/silty clay, high plasticity, yellow, grey, brown grading to pale grey, moisture > plastic limit, stiff to very stiff; base >3.0-5.6 m
- Playing fields - Residual: clay, high plasticity, pale grey, red, orange, trace ironstone, moisture > plastic limit, stiff to very stiff; base 2.2->6.15 m
- Playing fields - Bedrock: shale, extremely weathered, fine to medium grained, grey/brown, very low strength, Class V, locally interbedded siltstone/laminite; base >4.5->6.45 m
- Carparks 1-3 and access road (BH01-BH10, BH35-BH38) - Topsoil: silty clay, medium plasticity, grey to brown, trace grass rootlets, moisture < plastic limit; base 0.2-0.3 m
- Carparks/access road - Fill: silty clay/silty sand/silty gravelly clay, low to medium plasticity with trace sand to gravel, moist to >= plastic limit; base 0.3-2.5 m
- Carparks/access road - Alluvium: silty clay/clay, medium to high plasticity, pale orange/red through grey to dark grey, trace fine sand or gravel locally, moisture commonly >= plastic limit; base >2.0->3.0 m
- Carparks/access road - Residual: silty clay, medium to high plasticity, red to pale orange to grey, trace fine sand and gravel, moisture >= plastic limit, generally very stiff; base 0.8-1.5 m
- Carparks/access road - Bedrock: shale, extremely weathered, fine grained, dark grey, very low to low strength, Class V; base >1.1->2.0 m
- Centre of Excellence building (BH19, BH23) - Fill: silty clay, medium plasticity, dark brown, trace sand and grass rootlets, moisture < plastic limit; base 0.5 m
- Centre of Excellence building - Residual: silty clay, medium plasticity, brown to grey brown, moisture < plastic limit, very stiff; base 1.6-1.7 m
- Centre of Excellence building - Bedrock: shale, extremely weathered, fine grained, grey becoming pale brown red, very low to low strength, Class V; base >4.5->5.0 m
- Bridges (BH32, BH33, BH39, BH40, BH41) - Topsoil: silty sandy clay, low plasticity, brown, fine to medium grained sand, grass rootlets, moisture < plastic limit; base 0.2 m
- Bridges - Fill (BH39 and BH41 only): silty sandy clay/silty clay, low to medium plasticity, brown, fine to medium sand, moisture < plastic limit; base 1.5-2.0 m
- Bridges - Alluvium: silty clay/clay, low to high plasticity, yellow and brown, moisture < plastic limit, stiff; base 2.7-3.2 m
- Bridges - Residual: silty clay/clay, low to high plasticity, brown, red, orange, pale grey with fine sand, moisture < plastic limit, stiff to very stiff; base 2.3-4.5 m
- Bridges - Bedrock: shale, extremely weathered, dark grey, very low to low strength, Class V, base 4.5-6.0 m; shale, highly weathered, grey, low strength, Class IV, base 5.3-6.85 m; siltstone/laminite, slightly weathered, dark grey, medium strength, Class III/IV, base 6.0->8.36 m; siltstone/laminite, slightly weathered, pale grey, medium to high strength, Class III, base >8.12->8.21 m
- Sports field lighting (BH11, BH14, BH15, BH16, BH22, BH26, BH27, BH29, BH30, BH34) - Topsoil base 0.2-0.5 m; Fill (silty clay/silty gravelly clay, low to medium plasticity) base 0.8-2.5 m; Alluvium (silty clay/clay, medium to high plasticity, mottled, very soft to very stiff) base 3.0-5.6 m; Residual clay (medium to high plasticity, locally trace shale fragments, stiff to very stiff) base 0.5->6.15 m; Bedrock extremely weathered shale Class V base >4.5->6.3 m

## Rock

Ashfield Shale (Wianamatta Group) was reached in most boreholes at variable
depth reflecting the floodplain setting. It is shallowest under the Centre of
Excellence building, where extremely weathered shale was met at about 1.6-1.7 m
in BH19 and BH23, and shallow in BH15 under the lighting area. Under the
pavements, extremely weathered Class V shale was logged from as shallow as about
1.1-2.0 m. At the bridge locations the cored profile runs from extremely
weathered Class V shale (base 4.5-6.0 m) through highly weathered Class IV shale
(base 5.3-6.85 m) into slightly weathered Class III/IV and Class III
siltstone/laminite of medium to high strength below about 6.0-8.2 m. Point load
Is(50) results on core ranged from 0.044 to 0.83 MPa diametral and 0.082 to 1.6
MPa axial, classified very low to high strength. No RLs are recorded on the
logs, so rockhead is expressed in depth only.

## Groundwater

Section 8.4 states groundwater was not encountered in BH12, BH18, BH20 to BH22,
BH24 to BH26, BH30, BH31, BH33, BH35 and BH36 to depths of 1.8 m to 5 m at the
time of investigation, and notes levels may not have stabilised over the short
observation window. Circulating water used for the cored holes (BH32, BH33,
BH39, BH40, BH41) prevented any water level measurement. Later sections report
groundwater as encountered: about 1.8 m in BH35 and about 2 m in BH36 (Carpark
3), about 5 m in BH30 and about 2 m in BH31 (Field 4), and about 3 m in BH22, 5
m in BH26 and 5 m in BH30 (lighting). No standpipes or longer-term monitoring
were installed. See notes_for_reviewer - Section 8.4 and Sections
10.2.4/10.3.1/10.5 contradict each other for BH22, BH26, BH30, BH31, BH35 and
BH36.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Design subgrade CBR, Carparks 1 and 2 (preliminary) | 3 | % |
| Design subgrade CBR, Carpark 3 (preliminary) | 3 | % |
| Design subgrade CBR, access road (preliminary) | 3 | % |
| Assumed design traffic loading for carparks and access road | 5 x 10^5 | ESA |
| Preliminary pavement sub-base thickness | 270 | mm |
| Preliminary pavement base course thickness (DGB20) | 200 | mm |
| Preliminary pavement wearing course thickness (AC10) | 40 | mm |
| Preliminary total pavement thickness | 510 | mm |
| Estimated shrink-swell movement (AS2870 scope buildings, undisturbed moisture, no cut/fill) | 40 to 60 | mm |
| Allowable bearing pressure, shallow pad/strip footings on engineered fill (Level 1) or very stiff natural clay, min 0.8 m embedment | 150 | kPa |
| Allowable end bearing, shallow bored piers socketed min 0.6 m into competent extremely weathered shale (Centre of Excellence) | 700 | kPa |
| Ultimate unit shaft adhesion, shallow bored piers in shale (Centre of Excellence) | 50 | kPa |
| Light pole footings - very stiff residual clay, adopted undrained cohesion Cu | 150 | kPa |
| Light pole footings - very stiff residual clay, allowable bearing pressure | 250 | kPa |
| Light pole footings - very stiff residual clay, ultimate shaft adhesion | 30 | kPa |
| Light pole footings - very stiff residual clay, design Young's modulus | 30 | MPa |
| Light pole footings - Class V shale bedrock, allowable bearing pressure | 700 | kPa |
| Light pole footings - Class V shale bedrock, ultimate shaft adhesion | 50 | kPa |
| Light pole footings - Class V shale bedrock, design Young's modulus | 50 | MPa |
| Piled footings - depth of reactive clay over which shaft resistance should be ignored | 1.8 | m |
| Uplift screening check - proportion of compression shaft adhesion to adopt | 50 | % |
| Bridge foundations - Ashfield Shale Class III/IV and III, allowable bearing pressure | 2000 | kPa |
| Bridge foundations - Ashfield Shale Class III/IV and III, ultimate shaft adhesion | 350 | kPa |
| Bridge foundations - Ashfield Shale Class III/IV and III, design Young's modulus | 200 | MPa |
| Bridge bored pier assumed minimum socket length into competent Class III rock | 1 to 2 | m |
| Expected total settlement of bridge foundations at serviceability | less than about 1% of footing width or pile diameter | - |
| Engineered fill compaction, general fill (turf areas) | not less than 95 | % Standard MDD |
| Engineered fill compaction, upper formation zone beneath turf profile and trafficked areas | not less than 98 | % Standard MDD |
| Moisture control range about OMC for engineered fill | -2 to +2 | % of OMC |
| DGB20 base compaction, layers not exceeding 200 mm loose | at least 98 | % Modified MDD |
| Council minimum compaction - subgrade | 100 | % Standard |
| Council minimum compaction - sub-base layer | 98 | % Modified |
| Council minimum compaction - base course | 98 | % Modified |
| Minimum density testing frequency on granular pavement layers | 1 test per layer per 500 m2, or 3 tests per lot and 3 tests per visit, whichever is greater | - |
| Subsoil drain invert below pavement formation level | at least 200 | mm |
| Blinding concrete thickness if footing pour is delayed | at least 75 | mm |
| Field moisture content range (79 tests) | 7.3 to 28.0 | % |
| Liquid limit range | 29 to 77 | % |
| Plasticity index range | 12 to 59 | % |
| Linear shrinkage range | 5.5 to 18.5 | % |
| Soaked CBR range (7 samples) | 2.5 to 8 | % |
| CBR swell range | -0.5 to 2.0 | % |
| Maximum dry density range (CBR samples) | 1.53 to 1.86 | t/m3 |
| Percentage passing 0.075 mm (5 PSD samples) | 47 to 96 | % |
| pH range (35 samples) | 5.4 to 8.8 | - |
| Electrical conductivity range | <10 to 540 | uS/cm |
| Derived exposure classification (AS 2159 basis) | predominantly A1, with a small number of A2 | - |
| Cation exchange capacity range (11 samples) | 1.8 to 17 | meq/100g |
| Exchangeable sodium percentage range (11 samples) | 15 to 49 | % |
| SPT N value in very soft alluvium at BH12 | N=4 at about 1.5 m and N=2 at about 3.0 m | blows/300 mm |
| Aggressivity classification for concrete piles (AS 2159 Table 6.4.2(C)) | non aggressive, low permeability soils type B | - |
| Aggressivity classification for steel piles (AS 2159 Table 6.5.2(C)) | non aggressive, low permeability soils type B | - |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

- Strip topsoil across turf footprints and stockpile separately for reuse where the environmental consultant approves
- Treat all fill as uncontrolled unless placement and compaction records are produced
- Remove fill and unsuitable, disturbed or compressible material to expose competent natural subgrade, then inspect and proof roll before any filling
- Undercut and replace soft or pumping zones with engineered fill or imported granular material; use a temporary working platform where wet conditions persist
- Place all filling as engineered fill under Level 2 geotechnical control to AS 3798-2007 for fields and pavements, and Level 1 control for the Centre of Excellence building pad
- Set geotechnical hold points at completion of stripping, after soft spot treatment, before fill placement, and at acceptance of final platform level
- Stage earthworks to limit trafficking of exposed clay subgrades and re-proof roll after rain
- Expect localised very soft alluvium in Fields 2 and 3 near BH12 and allow extra undercut and replacement there
- For Field 4, plan deep fill removal (up to about 2.5 m) allowing for wet excavation and groundwater inflow, particularly near BH31, with sump pumping and staged excavation
- Adopt a preliminary design subgrade CBR of 3% for Carparks 1-3 and the access road, and confirm with further CBR testing after trimming and proof rolling
- Provide a capping layer beneath pavements and maintain positive drainage during construction and in the final works
- Use DGB20 base to TfNSW QA Specification 3051, compacted in layers not exceeding 200 mm loose
- Provide perimeter subsoil drains with invert at least 200 mm below pavement formation, connected to the site stormwater system
- Reassess AS 2870 differential movement after earthworks and immediately before building pad construction; design slabs using engineering principles allowing for reactivity
- For the Centre of Excellence building, either pad/strip footings at 150 kPa embedded at least 0.8 m, or shallow bored piers socketed at least 0.6 m into competent extremely weathered shale
- Pour high level footings promptly after excavation and cleaning; use 75 mm blinding concrete if the pour is delayed and prevent ponding in footing bases
- Use deep footings for all sports field light poles founded in very stiff residual clay or socketed into shale, except potentially BH15 where a shallow pad on shale may suit
- Ignore shaft resistance in the upper 1.8 m of reactive clay for piled footings and use 50% of compression shaft adhesion as an uplift screening value
- Use deep foundations for the vehicle and pedestrian bridges, with rock-socketed bored piers taken 1 to 2 m into competent Class III rock and founded below the design scour level
- Allow for temporary casing or drilling fluids through soft alluvium and below groundwater, and consider downdrag where new fill is placed
- Inspect all footing excavations, pile bores and rock sockets before reinforcement and concreting to confirm founding material, socket depth, cleanliness and groundwater inflow
- Use tremie placement where groundwater inflow prevents a dry founding surface
- Have CG review civil, structural, architectural and landscape drawings and the contractor's earthworks methodology before construction
- Re-engage CG if conditions differ materially from those described or if the design, layout or site levels change

## Stated limitations

- Prepared exclusively for Environmental Group Australia Pty Ltd, for the described development and purpose only, under CG's Terms of Engagement and proposal QU25-0109 Rev 0 dated 10 January 2025
- Conclusions rely on interpolation between boreholes; conditions can vary between test locations in ways the investigation cannot define
- Depths and layer thicknesses in Tables 2 to 6 are indicative only and may not represent the whole site
- No detailed contour survey was available at the time of reporting; site levels are based on walkover observations and aerial imagery
- Test locations were measured from the supplied plan to an accuracy of about +/- 5 m
- Groundwater levels may not have stabilised over the short observation period; no longer-term monitoring was undertaken and levels can fluctuate with rainfall, temperature and other factors
- Circulating water in the cored holes prevented groundwater measurement
- Foundation and pavement parameters are preliminary, to be confirmed by the structural and pavement designers and by construction-stage inspection
- AS 2870 provisions do not strictly apply to the Centre of Excellence building because of its size; the classification given is preliminary
- The report should not be used as part of a project specification without CG review and agreement, and must be kept whole and read with the attached Information Sheets
- Information supplied by the client and their agents was relied on and not independently verified

## Reviewer flags

Text extraction of the narrative and of Tables 1 to 16 is clean and legible.
Three things to check. First, a direct internal contradiction on groundwater:
Section 8.4 lists BH22, BH26, BH30, BH31, BH35 and BH36 among the holes where
groundwater was NOT encountered, but Sections 10.2.4, 10.3.1 and 10.5 report
groundwater encountered in exactly those holes at about 3 m (BH22), 5 m (BH26),
5 m (BH30), 2 m (BH31), 1.8 m (BH35) and 2 m (BH36). I have recorded both
statements rather than picking one. Second, the borehole logs in Appendix C have
a blank R.L. SURFACE field for all 41 holes, so no reduced levels exist anywhere
in this report and rockhead can only be quoted as depth below ground. The Water
column in the log graphics also extracted blank for the holes where water is
reported in the text, so the log-side evidence could not be cross-checked.
Third, Table 10 (salinity/exposure classification) has rotated column headers
that extracted as a vertical jumble above the data; the data rows themselves are
readable and in the order EC (uS/cm), multiplication factor, ECe, salinity
rating, pH, exposure classification, but a reviewer should confirm against the
source PDF before relying on individual rows. Table 11 (aggressivity) has the
same rotated-header issue. Also note Table 13 lists 18 PLSI rows while Table 1
schedules 20 PLSI tests. Minor typos in the source: 'laminate' is used for
'laminite' in Section 10.6, and Section 10.4.1 reads 'are likely produce'.

## Standards cited

AS 1726-2017, AS 2870-2011, AS 2159-2009, AS 3798-2007, AS 1289 series, AS 1289 3.1.2, 3.2.1, 3.3.1, 3.4.1, AS 1289 2.1.1, AS 1289 3.6.1, AS 1289.6.1.1, AS 4133.4.1, HB 160-2006, TfNSW QA Specification 3051, Austroads Guide to Pavement Technology Part 2: Pavement Structural Design (2017), APHA (aggressivity, EC/pH, CEC, ESP methods), CSIRO BTF-18

notes.title: CG26-0172-A - Osroy Avenue stormwater, Earlwood
notes.body:
# CG26-0172-A - Osroy Avenue stormwater, Earlwood

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG26-0172-A Rev 0.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG26-0172-A Rev 0 |
| Issued | 2026-02-25 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd, Suite 2.01, 828 Pacific Highway, Gordon NSW 2072 |
| Site | Steep vegetated corridor between Bayview Lane and Homer Street, off Osroy Avenue, Earlwood NSW (City of Canterbury Bankstown LGA) |
| Project | Proposed stormwater upgrade from Osroy Avenue to Homer Street, for Canterbury Bankstown Council |
| Document type | geotechnical investigation with AGS 2007 qualitative landslide risk assessment |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Core Geotech characterised the ground along the nominated rockface corridor for
a stormwater drainage upgrade and assessed slope instability hazards and risk
qualitatively to AGS (2007). Two concept options were considered: an open
channel of about 400 mm by 500 mm internal dimensions, or a nominally DN600
pipeline partly fixed above ground to the rockface with brackets and rock
anchors, possibly with intermediate drop structures. The assessment supports
concept planning and approvals only and excludes detailed design of
stabilisation, anchors, structural supports or temporary works; the client
advised that other parts of the broader drainage upgrade did not need
investigation.

## Fieldwork

- Site walkover survey and BYDA search plus contractor on-site services search
- 2 boreholes (BH01 and BH02) drilled on 3 February 2026 by Tightsight Sampling Pty Ltd, hand auger in soil and NMLC coring in rock with portable rock coring equipment, hole size 125 mm
- BH01 terminated at 4.13 m (surface RL 29.49 m); BH02 terminated at 3.77 m (surface RL 30.55 m)
- DCP tests carried out adjacent to the boreholes (DCP = 0 at BH01 surface, DCP = 7 at BH02 surface, with double bounce recorded at refusal)
- Rock core photographed and groundwater observations recorded during and shortly after drilling; boreholes backfilled by hand with spoil
- Disturbed soil and rock sampling for NATA-accredited laboratory testing (8 PLSI tests, 1 aggressivity suite)

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Unit 1 - Fill: silty sandy CLAY, low plasticity, grey, fine to medium grained sand, some grass rootlets, moisture < plastic limit; base 0.3-1.1 m
- Unit 2 - 'Probable' Residual (BH01 only): sandy CLAY, medium plasticity, brown and pale grey, fine to medium grained sand, moisture < plastic limit; base 1.5 m
- Unit 3a - Bedrock (BH01 only): SANDSTONE, extremely weathered, fine to medium grained, red, brown, pale grey, very low strength; base 1.69 m
- Unit 3c - Bedrock: sandstone, highly weathered, fine to medium grained, brown, very low strength, highly fractured to disaggregated, locally friable with soil-like infill, interpreted as a weathered seam or defect zone; base 2.85 m
- Unit 3b - Bedrock: SANDSTONE, slightly weathered, fine to medium grained, red and pale grey becoming grey, low to medium strength, Class IV/III; base >3.77 m (BH02) to >4.13 m (BH01)

## Rock

Hawkesbury Sandstone was reached in both holes. Extremely weathered very low
strength sandstone was logged in BH01 from about 1.5 m to 1.69 m; in BH02 the
fill passes into cored rock from about 0.3 m. Section 10.3 states competent
Class IV/III sandstone occurs at relatively shallow depth, typically below about
0.3 m to 1.69 m below existing ground level at the borehole locations. A
distinctly weaker highly weathered horizon (Unit 3c) was encountered in BH02 at
approximately 2.43 m to 2.85 m and may be localised. Point load Is(50) values
for the Hawkesbury Sandstone ranged from 0.0064 to 0.77 MPa, corresponding to
very low to medium strength, with estimated UCS of 0.096 to 11.55 MPa.

## Groundwater

Not encountered at the time of investigation. Both borehole logs record
GROUNDWATER NOT ENCOUNTERED. Circulating water used for the diamond drilling
prevented any groundwater level measurement. The report notes standing
groundwater and seepage can fluctuate with rainfall, temperature and other
factors.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Serviceability end bearing pressure, Hawkesbury Sandstone Class IV/III | 3000 | kPa |
| Ultimate compressive socket side shear, Hawkesbury Sandstone Class IV/III | 500 | kPa |
| Design Young's modulus, Hawkesbury Sandstone Class IV/III | 350 | MPa |
| Settlement basis for the quoted end bearing pressure | less than 1% of minimum footing dimension | - |
| Settlement at which ultimate socket side shear is mobilised | greater than 5% of minimum footing dimension | - |
| Point load Is(50) range, Hawkesbury Sandstone | 0.0064 to 0.77 | MPa |
| Estimated UCS range, Hawkesbury Sandstone | 0.096 to 11.55 | MPa |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - field moisture content | 2.5 | % |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - pH | 6.2 | - |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - electrical conductivity | 25 | uS/cm |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - resistivity | 40000 | Ohm.cm |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - chloride | 10 | ppm |
| BH01 3.88-3.95 m sandstone - sulphate | 10 | ppm |
| Aggressivity classification for concrete piles (AS 2159 Table 6.4.2(C)) | Mild, high permeability soils type A | - |
| Aggressivity classification for steel piles (AS 2159 Table 6.5.2(C)) | non aggressive, high permeability soils type A | - |
| Overall existing slope instability risk (AGS 2007 qualitative) | low to medium | - |
| Risk rating - rockfall from loosened blocks | Possible likelihood, Major consequence, High risk | - |
| Risk rating - localised wedge or toppling instability | Unlikely to Possible, Major, Medium to High | - |
| Risk rating - ravelling and shallow sloughing of soil or weathered sandstone | Possible, Moderate, Medium | - |
| Risk rating - construction induced loosening during drilling and fixing | Possible, Moderate to Major, Medium to High | - |
| Risk rating - fixings founded in highly weathered or weak sandstone bands | Unlikely to Possible, Moderate to Major, Medium to High | - |
| Risk rating - degraded legacy support elements or surface treatments | Unlikely to Possible, Major, Medium | - |
| Risk rating - water ingress, erosion or local undercutting | Unlikely to Possible, Moderate, Low to Medium | - |
| Risk rating - access and working at height constraints | Possible, Major, High | - |
| Option 1 open channel nominal internal dimensions | approximately 400 by 500 | mm |
| Option 2 pipeline nominal diameter | DN600 | - |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

- Treat the fill as uncontrolled under AS 2870-2011 because no placement, material or compaction records exist
- Carry out dilapidation surveys of underground services and nearby structures before construction, and have owners confirm the records
- Avoid conventional shallow footings for the stormwater infrastructure and support structures because of steep terrain, rock outcrop and variable near-surface materials
- Found supports, thrust blocks, headwalls, pits and pier supports in competent Class IV/III sandstone at depth
- Design socketed elements to extend past any highly weathered or low strength sandstone zone, such as the Unit 3c horizon logged in BH02
- Verify founding conditions at every rock anchor and bracket location; anchors must sit in competent sandstone, not in highly weathered bands, with proof testing where required
- Confirm final founding level and socket length during construction by inspecting excavations, reviewing drilling spoil and drill response, and short confirmatory coring where needed
- Establish delineated exclusion zones along the Homer Street footpath where required
- Have a suitably experienced geotechnical consultant carry out staged inspection of the rockface at and above proposed fixing locations, with scaling or removal of loose material where identified
- Do not assume the presence, condition or support function of legacy rock bolts and shotcrete without inspection
- Control stormwater discharge and temporary diversions and protect against scour at drop structures and outlets
- Undertake targeted supplementary investigation (test pits or short cores) at critical support locations where weaker weathered sandstone bands are suspected
- Review final civil and structural drawings and the contractor's methodology, including access arrangements and footpath protection
- Implement geotechnical inspection hold points at each support location before drilling and during socketing, and adjust socket lengths as needed
- Complete a post-installation inspection with periodic follow-up checks after major rainfall events
- Select concrete and steel appropriate to the assessed aggressivity
- Re-review the assessment once the final alignment, fixing locations and construction methodology are confirmed, or if the works materially change drainage, slope geometry or crest/toe loading

## Stated limitations

- Prepared exclusively for H & H Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd for the described development and purpose, under CG's Terms of Engagement and proposal QU25-0483 Rev 0 dated 28 October 2025
- The slope stability assessment is qualitative, indicative and based on a walkover plus limited boreholes and coring; it is not a detailed design of stabilisation measures, anchor systems, structural supports or temporary works
- Ratings reflect conditions at the time of inspection and may change once the final alignment and fixing locations are set, vegetation is cleared or drainage patterns are altered
- Depths and layer thicknesses in Table 2 are based on the two investigation locations and may not represent the whole site
- Test locations were measured from the supplied plan to an accuracy of about +/- 3 m
- Circulating water precluded groundwater measurement during diamond drilling; standing water and seepage can fluctuate seasonally
- Is(50) testing is not readily performed on extremely low to very low strength rock, so strength classification for weaker sequences relied on visual and tactile assessment
- Geotechnical design parameters are for preliminary sizing only; detailed foundation sizing and structural design remain with the project structural designer
- Vegetation, soil mantle and leaf litter obscure rock exposures and may conceal loosened blocks, open joints and debris
- Conclusions rely on interpolation between discrete test locations; variations between them cannot be explicitly defined
- Must not be used as part of a construction specification without CG's written agreement, and must be kept and reproduced whole with the attached Information Sheets

## Reviewer flags

Extraction is clean throughout; the narrative, Table 2 (strata), Table 4 (PLSI),
Table 5 (risk matrix) and Table 6 (foundation parameters) all read reliably. Two
caveats. Table 3 (aggressivity) has rotated column headers that extracted as a
vertical jumble; the single data row reads 2.5 / 6.2 / 25 / 40,000 / 10 / 10 and
I have mapped these to moisture content, pH, conductivity, resistivity, chloride
and sulphate in header order, which is consistent, but confirm against the
source PDF. Second, there is a small internal inconsistency in depth reporting
for the weak Unit 3c horizon: Table 2 gives its base at 2.85 m without an upper
bound or a borehole attribution, while Section 10.3 places it in BH02 at
approximately 2.43 m to 2.85 m; I have carried both. Note also that unlike the
companion report, RLs are present here (BH01 surface RL 29.49 m, BH02 surface RL
30.55 m, datum stated only as 'm'), so rockhead can be expressed as RL if
needed. No AS 2870 site classification is given because the works are drainage
infrastructure, not residential slabs and footings; AS 2870 is cited only for
the uncontrolled-fill definition. Also note Section 7.2 describes Hawkesbury
Sandstone as a 'Wianamatta Group' subgroup, which is a geological error in the
source (Hawkesbury Sandstone underlies the Wianamatta Group).

## Standards cited

AS 1726-2017, AS 2870-2011, AS 2159-2009, AS 3798-2007, AS 4133.4.1, HB 160-2006, AGS Landslide Risk Management Concepts and Guidelines (2007), Australian Geomechanics Vol 42 No 1 March 2007, Australian Geoguide LR8 (Construction Practice), APHA (aggressivity suite)

## Related notes

- [[AS 1726 soil and rock description]]
- [[AS 2159 piling]]
- [[AS 2870 residential site classification]]
- [[Rock socket length]]
- [[Bored pier inspection]]
- [[Rock weathering classes]]
- [[Rock strength classes]]
- [[DCP testing]]
- [[Groundwater observations]]
- [[Reduced levels and datums]]
- [[Borehole log conventions]]
- [[Library - salinity and sodic soils]]
- [[Soil description order]]

notes.title: CG26-0496-A - Toukley boat ramp
notes.body:
# CG26-0496-A - Toukley boat ramp

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG26-0496-A Rev 0.pdf`, held locally in the
> reference library — see [[Reference library]]. This note is a factual index of
> what the report contains and where to look. The report itself is not
> reproduced here; anything relied on for a job is read from the source.

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| Report | CG26-0496-A Rev 0 (cover page reads 'Ref: CG26-0496 Rev 0') |
| Issued | 2026-04-17 |
| Author | Core Geotech Pty Ltd |
| Client | EGA Pty Ltd, 36E Fitzroy Street, Marrickville NSW 2204 |
| Site | 20 Peel Street, Toukley NSW - foreshore of Tuggerah Lake, adjacent to Marine Rescue Tuggerah Lakes |
| Project | Proposed Boat Ramp Works (Toukley Marine Rescue boat ramp) |
| Document type | preliminary geotechnical investigation (land-based) |
| Extraction confidence | high |

## Scope

Land-based borehole investigation to support concept design of a boat ramp,
accessways and foreshore works. Covers subsurface profile, groundwater,
laboratory testing, ramp support options, preliminary pile founding parameters,
scour protection and aggressivity. The submerged portion of the ramp was not
investigated and is addressed by extrapolation.

## Fieldwork

- BYDA search before drilling; specialist on-site services search
- Field investigation on 1 April 2026, logged generally to AS1726:2017
- Site walkover of landform, site conditions and adjacent structures
- One borehole BH01 drilled with a Comacchio GEO 305 track mounted rig, 120mm continuous flight augers to 4.7m, with SPTs
- NMLC rock coring from 4.7m to termination at 10.37m; core photographed
- Groundwater observed during drilling and shortly after completion
- Disturbed soil and rock samples submitted to a NATA accredited laboratory under Chain of Custody
- Borehole backfilled by hand with excavated spoil
- Borehole location set out from the supplied plan to about +/-3m

## Subsurface profile as logged

- Road Base: Compacted road base material at surface; base 0.2m
- Fill: Silty SAND, fine grained, grey, brown with low plasticity fines, moisture condition = wet; base 0.7m
- Alluvium: Silty SAND, fine grained, grey with low plasticity fines, wet, loose to medium dense; base 1.7m
- Alluvium: Silty CLAY, medium to high plasticity, red brown to pale brown, yellow grey with some sand, moisture <= plastic limit, firm to stiff; base 4.5m
- Bedrock: SHALE, highly weathered, fine to medium grained, yellowish brown, very low strength; base 4.7m
- Bedrock: Conglomeratic Sandstone, moderately to highly weathered, light grey to pale brown, very coarse grained, rounded to subrounded gravel sized clasts in a finer sandy matrix, low to medium strength; base >10.37m

## Rock

Highly weathered very low strength shale from 4.5m to 4.7m over moderately to
highly weathered conglomeratic sandstone to beyond 10.37m. Is50 0.14 to 0.56MPa,
indicating low to medium strength, with estimated UCS of about 2MPa to 9MPa.
Weaker, highly weathered samples could not be tested and were classified by
visual and tactile assessment.

## Groundwater

Encountered in BH01 at about 0.6m depth at the time of investigation.
Circulating water during diamond drilling prevented measurement of levels in the
cored section. Standing groundwater and seepage may fluctuate with rainfall and
temperature; the low-lying foreshore setting means shallow groundwater influence
and water level fluctuation in nearshore soils are considered likely.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Borehole termination depth, BH01 | 10.37 | m |
| Auger depth before coring | 4.7 | m |
| Borehole diameter | 120 | mm |
| Groundwater depth in BH01 | about 0.6 | m |
| Field Moisture Content, alluvial soils | 19.5 to 34.4 | % |
| Field Moisture Content, weathered bedrock (shale, 4.5-4.95m) | 20.3 | % |
| Aggressivity, BH01 5.1-5.2m Conglomeratic Sandstone/Bedrock | FMC 3.5%, pH 9.0, conductivity 42 uS/cm, resistivity 23,800 Ohm.cm, chloride <10 ppm, sulphate <10 ppm | - |
| Is50, BH01 5.54-5.68m | 0.14 diametral / 0.56 axial - Low strength | MPa |
| Is50, BH01 7.46-7.58m | 0.31 diametral / 0.37 axial - Medium strength | MPa |
| Is50, BH01 10.14-10.27m | 0.25 diametral / 0.39 axial - Medium strength | MPa |
| Estimated UCS range | about 2 to 9 | MPa |
| Allowable end bearing pressure, piles in moderately weathered rock | up to 1000 | kPa |
| Allowable end bearing pressure, piles in very stiff alluvial silty clay | 400 | kPa |
| Ultimate shaft adhesion, very stiff alluvial silty clay | 50 | kPa (for embedment below about 1.5m beneath the lake bed) |
| Rock mattress minimum thickness (landward portion) | about 600 | mm |
| Depth to firm alluvial clay for rock mattress founding | about 1.5 to 1.7 | m |
| Aggressivity classification (AS2159-2009) | mild for concrete piles (Table 6.4.2(C)); non aggressive for steel piles (Table 6.5.2(C)); stated as applying to high permeability soils (type B) | - |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

- Rock mattress option: excavate uncontrolled fill and loose sandy alluvium to expose firm alluvial clay (about 1.5-1.7m), place a 600mm minimum rock mattress of durable cobbles and boulders, install a geotextile or geogrid separator, then compacted DGB or DGS40 and the concrete ramp slab; use larger boulders in the submerged portion
- Piled support option: driven or bored piles founded in very stiff alluvial silty clay or rock, more applicable to a floating pontoon or suspended ramp; detailed pile design required
- Land-based slab option: slab on ground after removal of uncontrolled fill and loose alluvium and replacement with controlled engineered fill to AS3798 - not suitable for the submerged or nearshore portion
- Detail the design to accommodate localised differential settlement, particularly at the transition between land-based and submerged sections
- Provide rock scour protection over a geotextile filter at the ramp toe and along the submerged portion; confirm extent, thickness and rock grading during detailed design
- Treat the existing fill as uncontrolled in accordance with AS3798-2007 since no records were available
- Undertake a project specific geotechnical assessment once the concept design is finalised; have CG review civil and structural drawings
- Inspect the ramp subgrade after excavation and confirm founding conditions before basecourse and concrete; place controlled fill under Level 1 supervision to AS3798-2007

## Stated limitations

- Investigation was land-based only; the submerged portion of the ramp was not directly assessed and comments there rely on extrapolation
- Only one borehole was drilled; the subsurface profile is expected to vary laterally, particularly towards the lake
- Pile founding parameters are preliminary and must be confirmed during detailed design and construction
- Based on concept level information; any change to layout, levels or structural system requires review
- Prepared for the exclusive use of EGA Pty Ltd for the described development
- Must be read in its entirety with the attached Information Sheets; not to be used as a project specification without CG's written agreement

## Reviewer flags

Table 4 (aggressivity) is column-scrambled in the extraction; values mapped by
header order. Document identity is inconsistent: cover reads 'Ref: CG26-0496 Rev
0' and 17 April 2026, the document status table reads CG26-0496-A Rev 0 dated
08.04.2026, and footers read CG26-0496-A Rev 0 / 17 April 2026. Consistency
issue on clay consistency: Table 2 describes the alluvial silty clay as 'firm to
stiff', while Section 9.2 and the pile parameters in Section 9.4 refer to 'very
stiff' alluvial silty clay (the BH01 log records the SPT interval as Very
stiff). Prepared by Jeevan Reddy, reviewed by Raj Singh.

## Standards cited

AS1726-2017 Geotechnical Site Investigation, AS2870-2011 Residential slabs and footings, AS2159-2009 Piling - Design and installation, AS3798-2007 Guidelines on earthworks for commercial and residential developments, AS4133.4.1 (PLSI), AS1289 2.1.1 (FMC), APHA (aggressivity/pH), NSW Boat Ramp Facility Guidelines, Transport for NSW, September 2015, NSW Environment & Heritage eSPADE, Gosford-Lake Macquarie Special 1:100,000 Geological Sheet 9131 and part sheet 9231

## Related notes

- [[AS 1726 soil and rock description]]
- [[AS 2159 piling]]
- [[AS 2870 residential site classification]]
- [[Rock weathering classes]]
- [[Rock strength classes]]
- [[Weathered siltstone]]
- [[Groundwater observations]]
- [[Borehole log conventions]]
- [[Library - salinity and sodic soils]]
- [[Soil description order]]

# CG26-0496 BH01 - borehole log, Toukley

> **Source document:** Core Geotech Pty Ltd, `CG26-0496 BH01 Soil.pdf`, held locally in the

| Extraction confidence | medium |

## Scope

First page of the gINT engineering log for borehole BH01, covering the soil
profile from surface to about 5.0m depth with SPT results and moisture contents.

## Fieldwork

- Borehole BH01 drilled 1 April 2026 (started and completed same day) by Stratacore Drilling Pty Ltd
- Comacchio GEO 305 track mounted drilling rig, 120mm hole size, vertical (slope 90 degrees), ADT method on this page
- Logged by JR, checked by RS; hole location per Drawing No. CG26-0496-1
- Borehole continued as a cored hole below the logged soil profile

## Subsurface profile as logged

- GP: Compacted road base material at surface (FILL)
- SM: Silty SAND, fine grained, grey, brown with low plasticity fines, moisture condition = wet (FILL)
- SM: Silty SAND, fine grained, grey with low plasticity fines, moisture condition = wet, Loose to Medium dense (ALLUVIUM) - from about 0.5m
- CI/CH: Silty CLAY, medium to high plasticity, red brown to pale brown, yellow grey with some sand, moisture condition >= plastic limit, Very stiff (ALLUVIUM) - from about 1.5m
- SHALE, highly weathered, fine to medium grained, yellowish brown, very low strength (BEDROCK) - from about 4.5m

## Rock

Highly weathered, fine to medium grained, yellowish brown shale of very low
strength logged as bedrock from about 4.5m; the SPT at that level recorded 7, 15
with double bounce. Borehole BH01 continued as a cored hole below this level.

## Groundwater

No groundwater information is given in this document.

See [[Groundwater observations]] for what a level in a hole does and does not
tell you.

## Design values as reported

| Value | Figure | Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| SPT at about 3.0-3.45m (Silty CLAY) | 4, 8, 17 (N=25), moisture 19.5% | blows |
| SPT at about 4.5m (SHALE) | 7, 15 Double Bounce, moisture 20.3% | blows |
| Hole size | 120 | mm |
| Slope / bearing | 90 degrees / not applicable | - |
| Depth range on this page | 0 to 5.0 | m |

**These are the report's numbers, not this vault's.** They apply to the site,
loading and construction method described above and carry the report's own
limitations. Re-derive or re-check before using them anywhere else.

## Recommendations

Not stated in the report.

## Stated limitations

Not stated in the report.

## Reviewer flags

This is a single log sheet (page 1 of 3) extracted from the borehole log for
BH01, not a report. The log header records no R.L. surface value and no datum,
and the water column is blank on this page, so groundwater is left null here
even though the parent report CG26-0496-A Rev 0 states groundwater was
encountered at about 0.6m. Depths are read from the depth scale column and are
approximate to the nearest 0.5m gridline because the graphic log column is
destroyed in text extraction; layer boundaries should be taken from Table 2 of
CG26-0496-A Rev 0 rather than from this extraction. gINT file stamp 17/4/26.

## Standards cited

None cited.

# Skills

184 action-based skills from three source families: 116 mined from the
practice documents, specifications, papers and guides in the local reference
library (`G materials`), 47 from the Rock Mechanics lecture playlist by Soil
Mechanics and Engineering Geology on YouTube (tagged `youtube-source`, each
linked to the exact minute of video), and 21 reconstructed from STS's own field
records on Google Drive — completed forms, blank templates, labelled photos
and scans (tagged `field-source`, catalogued in
[[Field records catalogue]]). Each note is a paraphrased working aid pointing
back to its source — what to do, what to check, and where the authoritative
wording lives.

To *learn* the vault rather than just consult it, start at [[Learning loop]] —
flashcard decks and staged learning paths are generated from these notes.

**Ground rules.** Nothing here replaces the source document, the project
specification or a qualified reviewer. Numeric criteria are cited by clause or
page, not reproduced. Notes tagged `ocr-source` came from scanned documents
read by OCR, and `youtube-source` notes were heard through auto-captions —
treat both sets' numbers and equations with extra suspicion and read them off
the source before use. `field-source` notes show what the records evidence, not
necessarily the current approved procedure. Confidence is the extractor's, not
an engineer's.

Not mined: the Australian Standards (see the section maps in
[[Reference library]]), the Core Geotech project reports (see
[[Project reports]]), and the reference textbooks (copyright — pointers only in
[[Library - reference texts and parameter sources]]).

notes.text: Skills 184 action based skills from three source families: 116 mined from the practice documents, specifications, papers and guides in the local reference library ( G materials ), 47 from the Rock Mechanics lecture playlist by Soil Mechanics and Engineering Geology on YouTube (tagged youtube source , each linked to the exact minute of video), and 21 reconstructed from STS's own field records on Google Drive — completed forms, blank templates, labelled photos and scans (tagged field source , catalogued in Field records catalogue). Each note is a paraphrased working aid pointing back to its source — what to do, what to check, and where the authoritative wording lives. To learn the vault rather than just consult it, start at Learning loop — flashcard decks and staged learning paths are generated from these notes. Ground rules. Nothing here replaces the source document, the project specification or a qualified reviewer. Numeric criteria are cited by clause or page, not reproduced. Notes tagged ocr source came from scanned documents read by OCR, and youtube source notes were heard through auto captions — treat both sets' numbers and equations with extra suspicion and read them off the source before use. field source notes show what the records evidence, not necessarily the current approved procedure. Confidence is the extractor's, not an engineer's. Not mined: the Australian Standards (see the section maps in Reference library), the Core Geotech project reports (see Project reports), and the reference textbooks (copyright — pointers only in Library reference texts and parameter sources). notes.title: Accept marginal granular material via shear strength
notes.body:
# Accept marginal granular material via shear strength

> **Source:** `RTA 3051.pdf` (Clause 8.2, Table 3051.4 and hold point), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** A defensible acceptance pathway for materials failing grading/particle-shape criteria but demonstrating adequate shear strength, limited to permitted traffic categories.

## Inputs

- Which criteria failed (retained fractions, mis-shapen particles, or fractured faces)
- Modified Texas Triaxial test results at the specified moisture/density conditioning
- Field performance and compaction-characteristics evidence
- Nominated particle size distribution and production consistency records

## Procedure

1. Confirm the material meets all other specification requirements and only fails the eligible criteria.
2. For unbound materials, restrict the pathway to the lower traffic categories; materials to be bound may use it for all categories if they also meet maximum-size and fines limits plus the bound-material spec.
3. Test the Modified Texas Triaxial classification number at the standard conditioning (with the open-graded moulding exception where water bleeds during test).
4. Control production against the nominated grading with the maximum-deviation table.
5. Submit through the hold point with production test results, field performance and consistency evidence; approval remains at the Principal's discretion.

## Decision rules

- Unbound strength-based acceptance is only available for Traffic Categories C and D (RTA 3051 Clause 8.2.1 and Figure 3051.2 notes).
- Texas triaxial classification-number ceilings vary by category and layer (e.g. tighter for base than subbase) per Table 3051.4.
- Grading control is by maximum deviation from the nominated distribution, tightest on the fine sieves (RTA 3051 Table 3051.4).

## Checks

- Conditioning at the specified fraction of optimum moisture and full standard-compaction density before triaxial testing.
- Hold point submission includes nominated PSD when grading was the failed criterion.

## Common errors

- Using the pathway for a heavy-traffic unbound base.
- Testing at the wrong moisture conditioning for open-graded materials.
- Treating the hold point as a formality - acceptance is discretionary.

## Caveats

- Verify edition currency; the Principal may impose extra conditions.
- Contract documents override.

## Standards cited

RMS T171, RMS T106/T107, RMS R73

notes.title: Adjust rock footing design for cut faces, horizontal loads and moment loading
notes.body:
# Adjust rock footing design for cut faces, horizontal loads and moment loading

> **Source:** `PELLS MOSTYN WONG (2019) CLASSIFICATION OF SANDSTONES AND SHALES IN THE SYDNEY.pdf` (Sections 4.2-4.4 (pp 36-37); uplift cone apex-angle update in Section 4.5 (p 37)), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** Bearing, sliding and rotation checks corrected for footings near excavation crests or carrying non-centric loads, where the standard centric-vertical guideline values do not apply.

## Inputs

- Footing position relative to excavation faces and boundaries
- Load cases: vertical, horizontal, moment components and their temporal correlation
- Rock mass UCS and defect orientations at the cut face
- Guideline bearing values and moduli from Tables 3 and 4

## Procedure

1. Recognise that the tabulated guideline pressures apply only to vertical centric loading on or below a horizontal surface.
2. For a footing at an excavation crest: take ultimate capacity of a narrow footing as roughly the rock mass unconfined strength (not the multiple applicable to laterally confined masses), halve the serviceability pressure (settlement approximately doubles), expect lateral movement toward the face of about half the vertical settlement, and footing rotation of roughly 0.5 to 1.0 times p/E, per the authors' generic 2D FEM guidance.
3. Inspect and probe the cut face for kinematically admissible wedges on adversely oriented defects; if present, ultimate bearing may be effectively zero and the design must change or the face be reinforced.
4. For horizontal loads: resist by base friction applied to the permanent vertical load only (friction coefficient about 0.7 may be conservatively adopted for concrete cast on clean sandstone), or by passive resistance of the excavation sides after inspection for adverse defects; ignore the top ~0.5 m of rock.
5. For moment loading: assume a linear no-tension base reaction, limit peak pressure to about twice the guideline value and average pressure to the guideline value, and analyse settlement plus rotation.

## Decision rules

- If adversely oriented defects daylight or nearly daylight in the face, kinematic failure governs regardless of class-based bearing values.
- Shale base friction is more complex than sandstone and depends on construction and inspection specifics; do not carry the sandstone friction coefficient across.
- In-situ stress relief movements of the excavation are additional to load-induced movements and must be assessed separately.

## Checks

- Face inspection scope written into the specification.
- Existing buildings at a new excavation crest checked for both bearing and kinematic failure modes.
- Vertical-horizontal capacity interaction reconsidered where lateral load is a significant case.

## Common errors

- Applying centric-loading guideline pressures to crest footings.
- Counting passive resistance without verifying defect orientations.
- Applying friction resistance to transient live load components.

## Caveats

- The crest-footing rules of thumb derive from generic 2D FEM analyses; analyse the specific case where geometry is not simple.
- Design reference only: factors and coefficients must be verified against the source paper and reviewed by a qualified engineer before use.

## Standards cited

Pells (1990) stress relief around Sydney basements, Pells (2001) Eastern Distributor face reinforcement

## Related

- [[Rock strength classes]]
- [[Library - Pells papers on Sydney sandstone and shale]]
- [[Soil description order]]

notes.title: Adopt saturated strength and stiffness values for Hawkesbury Sandstone design
notes.body:
# Adopt saturated strength and stiffness values for Hawkesbury Sandstone design

> **Source:** `substanceAndMassPropertiesForTheDesignOfEngineeringStructuresInTheHawkesburySandstone.pdf` (Pells, Australian Geomechanics Vol 39 No 3, Sept 2004; Sections 2.2.1-2.2.2, Tables 1-3 and Figures 1-2 (pp 2-5)), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** Substance UCS and modulus inputs selected on a saturated basis, avoiding the systematic overestimate that dry-tested Hawkesbury Sandstone produces.

## Inputs

- Laboratory UCS and modulus results with moisture condition recorded
- Sample provenance (facies, weathering, position relative to water table)
- The paper's wet/dry comparison datasets (Tables 1-3)

## Procedure

1. Check the moisture state of every strength/stiffness result; Hawkesbury Sandstone saturated strength is typically only about 0.3 to 0.7 of dry strength (Table 1), and saturated moduli are similarly reduced (Table 3).
2. Use saturated values for design of foundations and underground works below or near the water table; a degree of saturation above about 90% is enough to reach the fully saturated minimum strength.
3. Where only dry results exist, either retest saturated or apply a documented site-specific wet/dry ratio - never assume parity.
4. Select modulus at a stress range relevant to the application: low-stress secant moduli (0-6 MPa) differ from tangent moduli at 50% strength because the material stiffens with stress (Figures 2a/2b).
5. Adopt Poisson's ratio in the well-established 0.10-0.25 band (mean about 0.2) unless dilatancy near failure is relevant.

## Decision rules

- Resaturating dried specimens generally restores the saturated strength (for material from below the water table), so retesting is a valid recovery route.
- Clayey sandstones show the strongest wet/dry sensitivity; treat low wet/dry ratios as a durability warning as well.

## Checks

- Reported UCS statistics separated by wet/dry condition before averaging.
- Modulus basis (secant vs tangent, stress range) stated with every value.

## Common errors

- Mixing dry and saturated results in one design population.
- Using tangent modulus at 50% strength for low-stress foundation settlement problems.
- Ignoring that partial saturation above ~90% already gives minimum strength.

## Caveats

- Ratios are Hawkesbury-Sandstone-specific and scattered between sites; use site data where possible.
- Design reference only: values must be verified against the source tables and reviewed by a qualified engineer before use.

## Standards cited

ISRM suggested methods for UCS and deformability testing

notes.title: Apply edition-correct compaction criteria when reviewing legacy R44 Ed 3 lots
notes.body:
# Apply edition-correct compaction criteria when reviewing legacy R44 Ed 3 lots

> **Source:** `R044_E3_R15.pdf` (Clauses 7.1-7.2.3, Table R44.5 (Ed 3 Rev 15, Oct 2011)), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** Historic or legacy-contract earthworks conformity is assessed against the Ed 3 Rev 15 regime rather than current-edition values, avoiding false nonconformances.

## Inputs

- Contract confirmation that R44 Ed 3 Rev 15 (Oct 2011) applies
- Lot records: density, moisture, maximum density test results
- Lot location/type

## Procedure

1. Use the Ed 3 conformity table (Table R44.5) for lower limits of characteristic relative compaction - same 90/95/98/100/102 tiering as later editions but with different row definitions (e.g. the entire floor of cuttings and select fill adjacent to structures sit in the 98% tier, and material replacing unsuitable material near cutting floor level is carved out of the 95% row).
2. Restrict field density methods to sand replacement (T119) or nuclear gauge (T173) - the fixed volume extractive method is not in this edition; note the nuclear-gauge probe placement and companion sampling rules in Clause 7.2.2.
3. Determine oversize proportion via the T119 procedure and maximum density via T111 or T162 only (Clause 7.2.2); calculate relative compaction per T166 rounded to 0.1% (Clause 7.2.3).
4. Treat wetted-up or over-wet placed material per Clause 7.2: dry and recompact as a new lot, or remove to stockpile at contractor cost.
5. Apply lot homogeneity rules identical in substance to later editions before pooling results.

## Decision rules

- Single test method per lot; no mixing of T119 and T173 results statistically.
- Standard compaction reference applies (Clause 7.2.1) - do not judge against modified compaction ratios.
- Material placed over-wet must be reassessed as a new lot after drying and recompaction.

## Checks

- Laboratory independence per RMS Q
- Test hole repair method documented in the project quality plan
- Moisture methods T121/T180 only used with prior calibration against T120

## Common errors

- Judging an Ed 3 contract against current-edition tables or test method suites
- Using T165 (not available in this edition) and citing it for conformity
- Missing that this edition houses the Benkelman characteristic deflection formula in Annexure R44/A6, not the body

## Caveats

- This edition is superseded - confirm which edition the contract actually incorporates before using it.
- Contract documents override; annexure values are project-specific.

## Standards cited

RMS Q, RMS T111, RMS T119, RMS T162, RMS T166, RMS T173

## Related

- [[Skills]]

notes.title: Apply limit state load combinations and geotechnical reduction factors to rock foundation design
notes.body:
# Apply limit state load combinations and geotechnical reduction factors to rock foundation design

> **Source:** `Pells Paper on Foundations on sandstone and shale in The Sydney Region.pdf` (Section 5 (pp 25-27): load combinations 5.1, strength 5.2.1, serviceability 5.2.2), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** Strength and serviceability limit state checks for pads and sockets on Sydney rock using the paper's recommended phi_g values, filling the gap where AS 2159's tabulated factors do not cover rock-socket methods.

## Inputs

- Dead, live and wind load components (G, Q, Wu)
- Design method used for ultimate capacity (complete socket versus side-shear only)
- Quality of the local field-testing database for the geology
- Basis of deformation parameters (pressuremeter/large-scale in situ versus RQD/RMR correlation)

## Procedure

1. Form governing design actions: typically S* = 1.25G + 1.5Q and S* = 1.25G + Wu + psi_c Q for strength, and G + psi_l Q for long-term serviceability (psi_c = 0.4, or 0.6 for storage), treating earth pressure as live load and liquid load as dead load at strength state.
2. Compute ultimate geotechnical strength Rug by an accepted socket method, then check phi_g x Rug >= S*.
3. Select phi_g for complete sockets: 0.75 where substantial field test data exist for the geology (e.g. Hawkesbury sandstone, Melbourne mudstone), 0.65 for similar environments without specific data, 0.5 outside the worldwide database.
4. For side-shear-only sockets use the lower set: 0.6 / 0.5 / 0.35 for the same three categories.
5. For serviceability, apply a modulus reduction factor even though AS 2159 requires none: 0.75 where moduli come from pressuremeter or large-scale in situ measurement, 0.5 where estimated from RQD/RMR-type correlations; with class-table moduli chosen appropriately within their range, 0.75 may be adopted.
6. In the absence of structural requirements, design for settlements of roughly 5-15 mm.

## Decision rules

- The recommended phi_g values presume assured construction QC of sidewall and base cleanliness; without it, be very conservative and do not apply prescriptive factors.
- Serviceability frequently governs socket design, so the modulus reduction is not optional in practice.

## Checks

- All relevant AS 1170.1 combinations screened, not just the typical governing pair.
- phi_g category justified by documented local test data.
- Structural strength of the pile checked separately from geotechnical strength.

## Common errors

- Lifting phi_g values from AS 2159 Table 4.1 that do not cover rock-socket calculation methods.
- Taking full characteristic moduli for settlement prediction with no allowance for parameter uncertainty.
- Using complete-socket phi_g for a side-shear-only design.

## Caveats

- Written against 1989/1995 editions of the codes; map the recommendations onto current AS 2159/AS 1170 provisions before use.
- Design reference only: factors must be verified against the source paper and current standards, and reviewed by a qualified engineer before use.

## Standards cited

AS 2159-1995 Piling Code, AS 1170.1-1989 Loading Code

Form governing design actions: typically S = 1.25G + 1.5Q and S = 1.25G + Wu + psi c Q for strength, and G + psi l Q for long term serviceability (psi c = 0.4, or 0.6 for storage), treating earth pressure as live load and liquid load as dead load at strength state. 2. Compute ultimate geotechnical strength Rug by an accepted socket method, then check phi g x Rug = S . 3. Select phi g for complete sockets: 0.75 where substantial field test data exist for the geology (e.g. Hawkesbury sandstone, Melbourne mudstone), 0.65 for similar environments without specific data, 0.5 outside the worldwide database. 4. For side shear only sockets use the lower set: 0.6 / 0.5 / 0.35 for the same three categories. 5. For serviceability, apply a modulus reduction factor even though AS 2159 requires none: 0.75 where moduli come from pressuremeter or large scale in situ measurement, 0.5 where estimated from RQD/RMR type correlations; with class table moduli chosen appropriately within their range, 0.75 may be adopted. 6. In the absence of structural requirements, design for settlements of roughly 5 15 mm. Decision rules The recommended phi g values presume assured construction QC of sidewall and base cleanliness; without it, be very conservative and do not apply prescriptive factors. Serviceability frequently governs socket design, so the modulus reduction is not optional in practice. Checks All relevant AS 1170.1 combinations screened, not just the typical governing pair. phi g category justified by documented local test data. Structural strength of the pile checked separately from geotechnical strength. Common errors Lifting phi g values from AS 2159 Table 4.1 that do not cover rock socket calculation methods. Taking full characteristic moduli for settlement prediction with no allowance for parameter uncertainty. Using complete socket phi g for a side shear only design. Caveats Written against 1989/1995 editions of the codes; map the recommendations onto current AS 2159/AS 1170 provisions before use. Design reference only: factors must be verified against the source paper and current standards, and reviewed by a qualified engineer before use.
