notes.title: Transfer AX 01a test data from the SD card into Excel
notes.body:
# Transfer AX 01a test data from the SD card into Excel

> **Source:** `BedAnlAx01a_engl V40a.pdf` (Chapters 7-8, pp. 17-18; SD file path in Section 6.3, p. 13), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** The engineer can pull stored test records off the device's SD card into the supplied Excel template and generate per-test sheets for reporting.

## Inputs

- SD card from the AX 01a (all tests live in one file, X:\AX01\PDG.CRD)
- PC with a card reader and Microsoft Excel (2000 or later)
- Supplied template: ax.xlt for Excel 2000/XP/2003 or ax.xltm for 2007+ with macros enabled

## Procedure

1. Open the appropriate template from the SD card and enable macros in Excel's security settings (p. 17).
2. Copy PDG.CRD from the SD card to the hard disk and work from that copy (recommended, p. 18).
3. In the template press the read-card button, then use the read-file option to open the .CRD file - for the AX 01a, ignore the card-info/read-card/card-reader buttons meant for the older chip-card version.
4. Mark the datasets to transfer (click to toggle the blue selection; a select-all button exists) and run the data-to-Excel transfer; each test becomes its own sheet with table and graph.
5. Treat the generated sheets as static output - do not edit values, because the modulus results and graph points will not recalculate (p. 18).

## Decision rules

- Use read-file, not the card-reader path, for AX 01a data; the dedicated card reader is only for the previous device generation.
- Optionally export via the separate software to ASCII .csv or GGU .pdr formats when other programs need the data (p. 4).

## Checks

- Number of records shown matches the device's card-info count.
- Each transferred sheet reproduces the Ev values printed on site.

## Common errors

- Editing cells in the generated sheet and assuming moduli update - they do not.
- Working directly on the SD card instead of a copied working file.
- Macros disabled, so the template buttons do nothing.

## Caveats

- Excel macro-security menus described are for legacy Excel versions; modern Excel places these controls elsewhere.
- The SD card stores roughly 200 tests; deleting the card erases all records at once.

## Standards cited

None cited in the source passage.

notes.title: Use NR44 commentary to brief teams on R44 intent and economical material choices
notes.body:
# Use NR44 commentary to brief teams on R44 intent and economical material choices

> **Source:** `nr44 Earthworks Specification.pdf` (Foreword; commentary to Clauses 6.1.2 and 7.4.1 (NR44 Ed 2 Rev 0, April 2013)), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** Site and design teams apply R44 the way the Principal intends - right materials in the right zones, testing effort where it matters - reducing disputes.

## Inputs

- Project R44 edition and completed annexures
- Available cutting materials and their processing costs
- NR44 guide text (shaded = spec text of Ed 4 Rev 1; italics = commentary)

## Procedure

1. Use NR44's structure deliberately: shaded text reproduces R44 Ed 4 Rev 1 wording, italics carry the Principal's intent - quote the spec, apply the intent.
2. Selected Material Zone sourcing: NR44 stresses economy - the SMZ exists to put the best job-won materials directly under the pavement; a lesser material with adequate CBR can beat a hard rock needing expensive processing, and imported SMZ material is a fallback, not a default.
3. Proof rolling: the guide clarifies the clause is not intended to require proof rolling of every lift - it defines the method for when proof rolling is required or directed; plan test rolling at meaningful stages.
4. Pre-tender risk allocation: designate treatments for known problem materials (wet clays, low-CBR cutting floors) in the documents so contractors price them and stop-and-test cycles are avoided.
5. Use the guide's sampling/characteristic-value walk-throughs (CBR characteristic value Q, per-lot sample counts by tonnage) to train staff on how conformity is actually computed under RMS Q.

## Decision rules

- Never cite NR44 as a contractual requirement - it is explicitly not a contract document.
- Where NR44 commentary conflicts with the project's R44 edition or contract, the contract wins.
- Commentary can justify a sensible engineering position in a dispute narrative, but conformity is decided on R44 criteria.

## Checks

- Guide edition (based on R44 Ed 4 Rev 1) mapped against the project's R44 edition for clause renumbering
- Team briefings distinguish spec text from commentary
- Material selection decisions documented with the economy rationale

## Common errors

- Enforcing italicised commentary as if it were specification text
- Assuming every lift needs a witnessed proof roll
- Defaulting to imported select material without exhausting site-won sources

## Caveats

- Verify the R44 edition current for the project - NR44's clause pointers track Ed 4 Rev 1 and drift from later editions.
- Contract documents override both R44 and any guide interpretation.

## Standards cited

RMS R44 Ed 4 Rev 1, RMS Q

Proof rolling: the guide clarifies the clause is not intended to require proof rolling of every lift it defines the method for when proof rolling is required or directed; plan test rolling at meaningful stages. 4. Pre tender risk allocation: designate treatments for known problem materials (wet clays, low CBR cutting floors) in the documents so contractors price them and stop and test cycles are avoided. 5. Use the guide's sampling/characteristic value walk throughs (CBR characteristic value Q, per lot sample counts by tonnage) to train staff on how conformity is actually computed under RMS Q. Decision rules Never cite NR44 as a contractual requirement it is explicitly not a contract document. Where NR44 commentary conflicts with the project's R44 edition or contract, the contract wins. Commentary can justify a sensible engineering position in a dispute narrative, but conformity is decided on R44 criteria. Checks Guide edition (based on R44 Ed 4 Rev 1) mapped against the project's R44 edition for clause renumbering Team briefings distinguish spec text from commentary Material selection decisions documented with the economy rationale Common errors Enforcing italicised commentary as if it were specification text Assuming every lift needs a witnessed proof roll Defaulting to imported select material without exhausting site won sources Caveats Verify the R44 edition current for the project NR44's clause pointers track Ed 4 Rev 1 and drift from later editions. Contract documents override both R44 and any guide interpretation. Standards cited RMS R44 Ed 4 Rev 1, RMS Q Related Library RMS and TfNSW specifications Skills

notes.title: Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in-field reference aids
notes.body:
# Use the EI logging cheat sheet and correlation charts as in-field reference aids

> **Source:** [Google Drive — Field Sheets (STS blank templates + reference)/EI Geotech Soil Logging Cheat Sheet - rev1 Oct 19.pdf, Approx. Correlations Chart.pdf, PSP correlation.pdf](https://drive.google.com/file/d/13WeSy9SmwQe52-198FqjHYF2kWf4-CMI/view) (Printed field reference aids kept with the blank BH log templates: logging vocabulary/criteria sheet, index-test correlation tables, and a Perth Sand Penetrometer density chart). Reconstructed from STS's own
> field records on Google Drive — completed forms, labelled photos and
> scans, catalogued in [[Field records catalogue]]. It shows what the
> records evidence, not necessarily the current approved procedure —
> confirm against the current STS form and procedure before treating it
> as the standard method.

**Outcome.** Faster, standard-compliant field logging and on-the-spot sanity checks by reaching for the right printed aid instead of memory.

## Inputs

- EI Geotech Soil Logging Cheat Sheet (rev1 Oct 19) - soil and rock-core logging guide sheets
- Approximate Correlations Chart - consistency/density vs SPT N, DCP blows, cone resistance, unit weight and modulus relationships
- PSP correlation chart - Perth Sand Penetrometer blows per 150 mm vs density/vertical effective stress (Stockton beach sand basis)

## Procedure

1. Carry the three aids with the blank log sheets; they are companions to the OP GEO 007/008 logs, not standalone deliverables.
2. Reach for the soil logging cheat sheet when writing descriptions: it gives the description order, granular-vs-cohesive field tests, particle size limits, plasticity/ribbon criteria, consistency and density terms with field guides, moisture condition definitions, soil structure/cementation terms, fill identification cues, weathering and rock-defect abbreviations, defect description order with worked examples, and colour abbreviations.
3. Reach for the approximate correlations chart when converting between field indices - e.g. relating DCP blows or pocket penetrometer readings to consistency terms, SPT N or an indicative modulus - and treat every value as approximate.
4. Reach for the PSP correlation when interpreting Perth Sand Penetrometer counts in clean sands, noting it derives from a specific sand and overburden-stress dependence.
5. When a correlation drives a reported number (e.g. an inferred density index), note on the log that it is correlation-based and which aid was used.

## Decision rules

- The cheat sheet governs wording on the log; if memory and the sheet disagree, the sheet wins.
- Correlations are depth- and moisture-dependent guides (stated on the aids) - never present a correlated value as a measured one.
- PSP correlations apply to sands like the calibration material; outside that, log the raw blows and defer interpretation.

## Checks

- Descriptions on completed logs follow the cheat-sheet order and vocabulary.
- Any correlated parameter in notes or reports is traceable to the specific chart used.

## Common errors

- Quoting correlation-derived strengths without the 'approximate/guide only' caveat the charts themselves carry.
- Using the PSP chart for silty or clayey materials where the correlation basis does not hold.

## Caveats

- Reconstructed from STS field records — confirm against the current STS procedure before treating as the standard method
- This skill is deliberately a pointer: the aids' actual correlation values and criteria must be read from the source documents, not from this summary.

## Standards cited

AS 1726.1 (description terminology the cheat sheet operationalises)

- [[DCP testing]]
- [[Borehole log conventions]]
- [[Library - plate load testing]]

notes.title: Verify a rock fill compaction routine by trial sections under R44 Ed 3
notes.body:
# Verify a rock fill compaction routine by trial sections under R44 Ed 3

> **Source:** `R044_E3_R15.pdf` (Clause 7.3 with proof rolling per Clause 7.4.1 (Ed 3 Rev 15)), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** Rock fill placing is accepted on a verified procedure basis (routine + proof rolling), since density testing is invalid for coarse rock fill.

## Inputs

- Proposed grading, mixing, watering and rolling routine
- Trial section results and survey data
- Plant details (roller types, passes, speed, vibration frequency)

## Procedure

1. Develop the routine through constructed trial sections; each trial must respect the geometric limits in Clause 7.3 - length capped at 50 m, width at least twice the maximum roller drum width, and no trials within 1.5 m below the Selected Material Zone.
2. Include at least one vibrating roller in the routine; if in-situ modification (grid rolling) is used, verify the after-compaction grading.
3. Notify the witness point at least 3 working days before each trial with prior results, material specs, plant details, pass counts, speeds/frequencies and the in-process testing regime, including evidence of no remaining internal settlement and embankment stability.
4. Base verification on two successive (not merely contiguous, simultaneously built) trial sections.
5. Clear the hold point on compaction of rock fills by submitting trial conformity, the proposed routine, test results and survey reports; then police the routine (passes, moisture, layer control) during production.
6. Proof roll per the deflection clause as the ongoing conformity check.

## Decision rules

- Nonconforming in-process results stop placement: either redevelop the routine with new trials (hold point re-applies) or break down/sort the rock to earth fill and follow earth fill rules.
- Two contiguous sections built in one continuous operation do not count as two successive trials.
- All routine development and application costs sit inside the general earthworks rate - no separate claim.

## Checks

- Rock fill material actually meets rock fill definitions (otherwise earth fill compaction testing applies)
- Trial documentation covers all six submission detail items
- Production records show the nominated routine followed layer by layer

## Common errors

- Treating rock fill lots as density-testable and reporting invalid relative compaction
- Verifying off a single trial or two simultaneous strips
- Constructing trials high in the embankment inside the excluded zone below the SMZ

## Caveats

- Confirm the contract edition; later editions renumber this to Clause 7.5 with minor wording changes.
- Contract documents override.

## Standards cited

RMS T198, RMS Q

## Related

- [[Skills]]

notes.title: Verify and place geotextile on site
notes.body:
# Verify and place geotextile on site

> **Source:** `RMS Spec D & C R63.pdf` (Clauses 2.3-2.5, 3, 4.2-4.6, Tables R63.1-R63.2), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** Geotextile accepted through supply and placement hold points, then installed without damage and with correct overlaps and cover.

## Inputs

- Supplier Certificate of Compliance (not more than 12 months old) with NATA-endorsed results
- Batch/order size to define sampling lots
- Fill D90 for initial cover thickness

## Procedure

1. Release the supply hold point on the Certificate of Compliance and nominated usage locations; deliver rolls labelled and protected, at least 14 days before installation.
2. Sample per the frequency table (one roll for the initial area increment, then one per subsequent larger increment), cutting a representative sample away from roll ends, marked for direction; test grab/tear strength in both directions with the specified specimen counts and judge the lot on the characteristic value in the weaker direction.
3. Release the placement hold point on site test results submitted ahead of placement.
4. Prepare the surface (remove sharp objects, cut vegetation flush), place just ahead of the works, and cover within the time limit; rectify punctures/tears before covering.
5. Respect overlaps/seams, minimum initial cover-layer thickness by fill particle size, plant-movement restrictions and rock drop-height limits.

## Decision rules

- Sampling: one roll for the initial 10,000 m2 (or part), then one per 20,000 m2 (Clause 2.4.2).
- Cover placed geotextile within 48 hours (Clause 4.3).
- Overlap at least 500 mm where large deformations are expected; sewn seams must reach 100% of specified grab strength with two parallel stitch rows (Clause 4.5).
- Initial layer thickness: for D90 up to 150 mm, the larger of 3x particle size or 300 mm; for 150-400 mm, 2x particle size up to 500 mm (Table R63.2).
- Plant may travel only after 200 mm uncompacted cover; unrestricted movement only after compacted stable cover; rock drop height under 1.5 m directly on geotextile, otherwise interpose a finer aggregate cushion (Clauses 4.6.1-4.6.2).
- Retest-then-reject rule applies when the lot characteristic value falls below the specified limit (Clause 2.3.2).

## Checks

- Site test means compared against certificate means - drift beyond the stated standard-deviation rules makes deliveries nonconforming.
- No vibratory or heavy compaction plant on initial fill layers.
- Trench drain geotextile placed loose and fully enveloping the drainage media.

## Common errors

- Leaving geotextile exposed to UV beyond the covering window.
- Sampling from roll ends or unlabelled rolls, destroying traceability.
- Tracking plant directly on the geotextile before minimum cover.

## Caveats

- Verify edition currency; project deed documents override.

## Standards cited

AS 3706 series, AS 2001.2.3.2, AS 2001.2.13

## Related

- [[Library - RMS and TfNSW specifications]]
- [[Skills]]

notes.title: Verify external stability of reinforced soil wall
notes.body:
# Verify external stability of reinforced soil wall

> **Source:** `r057.pdf` (Clauses 4.2, 4.4, 4.7 (Ed 2 / Rev 9, June 2017)), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** A reinforced soil wall (RSW) external design certified by a geotechnical engineer against bearing, sliding, overall slip and eccentricity limit states.

## Inputs

- Wall geometry (mechanical height H, reinforcement length L, facing inclination)
- Characteristic foundation soil parameters (friction angle, cohesion, undrained strength) from site investigation
- Load combinations A-F with factored loads per the specification's load table
- Material and economic ramification factors from the specification tables
- RSW classification (major/minor) and design life from the project annexure

## Procedure

1. Derive design soil strength values by applying material factors to characteristic values (e.g. tan(phi*) = factor x tan(phi)).
2. Check bearing: compute design bearing pressure using an idealised Meyerhof distribution on an effective width reduced for eccentricity, and confirm the factored ultimate bearing capacity (calculated per Geoguide 1 Appendix A for soil or very weak rock foundations) is not less than it.
3. Check sliding at the base for both long-term (drained, soil-to-soil and reinforcement-to-soil interfaces with interaction coefficients) and short-term (undrained) conditions.
4. Run overall slip stability analyses on circular and non-circular surfaces with an extensive set of trial surfaces, using unfactored serviceability loads and constant-volume soil strengths, including reinforcement resistance where surfaces cut the block.
5. Check base eccentricity under serviceability loads and post-construction movements against the project annexure limits.
6. Have all external (geotechnical) design work carried out and certified by a geotechnical engineer; internal design is certified separately by the RSW designer.

## Decision rules

- Minimum overall slip factor of safety: 1.35 for walls not supporting bridge abutments, 1.6 for walls supporting abutments (constant-volume strength method); alternative peak-strength method requires 1.6 with capped peak parameters (r057 Clause 4.7.4).
- Serviceability eccentricity ratio e/L must stay below 1/6 (r057 Clause 4.7.6).
- Without site-specific test data, cap design friction angles for fills at 34 degrees; with pre-placement testing the reinforced fill may use up to 36 degrees; foundation soil cohesion and friction are capped at 20 kPa and 40 degrees (r057 Clause 4.2(l)).
- Ignore passive resistance in front of the toe when it would improve sliding safety; only count that material for bearing if excavation in front of the wall is restricted (r057 Clause 4.2(p)).
- Sill-beam abutments: serviceability bearing under the sill beam and sill-beam eccentricity are capped per Clause 4.6.7 (dead-load-only vs combined-load limits).

## Checks

- Confirm the design water table assumption: ground surface level in front of the wall unless flooded/submerged cases apply (r057 Clause 4.2(f)).
- Confirm liquefaction screening of granular foundations against the density-index/SPT thresholds in Clause 4.3.1.6 where earthquake load cases apply.
- Confirm all material factors used are stated in the design output and are no less stringent than the specification tables.

## Common errors

- Applying ultimate material factors in the overall slip check, which the specification requires to run with load factors of 1.0 and no material factors, judged instead on a factor of safety.
- Taking full passive toe resistance in the sliding check.
- Using peak friction angles where constant-volume values are required for the fills.

## Caveats

- Verify the edition is still current before use; R57 is periodically revised and successor TfNSW specifications may apply.
- Contract documents and the project-specific annexure override the base specification.
- Numeric limits above are cited from the referenced clauses only; confirm against the controlled document.

## Standards cited

AS 5100.3, BS 8006, AS 1170.4, Geoguide 1 (Hong Kong)

## Related

- [[Skills]]

notes.title: Verify formation surface levels against R44 level tolerances
notes.body:
# Verify formation surface levels against R44 level tolerances

> **Source:** `r044.pdf` (Clause 7.7, Table R44.11; batters per Tables R44.3 and R44.8 (Ed 5 Rev 1)), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** Each finished earthworks surface is confirmed inside its level tolerance band, or handled through the below-tolerance acceptance mechanism.

## Inputs

- Design surface levels and overlying course thicknesses
- Survey reports of finished surfaces
- Annexure R44/A4 deduction rate (for below-tolerance acceptance)

## Procedure

1. Identify the surface type and read its band from Table R44.11: top of Selected Material Zone (tight, plus-zero band), lower SMZ layer, underside of SMZ, verges, designed floor/foundation levels per foundation treatment type, transition zones, and cutting benches - bands widen with depth and treatment type.
2. Survey against design level minus nominated overlying thicknesses (Clause 7.7.1).
3. For median batters, check undulation against the two-zone rule: a tighter deviation limit within 2 m of the shoulder edge, a looser one beyond, both measured normal to the slope, and confirm the surface still sheds water without ponding (Clause 7.7.3).
4. Where the top of the SMZ is low but the overlying layer is outside the Contract, assess acceptance under Clause 7.7.2: no point above the upper limit, deduction applied at the Annexure R44/A4 rate to the volume below the lower limit, with the volume calculation method accepted by the Principal.
5. Check cutting and embankment batter faces separately against their own tolerance tables (Tables R44.3 and R44.8).

## Decision rules

- Plus-zero upper limits mean any high spot on the formation top is nonconforming - trim, don't negotiate.
- Below-tolerance acceptance with deduction is only available in the specific overlying-layer-not-in-Contract case; otherwise rectify.
- Ponding overrides numeric conformity on medians and open surfaces.

## Checks

- Correct tolerance row chosen for the foundation treatment type (drainage layers in rock cuttings have a deeper allowance)
- Survey density sufficient to catch localised highs/lows
- Level checks done before the surface is covered (linked to the Clause 7.6.2 hold point)

## Common errors

- Applying the generic formation tolerance to treatment-specific floor/foundation levels
- Accepting a high finished formation because the average is within band
- Missing that the transition zone and shallow embankment foundation level has a much wider band than formation surfaces

## Caveats

- Verify the spec edition is current for the project.
- Contract documents and completed annexures (deduction rates, thicknesses) override.

## Standards cited

TfNSW G71

For median batters, check undulation against the two zone rule: a tighter deviation limit within 2 m of the shoulder edge, a looser one beyond, both measured normal to the slope, and confirm the surface still sheds water without ponding (Clause 7.7.3). 4. Where the top of the SMZ is low but the overlying layer is outside the Contract, assess acceptance under Clause 7.7.2: no point above the upper limit, deduction applied at the Annexure R44/A4 rate to the volume below the lower limit, with the volume calculation method accepted by the Principal. 5. Check cutting and embankment batter faces separately against their own tolerance tables (Tables R44.3 and R44.8). Decision rules Plus zero upper limits mean any high spot on the formation top is nonconforming trim, don't negotiate. Below tolerance acceptance with deduction is only available in the specific overlying layer not in Contract case; otherwise rectify. Ponding overrides numeric conformity on medians and open surfaces. Checks Correct tolerance row chosen for the foundation treatment type (drainage layers in rock cuttings have a deeper allowance) Survey density sufficient to catch localised highs/lows Level checks done before the surface is covered (linked to the Clause 7.6.2 hold point) Common errors Applying the generic formation tolerance to treatment specific floor/foundation levels Accepting a high finished formation because the average is within band Missing that the transition zone and shallow embankment foundation level has a much wider band than formation surfaces Caveats Verify the spec edition is current for the project. Contract documents and completed annexures (deduction rates, thicknesses) override. Standards cited TfNSW G71 Related Library RMS and TfNSW specifications Skills

notes.title: Verify trench backfill compaction around drainage structures under R11
notes.body:
# Verify trench backfill compaction around drainage structures under R11

> **Source:** `r011.pdf` (Clauses 4.9.1-4.9.2, Tables R11.2 and R11.3 (Ed 5 Rev 2, Jan 2017)), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** A drainage structure backfill lot is accepted or rejected against R11's relative compaction and layering rules, with the correct field density test method used.

## Inputs

- Lot definition (structure type, zone: bed/haunch/side/overlay, foundation, general backfill)
- Field density and moisture test results with laboratory maximum density
- Layer thickness records during placement
- Oversize fraction (% retained on 37.5 mm sieve) of the fill
- Concrete age/strength records if backfilling against cast-in-place structures

## Procedure

1. Identify which R11 compaction category the lot falls into (open drain surface, trench base/foundation, select fill around pipes, side/overlay of box culverts, or backfill within the adjoining Selected Material Zone) and read the minimum characteristic relative compaction from Table R11.2 (values range from 95% to 102%).
2. Confirm fill was placed in layers not exceeding the compacted thickness limit in Clause 4.9.1 (150 mm unless directed otherwise).
3. Select the field density test method from Table R11.3 based on the oversize fraction: nuclear gauge or sand replacement for low oversize, sand replacement only for intermediate oversize, fixed volume extractive for fine cohesionless materials; note the nuclear gauge is barred for layers thicker than 300 mm.
4. Compute the characteristic value of relative compaction statistically per Specification RMS Q and round to 0.1% before comparing with Table R11.2.
5. For backfill against concrete structures, verify timing rules in Clause 4.9.1 were met (minimum concrete strength fraction for cast-in-place box culverts, minimum elapsed days for other structures) and that fill levels on opposite sides of box culverts stayed within the differential limit.

## Decision rules

- If more than 40% by mass is retained on the 37.5 mm sieve, do not report relative compaction - the result is invalid (Table R11.3 note).
- If the characteristic relative compaction is below the Table R11.2 minimum for that zone, the lot is nonconforming.
- If backfill within the adjoining earthworks Selected Material Zone is involved, the higher R44-linked compaction standard in Table R11.2 governs, not the general backfill value.
- Compact fill next to the structure first and work outwards toward the excavation face to avoid wedge action (Clause 4.9.1).

## Checks

- One test method only used per lot for statistical assessment
- Layer thickness records consistent with the compacted thickness limit
- Moisture control documented so nearby earthworks are not wetted up
- Box culvert side/overlay zones backfilled with Type SO Select Fill, with the 1000 mm minimum select fill envelope and geotextile separation where inside rock fill embankments

## Common errors

- Using the nuclear gauge on layers thicker than 300 mm or on material with 20-40% oversize
- Applying the general backfill compaction value to box culvert side/overlay zones, which carry a higher requirement
- Backfilling against green concrete before the strength/age criteria are met
- Letting backfill on one side of a box culvert run ahead of the other beyond the differential limit

## Caveats

- Verify the spec edition (Ed 5 Rev 2 here) is current for the project before relying on values.
- Contract documents and project-specific annexures override the base specification.

## Standards cited

RMS Q, RMS R44, RMS T119, RMS T165, RMS T166, RMS T173, AS 1597.2, AS 3725

## Related

- [[Library - RMS and TfNSW specifications]]
- [[Skills]]

notes.title: Verify unbound modified course conformity
notes.body:
# Verify unbound modified course conformity

> **Source:** `dc_r071.pdf` (Clauses 6.4-6.7, 7 and 8 (Tables R71.1)), held in the local reference library — see
> [[Reference library]]. This note is a paraphrased working aid, not the
> document. Values, clauses and criteria must be read from the source before
> they are relied on, and engineering conclusions need qualified review.

**Outcome.** Lot-by-lot conformity verdicts for a placed unbound/modified pavement course covering compaction, geometry, surface and readiness for sealing.

## Inputs

- Survey levels of underlying and finished surfaces (staff base area and seal-thickness corrections per the survey clause)
- In-situ density, moisture and reference density tests per lot
- Straightedge, ride-quality and ball-penetration measurements

## Procedure

1. Place layers within the allowed compacted thickness band and compact full depth; test each layer separately where multiple layers form the course.
2. Assess relative compaction as a characteristic value per lot against the material-designation table.
3. Check thickness, surface level, 3 m straightedge deviation, width and ride quality against their tolerances.
4. Before sealing: dry the base back, verify moisture over full depth, and run the ball penetration test at undisturbed density-test locations; then release the priming/sealing hold point on conformity reports.
5. Raise nonconformity reports and disposition nonconforming lots through the rectification hold point.

## Decision rules

- Layer compacted thickness must be 100-150 mm (dc_r071 Clause 6.5).
- Characteristic relative compaction: heavy-duty base 100% (modified compaction); heavy-duty subbase and non-heavy-duty material 102% (standard compaction) (dc_r071 Table R71.1).
- Base thickness tolerance -0/+20 mm with automatic level control (+10/+30 mm without); subbase plus/minus 10 mm; base level -0/+10 mm, subbase -10/+0 mm (dc_r071 Clauses 8.5-8.6).
- Surface deviation under a 3 m straightedge must not exceed 5 mm (dc_r071 Clause 8.7).
- Ride quality at or above 65 NAASRA counts/km (IRI 2.5 m/km) over 100 m requires rework or replacement (dc_r071 Clause 8.8).
- Base moisture at sealing must not exceed 70% of optimum (dc_r071 Clauses 6.7, 8.4.5).
- Ball penetration: sample average below 3.0 mm and lot characteristic below 2.5 mm (dc_r071 Clause 8.10).

## Checks

- Underlying surface levels higher than design are flagged as nonconforming before placing.
- Test holes reinstated to equivalent compaction.
- Weekly conformity certificate plus daily moisture/density submissions.

## Common errors

- Sealing over a base that has wetted up above the dryback limit.
- Assessing compaction on individual results rather than the lot characteristic value.
- Surveying thickness from unrecoverable points (points must be recoverable within the stated tolerance).

## Caveats

- Verify edition currency; project deed documents override.
- Tolerances cited from the referenced clauses only.

## Standards cited

RMS T111/T112/T119/T162/T166/T173, RMS T182/T188, RMS T271, RMS D&C Q6

## Related

- [[Library - RMS and TfNSW specifications]]
- [[Skills]]

notes.title: AS 1726 soil and rock description
notes.body:
# AS 1726 soil and rock description

AS 1726:2017 *Geotechnical site investigations* is the Australian standard that
sets out how ground is described and logged. It is the reason two engineers
logging the same core should produce comparable descriptions.

> The standard itself is copyright and is not reproduced here. Clause numbers
> are recorded so the passage can be found; check the actual document before
> relying on any of this on a job.

## What it governs

- The vocabulary for soil and rock description, and the order terms appear in —
  see [[Soil description order]].
- Weathering and strength classification for rock — see
  [[Rock weathering classes]] and [[Rock strength classes]].
- Sampling and in-situ test reporting requirements.
- What a borehole log must show — see [[Borehole log conventions]].

## Why the order matters

The description order is not stylistic. A log is read by people scanning a
column for a change in material, so the governing term comes first and the
qualifiers follow. Writing "brown clay, high plasticity" instead of
"CLAY: high plasticity, brown" breaks the scan.

## Related

- [[AS 2159 piling]] — founding requirements that rely on these descriptions
- [[Weathered siltstone]] — the description applied on most of our Sydney work

notes.title: AS 2159 piling
notes.body:
# AS 2159 piling

AS 2159:2009 *Piling — Design and installation* governs pile design and
construction, including bored piers.

> Summarised, not reproduced. Clause references are pointers, not quotations.

## What we lean on it for

- **Base cleanliness and concrete placement.** Clause 7.6.5(c) is the one cited
  in most of our inspection reports: loose or softened material at the base is
  removed before concrete, and concrete follows promptly after drilling,
  cleaning and geotechnical approval. See [[Bored pier inspection]].
- **Founding verification.** The pier is proved into the material the design
  assumed, not merely to a nominated depth.
- **Risk rating and the geotechnical strength reduction factor.** The standard
  ties the factor to how much site investigation and construction control there
  actually is — better investigation earns a higher factor.

## The practical consequence for inspections

Our sign-off is that the exposed founding material was competent and consistent
with the design assumption at the time of inspection. That is a narrower claim
than "the pile is adequate", and the report wording keeps it narrow. Acceptance
of the pile as a structural element remains with the design engineer — see
[[Socket compliance is indeterminate by default]].

## Related

- [[Rock socket length]]
- [[AS 1726 soil and rock description]]

notes.title: AS 2870 residential site classification
notes.body:
# AS 2870 residential site classification

AS 2870 *Residential slabs and footings* classifies sites by how much the soil
moves with moisture change, which then drives the footing design.

> Summarised. Class definitions and design tables live in the standard.

## Classes in short

- **A** — stable, little or no ground movement from moisture change (sand, rock)
- **S** — slightly reactive clay
- **M** — moderately reactive clay or silt
- **H1 / H2** — highly reactive clay
- **E** — extremely reactive clay
- **P** — problem site: fill, soft soil, mine subsidence, landslip, or where the
  above cannot be applied

## What decides the class

Characteristic surface movement `y_s`, calculated from soil reactivity and the
depth of the design suction change. Reactivity comes from shrink-swell index
testing, not from the description alone — a clay that looks the same in two
suburbs can classify differently.

## The trap

Fill, cut, and trees change the answer. A site with uncontrolled fill is P
regardless of the clay underneath it, and removing a large tree can leave years
of ongoing heave. Classification without checking site history is guesswork.

## Related

- [[Soil description order]]
- [[DCP testing]]
